# mokosh-server specification

This document is normative. Every requirement carries a stable id `SPEC-<section>.<n>`, uses "must" / "must not", and is
cited at its implementing or enforcing site in the code by a `// SPEC-<section>.<n>` comment (a `#` comment in TOML,
YAML, shell and Nushell). Where this document and another document disagree, this document and the code win; where this
document and the code disagree, the code is a defect to be tracked in an issue. Section 9 requirements are enforced by
the committed migrations themselves, which are immutable and therefore carry no comments.

## 1. Purpose and scope

### 1.1 Purpose and deployment shape

mokosh-server is the API server of a professional services automation (PSA) platform for managed service providers
(MSPs): a multi-tenant JSON-over-HTTP service backed by PostgreSQL in which each tenant is one MSP organization. Its
callers are the MSP's staff, the MSP's client contacts through a separate contact plane, and platform administrators who
operate the deployment. Domain behavior is specified in sections 3 to 15; this section and section 2 specify the process
around it.

- **SPEC-1.1**: The server must run in multi-tenant mode only: `AppConfig::is_multi_tenant` must return `true` in every
  environment, no setting selects a single-tenant mode, and startup must log the info line `Running in multi-tenant
  mode` once, before any configuration is read.
- **SPEC-1.2**: The server process must serve only the router returned by `create_api_router` (SPEC-2.55): it must serve
  no static file, browser client or user-interface asset, and a request matching no route must receive the HTML 404 page
  of SPEC-2.94.
- **SPEC-1.3**: The workspace crate `crates/mokosh-types`, which holds the wire types shared with the browser client,
  must depend only on `serde`, `serde_json`, `chrono`, `chrono-tz`, `uuid`, `validator` and `rust_decimal`, and must not
  depend on axum, sqlx, tokio, reqwest or the root package.
- **SPEC-1.4**: Identity provisioning for the hosted deployment profile must be delegated to the external OIDC identity
  provider (provider name `bunyip`, variables `BUNYIP_*`): the `saas` hosting profile must default authentication to
  `bunyip` then `local`, and the `self-hosted` profile must default it to `local` (SPEC-2.238, SPEC-2.239).

### 1.2 Non-goals

- **SPEC-1.5**: The server must not act as an OIDC provider: it must mount no OIDC discovery document, JWKS,
  authorization or userinfo endpoint of its own. `POST /api/v1/bunyip/oauth2/backchannel-logout` is a receiver for the
  identity provider's logout tokens, and the `/authorize` routes under `/integrations/` start outbound OAuth connections
  to third parties; neither is a provider endpoint.
- **SPEC-1.6**: The server must read application configuration only through keys declared in the registry (SPEC-2.178);
  a key not declared there has no reader, and a direct environment read outside the allowlisted entry points must fail
  the unit-test build (SPEC-2.224).
- **SPEC-1.7**: The scheduler must perform no leader election and take no distributed lock: every process that calls
  `Scheduler::start` must tick every job registered on it, so running several replicas runs every job once per replica
  per interval, and safety between replicas is the responsibility of each job (SPEC-2.119).
- **SPEC-1.8**: The server must not implement graceful shutdown: it must install no signal handler and call
  `axum::serve` without `with_graceful_shutdown`, so on SIGTERM or SIGINT the operating system's default action ends the
  process and in-flight requests, scheduler ticks and one-shot passes are cut off rather than drained (SPEC-2.57).

### 1.3 Process model

- **SPEC-1.9**: A deployment instance must be one operating-system process running one multi-threaded tokio runtime
  (`#[tokio::main]`) and one TCP listener bound to `{HOST}:{PORT}`; that listener must serve every tenant, tenant
  selection happening per request, and the server must start no per-tenant process or listener.
- **SPEC-1.10**: The `mokosh-server` binary must also host the operator subcommands: when `argv[1]` names a recognised
  subcommand the process must run only that subcommand and exit (SPEC-2.15), and must not load configuration through the
  registry, connect to the database or bind a port.
- **SPEC-1.11**: Background work must run inside the server process: the interval jobs listed in SPEC-2.130 must be
  ticked by the in-process scheduler and the one-shot passes of SPEC-2.128 must be spawned once at boot; no separate
  worker binary or process exists.
- **SPEC-1.12**: The listener must be bound only after configuration, secrets, database, migrations, providers and
  workers have been constructed (SPEC-2.55); a hard boot failure must end the process with a non-zero exit status and a
  diagnostic, and no port is bound before it (SPEC-2.58).
- **SPEC-1.13**: Tenant isolation must be enforced by the database as well as by service code: request-serving queries
  must run as the unprivileged `mokosh_app` role under the `tenant_isolation` row-level-security policy keyed on the
  `app.current_tenant` setting, so a query that omits its tenant filter returns no rows (SPEC-2.147, SPEC-2.149).

### 1.4 Retention and cleanup

The code covered by sections 1 and 2 owns no application data. Its retention-related behavior is limited to connection
recycling, one-time storage corrections and test-database cleanup; the row-expiry rule of each domain is specified with
its module.

- **SPEC-1.14**: A pooled database connection must be recycled after 600 seconds idle or 1800 seconds of age, and
  recycling must never delete or modify rows (SPEC-2.145).
- **SPEC-1.15**: The jobs that delete or expire rows must be registered on the scheduler at boot at these intervals:
  `status_retention` every 21600 seconds, `grant_invitations_expiry_sweep` every 3600 seconds and `contract_lifecycle`
  every 3600 seconds; the window and per-row rule of each is specified in its owning section (SPEC-15.2118, SPEC-5.245,
  SPEC-13.1350).
- **SPEC-1.16**: A one-shot correction pass must run once per process start and never on an interval; a pass that fails
  must log a warning naming the pass and must not stop the server, and it runs again at the next restart (SPEC-2.126).
- **SPEC-1.17**: A test database cloned by the test harness must be dropped when its test passes and kept, with its name
  printed, when it fails; template databases of older migration sets that have no session must be dropped when a new
  template is built (SPEC-2.271, SPEC-2.281).

## 2. Architecture

### 2.1 Workspace

The repository is one cargo workspace. The toolchain pin (`rust-toolchain.toml`) and the profile and dependency-hygiene
rules are specified in section 10 (SPEC-10.149, SPEC-10.151).

- **SPEC-2.1**: The workspace must resolve with `resolver = "2"` and contain exactly these five members: the root
  package `mokosh-server`, `crates/mokosh-types`, `crates/build-metadata`, `crates/mokosh-test-macros` and
  `crates/mokosh-test`.
- **SPEC-2.2**: The root package must build the library `mokosh_server` from `src/lib.rs` and two binaries:
  `mokosh-server` from `src/main.rs` and `mokosh-bootstrap` from `src/bin/mokosh-bootstrap.rs`.
- **SPEC-2.3**: The root package must define the cargo features `multi-tenant` and `server`, both enabled by default;
  the `server` feature must gate the `db` module's `Database`, `TenantTransaction`, `provision`, `identity` and
  `platform_admin` items, and the `multi-tenant` feature must gate `Database::begin_with_tenant` and
  `TenantTransaction`.
- **SPEC-2.4**: `crates/build-metadata` must have no dependencies and must be a build-dependency of the root package
  only; the root `build.rs` must call its `emit` function (SPEC-2.253).
- **SPEC-2.5**: `mokosh-test` must be reachable from the root package only as a dev-dependency, so nothing it defines is
  compiled into a release binary; `mokosh-test-macros` must be a proc-macro crate (`proc-macro = true`), and
  `mokosh-test` must re-export its `mokosh_test` attribute so a test binary names one crate.
- **SPEC-2.6**: A release build must abort the process on panic (`panic = "abort"`), so a boot-time `.expect` failure in
  a release binary ends the process by abort (SIGABRT) instead of unwinding to exit status 101 (SPEC-2.24).

### 2.2 Technology stack

The stack is declared in `Cargo.toml`. The statements below are the declarations a build or runtime behavior depends on;
versions are the requirement strings in the manifest, and `Cargo.lock` pins the resolved versions.

- **SPEC-2.7**: `tokio` must be built with its `full` feature set, which provides the multi-threaded runtime that
  `#[tokio::main]` starts.
- **SPEC-2.8**: `jsonwebtoken` 10 must be built with the `rust_crypto` provider feature; without a provider the first
  JWT sign or verify panics.
- **SPEC-2.9**: `tower-http` must be built with both `compression-gzip` and `compression-br`, so the compression layer
  can answer `Accept-Encoding: br` as well as gzip.
- **SPEC-2.10**: Outbound HTTP in the server must use `reqwest` 0.12 with default features off and `rustls-tls`, `json`
  and `stream` enabled, so outbound TLS does not use the system TLS stack.
- **SPEC-2.11**: SMTP must use `lettre` 0.11 with default features off and `tokio1-native-tls`, `builder`,
  `smtp-transport` and `pool` enabled, so the SMTP mailer uses native TLS and reuses pooled connections.
- **SPEC-2.12**: `sqlx` 0.8 must be built with `runtime-tokio`, `postgres`, `uuid`, `chrono`, `json`, `migrate`,
  `rust_decimal` and `ipnetwork`; PostgreSQL is the only database driver.
- **SPEC-2.13**: The three shared first-party crates (Stripe core, IP enrichment and provider
  status) must be git dependencies pinned by `rev` (commit 91e27f2b798128aa2cf54f742df8248564888bf0),
  never by branch or tag, so a change of their code is an explicit manifest edit.
- **SPEC-2.14**: `printpdf` 0.12 must be built with default features off and only the `png`, `jpeg`, `gif` and `webp`
  image codecs.

### 2.3 Runtime shape

`mokosh-server` is one long-running process. `src/main.rs` runs the steps below in order. A hard failure ends startup:
either `main` returns an error (the process prints `Error: <cause>` to stderr and exits with status 1) or a boot-time
`.expect` panics (exit status 101 in a debug build, abort in a release build, SPEC-2.6). A soft failure is logged and
boot continues; each step states which.

- **SPEC-2.15**: When `argv[1]` is a recognised operator subcommand (`mokosh_server::cli::is_subcommand`), `main` must
  call `run_cli` and return its result before the server's tracing subscriber is installed and before the environment
  file, the configuration provider or the database is touched.
- **SPEC-2.16**: The server path must install a `tracing` formatting subscriber filtered by `RUST_LOG` read from the
  process environment, defaulting to the filter `info` when `RUST_LOG` is unset or does not parse; because this runs
  before the `.env` file is loaded, a `RUST_LOG` defined only in `.env` must have no effect on the server path.
- **SPEC-2.17**: The server path must log the build banner at info level as `Starting <name> <describe> (<hash>) built
  <date>` (SPEC-2.252) before it reads any configuration.
- **SPEC-2.18**: The server path must load the first `.env` found in the working directory or its nearest ancestor with
  `dotenvy::dotenv`, which must not override a variable already present in the process environment; a missing file (an
  I/O not-found error) must be ignored, and any other load failure (unreadable or malformed file) must end startup with
  the error `.env could not be loaded: <cause>`.
- **SPEC-2.19**: Before any provider is built, `main` must read `MOKOSH_DEPLOYMENT_MODE` with the strict reader
  `DeploymentMode::from_env_for_providers`: an unrecognised value must end startup with an error naming the legal values
  `self-hosted` and `saas`, and an unset or blank value must select `self-hosted` at this step (the deployment-shape
  check of SPEC-2.25 refuses a blank value outside development).
- **SPEC-2.20**: Before any configuration read, `main` must refuse to boot when a retired storage variable name
  (`STORAGE_BACKEND`, `ATTACHMENT_DIR` or a bare `S3_*` name) is set non-blank: the replacement-naming message must be
  printed to stderr with `eprintln!` and also returned as the startup error.
- **SPEC-2.21**: `main` must call `config::init_from_env` with the hosting profile's Configuration default before
  `AppConfig` or any other consumer asks for a value; a failure (for example an unrecognised `CONFIG_BACKEND`) must end
  startup with that error (SPEC-2.186).
- **SPEC-2.22**: After the configuration provider is initialised, `main` must call `config::flags::check_boot`; a
  feature flag set to a non-blank unparseable value must end startup with the combined error of SPEC-2.221.
- **SPEC-2.23**: `main` must call `config::parse::check_boot::<Uuid>` for `OIDC_DEFAULT_TENANT_ID`; a set value that is
  not a UUID must end startup with an error naming the variable and the value, so the first request never silently
  resolves to a fallback tenant.
- **SPEC-2.24**: `main` must build `AppConfig` with `AppConfig::from_env()` and must panic with `Failed to load
  configuration` followed by the cause on any error it returns (an unset or dev-valued secret, a short `JWT_SECRET`, a
  malformed `ENCRYPTION_KEY`, or an unparseable `PORT`, `RUN_MIGRATIONS` or `MOKOSH_MAX_TENANTS`) instead of returning
  it.
- **SPEC-2.25**: After `AppConfig` is built, `main` must call `check_deployment_requirements` with the resolved
  environment; outside `development`, `dev` and `test` it must refuse to boot if any of `DATABASE_URL`,
  `MOKOSH_DEPLOYMENT_MODE`, `MOKOSH_APP_DATABASE_URL`, `BASE_URL`, `CLIENT_ORIGIN` and `SPA_BASE_URL` is unset or blank,
  with one error that starts `boot refused: <n> essential deployment-shape variable(s) unset in the '<environment>'
  environment` and contains a block per missing variable.
- **SPEC-2.26**: Each missing-variable block of the deployment-shape error must read `FATAL: <NAME> is unset in the
  '<environment>' environment.`, then `Purpose: <text>`, then, only for `MOKOSH_DEPLOYMENT_MODE`, `Available options:
  self-hosted | saas`, then `Example: <NAME>=<example value>`; every missing variable must be listed in one run, not one
  per boot attempt.
- **SPEC-2.27**: The environment names `development`, `dev` and `test` (exact, lower-case) must be the only ones that
  may use the built-in secret fallbacks, a short `JWT_SECRET`, a non-hex `ENCRYPTION_KEY` and unset deployment-shape
  variables; every other value, including an empty string, `Development` or `staging`, must be treated as a deployed
  environment. When `ENVIRONMENT` is unset the environment must be `development`.
- **SPEC-2.28**: `resolve_secret` must treat an unset or empty `JWT_SECRET`, `ENCRYPTION_KEY` or `BUNYIP_WEBHOOK_SECRET`
  as absent: in a development environment it must return the built-in development value, and elsewhere it must fail with
  `<NAME> is unset but required in the '<environment>' environment; the hardcoded dev fallback is only accepted in
  development/dev/test.`; a value equal to the built-in development value must fail outside development with `<NAME> is
  set to the known dev fallback value, which is refused in the '<environment>' environment.` followed by the instruction
  to set a real secret.
- **SPEC-2.29**: Outside the development environments a `JWT_SECRET` shorter than 32 bytes must fail with `JWT_SECRET
  must be at least 32 bytes in the '<environment>' environment; only development/dev/test accept a shorter secret.`; the
  development environments accept any length.
- **SPEC-2.30**: Outside the development environments `ENCRYPTION_KEY` must be exactly 64 ASCII hexadecimal characters,
  else `AppConfig::from_env` must fail with `ENCRYPTION_KEY must be a 64-character hex string in the '<environment>'
  environment (32 bytes, hex-encoded); only development/dev/test accept a raw 32-byte key.`
- **SPEC-2.31**: `AppConfig::from_env` must take `DATABASE_URL` as the trimmed-non-blank configured value; when it is
  unset or blank it must use `postgres://postgres:postgres@localhost:5432/mokosh` in a development environment and the
  empty string elsewhere, which `check_deployment_requirements` then refuses; `app_database_url` must be the non-blank
  `MOKOSH_APP_DATABASE_URL`, else `DATABASE_URL`.
- **SPEC-2.32**: Before any request pool is opened, `main` must call `db::provision::provision_roles` with
  `DATABASE_URL`; an error from it must end startup (SPEC-2.155).
- **SPEC-2.33**: `main` must open both pools with one `Database::new(app_database_url, database_url)` call; a connection
  failure must end startup before any migration runs (SPEC-2.146).
- **SPEC-2.34**: When `RUN_MIGRATIONS` is true (the default), `main` must run the embedded migrations on the migrator
  pool and log `Database migrations complete` at info; a migration failure must be logged at error as `Failed to run
  database migrations: <cause>` and must end startup, so the server never serves a half-migrated database. When
  `RUN_MIGRATIONS` is `false`, no migration may run and nothing may be logged about skipping.
- **SPEC-2.35**: `main` must log `Database connected` at info after the migration step, whether or not migrations ran.
- **SPEC-2.36**: `main` must call `modules::auth::bootstrap::maybe_bootstrap_admin` after migrations; an error from it
  must be logged at warn as `Admin bootstrap failed: <cause>` and boot must continue (the bootstrap rules are in
  SPEC-5.6).
- **SPEC-2.37**: `main` must log, at info and unconditionally, the line `Auth: bunyip-as-OP Resource-Server + legacy
  HS256 cookie (mokosh-auth removed)`; the line is fixed text and is not derived from which authentication providers
  resolved.
- **SPEC-2.38**: `main` must parse `ENCRYPTION_KEY` into the 32-byte key with `utils::crypto::parse_encryption_key` and
  must panic with `ENCRYPTION_KEY must be 32 bytes (or 64 hex chars)` if it does not parse; in a development environment
  the raw 32-byte form is accepted.
- **SPEC-2.39**: `main` must build the per-secret provider defaults of the hosting profile and install the
  application-tier secret providers with `app_secrets::init_from_env` before any provider-backed secret is read; a
  failure of either call must end startup.
- **SPEC-2.40**: `main` must resolve, once, the host's Google OAuth client, the Microsoft OAuth client and the Xero and
  Intuit applications from the application-tier secrets; a pair of which exactly one half is set must end startup with
  an error naming the missing key, and a pair with both halves unset must resolve to no client without error.
- **SPEC-2.41**: The Google and Microsoft client handles must each be created once and the same `Arc` handed to the
  contact-sync worker's service, to the router and to the settings write path, so a deployment operator's change to the
  client pair takes effect in the API and in the worker without a restart.
- **SPEC-2.42**: If `app_secrets::current()` returns `None` after `init_from_env` succeeded, `main` must end startup
  with the error `the application-tier secret providers were not installed, so no deployment-wide secret can be read or
  written` instead of panicking.
- **SPEC-2.43**: `main` must load the product-name setting into the process cache with
  `settings::app_name::resolve_and_cache` before any request can render it; a failure must be logged at warn as `could
  not load the app-name setting; using the default` with the error, and boot must continue with the built-in default
  name.
- **SPEC-2.44**: `main` must resolve the mail provider with `EmailConfig::from_env` using the hosting profile's Email
  default; an unrecognised `MAIL_PROVIDER` must end startup, and the chosen provider and its source (`profile` or
  `explicit`) must be logged at info as `email provider selected`.
- **SPEC-2.45**: `main` must panic when the mailer configuration cannot be loaded from the database settings or `SMTP_*`
  variables (`Failed to load Mailer config from DB settings / SMTP_* env (see .env.example)`), and must panic when the
  mailer for the selected provider cannot be built, which includes `MAIL_PROVIDER=smtp` with no `SMTP_HOST`.
- **SPEC-2.46**: `main` must verify the mail transport before serving: a verify failure must be logged at error as
  `email provider verify failed` with the error and must end startup; the log provider's verify must succeed without a
  network call and the SMTP provider's verify must perform a NOOP exchange with the relay.
- **SPEC-2.47**: `main` must construct the identity-provider bearer verifier only when its configuration resolves: on
  success it must log `Bunyip RS verifier mounted` at info with the issuer and audience, and on any configuration error
  it must log `Bunyip RS verifier disabled` at info with the reason and continue with no verifier (the legacy HS256 path
  still serves).
- **SPEC-2.48**: `main` must resolve the authentication provider selection from `AUTH_PROVIDERS` or the hosting
  profile's default, an invalid selection ending startup; it must log the selection with `record()` and install it
  process-wide before the router is built, so every later reader sees the same selection.
- **SPEC-2.49**: `main` must build the tenant-tier secret provider once with `secrets::provider_from_env` and share it
  with the router and the workers that read gateway credentials; a misconfiguration must panic with `secret provider
  configuration`.
- **SPEC-2.50**: `main` must build the object storage provider once with `storage::init_from_env` before any request is
  served; a misconfiguration must panic with `storage provider configuration`.
- **SPEC-2.51**: After every provider is built, `main` must compute the selection for all five capability kinds from the
  hosting profile and the overrides each capability reported, and log it with `record()`; it must perform no validation
  of its own (SPEC-2.241).
- **SPEC-2.52**: `main` must create one `FeatureSnapshot` with every toggle off and share it with the feature-toggle
  refresh job and both routers; a request served before the refresh job's first tick completes sees every feature off,
  whatever the database rows say.
- **SPEC-2.53**: `main` must build the IP2Location service from `IP2LOCATION_DB_PATH` only when the path is set
  non-blank; an unset path must log `IP2LOCATION_DB_PATH unset; login-location alerts disabled` at info, and a `.BIN`
  that fails to load must log `Failed to load IP2Location DB; login-location alerts disabled` at warn with the path and
  error; neither case may end startup, and login must be unaffected.
- **SPEC-2.54**: `main` must build the IP2Proxy enrichment service from `IP2PROXY_DB_PATH` independently of the
  geolocation service: an unset path must log `IP2PROXY_DB_PATH unset; IP enrichment disabled` at info, and a `.BIN`
  that fails to load must log `Failed to load IP2Proxy DB; IP enrichment disabled` at warn; neither case may end
  startup.
- **SPEC-2.55**: `main` must build the router with exactly one `create_api_router` call, after every provider, worker
  and secret above is ready and after `Scheduler::start`; it is the last construction step before the listener binds.
- **SPEC-2.56**: `main` must bind a TCP listener on the socket address `{HOST}:{PORT}` and log `Server listening on
  http://<addr>` at info after the bind succeeds; the address must parse as an IP literal and port (so a host name, or
  an IPv6 address without brackets, must end startup with an address-parse error), and a bind failure such as a port
  already in use must end startup with the operating-system error.
- **SPEC-2.57**: `main` must serve the router with `axum::serve` over
  `into_make_service_with_connect_info::<SocketAddr>()`, so handlers can read the peer address, with no
  graceful-shutdown handler and no signal handling; `axum::serve` returning an error must end the process with status 1
  (SPEC-1.8).
- **SPEC-2.58**: When `main` returns an error the process must exit with status 1 after writing `Error: <debug form of
  the error>` to stderr (a multi-line message therefore appears with escaped newlines).
- **SPEC-2.59**: `run_cli` must load `.env.infisical` and then `.env` (each found in the working directory or its
  nearest ancestor) without overriding variables already set (so a variable present in both files takes the
  `.env.infisical` value), ignoring a missing file and failing with `env file could not be loaded: <cause>` for any
  other load error, and must then install a tracing subscriber with the same `RUST_LOG`-or-`info` rule as the server
  path, now able to see a `RUST_LOG` from those files.
- **SPEC-2.60**: A subcommand error must be written to stderr as `error: <cause chain>` and the process must exit with
  status 1 through `std::process::exit(1)`; a subcommand that succeeds must return `Ok` from `main`, exit status 0.

### 2.4 Request pipeline

The router is built by `create_api_router` in `src/api/router.rs`; the JSON sanitiser lives in `src/utils/text.rs` and
the error envelope in `src/utils/error.rs`. Authentication extractors and the per-module gates are specified in section
5, and tenant-scoped database access in section 2.6.

- **SPEC-2.61**: The router must wrap every response, from every mount and from the fallback, in five layers, outermost
  first: security response headers, CORS, response compression, request tracing, JSON body sanitising.
- **SPEC-2.62**: Every response (API, contact API, webhook receivers and the fallback page) must carry the headers added
  by the security-headers layer, because that layer is outermost.
- **SPEC-2.63**: The CORS layer must answer a preflight request before the JSON sanitiser or any route runs, because
  CORS wraps sanitising.
- **SPEC-2.64**: The router must allow cross-origin requests only for origins accepted by the `CORS_ORIGIN` matcher,
  with the methods GET, POST, PUT, DELETE, PATCH and OPTIONS, the request headers Authorization, Content-Type, Accept
  and X-Forwarded-Host, credentials allowed, and a preflight cache lifetime of 600 seconds.
- **SPEC-2.65**: The router must compress responses with the default compression layer: a client that advertises
  `br,gzip` must get `Content-Encoding: br`, and a client that advertises only `gzip` must get `Content-Encoding: gzip`.
- **SPEC-2.66**: The JSON sanitiser must be layered once on the combined router, so it sees the full `/api/v1/...` path
  before nesting strips the prefix and runs for every mount; the signed prefixes are exempted inside the function by
  path, not by which mount the layer wraps.
- **SPEC-2.67**: The sanitiser must forward a request unchanged when its path starts with `/api/v1/bunyip/`,
  `/api/v1/rmm/alerts`, `/api/v1/rmm/status`, `/api/v1/stripe/`, `/api/v1/paypal/` or `/api/v1/webhooks/`, so that
  signature and echo checks see the original bytes.
- **SPEC-2.68**: The sanitiser must forward a request unchanged and unbuffered when its Content-Type is not
  `application/json` or `application/<x>+json` (parameters such as charset ignored, case-insensitive), or when the
  header is not visible ASCII, so the extractor rejects it.
- **SPEC-2.69**: The sanitiser must forward a JSON request unchanged and unbuffered when its Content-Length header is
  greater than 25 MiB (26,214,400 bytes); the route's own body limit then decides acceptance.
- **SPEC-2.70**: The sanitiser must answer 413 with code `PAYLOAD_TOO_LARGE` and message `The request body could not be
  read.` when a JSON body with a missing or understated Content-Length cannot be buffered within 25 MiB, and must log a
  warning naming the path and the cause.
- **SPEC-2.71**: The sanitiser must forward an empty body, or a body that is not valid JSON, with its original bytes, so
  the `Json` extractor produces the 400.
- **SPEC-2.72**: For a valid JSON body the sanitiser must replace the body with an empty one, remove the Content-Length
  header, and hand the parsed, sanitised tree to the `Json` extractor through a request extension.
- **SPEC-2.73**: The router must mount exactly seven trees: `/api/v1` (session), `/api/v1/public` (no authentication),
  `/api/v1/contact` (contact Bearer), and the four self-authenticating receivers `/api/v1/bunyip`, `/api/v1/stripe`,
  `/api/v1/paypal` and `/api/v1/webhooks` (signature or echo verification).
- **SPEC-2.74**: The `/api/v1/bunyip` mount must carry `POST /webhooks/account-deleted` and `POST
  /webhooks/mokosh-grant-changed`, both outside the session middleware and authenticated by an HMAC over the raw body.
- **SPEC-2.75**: The account-deleted webhook must run on the migrator (BYPASSRLS) pool because it is pre-authentication
  and resolves the tenant from the `users` row it reads.
- **SPEC-2.76**: When a Bunyip verifier is configured the router must mount `POST
  /api/v1/bunyip/oauth2/backchannel-logout` outside the session middleware and outside the error-envelope normaliser,
  authenticated by the logout token's own signature; when no verifier is configured the route must not be mounted and a
  request to it reaches the fallback.
- **SPEC-2.77**: `POST /api/v1/stripe/webhooks/{tenant_id}` and `POST /api/v1/paypal/webhooks/{tenant_id}` must be
  served by one shared handler that differs only in provider id (`stripe` or `paypal`) and the billing state passed in.
- **SPEC-2.78**: The router must serve invoice-issuer webhooks at exactly `POST /api/v1/webhooks/xero` and `POST
  /api/v1/webhooks/quickbooks`, one URL per provider and no tenant id in the path.
- **SPEC-2.79**: When the `multi-tenant` cargo feature is off, the router must not mount `/tenants`, `/teams` or `/me`,
  and a request to any of them reaches the fallback.
- **SPEC-2.80**: The `/api/v1/contact` mount must serve the contact portal routes merged with the branding module's
  contact routes.
- **SPEC-2.81**: On `/api/v1` a request must pass, outermost first: the error-envelope normaliser, the database,
  settings and platform-admin request extensions, the contact-plane middleware, the staff auth middleware, then the
  first-visit demo seeding middleware.
- **SPEC-2.82**: The contact-plane middleware must run on every `/api/v1` request, so a contact Bearer on a dual-plane
  route (tickets, invoices, quotes) is recorded as contact authentication state and never overwrites an authenticated
  staff request.
- **SPEC-2.83**: The seeding middleware must run inside the auth middleware so it sees the resolved tenant and user.
- **SPEC-2.84**: `/api/v1` must serve `GET /health`, `GET /ready`, `GET /version`, `GET /version/check`, the public
  provider summary and `/grants/invitations/by-token/*` without a session.
- **SPEC-2.85**: `/api/v1/public` must serve, without a session, the feature map, the Xero and QuickBooks OAuth
  redirects, the contact-sync OAuth redirects, the tenant logo, public branding assets, knowledge-base inline images,
  inline ticket images and the request forms.
- **SPEC-2.86**: A non-JSON 4xx response from any wrapped mount must be replaced by the JSON envelope
  `{"error":{"code","message"}}` with the same status, discarding the original body and headers: 400 `BAD_REQUEST` (`The
  request was malformed or could not be read.`), 413 `PAYLOAD_TOO_LARGE`, 415 `UNSUPPORTED_MEDIA_TYPE` (`Content-Type
  must be application/json.`), 411 `LENGTH_REQUIRED`, 405 `METHOD_NOT_ALLOWED`, 422 `BAD_REQUEST` (`The request body did
  not match the expected format.`), any other 4xx `BAD_REQUEST`.
- **SPEC-2.87**: A response that is JSON (`Content-Type` starting `application/json`), or whose status is not 4xx, must
  pass the error-envelope normaliser unchanged.
- **SPEC-2.88**: The normaliser must be layered separately on `/api/v1`, `/api/v1/bunyip`, `/api/v1/stripe`,
  `/api/v1/paypal`, `/api/v1/webhooks` (once for `/xero`, once for `/quickbooks`), `/api/v1/public` and
  `/api/v1/contact`: eight instances. The fallback page and the back-channel logout route must not be wrapped.
- **SPEC-2.89**: Every request to `/api/v1/public/*` must be charged against a per-client-IP budget of 60 requests per
  minute (`PUBLIC_API_PER_MIN`), the IP being the trusted-proxy-aware client IP; a request past the budget must answer
  429 with a `Retry-After` header (whole seconds, at least 1) and `Cache-Control: no-store`, without reaching the
  handler.
- **SPEC-2.90**: A 429 from the limiter must carry the JSON body `{"error":"rate_limited","message":"Too many requests,
  please try again shortly","retry_after_seconds":<n>}`.
- **SPEC-2.91**: Any `AppError::RateLimited` must render through the same 429 response; with no computed wait it must
  use `Retry-After: 60`.
- **SPEC-2.92**: A request by a principal whose user row is soft-deleted must be answered 410 with code
  `ACCOUNT_DELETED` and message `Account has been deleted.`
- **SPEC-2.93**: A credential extractor must answer 401 with code `TOKEN_EXPIRED` and message `Your session has
  expired.` for an expired Bearer, and must set `WWW-Authenticate` to `Bearer error="invalid_token",
  error_description="The access token expired"` (expired), `Bearer error="invalid_token"` (any other rejected Bearer),
  `Bearer error="invalid_token", error_description="The session was ended at the identity provider"` (ended session), or
  bare `Bearer` (no credential presented); a 401 from any other path must carry no challenge.
- **SPEC-2.94**: A GET to any path matching none of the seven mounts must answer 404 with an HTML page titled `API
  endpoint` whose heading is `This is an API endpoint.` and which links back to the frontend.
- **SPEC-2.95**: The fallback page link must be `https://<domain>` when the Host header starts with `api.msp.` (for
  example `api.msp.example.com` gives `https://example.com`), and otherwise the configured client origin.
- **SPEC-2.96**: The fallback page must render without the database and must HTML-escape the application name.
- **SPEC-2.97**: `GET /api/v1/health` must answer 200 with the body `OK` and must perform no dependency check.
- **SPEC-2.98**: `GET /api/v1/ready` must answer 200 with
  `{"status":"ready","checks":{"db":"ok","infisical":"ok"|"skipped"}}` when every check passes; otherwise it must answer
  503 with `"status":"not_ready"` and each failing check replaced by the string `error: <cause>`. Every response must be
  `Content-Type: application/json` with `Cache-Control: no-store`.
- **SPEC-2.99**: The readiness database check must run `SELECT 1` on the serving pool and must treat no answer within 3
  seconds as a failure with the value `error: db ping exceeded 3s`.
- **SPEC-2.100**: The readiness Infisical probe must `GET <INFISICAL_ADDRESS without trailing slash>/api/status` with a
  1 second timeout; the address is read once, on the first `/ready` request, and cached with its HTTP client for the
  life of the process, and a blank or unset address at that moment means the check reports `skipped` for the life of the
  process.
- **SPEC-2.101**: A configured Infisical probe must report `ok` on a 2xx reply and must fail readiness (503) with
  `error: <scheme://host[:port]>: <cause>` on a connection error, timeout or non-2xx status; the address shown must not
  include userinfo, query or fragment.
- **SPEC-2.102**: `GET /api/v1/version` must return the build's `VersionInfo` as JSON with no authentication
  (SPEC-2.251).
- **SPEC-2.103**: The `CORS_ORIGIN` list must be parsed once, at router construction; a malformed entry must abort
  startup with a panic naming the entry and never defer the failure to request time.
- **SPEC-2.104**: A request `Origin` must be checked against the parsed rules by byte comparison only, with no parsing
  at request time.
- **SPEC-2.105**: An empty `CORS_ORIGIN` entry (after trimming whitespace) must abort startup with the panic
  `CORS_ORIGIN entry is empty`.
- **SPEC-2.106**: A wildcard entry with nothing after `https://*.` or `http://*.` must abort startup.
- **SPEC-2.107**: A wildcard entry whose suffix contains another `*` must abort startup, because only the leftmost label
  may be a wildcard.
- **SPEC-2.108**: A wildcard entry whose suffix contains no dot must abort startup.
- **SPEC-2.109**: An entry with `*` anywhere other than a leading `https://*.` or `http://*.` (including a bare `*`)
  must abort startup.
- **SPEC-2.110**: An exact entry that is not a valid HTTP header value must abort startup.
- **SPEC-2.111**: An exact entry must match an `Origin` only when the bytes are identical, case-sensitively and with no
  normalisation (a trailing slash or a different case does not match).
- **SPEC-2.112**: A wildcard entry must match only an `Origin` that begins with the entry's own scheme, so
  `https://*.x.example.com` never matches an `http://` origin.
- **SPEC-2.113**: A wildcard entry must match when the origin's host part ends with the stored suffix, so any number of
  leading labels match (`a.b.client.example.com` matches `https://*.client.example.com`).
- **SPEC-2.114**: A wildcard entry must not match the bare apex (`https://client.example.com`) or an empty leading label
  (`https://.client.example.com`): the host must be strictly longer than the stored suffix.
- **SPEC-2.115**: A wildcard suffix comparison must be case-sensitive and byte-for-byte against the configured text, so
  an upper-case `Origin` host does not match a lower-case entry.
- **SPEC-2.116**: A wildcard suffix must be stored with a leading dot and with any port written in the entry, so an
  entry `https://*.client.example.com:8443` matches only origins ending `.client.example.com:8443`, and an entry without
  a port does not match an origin that carries one.

### 2.5 Background jobs

Periodic work runs on the shared scheduler (`src/scheduler/mod.rs`) and one-time corrections run through
`src/scheduler/one_shot.rs`; both are started from `main`. What each job does is specified with its owning module.

- **SPEC-2.117**: A registered job must implement `Job` with a `name()` that is unique among the jobs of one scheduler
  and a `run()` returning `AppResult<()>`; the scheduler must give each registration its own tokio task and tick it at
  the interval it was registered with.
- **SPEC-2.118**: Registering a second job whose `name()` equals an existing one must panic with `scheduler: duplicate
  job name "<name>"` at registration, and `Scheduler::start` must re-check the names and panic with `scheduler:
  duplicate job name "<name>" at start`, so a duplicate is never silently shadowed.
- **SPEC-2.119**: `Scheduler::start` must consume the scheduler, spawn one task per registered job in registration
  order, log `scheduler: spawning job` at info with the fields `job`, `interval_secs` and `wakeable` for each, and
  return the join handles; the caller keeps them alive or drops them.
- **SPEC-2.120**: Each job's first tick must fire immediately at start and then every `interval`, using tokio's
  `interval` with missed ticks skipped rather than queued; a tick runs to completion before the next iteration, so one
  job never overlaps itself.
- **SPEC-2.121**: Every tick must run inside an info span named `scheduler_tick` carrying the field `job`, kept attached
  to the tick's future across threads.
- **SPEC-2.122**: A tick whose `run()` returns `Err` must be logged at warn as `scheduler tick failed; will retry on
  next interval` with the fields `job` and `error`, and the loop must continue with the next interval; the scheduler
  never stops a job or retries early on an error.
- **SPEC-2.123**: A panic inside `run()` must end only that job's task in a build that unwinds; the scheduler must not
  restart it and no code observes its join handle, so the job stops ticking until the process restarts (a release build,
  which aborts on panic, ends the whole process instead).
- **SPEC-2.124**: A job registered with `register_wakeable` must keep its registered interval; calling `JobWake::wake`
  must run it as soon as it is free, logging `scheduler: woken on demand` at debug, without shifting the interval's own
  schedule.
- **SPEC-2.125**: Any number of `wake` calls made before the job next waits must collapse into a single extra run,
  because the underlying `Notify` retains at most one permit; a wake that arrives while the job is running must not be
  lost.
- **SPEC-2.126**: `spawn_once(name, task)` must spawn the task on the tokio runtime exactly once and return its join
  handle without awaiting it, inside an info span `one_shot` with the field `job`; it must never re-run the task on an
  interval (SPEC-1.16).
- **SPEC-2.127**: When a one-shot task finishes with `Ok` it must log `one-shot pass complete` at debug; when it returns
  `Err` it must log at warn `one-shot pass <name> failed; it runs again at the next restart` with the error, and the
  failure must not stop the server or any other task.
- **SPEC-2.128**: `main` must spawn five one-shot passes with `spawn_once` and must not await them:
  `kb_attachment_move`, `tenant_logo_move`, the branding-asset move (armed by `branding::mover::arm` with the storage
  root), `gateway_credential_move` and `contact_sync_client_secret_cleanup`; they must be started before
  `Scheduler::start` and before the listener binds, and the listener must not wait for them.
- **SPEC-2.129**: A local variable in `main.rs` whose name ends in `_mover` or `_cleanup` must never be passed to
  `scheduler.register`, and the number of such variables must equal the number of `ONE_SHOT_NAME` references in
  `main.rs`; a unit test reads `main.rs` and fails otherwise.
- **SPEC-2.130**: `main` must register exactly fourteen interval jobs on one `Scheduler`, each at the interval below,
  and must call `Scheduler::start` exactly once after the last registration, holding the returned handles until `main`
  ends; no other interval job may be started.
- **SPEC-2.131**: The job `feature_toggle_refresh` must be registered at the interval constant `REFRESH_INTERVAL_SECS`
  of the features module (60 seconds), sharing the `FeatureSnapshot` of SPEC-2.52 (see SPEC-15.2107).
- **SPEC-2.132**: The job `asset_signature_detector_refresh` must be registered at the interval constant
  `REFRESH_INTERVAL_SECS` of the asset-catalog module (60 seconds).
- **SPEC-2.133**: The job `notifications_dispatcher` must be registered at 5 seconds, the only job at that cadence.
- **SPEC-2.134**: The job `rmm_sync` must be registered at 60 seconds.
- **SPEC-2.135**: The job `contact_sync` must be registered as a wakeable job at 60 seconds, and the same `JobWake`
  handle must be passed to `create_api_router`, so a request that commits an import run starts it without waiting for
  the next tick.
- **SPEC-2.136**: The job `contract_lifecycle` must be registered at 3600 seconds (see SPEC-13.1350).
- **SPEC-2.137**: The job `recurring_invoicing` must be registered at 3600 seconds (see SPEC-13.42).
- **SPEC-2.138**: The job `sla_sweep` must be registered at 60 seconds.
- **SPEC-2.139**: The job `calendar_reminders` must be registered at 60 seconds (see SPEC-7.395).
- **SPEC-2.140**: The job `grant_invitations_expiry_sweep` must be registered at the module constant
  `GRANT_INVITATIONS_SWEEP_INTERVAL` (3600 seconds, see SPEC-5.245).
- **SPEC-2.141**: The job `scheduled_reports` must be registered at 60 seconds.
- **SPEC-2.142**: The job `scheduled_dashboards` must be registered at 60 seconds.
- **SPEC-2.143**: The job `invoice_reminders` must be registered at 3600 seconds, built with mail delivery and the
  single-page-app origin (see SPEC-13.43).
- **SPEC-2.144**: The job `status_retention` must be registered at 21600 seconds (6 hours, see SPEC-15.2118).

### 2.6 Database and tenancy

Two connection pools back the server: an unprivileged `mokosh_app` pool (`NOSUPERUSER NOBYPASSRLS`) that serves requests
under row-level security, and a privileged `mokosh_migrator` pool (`BYPASSRLS`) for migrations, bootstrap, the cross-
tenant workers and the few pre-authentication paths. The `tenant_isolation` policy and the tables it covers are
specified in section 9.

- **SPEC-2.145**: Each pool must be capped at 20 connections with a minimum of 2, a 30-second acquire timeout, a
  600-second idle timeout and an 1800-second maximum connection lifetime; a connection failure must be returned as
  `AppError::Database("Failed to connect to database (<label>): <cause>")` where the label is `migrator` or `app`.
- **SPEC-2.146**: `Database::new(app_url, migrator_url)` must connect the migrator pool first and then the app pool,
  must reuse the migrator pool as the app pool when the two URLs are identical (one pool of at most 20 connections, not
  two), and must log `Connected to database (app + migrator pools)` at info on success.
- **SPEC-2.147**: `Database::pool()` must return the unprivileged app pool; a serving query that does not go through
  `begin_with_tenant` returns no rows from a row-level-security table.
- **SPEC-2.148**: `Database::migrator_pool()` must return the privileged BYPASSRLS pool; every bare `.pool()` call
  elsewhere in `src/` must carry a `SAFETY (PMS-285` note within the preceding 8 lines or `scripts/check-pool-safety.nu`
  fails (SPEC-10.171).
- **SPEC-2.149**: `Database::begin_with_tenant(tenant_id)` (feature `multi-tenant`) must begin a transaction on the app
  pool and run `SELECT set_config('app.current_tenant', $1, true)` with the tenant id bound as a parameter; the `true`
  argument makes the setting transaction-local, so the tenant never leaks to the next request that reuses the pooled
  connection.
- **SPEC-2.150**: `TenantTransaction` must expose `tenant_id()`, `commit()` and `rollback()` (each consuming the value
  and returning `AppResult<()>`), must dereference to the underlying `PgConnection` so `.execute(&mut *tx)` works, and,
  when dropped without `commit`, must roll the transaction back (sqlx `Transaction` drop behavior).
- **SPEC-2.151**: `Database::health_check` must run `SELECT 1` on the app pool and, on failure, return
  `AppError::Database("Health check failed: <cause>")`.
- **SPEC-2.152**: `Database::run_migrations` must apply the migrations embedded from `./migrations` on the migrator pool
  with `set_ignore_missing(true)` (so versions applied by another migrator are not an error), log `Database migrations
  completed` at info, and on failure return `AppError::Database("Migration failed: <cause>")`.
- **SPEC-2.153**: `Database::from_pool(pool)` must use the one pool as both the app and the migrator pool, so row-level
  security does not bite for the role that pool connected as.
- **SPEC-2.154**: `Database::from_pools(app, migrator)` must keep the two pools distinct, so a test can connect the app
  pool as the unprivileged role and exercise row-level security.
- **SPEC-2.155**: `provision_roles(database_url)` must first probe and classify the deployment as `BothExist`,
  `MigratorConnectsAppMissing`, `AppPasswordMismatch` or `MigratorCannotConnect`; `BothExist` must log `mokosh_app
  present and able to log in; skipping role provisioning` at info and return `Ok` without needing any admin credential.
- **SPEC-2.156**: The probe must connect with `DATABASE_URL` (one connection, 10-second acquire timeout): a failed
  connect is `MigratorCannotConnect`; otherwise the role `mokosh_app` must exist with `rolcanlogin = TRUE` (a role that
  is missing or `NOLOGIN` is `MigratorConnectsAppMissing`, and a failed `pg_roles` query is logged at warn and treated
  the same way); when it can log in and `MOKOSH_APP_DATABASE_URL` is set non-blank, one login attempt with that URL
  decides `AppPasswordMismatch`, and an unset URL is `BothExist`.
- **SPEC-2.157**: Only SQLSTATE `28P01` (invalid password) from the app login attempt must classify as
  `AppPasswordMismatch`; any other failure (timeout, unreachable host, missing database, too many connections) must
  classify as `BothExist`, so a transient probe failure cannot force a full provision.
- **SPEC-2.158**: When the probe is not `BothExist` and `MOKOSH_ADMIN_DATABASE_URL` is unset or empty, `provision_roles`
  must fail with `AppError::Database` whose message names the actual state (app password mismatch, `mokosh_app` missing
  or unable to log in, or migrator unable to connect) and the variable to set; with the URL set it must connect with it
  (one connection, 30-second acquire timeout), run the statements, and close that pool once they have succeeded.
- **SPEC-2.159**: `MOKOSH_APP_PASSWORD` must be required (non-empty) whenever provisioning runs, and
  `MOKOSH_MIGRATOR_PASSWORD` must be required only when the migrator statements will run; an unset or empty required
  variable must fail with `<NAME> is required to provision DB roles but is unset`.
- **SPEC-2.160**: For the `AppPasswordMismatch` probe only, the statements must be limited to `mokosh_app` (role,
  password and grants), so reconciling the app role's password never rewrites `mokosh_migrator`'s password or the
  default-privilege grants.
- **SPEC-2.161**: The migrator statements must create `mokosh_migrator` as `LOGIN BYPASSRLS` if absent, then `ALTER
  ROLE` it to the same attributes and the configured password, then `GRANT ALL ON SCHEMA public` and `GRANT CREATE ON
  DATABASE <db>` to it, so migrations can install the trusted extensions.
- **SPEC-2.162**: The app statements must create `mokosh_app` as `LOGIN NOSUPERUSER NOBYPASSRLS` if absent, then `ALTER
  ROLE` it to the same attributes and the configured password, then grant `CONNECT` on the database, `USAGE` on schema
  `public`, DML on all current tables, `USAGE, SELECT` on all current sequences and `EXECUTE` on all current functions.
- **SPEC-2.163**: The default-privilege statements must run after both roles exist and grant, for objects the migrator
  creates in `public`, DML on tables, `USAGE, SELECT` on sequences and `EXECUTE` on functions to `mokosh_app`, so
  objects created by later migrations are usable by the app role.
- **SPEC-2.164**: Password values must be embedded as single-quoted SQL literals with embedded single quotes doubled,
  and role and database names as double-quoted identifiers with embedded double quotes doubled.
- **SPEC-2.165**: A provisioning statement that fails must end startup with an error naming the failed step and the
  database cause; the error must not contain the statement text when it embeds a password literal.
- **SPEC-2.166**: Every query in `src/db/identity.rs` must be called with the migrator (BYPASSRLS) pool; `identities`
  has no `tenant_id` and no row-level security, and a caller that passes the app pool reads zero `tenant_memberships`
  rows because of that table's `tenant_isolation` policy.
- **SPEC-2.167**: `IdentityRepo::find_by_email` and `find_id_by_email`, and
  `MembershipRepo::find_id_by_email_and_tenant`, must match the email case-insensitively (`lower(email) = lower($1)`);
  `find_by_id` must match the exact id, and each lookup must return `None` when no row matches.
- **SPEC-2.168**: `MembershipRepo::list_active_for_identity` must return only memberships with status `active`, ordered
  by `joined_at` ascending; `find` must return the membership of the given identity and tenant whatever its status.
- **SPEC-2.169**: `MembershipRepo::list_views_for_identity` must collect grant-arm rows first (grants not revoked and
  with a role, ordered by `granted_at`, matched to the identity through a user row's Bunyip user id or through the
  grant's grantee email compared case-insensitively) and then append the identity's active memberships ordered by
  `joined_at`, skipping any tenant already present from a grant, so a grantee's seat keeps its grant designation; a
  grant view must have status `active` and carry both grant ids, and `is_active` must be true for the view whose tenant
  equals `active_tenant_id`.
- **SPEC-2.170**: A database error while reading the grant arm of `list_views_for_identity` must be returned to the
  caller, not treated as an identity with no grants.
- **SPEC-2.171**: `IdentityRepo::record_identity_mfa_success(identity, step)` must set `mfa_last_totp_step` only where
  the stored step is strictly lower than `step` and return `true` when a row changed; `false` (zero rows) is a replay
  and the caller must fail closed.
- **SPEC-2.172**: Every read and write in `src/db/platform_admin.rs` must run on the migrator pool: `platform_admins` is
  exempt from row-level security because it is read on the pre-authentication login path, and its credential lifecycle
  is independent of `users`, `identities` and `tenant_memberships`.
- **SPEC-2.173**: `PlatformAdminRepo::find_by_email` must match the email case-insensitively and `find_by_id` the exact
  id, each returning `None` when no row matches.
- **SPEC-2.174**: `advance_totp_step(admin, step)` must update `mfa_last_totp_step` only where the stored step is
  strictly lower and return `true` only when exactly one row changed, so two logins presenting the same code cannot both
  succeed.
- **SPEC-2.175**: `stage_mfa_secret` must store the sealed secret and set `mfa_enabled` to false, `mfa_last_totp_step`
  to 0 and the recovery-code hashes to empty, so a misconfigured authenticator cannot lock the operator out before
  `enable_mfa` confirms it with a live code.
- **SPEC-2.176**: `enable_mfa` must set `mfa_enabled` to true together with the sealed secret and the recovery-code
  hashes in one write and reset `mfa_last_totp_step` to 0; `disable_mfa` must set `mfa_enabled` to false, clear the
  secret, reset the step to 0 and clear the recovery-code hashes in one write.
- **SPEC-2.177**: `spend_recovery_code(admin, hash)` must remove the hash from the admin's recovery-code array and
  return `true` only when exactly one row changed; an unknown code or a code already spent must return `false`.

### 2.7 Configuration provider registry

Every configuration key is declared once in a registry (`src/config/registry.rs`) with a tier, and one read path
(`config::get`) serves every consumer. The variable-by-variable reference is section 6. The bullets before the
`AppConfig` group describe `src/config/`; the `AppConfig` group describes how `src/main.rs` interprets the values.

- **SPEC-2.178**: `ConfigKey` values must come only from the `declare_keys!` macro (fields are private and the
  constructor is test-only), so a read or flag naming an undeclared key must fail to compile, and each declaration must
  state its tier, its `since` release and whether it is required.
- **SPEC-2.179**: A `Bootstrap`-tier key must be resolved once per process and carried unchanged across every refresh;
  an `Application`-tier key must be re-resolved from the provider on every refresh.
- **SPEC-2.180**: Code outside `src/config/` that is not listed in `ENTRY_POINTS` must read configuration only through
  `config::get`, `config::has` or `config::served_by`, which answer from the current generation; `get` must return the
  held string unchanged, so a blank value is `Some("")` and an unheld key is `None`.
- **SPEC-2.181**: `has` and `served_by` must report a key as held when any provider held it at resolution time,
  including when its value is blank, and must report absence only when no provider held it.
- **SPEC-2.182**: `refresh` must build a complete candidate generation from the installed provider (application-tier
  keys re-read, bootstrap-tier keys copied from the previous generation), number it previous plus one, and swap it in
  under the write lock, so a reader holds either the old or the new generation and never a mix.
- **SPEC-2.183**: `try_refresh` must reject, and keep the live generation and its counter unchanged, when any key named
  in `required_keys` resolves to no provider in the candidate; the rejection must name the unresolved keys and the
  provider consulted, never a value.
- **SPEC-2.184**: `try_refresh` must reject a request whose `required_keys` include a bootstrap-tier key before
  resolving anything (no provider read, empty `providers_consulted`), naming the refused keys, and must leave the live
  generation and its counter unchanged.
- **SPEC-2.185**: `refuse_refresh_of_bootstrap` must return `AppError::Configuration` with the text `bootstrap keys
  cannot be refreshed; <KEY> is Bootstrap tier` for a bootstrap-tier key and `Ok(())` for an application-tier key.
- **SPEC-2.186**: `init_from_env` must run at boot before any other configuration read; it must select the provider from
  `CONFIG_BACKEND` (blank means the hosting profile's Configuration default), install it, resolve generation 1, and log
  `configuration provider selected` at info with the provider, the source (`profile` or `explicit`) and the key count.
- **SPEC-2.187**: `init_from_env` must fail with `AppError::Configuration` (`the configuration provider was already
  resolved as <installed> before startup selected <chosen>; a read ran before init_from_env`) when a read already
  installed a different provider, and must continue when the installed provider is the same.
- **SPEC-2.188**: `init_from_env` must log at warn, naming the key, for every unresolved key that carries a `feature`
  annotation, and must stay silent for unresolved keys without one.
- **SPEC-2.189**: `CONFIG_BACKEND` blank must resolve to the hosting profile's Configuration default (`environment`,
  source `profile`); a non-blank value is trimmed and matched exactly against `environment`, `file`, `database` or
  `bunyip` (source `explicit`).
- **SPEC-2.190**: `CONFIG_BACKEND` naming a known provider other than `environment` must end boot with
  `AppError::Configuration` (`CONFIG_BACKEND "<name>" names a provider the single-provider slot cannot yet construct
  (only 'environment' is reachable that way); enable it through CONFIG_PROVIDERS instead ...`), and an unknown name must
  end boot with `configuration provider "<name>" is not a known kind; expected one of: environment, file, database,
  bunyip`, never falling back to the default.
- **SPEC-2.191**: `check_staleness` must pair the recorded generation with a live `has` probe per registry key and
  report one of unchanged, appeared, disappeared or changed-provider per key, carrying key names, provider names,
  generation number, actor and timestamps but no value.
- **SPEC-2.192**: The staleness report must distinguish a provider that cannot enumerate (`Unsupported`) from one that
  holds no keys (`Supported` with an empty list).
- **SPEC-2.193**: The server process must not install a provider chain: `init_chain` has no caller in the server boot
  path, `config::get` reads only the single installed provider, and `CONFIG_PROVIDERS` is consumed only by
  `build_chain_from_env`, which the operator CLI calls.
- **SPEC-2.194**: `CONFIG_PROVIDERS` must be a comma-separated priority list with the first entry highest and blank
  meaning the profile default; an empty entry must be refused (`CONFIG_PROVIDERS entry #<n> is empty ...`) and a
  repeated provider must be refused (`CONFIG_PROVIDERS lists <name> twice ...`), both as `AppError::Configuration`.
- **SPEC-2.195**: Chain resolution must serve each key from the first provider that holds a decodable value and must
  list every other holding provider as also-held; a provider whose `has` is true but whose `get` returns `None` must not
  be taken as the serving copy.
- **SPEC-2.196**: Chain classification must be non-fatal for configuration: `Used` logs info, `Missing` logs warn naming
  the key, `Duplicate` logs one warn per ignored provider naming winner and loser, and `HigherEmptyLowerHolds` logs a
  warn naming the top provider that lacks the key and the lower provider that serves it.
- **SPEC-2.197**: Building a chain that enables the database provider without a database handle must fail with
  `AppError::Configuration` (`CONFIG_PROVIDERS enables the database provider, but the chain builder was called without a
  database handle ...`).
- **SPEC-2.198**: The environment provider must answer `get` with `None` and log at error (`environment variable is set
  but unreadable; treating it as unset`, with the key) when a variable is set but not valid UTF-8, while `has` must
  still report it as held, so absent and undecodable stay distinguishable in a presence report.
- **SPEC-2.199**: The environment provider must return a set-but-empty variable as `Some("")`, not `None`.
- **SPEC-2.200**: The environment provider's `list` must return only the declared registry keys present in the
  environment, never other process variables.
- **SPEC-2.201**: The file provider must read `CONFIG_FILE_DIR` directly (trimmed; unset or blank means not enabled)
  and, when set, load one file per declared registry key, named exactly as the key, once at construction; later changes
  on disk must not be visible until the provider is rebuilt.
- **SPEC-2.202**: A `CONFIG_FILE_DIR` that does not exist must yield a silent provider holding nothing (writes then
  create the directory); one naming a path that is not a directory must log at error (`CONFIG_FILE_DIR names a path that
  is not a directory ...`) and hold nothing with writes refused; one whose metadata cannot be read must log at error
  (`CONFIG_FILE_DIR could not be read ...`).
- **SPEC-2.203**: A key file that exists but cannot be read must log at error with the path and key (`the file
  configuration provider cannot read <KEY>; treating it as unheld`) and leave only that key unheld; a missing key file
  must be silent, and files not named for a declared key must be ignored.
- **SPEC-2.204**: The file provider must remove exactly one trailing `\r\n` or `\n` from a file's contents and keep
  everything else, including other whitespace, and an empty file must read as `Some("")`.
- **SPEC-2.205**: The file provider's `set` and `delete` must refuse a bootstrap-tier key with `AppError::Configuration`
  (`<KEY> is a bootstrap-tier key and cannot be written to / deleted from the file configuration provider`) before
  touching the filesystem.
- **SPEC-2.206**: The file provider's `set` must refuse with `file configuration provider has no directory; set
  CONFIG_FILE_DIR to enable writes` when no directory is configured, and `delete` of an absent file must succeed.
- **SPEC-2.207**: `DatabaseProvider::build` must return `AppError::Configuration` (`the database configuration provider
  cannot serve bootstrap-tier keys ...: <KEYS>`) listing every bootstrap-tier key it was given, before any database
  query.
- **SPEC-2.208**: `DatabaseProvider::build` must preload the `app_config` rows for only the given keys in one query and
  serve them from memory; a preload failure must fail the build with `AppError::Database` (`could not preload
  app_config: ...`).
- **SPEC-2.209**: The database provider's `set` must upsert the `app_config` row through the migrator pool and then
  update its cache, so a read after a successful write sees the value; on a failed write it must return
  `AppError::Database` (`could not write app_config row: ...`) and leave the cache unchanged; `delete` must do the same
  and treat an absent row as success.
- **SPEC-2.210**: The database provider's `set` and `delete` must refuse a bootstrap-tier key with
  `AppError::Configuration` before any query.
- **SPEC-2.211**: The Bunyip configuration provider must request only the keys in `SERVED_KEYS` (today
  `ABUSE_CONTACT_EMAIL`, fetched as `mokosh/abuse_contact_email`), one request each, and must hold no other key.
- **SPEC-2.212**: The Bunyip provider must read `BUNYIP_CONFIG_URL` directly (trimmed; unset or blank builds an empty
  provider that makes no request); when set, `BUNYIP_CONFIG_CLIENT_ID` and `BUNYIP_CONFIG_CLIENT_SECRET` are required,
  each read first from the file named by `<NAME>_FILE` (trimmed contents) and otherwise from `<NAME>`.
- **SPEC-2.213**: When `BUNYIP_CONFIG_URL` is set and a credential half is blank or unset, the Bunyip provider must fail
  with `AppError::Configuration` (`BUNYIP_CONFIG_URL is set, so <NAME> must be set too; ...`); an unreadable
  `<NAME>_FILE` must log at error with the path and then fall back to `<NAME>`.
- **SPEC-2.214**: A Bunyip key fetch (`GET <url>/v1/host/config/<key>` with HTTP Basic) must treat 404 as an unheld key
  and log at info, must treat a missing, blank or non-string `data.value` as unheld, and must trim the value.
- **SPEC-2.215**: A Bunyip 401 must fail the provider build with an `external_service` error naming
  `BUNYIP_CONFIG_CLIENT_ID` and the `machine-client rotate` remedy, a 403 must fail it with text naming the key and the
  registration allow-list remedy, and any other non-success status, a transport failure or a malformed envelope must
  also fail the build rather than leave the key unheld.
- **SPEC-2.216**: The Bunyip provider's `set` must always return `AppError::Configuration` (`bunyip provider write is
  not implemented`), and its `delete` must use the trait default refusal (`bunyip provider does not support deletes`).
- **SPEC-2.217**: A `Flag<T>` must pair one declared registry key with a typed default (`Constant`, or `PerProfile` with
  a self-hosted and a saas value) and must read through the current generation, so a refresh changes the next read.
- **SPEC-2.218**: The declared flags and defaults must be: `ORGANIZATIONS_ENABLED` false on self-hosted and true on
  saas, `LOGIN_APPROVAL_ENABLED` false in both, and `ALLOW_UNINVITED_BUNYIP_SIGNUP` false in both.
- **SPEC-2.219**: `Flag::read` must return the flag default when the key is unheld or blank, and must return the default
  and log at warn (`flag value failed to parse; serving the flag's default`, with the key and the raw value) when the
  value does not parse.
- **SPEC-2.220**: A boolean flag must accept, trimmed and case-insensitive, `1`, `true` and `yes` as true and `0`,
  `false` and `no` as false; any other non-blank value is unparseable.
- **SPEC-2.221**: `config::flags::check_boot` must fail when any declared flag is set to a non-blank unparseable value,
  with one combined error (`boot refused: <n> feature flag(s) set to an unparseable value.` plus a line per flag naming
  the key and the raw value); an unset or blank flag must pass.
- **SPEC-2.222**: A `PerProfile` flag default must be resolved on every read from `MOKOSH_DEPLOYMENT_MODE` with the
  lenient reader (an unrecognised mode yields self-hosted with a warn log), not frozen at construction.
- **SPEC-2.223**: Only the files in `ENTRY_POINTS` (each with a stated reason) and the files under `src/config/` may
  read the environment directly; every other file under `src/` must not.
- **SPEC-2.224**: `cargo test --lib` must fail when a file outside `src/config/` and `ENTRY_POINTS` contains a direct
  environment read, naming the offending files; it must also fail when an `ENTRY_POINTS` entry no longer reads the
  environment, names a missing file, or has a reason of 30 characters or fewer.
- **SPEC-2.225**: `src/config/variables.toml` must hold the since and required facts for variables read outside the
  registry (starting with `MOKOSH_DEPLOYMENT_MODE`, required); it is documentation data for `scripts/config-docs.nu` and
  no Rust code reads it.
- **SPEC-2.226**: The registry keys declared required must be exactly `DATABASE_URL`, `MOKOSH_APP_DATABASE_URL`,
  `ENCRYPTION_KEY`, `BASE_URL`, `JWT_SECRET`, `BUNYIP_WEBHOOK_SECRET`, `CLIENT_ORIGIN` and `SPA_BASE_URL`, each one that
  boot refuses to start without outside the development environments (SPEC-2.25, SPEC-2.28).
- **SPEC-2.227**: The bootstrap tier must be exactly `DATABASE_URL`, `MOKOSH_APP_DATABASE_URL`, `ENCRYPTION_KEY`,
  `APP_SECRETS_DIR`, `CONFIG_FILE_DIR`, `CONFIG_PROVIDERS`, `BUNYIP_CONFIG_URL`, `BUNYIP_CONFIG_CLIENT_ID`,
  `BUNYIP_CONFIG_CLIENT_SECRET` and `AUTH_PROVIDERS`; every other key is application tier.
- **SPEC-2.228**: `parse_optional` must treat an unset or blank value as "use the default" and a set but unparseable
  value as the error `<KEY> is set to "<raw>", which is not a valid value: <cause>`; `parse_positive` must additionally
  refuse zero and negative values with `<KEY> must be a positive value, got <n>`.
- **SPEC-2.229**: A configuration provider name given in `CONFIG_BACKEND` or `CONFIG_PROVIDERS` must be trimmed and then
  matched case-sensitively.
- **SPEC-2.230**: `AppConfig` must take the bind host from `HOST` (default `0.0.0.0` when unset) and the port from
  `PORT` (default 8080 when unset or blank, an unparseable value being a boot error through `parse_optional`); a blank
  but set `HOST` is taken as the empty string and fails the socket-address parse of SPEC-2.56.
- **SPEC-2.231**: `AppConfig.run_migrations` must be the parsed `RUN_MIGRATIONS` boolean (default true when unset or
  blank); a set value other than the exact lower-case `true` or `false` must be a boot error naming the variable and the
  value.
- **SPEC-2.232**: `AppConfig.max_tenants` must be the parsed `MOKOSH_MAX_TENANTS` positive integer, `None` (uncapped)
  when the variable is unset or blank; a set value that is zero, negative or not an integer must be a boot error naming
  the variable and the value.
- **SPEC-2.233**: `AppConfig.client_origin` must be `CLIENT_ORIGIN` or `http://localhost:4301` when unset;
  `spa_base_url` must be the trimmed non-blank `SPA_BASE_URL`, else `client_origin`; `base_url` must be `BASE_URL` or
  `http://localhost:8080` when unset.
- **SPEC-2.234**: `AppConfig.cors_origins` must be the `CORS_ORIGIN` value split on commas with each entry trimmed and
  empty entries dropped; when that list is empty or the variable is unset the list must be `[client_origin]`.
- **SPEC-2.235**: `AppConfig.abuse_contact_email`, `public_api_base_url`, `ip2location_db_path` and `ip2proxy_db_path`
  must be the trimmed value when non-blank and `None` otherwise, `public_api_base_url` additionally losing every
  trailing `/`; `login_approval_enabled` must be the `LOGIN_APPROVAL_ENABLED` flag (default off) and `deployment_mode`
  the lenient `MOKOSH_DEPLOYMENT_MODE` reading.

### 2.8 Provider seams

Five capabilities are selected by name and resolved once at boot: Configuration, Tenant secrets, Authentication, Email
and Object storage. Defaults come from the hosting profile in `src/utils/deployment.rs`; `docs/providers.md` is the
contract for the model.

- **SPEC-2.236**: `MOKOSH_DEPLOYMENT_MODE` must accept, trimmed and case-insensitive, `self-hosted`, `self_hosted`,
  `selfhosted` or blank for self-hosted and `saas` for saas; the strict reader used by provider selection must refuse
  any other value with `AppError::Configuration` (`MOKOSH_DEPLOYMENT_MODE "<value>" is not a known deployment mode;
  expected 'self-hosted' or 'saas'. ...`).
- **SPEC-2.237**: The lenient mode reader (used for mail dispatch and flag defaults) must use self-hosted for an
  unrecognised value and log at warn `unrecognised MOKOSH_DEPLOYMENT_MODE; falling back to self-hosted.` followed by the
  two valid values.
- **SPEC-2.238**: The self-hosted profile must default Configuration to `environment`, Tenant secrets to `database`,
  Authentication to `local`, Email to `log` and Storage to `local`, naming no externally hosted provider.
- **SPEC-2.239**: The saas profile must default Configuration to `environment`, Tenant secrets to `database`,
  Authentication to `bunyip` then `local` (bunyip first), Email to `smtp` and Storage to `local`.
- **SPEC-2.240**: A capability's single default must be the first provider in its profile row, so saas Authentication
  starts on `bunyip`.
- **SPEC-2.241**: An explicit selection must override the profile for its own capability only and be recorded with
  source `explicit`; an unset or empty override must keep the profile row with source `profile`; boot must log `provider
  selected` at info once per capability with the mode, kind, providers and source.
- **SPEC-2.242**: The saas profile must declare `GOOGLE_CONTACTS_CLIENT_ID` and `GOOGLE_CONTACTS_CLIENT_SECRET` to the
  `bunyip` secret provider; self-hosted must declare none.
- **SPEC-2.243**: `SECRET_BACKEND` must accept `database` or `infisical` and end boot with `AppError::Configuration`
  otherwise (`SECRET_BACKEND "<v>" is not a known provider; expected 'database' or 'infisical'`), pointing at
  `APP_SECRET_BACKEND` when the name is an application-tier-only provider.
- **SPEC-2.244**: `AUTH_PROVIDERS` (comma list, bootstrap tier) must accept `bunyip` and `local`, refuse an empty entry
  and a duplicate, and end boot with `AUTH_PROVIDERS name "<v>" is not a known authentication provider; expected
  'bunyip' or 'local'` for any other name.
- **SPEC-2.245**: `MAIL_PROVIDER` must accept `log`, `smtp` or `bunyip` and end boot with `MAIL_PROVIDER "<v>" is not a
  known provider; expected 'log', 'smtp' or 'bunyip'` otherwise.
- **SPEC-2.246**: `STORAGE_PROVIDER` must accept `local` or `s3` and end boot with `STORAGE_PROVIDER <v> is not a known
  provider; expected 'local' or 's3'` otherwise; the retired name `STORAGE_BACKEND` is refused by the boot environment
  check of SPEC-2.20.
- **SPEC-2.247**: `APP_SECRET_BACKEND` must accept `environment`, `file`, `database`, `infisical` or `bunyip` and end
  boot with an error ending `expected one of: environment, file, database, infisical, bunyip` otherwise.
- **SPEC-2.248**: `main` must take every provider default it passes down from the hosting profile: the Configuration,
  Secrets (both tiers), Email and Storage defaults as one provider name each, and the Authentication default as the
  profile's ordered list.
- **SPEC-2.249**: The Authentication override handed to `resolve_providers` must be the list `bunyip`, `local` whenever
  the Bunyip verifier was mounted, and none otherwise; the boot record therefore reports authentication as explicit
  exactly when a verifier is mounted.

### 2.9 Version and build metadata

- **SPEC-2.250**: Every `VersionInfo` field must be a compile-time `env!()` constant (crate name, crate version,
  `MOKOSH_GIT_DESCRIBE`, `MOKOSH_GIT_HASH`, `MOKOSH_BUILD_DATE`); the server binary must not invoke git at run time.
- **SPEC-2.251**: `VersionInfo` must serialize to JSON with the fields `name`, `version`, `git_describe`, `git_hash` and
  `build_date`, and `banner()` must render `<name> <git_describe> (<git_hash>) built <build_date>`.
- **SPEC-2.252**: `banner()` must be the single line the server logs at startup (SPEC-2.17) and is built from the same
  constants as `GET /api/v1/version`.
- **SPEC-2.253**: The root `build.rs` must delegate `MOKOSH_GIT_HASH`, `MOKOSH_GIT_DESCRIBE` and `MOKOSH_BUILD_DATE`
  emission to `build_metadata::emit(".git")` and must also rerun when anything under `migrations/` changes, because
  `sqlx::migrate!` registers no build dependency on stable.
- **SPEC-2.254**: `MOKOSH_GIT_HASH` must come from a non-blank pre-set variable of that name (trimmed), else from `git
  rev-parse --short=12 HEAD`, else the string `unknown`; a failing, absent or empty `git` falls through without failing
  the build.
- **SPEC-2.255**: `MOKOSH_GIT_DESCRIBE` must come from a non-blank pre-set variable, else `git describe --tags --always
  --dirty`, else `v` followed by the consuming crate's `CARGO_PKG_VERSION` (`v0.0.0` when that is unset).
- **SPEC-2.256**: `MOKOSH_BUILD_DATE` must come from a non-blank pre-set variable, else from `SOURCE_DATE_EPOCH`
  (seconds, when it parses) else the current time, formatted `YYYY-MM-DDTHH:MM:SSZ` in UTC.
- **SPEC-2.257**: `build_metadata::emit(git_dir)` must print `cargo:rustc-env` for the three values and
  `cargo:rerun-if-env-changed` for the three variables and `SOURCE_DATE_EPOCH`, and `cargo:rerun-if-changed` for
  `<git_dir>/HEAD`, `<git_dir>/refs` and `<git_dir>/index`.
- **SPEC-2.258**: When `MOKOSH_UPDATE_CHECK_URL` is unset or blank, `GET /api/v1/version/check` must answer 200 with
  `{"status":"disabled","current_version":"<version>"}`, make no outbound request and never build the probe client.
- **SPEC-2.259**: `version_check` must answer 200 for `disabled`, `up_to_date` and `update_available` results and 502
  for an `error` result, with `Content-Type: application/json` and `Cache-Control: no-store`; the body field `status` is
  the snake_case variant name.
- **SPEC-2.260**: With a URL configured the check must `GET` it (trailing `/` removed) with a 5-second timeout and
  expect a 2xx JSON object with a string `version` and an optional `release_url`; a request failure must answer
  `{"status":"error"}` with the message `<display url>: request failed` and log the cause at warn, a non-2xx status the
  message `<display url>: status <status>`, and an unparseable body the message `<display url>: invalid manifest` with a
  warn log.
- **SPEC-2.261**: The display URL in an error message must be the configured URL with userinfo, query and fragment
  removed, so a credential embedded in the configured value never reaches a response body or a log field.
- **SPEC-2.262**: A successful check result must be reused for 15 minutes and a failed one for 60 seconds, from one
  process-wide cache entry, without a network request; the `disabled` result is not cached, and the probe configuration
  is read once on the first call and kept for the life of the process.
- **SPEC-2.263**: A manifest version must count as newer only when its numeric release components, compared left to
  right with missing components as 0, exceed the running version's; a leading `v` and anything after the first `-` or
  `+` must be ignored (so a pre-release equals its release), and a non-numeric component must count as 0 and be logged
  at warn.
- **SPEC-2.264**: A failure to build the probe's HTTP client must be reported as an `error` result with a log line
  naming the cause, not as a `disabled` check.

### 2.10 Test infrastructure

The `#[mokosh_test]` attribute (`crates/mokosh-test-macros`, `crates/mokosh-test`) replaces `#[sqlx::test]`: every
test's database is cloned from one migrated template database instead of being migrated from scratch.

- **SPEC-2.265**: `#[mokosh_test]` must take no arguments; any argument must be a compile error `#[mokosh_test] takes no
  arguments; the template is built from ./migrations`, because the template is always built from `./migrations`.
- **SPEC-2.266**: The annotated function must be `async` and take exactly one argument (the pool); any other shape must
  be a compile error, not a runtime one.
- **SPEC-2.267**: The macro must expand to a plain `#[test]` function that acquires a database, passes its pool to the
  original body as an inner async function, and, when the body panics, still runs the cleanup below before re-raising
  the panic.
- **SPEC-2.268**: The generated test must run its body on a current-thread tokio runtime with every driver enabled,
  matching what `#[sqlx::test]` built.
- **SPEC-2.269**: Cleanup must run in this order: close the pool (bounded as in SPEC-2.270), drop the pool, drop the
  runtime, then finish the database; dropping the database before the runtime leaves a connected backend and PostgreSQL
  refuses the `DROP DATABASE`.
- **SPEC-2.270**: `close_pool` must bound `pool.close()` to 10 seconds and, on timeout, print `test <path> held onto
  Pool after exiting` to stderr instead of blocking the process on a leaked pool.
- **SPEC-2.271**: `finish(db, passed)` must keep a failing (panicked) test's database and print `test database kept for
  inspection: <name> (drop it with: DROP DATABASE "<name>")`, and must drop a passing test's database.
- **SPEC-2.272**: `drop_database` must poll `pg_stat_activity` for sessions on the database, up to 60 polls 50 ms apart,
  and run a plain `DROP DATABASE IF EXISTS` (never `WITH (FORCE)`) only when none remain; a database still occupied must
  be left in place with its sessions printed, and a failing connect or drop must print the cause.
