- **SPEC-5.458**: Setting a password must answer 400 "Invalid or expired setup token" for a token that does not parse as
  {contact-uuid}.{secret}, for a secret that matches no portal_setup_tokens row of that contact by SHA-256 lookup hash,
  and for a hash that fails verification; the verification must run even when no row matched, and the rejection reason
  must be logged at debug only.
- **SPEC-5.459**: Setting a password with a token whose row is already used must answer 410 "Setup token already used",
  and with a token whose expires_at has passed must answer 400 "Invalid or expired setup token".
- **SPEC-5.460**: Setting a password must hold the new password to the shared password policy (minimum 12 characters,
  zxcvbn score of at least 3, common-password blocklist, with the contact's names, email and tenant name as hints) and
  must answer 400 with the policy message, changing nothing, when it fails.
- **SPEC-5.461**: A successful set-password must, in one transaction, store the new password hash, set is_portal_user
  true, reset the failure counter and lock, mark the redeemed token and every other unused token of the contact used,
  and revoke every unrevoked session of the contact; after commit it must write audit portal.setup_password and answer
  204.
- **SPEC-5.462**: The routes /auth/forgot-password, /auth/reset-password and /auth/login-link/select must not exist and
  must answer 404; a portal password is reissued by the MSP resending the setup link, which redeems at
  /auth/set-password.
- **SPEC-5.463**: POST /api/v1/contact/auth/login-link must answer a 422 validation error when email is not a valid
  address, and otherwise must answer 204 with no body whether or not a portal contact matched.
- **SPEC-5.464**: The login-link request must create no intent and send no mail, still answering 204, when neither
  portal_id nor a non-blank slug is given, when the portal_id or slug resolves to no company of an active tenant, when
  20 or more intents were created from the same IP in the last minute, when 5 or more were created for the same email
  (case-insensitive) in the last 15 minutes, or when no portal contact with that email exists in the resolved company
  (company must have a portal_slug); the missing-identifier, per-IP and per-email drops must be logged at info.
- **SPEC-5.465**: A login-link request that passes the checks must insert a portal_login_intents row for the tenant and
  company holding the email, a hash of a 32-character random secret, an expiry 15 minutes ahead, the client IP and user
  agent, and must dispatch notification event auth.login_link with recipient_email and magic_link_url {SPA base
  URL}/portal/pick?token={intent-uuid}.{secret}.
- **SPEC-5.466**: When no notification dispatcher is configured, the login-link request must log a warning that the
  intent was persisted without a message; a database error during the request must propagate as an error response
  instead of the 204.
- **SPEC-5.467**: POST /api/v1/contact/auth/login-link/redeem must answer 400 "This link is invalid or has expired",
  with the same text for every cause, when the token does not parse as {intent-uuid}.{secret}, names no intent, is
  already used, is expired, has a secret that does not verify, or resolves to no portal contact (is_portal_user true,
  tenant active, company with portal_slug, matching the intent's company when it has one); the cause must be logged at
  debug or warn.
- **SPEC-5.468**: Redeeming a link for a contact with MFA enabled and no mfa_code or recovery_code must answer 200 with
  auto.mfa_required true and empty tokens and must leave the link unused; with a code it must answer 429 while the
  contact is locked, and on a refused code must answer 401, increment the failure counter, write audit portal.mfa_failed
  and leave the link unused.
- **SPEC-5.469**: Redeeming a link for exactly one matching contact must mark the intent used before anything is minted;
  if the contact has no password hash it must answer 200 with auto.password_setup_url {SPA base
  URL}/portal/{slug}/set-password?token={contact-uuid}.{secret} (a fresh token valid 72 hours, invalidating the
  contact's earlier unused tokens) and no session; otherwise it must mint a session as login does, reset the failure
  counter and lock, write audit portal.login_link and set the cookie.
- **SPEC-5.470**: Redeeming a link that matches more than one contact must mark the intent used and answer the same 400
  "This link is invalid or has expired"; the intent row must be locked for the whole decision so that two concurrent
  redeems produce one winner.
- **SPEC-5.471**: GET /api/v1/contact/auth/me must answer 401 without an authenticated contact and otherwise return the
  contact's id, tenant_id, company_id, email (empty string when null), first_name, last_name, company_name, portal_slug
  (empty string when null), roles as {id, name} ordered by name, caps, mfa_enabled and effective_branding.
- **SPEC-5.472**: A contact's capability set must be the distinct union of capabilities of every role assigned to the
  contact in its tenant, sorted ascending, read from the database on each call; a contact with no assignment must have
  an empty set.
- **SPEC-5.473**: PUT /api/v1/contact/auth/me must require capability settings:manage_own (checked against the database,
  else 403), must answer 422 when first_name or last_name is outside 1..=100 characters or phone or mobile exceeds 32,
  must update only the supplied names, phone, mobile and timezone (absent fields unchanged), must not accept an email
  change, and must return the updated contact.
- **SPEC-5.474**: A self update must lock the edited fields for a contact linked to an external sync source in the same
  transaction, and must answer 404 "Contact not found" when no contact row was updated.
- **SPEC-5.475**: PUT /api/v1/contact/auth/me/password must answer 401 without changing anything when current_password
  is wrong, 400 with the policy message when new_password fails the password policy, and otherwise must store the new
  hash, revoke every unrevoked session whose family differs from the caller's own (every session when the caller's
  session row no longer exists), write audit portal.password_changed and answer 204.
- **SPEC-5.476**: The re-authentication routes (change password, MFA setup, enable and disable) must share one failure
  budget per client IP (10 per minute) and per contact (5 per minute) that is checked before the password is compared,
  answering 429 with the wait when spent; only a 401 outcome may spend budget, and a weak password or a database error
  must not.
- **SPEC-5.477**: Re-authentication must answer 401 when the contact does not exist, is not a portal user, has no
  password hash, or the supplied current password does not verify.
- **SPEC-5.478**: POST /api/v1/contact/auth/me/mfa/setup must re-authenticate with current_password, answer 409 "MFA is
  already enabled" when MFA is on, and otherwise store a freshly generated TOTP secret sealed at rest without enabling
  MFA (replacing any earlier staged secret), write audit portal.mfa_setup_started, and return the base32 secret and an
  otpauth provisioning_uri labelled {app name}:{email}.
- **SPEC-5.479**: POST /api/v1/contact/auth/me/mfa/enable must answer a 422 validation error when code is not 6 to 8
  characters, re-authenticate with current_password, answer 409 "MFA is already enabled" when on, 400 "MFA enrollment
  has not been started" when no secret is staged, and 400 "Invalid MFA code" when the code does not verify; on success
  it must set portal_mfa_enabled, store the sealed secret and the hashes of newly generated recovery codes, write audit
  portal.mfa_enabled, and return the recovery codes once.
- **SPEC-5.480**: POST /api/v1/contact/auth/me/mfa/disable must answer a 422 validation error when code is not 6 to 20
  characters, re-authenticate with current_password, answer 401 when MFA is not enabled or the code is refused (a code
  of only digits is checked as TOTP, anything else as a recovery code), and otherwise must clear the enabled flag,
  secret, enrolment time and recovery-code hashes, write audit portal.mfa_disabled, and answer 204.
- **SPEC-5.481**: GET /api/v1/contact/auth/me/sessions must return one entry per rotation family of the caller that has
  an unrevoked, unexpired row, using the newest such row for expires_at, user_agent and ip_address (address without
  prefix, both omitted when null), issued_at as the family's earliest created_at, last_seen_at as that newest row's
  created_at, id as the family id, current true for the caller's own family, ordered newest issued_at first.
- **SPEC-5.482**: DELETE /api/v1/contact/auth/me/sessions/{session_id} must answer 400 "Use /auth/logout to sign out of
  the current session" for the caller's own family, 204 without effect for a family id that is unknown or belongs to
  another contact or tenant, and otherwise must revoke the family, write audit portal.session_revoked and answer 204.
- **SPEC-5.483**: GET /api/v1/contact/companies/self/branding must require capability settings:manage_company_branding
  (else 403) and return the tenant branding, the caller's own company branding and the effective branding; it must
  answer 404 "company not found" when the company row is missing.
- **SPEC-5.484**: PATCH /api/v1/contact/companies/self/branding must require capability settings:manage_company_branding
  (else 403), answer a 422 validation error on field branding ("must be an object of branding keys") when the body is
  not a JSON object, apply the company branding patch validation and the tenant asset-ownership check, merge the patch
  into the caller's own company branding only (an explicit null clears a key), answer 404 "company not found" when no
  row matched, and return the same body as GET.
- **SPEC-5.485**: POST /api/v1/contact/access-requests must answer a 422 validation error when note exceeds 500
  characters, 400 "There is no portal area called <area>." when area is not in ACCESS_AREAS, and 400 "You can already
  see <label>." when the contact's capability set, loaded fresh, already holds the area's proving capability.
- **SPEC-5.486**: A valid access request must insert a portal_access_requests row (tenant, contact, company, area key,
  note trimmed, absent when blank) and answer {id, area, status "open", requested_at}; a request for an area that
  already has an open request from the same contact must return that existing request's id and requested_at without
  inserting a row, writing audit or sending mail.
- **SPEC-5.487**: A newly created access request must write audit portal.access_requested and then dispatch notification
  event portal.access_requested with the contact name, email, company name, area label, note line, contact URL and
  request id, addressed to the company's account manager when one is set; a missing dispatcher must send nothing, an
  unreadable contact or company must be logged at warn, and a dispatch failure must be logged at warn without failing
  the request.
- **SPEC-5.488**: GET /api/v1/contact/dashboard/summary must require only an authenticated contact and return
  open_tickets (company tickets whose status is not closed), unpaid_invoices (balance_due above 0 and status not paid,
  void or written_off), active_quotes (status sent) and active_contracts (status active), each scoped to the caller's
  company and tenant and each 0 when the caller's freshly loaded capabilities lack tickets:read, invoices:read,
  quotes:read or contracts:read respectively.
- **SPEC-5.489**: The dashboard recent_activity must hold at most 10 items ordered by occurred_at (latest of updated_at
  and created_at) descending across tickets (title), invoices (invoice number), quotes (title, else quote number) and
  contracts (name), kind "ticket", "invoice", "quote" or "contract", of the caller's company only and only for kinds
  whose read capability the caller holds.
- **SPEC-5.490**: GET /api/v1/contact/portal/{handle}/host must need no authentication; a handle of only ASCII digits
  must be looked up as the company's portal_id (a number too large for i64 answers 404) and any other handle as a legacy
  portal_slug, and the response must give company_name, portal_slug (empty when null), tenant_display_name, the raw
  tenant_status even when the tenant is suspended, and effective_branding; an unknown handle must answer 404 "portal
  host not found".
- **SPEC-5.491**: GET /api/v1/contact/portal/{slug}/resolve-to-portal-id must need no authentication and return
  {"portal_id": <number>}, answering the same 404 "portal id not found" for an unknown slug and for a company with no
  portal_id.
- **SPEC-5.492**: Every /api/v1/contact/payment-methods route must require an authenticated contact (401) holding
  capability payment_methods:manage_own (else 403), checked against the database on each request.
- **SPEC-5.493**: POST /api/v1/contact/payment-methods must answer 400 "success_url must be a valid URL." or "cancel_url
  must be a valid URL." when either does not parse as a URL, 400 "No active payment provider is configured for this
  account." when the tenant has no active provider for the optional provider argument, and otherwise create a hosted
  setup session pre-filled with the contact's email and return {"checkout_url": <url>}.
- **SPEC-5.494**: GET /api/v1/contact/payment-methods must return only the caller's own saved cards (id, provider,
  brand, last4, exp_month, exp_year, is_default, created_at) of the caller's tenant, default first and then newest
  first.
- **SPEC-5.495**: DELETE /api/v1/contact/payment-methods/{id} must answer 404 "Payment method not found" before
  contacting any provider when the card is not the caller's own; otherwise it must detach the card on its provider first
  and delete the row only after the detach succeeds, and must answer 400 naming the gateway, leaving the row, when that
  gateway is no longer active; when the deleted card was the default, the newest remaining card must become the default;
  success is 204.
- **SPEC-5.496**: PUT /api/v1/contact/payment-methods/{id}/default must, in one transaction, clear the contact's current
  default before marking the given card default, answering 404 "Payment method not found" and rolling back when the card
  is not the caller's own, and 204 on success.
- **SPEC-5.497**: Recording a card from a verified provider setup webhook must insert it idempotently on (tenant,
  provider, provider card id), store the brand lower-cased, and make it the default only when the contact had no saved
  card.
- **SPEC-5.498**: Detaching every card for a contact deletion must lock the contact's card rows in the caller's
  transaction, detach them all on their providers concurrently, and return the first error (400 naming the gateway when
  one is no longer active) without deleting any row.
- **SPEC-5.499**: Contact auth events (login, failed login, MFA failure, logout, replay, password changes, MFA changes,
  session revoke, access request) must be written to the audit log as entity portal_contact with the event subtype and,
  where the caller supplies them, the client IP and user agent; a failed audit write must be logged at warn with
  tenant_id, contact_id and subtype and must not change the response.

### 5.6 Members, invitations, teams and audit

#### Audit write path and request context

- **SPEC-5.500**: Extracting an `AuditCtx` from a request must never reject the request. It must take `tenant_id` and
  `user_id` from the request's `AuthState` extension, and must yield both as `None` when no `AuthState` is present.
- **SPEC-5.501**: When connection info is present, `AuditCtx.ip` must be the client address resolved by
  `extract_client_ip` against the configured trusted proxies: the forwarded-for chain is honoured only when the socket
  peer is a trusted proxy, otherwise the peer address is recorded. When connection info is absent, `ip` must be `None`.
- **SPEC-5.502**: `AuditCtx.user_agent` must be the `User-Agent` header value, and must be `None` when the header is
  absent or is not valid UTF-8.
- **SPEC-5.503**: `AuditCtx::system(tenant_id)` must set only `tenant_id`; `user_id`, `ip` and `user_agent` must be
  `None`.
- **SPEC-5.504**: The audit action verbs written to `audit_log.action` must be exactly `create`, `update`, `delete`,
  `view`, `login`, `logout`, `export` and `import`.
- **SPEC-5.505**: `audit_write` must insert exactly one `audit_log` row carrying the given tenant, `ctx.user_id`, the
  action verb, entity type, optional entity id, optional old and new JSON snapshots, `ctx.ip` and `ctx.user_agent`,
  using the supplied executor. When the executor is a transaction the row must commit or roll back with it, and a failed
  insert must return the database error to the caller (the mutation fails; it is not skipped).
- **SPEC-5.506**: `audit_auth_event` must write an `audit_log` row with entity type `auth`, `entity_id` equal to the
  acting user id (NULL when unknown), `user_id` equal to the same user id, and no old or new snapshot.
- **SPEC-5.507**: `audit_portal_event` must write an `audit_log` row with entity type `portal_contact`, `user_id` NULL,
  `entity_id` equal to the contact id (NULL when unknown), no old snapshot, and the new snapshot `{"event": <subtype>}`.

#### Audit log read endpoints

- **SPEC-5.508**: `GET /api/v1/audit-log` and `GET /api/v1/audit-log/export.csv` must require an authenticated caller
  with role `super_admin` or `admin`; other roles must receive 403. The router must expose only GET routes for the audit
  log, so the API offers no way to update or delete an audit row.
- **SPEC-5.509**: `GET /api/v1/audit-log` must return a paginated page of only the caller's tenant rows. A `sort` query
  parameter must be rejected with 422 (field `sort`), `per_page` above 100 must be rejected with 422 (field `per_page`),
  and `entity_type` or `action` longer than 100 characters must be rejected with 422.
- **SPEC-5.510**: The audit log filters `user_id`, `entity_type` and `action` must match by exact equality, `from` must
  keep rows with `timestamp >= from`, `to` must keep rows with `timestamp <= to` (both inclusive), and all supplied
  filters must combine with AND. The page and the `total` count must use the same filtered set.
- **SPEC-5.511**: The audit log page must be ordered by `timestamp` descending, and the read of page and count must run
  inside one transaction carrying the tenant context when a tenant is given. When no tenant is given the service must
  read all tenants on the privileged pool; no HTTP route passes no tenant.
- **SPEC-5.512**: Each audit log entry must carry `user_name`, the actor's `first_name` and `last_name` joined by a
  space and trimmed, or `null` when `user_id` is NULL, the user row is missing, or both names are blank.
- **SPEC-5.513**: Each audit log entry must carry `entity_name` resolved from the row named by `entity_id` for entity
  types `auth` and `contacts` (trimmed full name), `companies`, `sites`, `contracts`, `contract_items`, `rate_cards`,
  `projects`, `assets`, `credential_vault`, `tax_rates` (`name`), `invoices` (`invoice_number`), `tickets` (`T` followed
  by the ticket number) and `payment_gateway_configs` (`provider`). For any other entity type, or when the row is gone,
  `entity_name` must be `null`.
- **SPEC-5.514**: When a returned audit entry has a `user_id` but no resolved `user_name`, the service must log one INFO
  line for surface `audit.list` listing those user ids (never names). When a returned entry of type `auth` or `contacts`
  has an `entity_id` but no `entity_name`, it must log one INFO line for surface `audit.list.entity_name` with those
  ids. Entries of other entity types with a `null` `entity_name` must not be logged.

#### Audit CSV export

- **SPEC-5.515**: `GET /api/v1/audit-log/export.csv` must apply the same filters and the same validation (422 on an
  over-long `entity_type` or `action`) as the JSON listing, scoped to the caller's tenant, newest first, and must
  respond 200 with `Content-Type: text/csv; charset=utf-8` and a `Content-Disposition` attachment header naming
  `audit-log.csv`.
- **SPEC-5.516**: The CSV body must start with the header line
  `timestamp,actor,actor_id,action,entity_type,entity_id,entity_name,ip_address,user_agent`, then one line per entry,
  every line ending in `\n`. `timestamp` must be RFC 3339; `actor` must be `System` when there is no resolved name;
  `actor_id`, `entity_id`, `entity_name`, `ip_address` and `user_agent` must be empty when absent.
- **SPEC-5.517**: A CSV field containing a comma, double quote, carriage return or line feed must be wrapped in double
  quotes with each embedded double quote doubled; all other fields must be written unquoted.
- **SPEC-5.518**: The CSV export must contain every matching row up to a ceiling of 50,000 newest rows, and must not
  return a smaller page than the ceiling without the caller being told. If the response cannot be built the endpoint
  must return 500 `Internal error`.

#### Per-record change history

- **SPEC-5.519**: `GET /api/v1/audit-log/entity/{entity_type}/{entity_id}` must be open to any authenticated caller and
  must answer 404 (`history not found`) for an `entity_type` outside `tickets`, `tasks`, `projects`, `assets` and
  `kb_articles`. A `sort` parameter must be rejected with 422.
- **SPEC-5.520**: The history must return a paginated, tenant-scoped list ordered by `timestamp` descending of the
  `audit_log` rows whose entity type and entity id equal the request, plus a `total` computed with the same predicate as
  the page.
- **SPEC-5.521**: For `entity_type` `tickets`, the history must also include `ticket_notes` rows whose action is not
  `create` and whose `new_values.ticket_id` equals the ticket id as text. `ticket_notes` rows with action `create` must
  not be included, and each entry must report its own `entity_type` and `entity_id`.
- **SPEC-5.522**: A history entry's `user_name` must be the actor's trimmed full name from a user of the same tenant,
  falling back to the user's email when both names are blank, and `null` only when `user_id` is NULL or the user row is
  gone. A `Some` `user_id` with no resolved name must be logged at INFO under surface `audit.list_entity_history` with
  the user ids.
- **SPEC-5.523**: `field_changes` must return, sorted by field name, one `{field, old, new}` for every key of the new
  snapshot whose value differs from the old snapshot's value, excluding `updated_at`, `created_at`, `id`, `tenant_id`
  and `last_updated_by_id`; `old` must be `null` when the key is absent from the old snapshot. It must return an empty
  list unless both snapshots are JSON objects. Keys present only in the old snapshot must not be reported.
- **SPEC-5.524**: History entries must report `changes` with each field name humanized (one trailing `_id` removed, then
  underscores replaced by spaces, for example `assigned_to_id` becomes `assigned to`), and `changed_fields` must be
  those same humanized names in the same order. The stored audit rows must keep the original column names.
- **SPEC-5.525**: `is_task_marker_only_change` must return true only when the single changed field is `description`,
  both old and new are strings, and the strings are equal after `[x]` and `[X]` are replaced by `[ ]`. It must return
  false for no change, for any other changed field, for any additional changed field, and when the description goes
  between `null` and text.

#### Members list

- **SPEC-5.526**: `GET /api/v1/members` must require role `super_admin`, `admin` or `manager`; other roles must receive
  403. It must be scoped to the caller's tenant.
- **SPEC-5.527**: The members request must be rejected with 422 when `q` exceeds 200 characters, when `kind` is not one
  of `user`, `guest`, `everyone` (field `kind`, message `kind must be one of user, guest, everyone`), when `role` is not
  one of `super_admin`, `admin`, `manager`, `technician`, `dispatcher`, `sales`, `finance`, `read_only` (field `role`,
  message `role is not in the allowed set`), or when a `sort` parameter is present (field `sort`).
- **SPEC-5.528**: The members list must include every native user of the tenant except soft-deleted users and users
  whose email matches `system+%@mokosh.local`. Each is a `User` row carrying user id, email, names, role, status,
  `last_login_at`, and team chips.
- **SPEC-5.529**: A `User` row's `placed_by_grant_id` must be the id of the tenant's non-revoked guest grant whose
  grantee equals the user's `bunyip_user_id`, as text, and must be `null` when there is none.
- **SPEC-5.530**: Every non-revoked guest grant for the tenant whose grantee has no user row in the tenant must be an
  `UnplacedGuest` row carrying `grant_id`, `grantee_email`, `role`, `granted_at` and a `null` `grantee_name`.
- **SPEC-5.531**: `kind=user` must return only native users without a grant, `kind=guest` must return users with a grant
  plus unplaced guests, and `kind` absent or `everyone` must return both.
- **SPEC-5.532**: `q` (ignored when empty) must keep only user rows whose email, first name or last name contains it
  case-insensitively; the characters `%` and `_` in `q` must be treated as wildcards. `q` must not filter unplaced
  guests.
- **SPEC-5.533**: `role` must keep user rows whose own `users.role` equals it and unplaced guests whose grant `role`
  equals it.
- **SPEC-5.534**: `team_id` must keep only users who are members of that team in the tenant and must exclude all
  unplaced guests. A team id that does not exist must yield an empty page with `total` 0, not a 404.
- **SPEC-5.535**: The merged set must be ordered by lowercase last name, lowercase first name, lowercase email, then id
  text. Unplaced guests sort with empty last and first name, so they precede users, ordered by lowercase grantee email
  and grant id. `total` must count the filtered set and the page must apply `LIMIT per_page OFFSET (page-1)*per_page`.
- **SPEC-5.536**: For each `User` row on the returned page the response must list the team chips (`team_id`,
  `team_name`, `color`) of the tenant's active teams the user belongs to, and an empty list when there are none.
  Archived teams must not appear.
- **SPEC-5.537**: The members response must carry `rows`, `total`, `page`, `per_page` (the effective limit, 1 to 100)
  and `bunyip_reachable`, which must always be `true`.
- **SPEC-5.538**: The members queries must constrain users by the caller's tenant id and grants by the caller's tenant
  slug. If the tenant slug cannot be read the request must fail with the database error (500), not return an empty list.

#### Invitations

- **SPEC-5.539**: `GET /api/v1/invitations`, `POST /api/v1/invitations` and `DELETE /api/v1/invitations/{id}` must
  require role `super_admin` or `admin`; other roles must receive 403.
- **SPEC-5.540**: Creating an invitation must reject an invalid `email` with 422, and a `role` outside `admin`,
  `manager`, `technician`, `dispatcher`, `sales`, `finance` (so `super_admin` and `read_only` are refused) with 400 and
  message `Role must be one of admin, manager, technician, dispatcher, sales, finance`. An omitted `role` must default
  to `admin`.
- **SPEC-5.541**: Creating an invitation with a `team_id` must verify that an active team with that id exists in the
  caller's tenant, and must otherwise fail with 422 field `team_id`, message `does not exist in this tenant`, without
  writing the invitation.
- **SPEC-5.542**: Creating an invitation must store the email trimmed and lowercased, status `pending`, `invited_by` the
  caller, and `expires_at` 14 days after creation, and must return the invitation (`id`, `email`, `role`, `status`,
  `invited_by`, `expires_at`, `created_at`, `team_id`).
- **SPEC-5.543**: Creating an invitation for an email that already has a pending invitation in the tenant (compared
  case-insensitively) must update that row's role, `invited_by`, `expires_at` and `team_id` and keep its id, and must
  not fail with a conflict.
- **SPEC-5.544**: In the same transaction, creating an invitation must change the tenant's `kind` from `personal` to
  `org`. Only when that change happened must it also set the tenant's `timesheets` module to enabled. A tenant already
  of another kind must keep its module settings.
- **SPEC-5.545**: Creating an invitation must write an audit row (`create`, entity `tenant_invitations`, new snapshot of
  the row) in the same transaction, so that a failed audit write rolls back the invitation.
- **SPEC-5.546**: After the invitation transaction commits, and only when both an accept-link base URL and a
  notifications dispatcher are configured, the service must dispatch `invitations.created` with the recipient email,
  salutation, tenant name, role, `ttl_days` 14, app name and app URL. A dispatch failure must be logged at WARN with the
  invite id and recipient and must not roll back the invitation or change the response status.
- **SPEC-5.547**: Listing invitations must return only invitations with status `pending` in the caller's tenant, newest
  `created_at` first, paginated with a `total`; it must not filter on `expires_at`. A `sort` parameter must be rejected
  with 422.
- **SPEC-5.548**: `newest_pending_for(email)` must trim and lowercase the email and return, across all tenants, the most
  recently created invitation with status `pending` and `expires_at` in the future (`id`, `tenant_id`, `role`,
  `team_id`), or `None`. It must be called only from the pre-session login path and never from a route handler.
- **SPEC-5.549**: Accepting an invitation must set its status to `accepted` with `accepted_at` and `accepted_by` only
  while its status is still `pending`. When no row was updated (already accepted or revoked) it must roll back, return
  success, and enrol nobody.
- **SPEC-5.550**: Accepting an invitation that names a team must, in the same transaction, add the accepting user to
  that team with role `member`, only when the team is active and belongs to the invitation's tenant. An existing
  membership must be left unchanged. A missing or archived team must not fail the acceptance.
- **SPEC-5.551**: Revoking must set the status of a `pending` invitation of the caller's tenant to `revoked` and answer
  200 with an empty body. An unknown id, an id from another tenant, or an invitation that is not pending must answer 404
  `Invitation not found`.

#### Teams

- **SPEC-5.552**: The teams router must expose `GET` and `POST` on `/api/v1/teams`; `GET`, `PUT` and `DELETE` on
  `/api/v1/teams/{team_id}`; `GET` and `POST` on `/api/v1/teams/{team_id}/members`; `PUT` and `DELETE` on
  `/api/v1/teams/{team_id}/members/{user_id}`; and `GET /api/v1/me/teams`. Every route must require an authenticated
  caller.
- **SPEC-5.553**: `GET /api/v1/teams` must return the tenant's teams ordered by `name`, paginated with a `total` that
  uses the same filters, and each team must carry `member_count` (0 for a team without members). A `sort` parameter must
  be rejected with 422.
- **SPEC-5.554**: The `active` query parameter must be compared case-insensitively: `all` returns active and archived
  teams, `false`, `0` or `no` return only archived teams, and every other value or no value returns only active teams.
  `manager_id` must keep only teams with that manager.
- **SPEC-5.555**: `POST /api/v1/teams` must require role `super_admin` or `admin` (403 otherwise), reject a `name`
  shorter than 1 or longer than 255 characters with 422, and answer 201 with the created team (active, `member_count`
  absent).
- **SPEC-5.556**: A team `color`, on create and update, must be exactly `#` followed by six hexadecimal digits, and must
  otherwise be rejected with 422 field `color`. The messages are `must be a 7-character hex color like #6366F1` for a
  wrong length, `must start with '#' (e.g. #6366F1)` for a missing `#`, and `must be hex digits after the '#' (e.g.
  #6366F1)` for a non-hex digit.
- **SPEC-5.557**: A `manager_id` on create or update must belong to a non-deleted user of the caller's tenant, and must
  otherwise be rejected with 422 field `manager_id`, message `user not found in this tenant`, identical for a missing
  user and for a user of another tenant.
- **SPEC-5.558**: A team name must be unique case-insensitively among the tenant's active teams: creating a team, or
  renaming one, to a colliding name must fail with 409 `A team with this name already exists`. On update the team being
  renamed must be excluded, so changing only the case of its own name succeeds.
- **SPEC-5.559**: Creating a team must write an audit row (`create`, entity `teams`, new snapshot) in the same
  transaction as the insert.
- **SPEC-5.560**: `GET /api/v1/teams/{team_id}` must return the team of the caller's tenant, or 404 `Team not found`.
  With `include=members` (case-insensitive) it must return `{team, members}` with the member roster; otherwise it must
  return the team alone.
- **SPEC-5.561**: `PUT /api/v1/teams/{team_id}`, `DELETE /api/v1/teams/{team_id}`, `POST
  /api/v1/teams/{team_id}/members`, `PUT` and `DELETE /api/v1/teams/{team_id}/members/{user_id}` must be allowed for
  role `super_admin` or `admin`, or for the caller whose id equals the team's `manager_id`. Any other caller must
  receive 403 `Only an administrator or this team's manager may make this change.`, and for a non-admin caller a team
  that does not exist in the tenant must answer 404 before the 403 check can apply. The check must run before body
  validation.
- **SPEC-5.562**: `PUT /api/v1/teams/{team_id}` must change only the supplied fields (`name`, `description`,
  `manager_id`, `color`, `is_active`) and always refresh `updated_at`. An explicit `null` `manager_id` must clear the
  manager, and an absent one must leave it. A missing team must answer 404 `Team not found`.
- **SPEC-5.563**: A successful team update must write an audit row (`update`, entity `teams`, before and after
  snapshots) in the same transaction, and return the freshly read team.
- **SPEC-5.564**: `DELETE /api/v1/teams/{team_id}` must archive the team by setting `is_active` to false (never delete
  the row or its member rows), write an audit row (`update`, before and after snapshots) in the same transaction, and
  answer 204. A team missing from the tenant must answer 404 `Team not found`.
- **SPEC-5.565**: `GET /api/v1/teams/{team_id}/members` must answer 404 `Team not found` when the team is not in the
  caller's tenant (archived teams are readable), else return the roster ordered by user last name then first name with
  `user_id`, `email`, names, `avatar_url`, `role` and `joined_at`, excluding soft-deleted users.
- **SPEC-5.566**: Adding a team member must default the role to `member`, accept only `leader` or `member` (otherwise
  422 field `role`, message `must be 'leader' or 'member'`), and require the `user_id` to be a non-deleted user of the
  caller's tenant (otherwise 422 field `user_id`, message `user not found in this tenant`).
- **SPEC-5.567**: Adding a team member to a team missing from the tenant must answer 404 `Team not found`; adding a user
  already in the team must answer 409 `User is already a member of this team`; success must answer 201 with the tenant,
  team, user, role and stored `joined_at`, and write an audit row (`create`, entity `team_members`, `entity_id` the user
  id) in the same transaction.
- **SPEC-5.568**: Changing a member's role must accept only `leader` or `member` (422 field `role` otherwise), answer
  404 `Team member not found` when the membership does not exist, write an audit row (`update`, entity `team_members`,
  before and after snapshots) in the same transaction, and return the stored membership.
- **SPEC-5.569**: Removing a team member must delete the membership, write an audit row (`delete`, before snapshot) in
  the same transaction, and answer 204. When the membership does not exist it must answer 204 without writing an audit
  row.
- **SPEC-5.570**: `GET /api/v1/me/teams` must return the active teams of the caller's tenant that the caller belongs to,
  ordered by `name`, without `member_count`.
- **SPEC-5.571**: A team member's `leader` role must grant no additional authorization: write access to a team depends
  only on the rules in SPEC-5.561. Every teams query must filter by the caller's tenant id and run in a tenant-scoped
  transaction, except the manager, user and name-uniqueness probes, which filter explicitly by tenant id.

## 6. Configuration

Configuration keys are declared once in `src/config/registry.rs` and resolved at boot into a numbered generation. A key
has a tier, a `since` release and a `required` flag; a variable read outside the registry carries the same facts in
`src/config/variables.toml`. `docs/configuration.md` is generated from those two sources and is not a source of truth.
The behavior of each consumer is specified in the section that owns it (sections 3, 4, 5, 13 and 15) and is referenced
here by id; this section states what only the configuration layer decides: the key, its tier, its default, how its value
is parsed and what makes boot refuse. In quoted error texts, `{x:?}` is the value written in double quotes and `{x}` is
the value as given.

### 6.1 Registry, tiers and resolution

- **SPEC-6.1**: Every configuration key read through `crate::config::get`, `has` or `served_by` must be a constant
  declared by the `declare_keys!` macro in `src/config/registry.rs`, which emits the key name, its tier, its `since`
  release and its `required` flag from one declaration. A read that names a key the registry does not declare must fail
  to compile, because `get` accepts only a `&'static ConfigKey`.
- **SPEC-6.2**: Every declared key name must be unique in the registry and must consist only of `A-Z`, `0-9` and `_` and
  begin with a letter, so that every provider can address it.
- **SPEC-6.3**: The registry must declare exactly these keys in the bootstrap tier, in this order: `DATABASE_URL`,
  `MOKOSH_APP_DATABASE_URL`, `ENCRYPTION_KEY`, `APP_SECRETS_DIR`, `CONFIG_FILE_DIR`, `CONFIG_PROVIDERS`,
  `BUNYIP_CONFIG_URL`, `BUNYIP_CONFIG_CLIENT_ID`, `BUNYIP_CONFIG_CLIENT_SECRET`, `AUTH_PROVIDERS`. Every other declared
  key must be in the application tier. A bootstrap key is what a provider is built from or what chooses which providers
  run, so it is resolved once per process and changing it needs a restart.
- **SPEC-6.4**: The registry must flag exactly these keys `required`, in this order: `DATABASE_URL`,
  `MOKOSH_APP_DATABASE_URL`, `ENCRYPTION_KEY`, `BASE_URL`, `JWT_SECRET`, `BUNYIP_WEBHOOK_SECRET`, `CLIENT_ORIGIN`,
  `SPA_BASE_URL`. `required` means the server refuses to start without the key outside the `development`, `dev` and
  `test` environments (see SPEC-6.35 to SPEC-6.43). `MOKOSH_DEPLOYMENT_MODE` is also required but is read outside the
  registry, so `variables.toml` carries its `required = true`.
- **SPEC-6.5**: Every key must state `since` as a release of the form `vX.Y.Z`. A key that became required after it was
  added must state `required "vX.Y.Z"` with a release later than `since`, and only a `required` key may state one. The
  registry states: `MOKOSH_APP_DATABASE_URL` since `v0.3.0` required since `v0.14.0`; `ENCRYPTION_KEY` since `v0.1.0`
  required since `v0.4.0`; `JWT_SECRET` since `v0.1.0` required since `v0.4.0`; `BASE_URL` since `v0.1.0` required since
  `v0.14.0`; `CLIENT_ORIGIN` since `v0.2.0` required since `v0.14.0`; `SPA_BASE_URL` since `v0.12.0` required since
  `v0.14.0`; `DATABASE_URL` since `v0.1.0` and `BUNYIP_WEBHOOK_SECRET` since `v0.6.0`, both required from `since`.
- **SPEC-6.6**: A generation must record, for every declared key, the value and the name of the provider that served it.
  `crate::config::get` must answer `Some(value)` for any value a provider holds, including the empty string, and `None`
  only when no provider holds the key; trimming, blank-as-unset and defaults belong to the caller, so a compose variable
  forwarded but unset (an empty string) is a held value.
- **SPEC-6.7**: `config::init_from_env` must be called once at boot before any other configuration read. It must install
  the provider chosen by `CONFIG_BACKEND` (or the hosting profile's default), resolve the first generation, and log at
  info "configuration provider selected" with the provider name, whether the profile or the operator decided it, and the
  number of declared keys. When a provider other than the chosen one was already installed by an earlier read, it must
  fail boot with the message "the configuration provider was already resolved as {installed} before startup selected
  {chosen}; a read ran before init_from_env".
- **SPEC-6.8**: After resolving, boot must log at warn "no provider holds {KEY}; {feature}" for every unresolved key
  that carries a `feature` annotation, and must log nothing for an unresolved key without one. The registry declares no
  `feature` annotation, so a missing key produces no such warning.
- **SPEC-6.9**: `config::refresh` must build a complete new generation and install it atomically. The bootstrap-tier
  entries must be copied unchanged from the previous generation and every application-tier key must be re-resolved. When
  the refresh is rejected, `refresh` must return the previous generation, which stays live.
- **SPEC-6.10**: `config::try_refresh` must reject, before any provider is consulted, a request that requires a
  bootstrap-tier key, naming those keys. Otherwise it must build a candidate numbered one above the live generation and,
  when any required key has no serving provider in it, reject the request naming the unresolved keys and the providers
  consulted, leaving the live generation and its number unchanged. A rejection and an outcome's `Debug` output must name
  only keys and provider names, never a value.
- **SPEC-6.11**: `config::refuse_refresh_of_bootstrap` must return a configuration error "bootstrap keys cannot be
  refreshed; {KEY} is Bootstrap tier" for a bootstrap-tier key and `Ok` for an application-tier key.
- **SPEC-6.12**: `config::check_staleness` must pair each declared key's recorded serving provider with a live presence
  probe of the installed provider and classify it as exactly one of: unchanged, appeared since resolution, disappeared
  since resolution, or changed provider since resolution. It must never read or return a value, and it must report a
  provider that cannot enumerate its keys as unsupported, distinct from a provider that enumerated none.
- **SPEC-6.13**: The environment provider must answer a variable that is set but not valid UTF-8 as absent, and must log
  at error, naming the key, that the variable is set but unreadable. Its presence probe must still report the variable
  as held, so the failure stays distinguishable from a variable that is not set.
- **SPEC-6.14**: The environment provider must enumerate only declared registry keys that are present in the process
  environment, never the rest of the process environment.
- **SPEC-6.15**: `CONFIG_BACKEND` is not a registry key and is read only by `ConfigSelection::from_env`. A blank or
  unset value must take the hosting profile's configuration provider, and the only provider reachable through it is
  `environment`. A name of another kind (`file`, `database`, `bunyip`) must fail boot with a configuration error
  "CONFIG_BACKEND {name:?} names a provider the single-provider slot cannot yet construct (only 'environment' is
  reachable that way); enable it through CONFIG_PROVIDERS instead once the chain wiring lands (PMS-987)". A name of no
  kind must fail boot with "configuration provider {name:?} is not a known kind; expected one of: environment, file,
  database, bunyip", and must not fall back to the default.
- **SPEC-6.16**: `CONFIG_PROVIDERS` is a bootstrap key read only by the provider operator commands through
  `build_chain_from_env`; the running server does not install a configuration chain, so setting it must not change which
  provider serves the server's configuration. The parser must split on commas, trim each entry, and fail with
  "CONFIG_PROVIDERS entry #{n} is empty; a comma-separated priority list cannot carry a blank name" for a blank entry
  and "CONFIG_PROVIDERS lists {provider} twice; a provider cannot appear more than once, priority would be ambiguous"
  for a repeated provider. An unset or blank value must yield the hosting profile's single default provider, and the
  first entry of a list is the highest priority.
- **SPEC-6.17**: A configuration chain must resolve each key from the first provider, in priority order, that holds it
  and can decode it. Every other provider that holds the key, including one that holds it but cannot decode it, must be
  reported as also holding it. Each key must be classified as served by the top provider alone, missing, duplicated
  across providers, or served by a lower provider while the top one does not hold it. Classification must log at info
  for a served key, and at warn for a missing key, for each duplicate (naming the serving and the ignored provider) and
  for a lower provider serving a key the top provider lacks. A log line must name the key and providers and never the
  value.
- **SPEC-6.18**: Building a chain that enables the database provider without a database handle must fail with a
  configuration error that begins "CONFIG_PROVIDERS enables the database provider, but the chain builder was called
  without a database handle".
- **SPEC-6.19**: The file configuration provider must read the directory named by `CONFIG_FILE_DIR` once, at
  construction, taking one file per declared key named exactly as the key. An unset or blank `CONFIG_FILE_DIR` and a
  directory that does not exist must produce an empty provider with no log line. A path that exists but is not a
  directory must produce an empty provider and an error log "CONFIG_FILE_DIR names a path that is not a directory; the
  file configuration provider holds nothing". A path whose metadata cannot be read must produce an empty provider and an
  error log "CONFIG_FILE_DIR could not be read; the file configuration provider holds nothing" with the cause.
- **SPEC-6.20**: The file configuration provider must hold a key's value as the file's contents with exactly one
  trailing newline (`\r\n` or `\n`) removed and every other character preserved. A file that exists but cannot be read
  must be logged at error, naming the path and the key, and the key must be treated as not held. A file whose name is
  not a declared key must be ignored.
- **SPEC-6.21**: The file configuration provider's `set` and `delete` must refuse a bootstrap-tier key with a
  configuration error "{KEY} is a bootstrap-tier key and cannot be written to the file configuration provider" (or
  "deleted from"), before touching the filesystem. `set` on a provider with no directory must fail with "file
  configuration provider has no directory; set CONFIG_FILE_DIR to enable writes". `delete` of a file that is already
  absent must succeed.
- **SPEC-6.22**: `DatabaseProvider::build` must refuse, before any database access, a key list that contains a
  bootstrap-tier key, with a configuration error "the database configuration provider cannot serve bootstrap-tier keys
  (the credential used to reach the database cannot come from the database): {KEY, KEY}" naming every offender.
  Otherwise it must preload the listed keys from the `app_config` table once and serve every later read from that cache.
- **SPEC-6.23**: The database configuration provider's `set` must upsert the `app_config` row through the privileged
  migrator pool and update its cache, so a read after the write sees the value; `delete` must remove the row and the
  cached value, and a row that is already absent must not be an error. Either operation on a bootstrap-tier key must be
  refused with the same wording as the file provider, with "database" as the provider name. A failed database write must
  return a database error "could not write app_config row: {cause}" (or "could not delete app_config row: {cause}") and
  leave the cache unchanged.
- **SPEC-6.24**: The Bunyip configuration provider must be built from `BUNYIP_CONFIG_URL`, `BUNYIP_CONFIG_CLIENT_ID` and
  `BUNYIP_CONFIG_CLIENT_SECRET`. An unset or blank `BUNYIP_CONFIG_URL` must yield an empty provider that sends no
  request. When the URL is set and either credential half is blank, building must fail with a configuration error
  "BUNYIP_CONFIG_URL is set, so {NAME} must be set too; the Bunyip configuration provider needs both halves of its
  machine credential". Each credential half must be read from the file named by `{NAME}_FILE` first, falling back to
  `{NAME}`; an unreadable `{NAME}_FILE` must be logged at error with the path and the cause. A trailing `/` of the URL
  must be removed.
- **SPEC-6.25**: The Bunyip configuration provider must serve only the keys in its allow-list, which holds
  `ABUSE_CONTACT_EMAIL` mapped to the remote key `mokosh/abuse_contact_email`, and for each it must send `GET
  {BUNYIP_CONFIG_URL}/v1/host/config/{remote key}` with the machine credential as HTTP Basic and a 10 second timeout. A
  404 must leave the key unheld and log at info that bunyip holds no value for it. A 401 must fail the build with an
  external-service error that names `BUNYIP_CONFIG_CLIENT_ID` and `bunyip-api machine-client rotate`. A 403 must fail
  the build with an error that names the key and `bunyip-api machine-client register --name mokosh-host-config
  --config-key {remote key}`. Any other non-2xx status must fail the build with "bunyip answered {status} for {key}:
  {body}". A transport failure must fail the build with "could not reach bunyip at {url}: {cause}. Check
  BUNYIP_CONFIG_URL and that bunyip is reachable from this host.". The value is `data.value` of the response envelope,
  trimmed, and a blank or absent value leaves the key unheld.
- **SPEC-6.26**: The Bunyip configuration provider's `set` and `delete` must always fail with a configuration error
  ("bunyip provider write is not implemented" for `set`, "bunyip provider does not support deletes" for `delete`), so
  the provider is read-only.
- **SPEC-6.27**: `parse_optional` must treat an unset value or one that is blank after trimming as "use the caller's
  default", and must parse any other value after trimming. A value that does not parse must be an error of the form
  "{KEY} is set to {raw:?}, which is not a valid value: {parse error}", naming the key and the raw value, and must never
  be replaced by the default.
- **SPEC-6.28**: `parse_positive` must apply `parse_optional` and additionally reject a value that is not strictly
  greater than the type's zero with "{KEY} must be a positive value, got {value}", so a cap of zero or below is an error
  and is not read as uncapped.
- **SPEC-6.29**: `config::parse::check_boot` must fail with the `parse_optional` message when a key that is read later
  by its own accessor (`OIDC_DEFAULT_TENANT_ID` as a UUID) is set to a value that does not parse, so the typo ends boot
  and does not wait for the first read.
- **SPEC-6.30**: A feature flag must be a declared application-tier key with a typed default. The boolean flag parser
  must accept `1`, `true` and `yes` as true and `0`, `false` and `no` as false, case-insensitively and after trimming,
  and must reject every other value. `Flag::read` must return the parsed value; for an unset or blank value it must
  return the flag's default; for a set value that does not parse it must log at warn "flag value failed to parse;
  serving the flag's default" with the key and the raw value and return the default.
- **SPEC-6.31**: The flag defaults must be: `ORGANIZATIONS_ENABLED` false on `self-hosted` and true on `saas`, resolved
  against the lenient deployment-mode reader at every read; `LOGIN_APPROVAL_ENABLED` false;
  `ALLOW_UNINVITED_BUNYIP_SIGNUP` false. No code outside the configuration module reads `ORGANIZATIONS_ENABLED`, so
  setting it changes no behavior.
- **SPEC-6.32**: `config::flags::check_boot` must run over every declared flag at boot and, when any flag is set to a
  non-blank value that does not parse, fail boot with "boot refused: {n} feature flag(s) set to an unparseable value."
  followed by a blank line and one "{KEY} is set to {raw:?}, which is not a valid value" line per flag. An unset or
  blank flag must pass.
- **SPEC-6.33**: No source file outside `src/config/` and the files named in `config::guard::ENTRY_POINTS` may read the
  process environment directly; every entry must carry the reason it cannot go through the provider. A new direct read
  must fail `cargo test --lib`.
- **SPEC-6.34**: `src/config/variables.toml` must list every variable the server reads outside `crate::config::get`,
  with `name`, `since`, `required` and the reading file, plus the removed variables and the per-release change notes. It
  is documentation data for `scripts/config-docs.nu`, is not read by the server, and a variable's `required = true`
  there must mean boot refuses it outside the `development`, `dev` and `test` environments.

### 6.2 Boot-time refusals

- **SPEC-6.35**: An environment is a development environment only when `ENVIRONMENT` is exactly `development`, `dev` or
  `test` (lower case, no surrounding whitespace). Every other value, including a blank value, `Development` and
  `production`, must be treated as deployed. An unset `ENVIRONMENT` must resolve to `development`.
- **SPEC-6.36**: A `.env` file in the working directory must be loaded before any variable is read, without overriding a
  variable already in the process environment. A missing `.env` must be ignored. A `.env` that exists but cannot be
  loaded must end boot with ".env could not be loaded: {cause}".
- **SPEC-6.37**: Boot must read `MOKOSH_DEPLOYMENT_MODE` strictly, before the database is touched, and must fail with
  the error in SPEC-4.60 for an unrecognised value.
- **SPEC-6.38**: Before any configuration is read, boot must refuse to start when any retired storage variable
  (`STORAGE_BACKEND`, `ATTACHMENT_DIR`, `S3_ENDPOINT`, `S3_BUCKET`, `S3_REGION`, `S3_PATH_STYLE`, `S3_ACCESS_KEY_ID`,
  `S3_SECRET_ACCESS_KEY`) is set to a non-blank value. It must print the refusal to standard error and return it,
  listing every set variable as "  - {old} -> {new}" with its replacement (`STORAGE_PROVIDER`, `STORAGE_ROOT`,
  `STORAGE_S3_ENDPOINT`, `STORAGE_S3_BUCKET`, `STORAGE_S3_REGION`, `STORAGE_S3_PATH_STYLE`, `STORAGE_S3_ACCESS_KEY_ID`,
  `STORAGE_S3_SECRET_ACCESS_KEY`). A retired variable must never supply a value (see SPEC-3.50).
- **SPEC-6.39**: Boot must resolve `JWT_SECRET`, `ENCRYPTION_KEY` and `BUNYIP_WEBHOOK_SECRET` as follows. In a
  development environment an unset or empty value must take the built-in development value for that key. Outside it, an
  unset or empty value must fail boot with "{KEY} is unset but required in the '{environment}' environment; the
  hardcoded dev fallback is only accepted in development/dev/test.", and a value equal to the built-in development value
  must fail boot with "{KEY} is set to the known dev fallback value, which is refused in the '{environment}'
  environment. Set a real secret (only development/dev/test accept the dev default).". A value is not trimmed, so a
  whitespace-only value counts as set.
- **SPEC-6.40**: Outside a development environment, `JWT_SECRET` must be at least 32 bytes long; a shorter value must
  fail boot with "JWT_SECRET must be at least 32 bytes in the '{environment}' environment; only development/dev/test
  accept a shorter secret.".
- **SPEC-6.41**: Outside a development environment, `ENCRYPTION_KEY` must be exactly 64 ASCII hexadecimal characters;
  any other value must fail boot with "ENCRYPTION_KEY must be a 64-character hex string in the '{environment}'
  environment (32 bytes, hex-encoded); only development/dev/test accept a raw 32-byte key.". In a development
  environment the value must still parse as a 32-byte key (SPEC-4.33), or boot must stop later, after the database is
  connected, with a panic "ENCRYPTION_KEY must be 32 bytes (or 64 hex chars)".
- **SPEC-6.42**: `AppConfig::from_env` must evaluate, in this order, `JWT_SECRET`, its length, `ENCRYPTION_KEY`,
  `BUNYIP_WEBHOOK_SECRET`, the `ENCRYPTION_KEY` shape, `PORT`, `RUN_MIGRATIONS` and `MOKOSH_MAX_TENANTS`, and must stop
  at the first failure and report only that one.
- **SPEC-6.43**: After `AppConfig::from_env` and outside a development environment, boot must check these six variables
  in this order and refuse to start when any resolves to unset or to a value that is blank after trimming:
  `DATABASE_URL`, `MOKOSH_DEPLOYMENT_MODE`, `MOKOSH_APP_DATABASE_URL`, `BASE_URL`, `CLIENT_ORIGIN`, `SPA_BASE_URL`. All
  missing variables must be reported in one error that begins "boot refused: {n} essential deployment-shape variable(s)
  unset in the '{environment}' environment. Only development/dev/test accept unset values here; every other environment
  must declare the shape.".
- **SPEC-6.44**: Each missing variable in that error must be one block of the form "FATAL: {name} is unset in the
  '{environment}' environment." followed by an indented "Purpose:" line, an indented "Available options: self-hosted |
  saas" line for `MOKOSH_DEPLOYMENT_MODE` only, and an indented "Example:" line with a sample assignment. In a
  development environment the check must pass without reading any of the six.
- **SPEC-6.45**: Outside a development environment an unset `DATABASE_URL` must leave the privileged connection string
  empty and be refused by the essential-variable check; in a development environment it must default to
  `postgres://postgres:postgres@localhost:5432/mokosh`. `MOKOSH_APP_DATABASE_URL`, when unset or blank, must default to
  the resolved `DATABASE_URL`, which makes the request pool use the privileged role and row level security inert;
  outside a development environment that state is refused by the essential-variable check.
- **SPEC-6.46**: A set-but-unparseable `PORT` (a `u16`), `RUN_MIGRATIONS` (a boolean) or `MOKOSH_MAX_TENANTS` (a
  positive `usize`) must end boot with the `parse_optional` or `parse_positive` message of SPEC-6.27 or SPEC-6.28, and a
  set-but-unparseable `OIDC_DEFAULT_TENANT_ID` (a UUID) or feature flag must end boot with the message of SPEC-6.29 or
  SPEC-6.32. A failure inside `AppConfig::from_env` must stop the process with a panic whose message begins "Failed to
  load configuration".
- **SPEC-6.47**: Boot must fail when the listen address "{HOST}:{PORT}" does not parse as a socket address, and when the
  address cannot be bound, with a non-zero exit and the underlying cause.
- **SPEC-6.48**: When `RUN_MIGRATIONS` is true, boot must run the embedded migrations before serving, and a failed
  migration must log at error "Failed to run database migrations: {cause}" and end boot with a non-zero exit.
  `RUN_MIGRATIONS=false` must skip the step.
- **SPEC-6.49**: Boot must refuse an unrecognised `SECRET_BACKEND`, `APP_SECRET_BACKEND`, `STORAGE_PROVIDER`,
  `MAIL_PROVIDER` or `AUTH_PROVIDERS` value with a configuration error that names the variable, the offending value and
  the legal values, and must never substitute the hosting profile's default (SPEC-6.70, SPEC-6.72, SPEC-6.93, SPEC-6.90,
  SPEC-6.77).
- **SPEC-6.50**: Boot must end with a non-zero exit when the application-tier secret survey classifies any governed
  secret as misplaced (absent from the declared provider but present in another) or unavailable (declared to a provider
  the process could not build), with one line per secret naming the secret and the provider (SPEC-3.4, SPEC-3.6). It
  must also end boot, naming the missing key, when a client id or secret of the Google Contacts, Microsoft 365, Xero or
  QuickBooks application is held without its pair (SPEC-6.76).
- **SPEC-6.51**: Boot must end with a non-zero exit when the selected mail provider's transport fails its boot
  verification, logging at error "email provider verify failed" with the cause. A configuration that cannot build the
  selected provider (SPEC-6.90) must also end boot.

### 6.3 Core keys

- **SPEC-6.52**: `ENVIRONMENT` (application, since `v0.1.0`) selects the rule of SPEC-6.35. The server's production
  check must be the exact string `production`, and the demo-seed gate must compare `production` case-insensitively
  (SPEC-15.2053).
- **SPEC-6.53**: `HOST` (application, since `v0.1.0`) must default to `0.0.0.0` and `PORT` (application, since `v0.1.0`)
  must default to `8080` only when the variable is unset or `PORT` is blank; a blank `HOST` must be used as given and
  fail the socket address parse of SPEC-6.47.
- **SPEC-6.54**: `RUN_MIGRATIONS` (application, since `v0.1.0`) must default to true when unset or blank and must accept
  only the literals `true` and `false`, so `1`, `yes` and `TRUE` must end boot with "RUN_MIGRATIONS is set to \"{raw}\",
  which is not a valid value: provided string was not `true` or `false`".
- **SPEC-6.55**: `BASE_URL` (application, since `v0.1.0`) is the base of platform-owned emailed links and must default
  to `http://localhost:8080` only when unset; it is required outside development environments (SPEC-6.43).
- **SPEC-6.56**: `CLIENT_ORIGIN` (application, since `v0.2.0`) is the browser origin of the client host, the default for
  `CORS_ORIGIN` and the base of password-reset and invitation links, and must default to `http://localhost:4301` only
  when unset; it is required outside development environments (SPEC-6.43).
- **SPEC-6.57**: `SPA_BASE_URL` (application, since `v0.12.0`) is the browser origin of the application client and the
  base of emailed links to client-only pages. It must be trimmed, and an unset or blank value must take the resolved
  `CLIENT_ORIGIN`. It is required outside development environments (SPEC-6.43).
- **SPEC-6.58**: `CORS_ORIGIN` (application, since `v0.2.0`) must be split on commas, each entry trimmed and each blank
  entry dropped; when no entry remains the allowed origins must be the single `CLIENT_ORIGIN`. An entry must be an exact
  origin that is a valid HTTP header value, or `https://*.{suffix}` or `http://*.{suffix}` where the suffix has no
  further `*` and contains a dot, which matches any origin of that scheme whose host ends with `.{suffix}`. A malformed
  entry must panic router construction at boot, naming the entry, and must never be skipped.
- **SPEC-6.59**: `PUBLIC_API_BASE_URL` (application, since `v0.12.0`) must be trimmed and stripped of trailing `/`, and
  an unset or blank value must mean none: the tenant logo is then omitted from client-facing email (SPEC-15.519).
- **SPEC-6.60**: `ABUSE_CONTACT_EMAIL` (application, since `v0.12.0`) must be trimmed, and an unset or blank value must
  mean none: the abuse-report line is then omitted from request-form email, and no other address is substituted.
- **SPEC-6.61**: `PORTAL_COOKIE_DOMAIN` (application, since `v0.19.0`) must add a `Domain` attribute to the portal
  refresh cookie only when it is non-blank after trimming (SPEC-5.449).
- **SPEC-6.62**: `MOKOSH_MAX_TENANTS` (application, since `v0.14.0`) must be read once at boot as a positive integer; an
  unset or blank value must leave tenant creation uncapped (SPEC-5.332), and a malformed or non-positive value must end
  boot (SPEC-6.46). A change takes effect on the next restart.
- **SPEC-6.63**: `MOKOSH_UPDATE_CHECK_URL` (application, since `v0.3.0`) when unset or blank after trimming must make
  `GET /api/v1/version/check` answer a disabled status with HTTP 200 and send no outbound request. When set, the check
  must use a 5 second timeout, cache a success for 15 minutes and a failure for 60 seconds, answer a failed check with
  HTTP 502, and omit userinfo, query and fragment of the URL from the failure message.
- **SPEC-6.64**: `RUST_LOG` (read outside the registry, since `v0.1.0`) must set the tracing filter, falling back to
  `info` when it is unset or invalid. It is read before the `.env` file is loaded, so a `RUST_LOG` defined only in
  `.env` has no effect.
- **SPEC-6.65**: `MOKOSH_DEPLOYMENT_MODE` (read outside the registry, since `v0.14.0`, required) is `self-hosted` or
  `saas`; an empty value means `self-hosted`; its readers are specified in SPEC-4.59 to SPEC-4.63, and it is required
  outside development environments (SPEC-6.43).
- **SPEC-6.66**: `DATABASE_URL` (bootstrap, since `v0.1.0`, required) is the privileged connection string used for
  migrations, bootstrap, role provisioning and the cross-tenant workers, and `MOKOSH_APP_DATABASE_URL` (bootstrap, since
  `v0.3.0`, required since `v0.14.0`) is the request-serving connection string; the defaults and refusals are in
  SPEC-6.45 and SPEC-6.43.
- **SPEC-6.67**: `MOKOSH_ADMIN_DATABASE_URL` (since `v0.4.0`), `MOKOSH_MIGRATOR_PASSWORD` (since `v0.3.0`) and
  `MOKOSH_APP_PASSWORD` (since `v0.3.0`) are optional and are read only by role provisioning at boot. When roles must be
  created or reconciled and `MOKOSH_ADMIN_DATABASE_URL` is empty or unset, boot must fail with a database error that
  names the missing variable and the state found, and a password variable needed by the statements that will run must
  fail with "{KEY} is required to provision DB roles but is unset".

### 6.4 Secrets, authentication and identity provider

- **SPEC-6.68**: `JWT_SECRET` (application, since `v0.1.0`, required since `v0.4.0`) is the signing key of server-issued
  tokens, and `BUNYIP_WEBHOOK_SECRET` (application, since `v0.6.0`, required) is the shared secret of identity-provider
  webhooks, whose value is used as raw bytes; both follow SPEC-6.39 and `JWT_SECRET` follows SPEC-6.40.
- **SPEC-6.69**: `ENCRYPTION_KEY` (bootstrap, since `v0.1.0`, required since `v0.4.0`) is the key for secrets at rest
  and follows SPEC-6.39 and SPEC-6.41.
- **SPEC-6.70**: `SECRET_BACKEND` (read outside the registry, since `v0.14.0`) selects the tenant-tier secret provider
  and accepts only `database` and `infisical`; blank or unset takes the hosting profile's default, `database`. A value
  that is valid only for the application tier must fail with a message naming `APP_SECRET_BACKEND`, and any other value
  with "SECRET_BACKEND {value:?} is not a known provider; expected 'database' or 'infisical'" (SPEC-3.20, SPEC-3.21).
- **SPEC-6.71**: `SECRET_BACKEND=infisical` must require `INFISICAL_ADDRESS`, `INFISICAL_PROJECT_ID`,
  `INFISICAL_CLIENT_ID` and `INFISICAL_CLIENT_SECRET` to be non-blank after trimming and must fail boot with
  "SECRET_BACKEND=infisical requires {NAME} to be set" for the first one missing; `INFISICAL_ENVIRONMENT` must default
  to `dev` when unset or blank. `INFISICAL_PROJECT_ID`, `INFISICAL_CLIENT_ID`, `INFISICAL_CLIENT_SECRET` and
  `INFISICAL_ENVIRONMENT` are read outside the registry (since `v0.1.0`).
- **SPEC-6.72**: `APP_SECRET_BACKEND` (read outside the registry, since `v0.16.0`) selects the application-tier secret
  provider among `environment`, `file`, `database`, `infisical` and `bunyip`; blank or unset takes the hosting profile's
  default. A value outside that list must fail boot with "APP_SECRET_BACKEND {value:?} is not a known application-tier
  secret provider; expected one of: environment, file, database, infisical, bunyip" (SPEC-3.3).
- **SPEC-6.73**: `APP_SECRETS_DIR` (bootstrap, since `v0.14.0`) must enable the file application-secret provider only
  when it is non-blank after trimming (SPEC-3.6, SPEC-3.8).
- **SPEC-6.74**: `BUNYIP_SECRETS_URL`, `BUNYIP_SECRETS_CLIENT_ID` and `BUNYIP_SECRETS_CLIENT_SECRET` (read outside the
  registry, since `v0.18.0`) must enable the bunyip application-secret provider only when the URL is non-blank, and a
  URL without both credential halves must fail boot (SPEC-3.12). On `saas`, the profile must declare
  `GOOGLE_CONTACTS_CLIENT_ID` and `GOOGLE_CONTACTS_CLIENT_SECRET` to the `bunyip` provider; on `self-hosted` it must
  declare none.
- **SPEC-6.75**: `INFISICAL_ADDRESS` (application, since `v0.12.0`) must be treated as unset when blank after trimming.
  When non-blank it must enable the Infisical application-secret provider and the Infisical probe of the readiness
  endpoint; when blank the readiness endpoint must report Infisical as skipped and not as failed.
- **SPEC-6.76**: `SMTP_PASSWORD` (application, since `v0.2.0`) is read by the mailer through the configuration provider,
  and `GOOGLE_CONTACTS_CLIENT_ID` and `GOOGLE_CONTACTS_CLIENT_SECRET` (since `v0.14.0`), `MICROSOFT_CONTACTS_CLIENT_ID`
  and `MICROSOFT_CONTACTS_CLIENT_SECRET`, `XERO_CLIENT_ID`, `XERO_CLIENT_SECRET`, `XERO_WEBHOOK_KEY`,
  `QUICKBOOKS_CLIENT_ID`, `QUICKBOOKS_CLIENT_SECRET` and `QUICKBOOKS_VERIFIER_TOKEN` (all since `v0.17.0`) are governed
  application secrets read through the application-secret provider. A client id without its secret, or the reverse, must
  end boot with a configuration error "{Application} is half configured: {present} is set and {missing} is not. A client
  id and its secret have to come from the same ..., so add {missing} beside it or remove both." where {Application} is
  "Google Contacts", "Microsoft 365 Contacts", or the Xero or QuickBooks provider name followed by " invoicing".
- **SPEC-6.77**: `AUTH_PROVIDERS` (bootstrap, since `v0.14.0`) is a comma-separated priority list of `bunyip` and
  `local`; blank or unset takes the hosting profile's list (`local` on `self-hosted`, `bunyip,local` on `saas`). An
  unknown name, a repeated name or a blank entry must fail boot with a configuration error naming the legal values
  (SPEC-5.178, SPEC-5.179).
- **SPEC-6.78**: `OIDC_ISSUER` and `OIDC_AUDIENCE` (application, since `v0.3.0`) must mount the identity-provider token
  verifier only when both are present. An absent one must fail the verifier configuration with "OIDC_ISSUER must be set
  (e.g. {url})" or "OIDC_AUDIENCE must be set (e.g. {url})", the issuer's trailing `/` must be removed (SPEC-5.113,
  SPEC-5.114), and boot must log at info "Bunyip RS verifier disabled" with the reason and continue.
- **SPEC-6.79**: `OIDC_JWKS_CACHE_TTL_SECS` (since `v0.3.0`) must default to 600 and `OIDC_LEEWAY_SECONDS` (since
  `v0.3.0`) to 30, both parsed as `u64` seconds; a set value that does not parse must be an error naming the key and the
  raw value (SPEC-5.115) and the verifier must then be disabled.
- **SPEC-6.80**: `OIDC_DEFAULT_TENANT_ID` (application, since `v0.3.0`) must be a UUID, checked at boot by SPEC-6.29.
  The tenant a first-seen identity-provider user lands in must be this UUID, else the UUID
  `00000000-0000-0000-0000-000000000001`, and an unparseable value seen after boot must log at warn and use that
  fallback (SPEC-5.174, SPEC-15.2054).
- **SPEC-6.81**: `OIDC_BACKCHANNEL_CLIENT_ID` (application, since `v0.15.0`) must be trimmed, and a blank or unset value
  must make the back-channel logout receiver reject every logout token (SPEC-5.133).
- **SPEC-6.82**: `ADMIN_EMAIL` and `ADMIN_PASSWORD` (application, since `v0.1.0`) must create the first platform
  administrator only when both are non-blank and no platform administrator exists (SPEC-5.6 to SPEC-5.9). A failure must
  be logged at warn "Admin bootstrap failed" and must not stop boot.
- **SPEC-6.83**: `ALLOW_UNINVITED_BUNYIP_SIGNUP` (application, since `v0.16.0`) is a boolean flag, default false, which
  opens just-in-time personal-tenant provisioning to a first-seen identity-provider user and never relaxes the
  requirement that the provider has verified the email address.
- **SPEC-6.84**: `LOGIN_APPROVAL_ENABLED` (application, since `v0.8.0`) is a boolean flag, default false, read once at
  boot into the authentication service, so a change needs a restart.
- **SPEC-6.85**: `BUNYIP_API_BASE_URL`, `BUNYIP_DIRECTORY_CLIENT_ID` and `BUNYIP_DIRECTORY_CLIENT_SECRET` (application,
  since `v0.16.0`) must be set together or all left unset (SPEC-5.200, SPEC-5.201). A partial set must make router
  construction log at warn "PMS-1208 Bunyip directory client disabled: partial configuration. Grant invitations will be
  created without the SaaS-mode existence check." and boot must continue without the directory client.
- **SPEC-6.86**: `BUNYIP_STATUS_CLIENT_ID` and `BUNYIP_STATUS_CLIENT_SECRET` (application, since `v0.14.0`) must enable
  the machine credential of the provider status endpoints only when both are non-empty; when either is empty the
  endpoints must gate on the administrator session alone (SPEC-3.71, SPEC-3.72).
- **SPEC-6.87**: `BUNYIP_CONFIG_URL`, `BUNYIP_CONFIG_CLIENT_ID`, `BUNYIP_CONFIG_CLIENT_SECRET`, `CONFIG_FILE_DIR` and
  `CONFIG_PROVIDERS` (bootstrap, since `v0.14.0`) are consumed by the configuration providers of SPEC-6.19 to SPEC-6.26,
  and `CONFIG_BACKEND` (since `v0.14.0`) by SPEC-6.15.
- **SPEC-6.88**: `MOKOSH_SEED_TENANT_ID` (application, since `v0.3.0`) must name the template tenant whose configuration
  is copied to a new tenant, defaulting to `00000000-0000-0000-0000-000000000001`, and a value that is not a UUID must
  fail the copy with "MOKOSH_SEED_TENANT_ID is not a valid UUID: {cause}" (SPEC-5.351).
- **SPEC-6.89**: `MOKOSH_DEMO_SEED` (application, since `v0.3.0`) enables first-visit demo seeding outside production
  only for `1`, `true`, `yes` or `on` (SPEC-15.2053).

### 6.5 Mail, storage, network and uploads

- **SPEC-6.90**: `MAIL_PROVIDER` (application, since `v0.14.0`) accepts `log`, `smtp` and `bunyip`; any other non-blank
  value must fail boot with "MAIL_PROVIDER {value:?} is not a known provider; expected 'log', 'smtp' or 'bunyip'". Unset
  or blank takes `smtp` when `SMTP_HOST` is non-blank, otherwise the hosting profile's default (SPEC-4.68, SPEC-4.69).
- **SPEC-6.91**: `SMTP_HOST`, `SMTP_USERNAME` and `SMTP_FROM` (application, since `v0.2.0`) and `SMTP_PORT` and
  `SMTP_TLS` (since `v0.2.0`) must default as follows: `SMTP_PORT` to `587` (parsed as `u16`, a bad value ending boot
  with the `parse_optional` message), `SMTP_FROM` to `Mokosh <noreply@example.com>`, `SMTP_TLS` to `starttls` with
  `implicit`, `starttls` and `none` accepted (SPEC-4.66). An `SMTP_FROM` that is not a valid mailbox must fail the SMTP
  mailer build with "SMTP_FROM {value}: {cause}". `SMTP_USERNAME` set without a non-empty `SMTP_PASSWORD` must fail with
  "SMTP_USERNAME is set but SMTP_PASSWORD is empty" (SPEC-4.67).
- **SPEC-6.92**: `BUNYIP_MAILER_URL`, `BUNYIP_MAILER_CLIENT_ID` and `BUNYIP_MAILER_CLIENT_SECRET` (application, since
  `v0.16.0`) are read only when `MAIL_PROVIDER=bunyip`. A blank URL must fail boot with "MAIL_PROVIDER=bunyip requires
  BUNYIP_MAILER_URL; the selected provider has no relay to send through", and a blank credential half with
  "BUNYIP_MAILER_URL is set, so {NAME} must be set too; the Bunyip mailer relay needs both halves of its machine
  credential".
- **SPEC-6.93**: `STORAGE_PROVIDER` (since `v0.15.0`) accepts `local` and `s3`, blank or unset takes the hosting
  profile's default (`local`), and any other value must fail boot with "STORAGE_PROVIDER {value} is not a known
  provider; expected 'local' or 's3'" (SPEC-3.46).
- **SPEC-6.94**: `STORAGE_ROOT` (since `v0.15.0`) must default to the relative path `./attachments` when unset or blank
  (SPEC-3.48).
- **SPEC-6.95**: `STORAGE_S3_ENDPOINT`, `STORAGE_S3_BUCKET`, `STORAGE_S3_ACCESS_KEY_ID` and
  `STORAGE_S3_SECRET_ACCESS_KEY` (since `v0.15.0`) are required when the provider is `s3`; `STORAGE_S3_REGION` (since
  `v0.15.0`) must default to `us-east-1` and `STORAGE_S3_PATH_STYLE` (since `v0.15.0`) to path-style addressing
  (SPEC-3.54). All `STORAGE_*` variables are read outside the registry.
- **SPEC-6.96**: `ATTACHMENT_MAX_BYTES` (application, since `v0.4.0`) must default to 26214400 bytes (25 MiB) and
  `KB_ATTACHMENT_MAX_BYTES` (application, since `v0.14.0`) to 5242880 bytes (5 MiB) when unset or blank (SPEC-7.45,
  SPEC-15.1098).
- **SPEC-6.97**: `TENANT_LOGO_MAX_BYTES` (application, since `v0.12.0`) must default to 1048576 bytes, and
  `BRANDING_TENANT_FAVICON_MAX_BYTES`, `BRANDING_TENANT_BACKGROUND_MAX_BYTES`, `BRANDING_COMPANY_LOGO_MAX_BYTES`,
  `BRANDING_COMPANY_FAVICON_MAX_BYTES` and `BRANDING_COMPANY_BACKGROUND_MAX_BYTES` (application, since `v0.14.0`) to
  524288, 2097152, 1048576, 524288 and 2097152 bytes (SPEC-5.377, SPEC-15.2085).
- **SPEC-6.98**: Each upload cap must be parsed with `parse_positive`, so a malformed, zero or negative value must
  produce a configuration error naming the key and the raw value and must never fall back to the default. The ticket
  attachment, KB attachment and tenant logo caps are read when the router is built, so such a value must end boot with a
  panic "{KEY} invalid"; the five other branding caps are read at each upload, so such a value must fail that upload
  with a configuration error and must not end boot.
- **SPEC-6.99**: `IP2LOCATION_DB_PATH` (application, since `v0.7.0`) must be trimmed and a blank or unset value must
  disable login-location alerts, logging at info "IP2LOCATION_DB_PATH unset; login-location alerts disabled". A path
  whose database cannot be loaded must log at warn "Failed to load IP2Location DB; login-location alerts disabled" with
  the path and cause, and boot must continue (SPEC-4.5).
- **SPEC-6.100**: `IP2PROXY_DB_PATH` (application, since `v0.11.0`) must be trimmed and a blank or unset value must
  disable IP enrichment, logging at info "IP2PROXY_DB_PATH unset; IP enrichment disabled". A path whose database cannot
  be loaded must log at warn "Failed to load IP2Proxy DB; IP enrichment disabled" with the path and cause, and boot must
  continue.
- **SPEC-6.101**: `TRUSTED_PROXY_CIDR` (application, since `v0.7.0`) must be read once per process as a comma-separated
  CIDR list that defaults to the built-in private ranges (SPEC-4.13).
- **SPEC-6.102**: `OUTBOUND_PRIVATE_ALLOWLIST` (application, since `v0.14.0`) must be read once per process and an unset
  or blank value must exempt nothing (SPEC-4.11). A non-empty allow-list must log at info "OUTBOUND_PRIVATE_ALLOWLIST
  exempts private outbound targets" with the number of hosts and networks.
- **SPEC-6.103**: `STRIPE_API_BASE` (application, since `v0.10.0`) and `PAYPAL_API_BASE` (application, since `v0.14.0`)
  must override the payment API base URL when non-blank (SPEC-13.714, SPEC-13.734).

## 7. Service desk

Requirements for the service desk modules: `src/modules/tickets`, `ticket_templates`, `sla`, `workflows`, `forms`, `email_intake`, `calendar`, `projects`, `approvals`, `notifications`. Each `SPEC-7.<n>` below is cited at its implementing or enforcing site with a `// SPEC-7.<n>` comment in the file's own comment syntax.

### 7.1 Tickets

- **SPEC-7.1**: Ticket_number is formatted "T{:06}" from the tenant's next sequence value.
- **SPEC-7.2**: A new ticket always starts in the tenant's is_default status (the create request carries no status_id);
  an omitted priority_id or queue_id resolves to that tenant's is_default row and a supplied one is used as given. A
  tenant with no default status, priority or queue answers a 500 configuration error naming the missing default.
- **SPEC-7.3**: Create validates company_id, type_id, category_id, contact_id, site_id, assigned_to_id, team_id,
  contract_id, sla_id and asset_id against the caller's own tenant in one query; the first missing id, in that order,
  answers 400 "Referenced {table} not found in this tenant". priority_id, queue_id, source_kb_article_id and
  procedure_kb_article_id are not covered by this check.
- **SPEC-7.4**: A parent_ticket_id on create must name a ticket of the same tenant and the same company that has no
  parent itself. A missing, cross-company or already-nested parent answers 422 on field parent_ticket_id ("must be a
  ticket of this organization", "must be a ticket of the same company", "already has a parent; tickets nest one level
