- **SPEC-7.401**: Approve_time_off rejects a status other than exactly "approved" or "rejected" with 400 "Status must be approved | rejected; got `<status>`."; approving/rejecting time off requires RequireManager, stamps approved_by_id with the caller for either decision, and a missing id answers 404 "Time off request".
- **SPEC-7.402**: Only status = 'approved' time off rows block dispatch; pending and rejected requests never block.
- **SPEC-7.403**: On_call_now considers only schedules with is_active = true, resolving exactly one OnCallNowResponse per schedule.
- **SPEC-7.404**: Weekly picks user_ids[ISO_week(now) % len], daily picks user_ids[day_of_year(now) % len], any other rotation_type picks user_ids[0], and an empty or missing user_ids resolves to null; the chosen entry must be a UUID string, and any other value also resolves to null with no log line.
- **SPEC-7.405**: Create_on_call requires RequireManager in addition to RequireCalendar; also, delete_on_call requires RequireManager in addition to RequireCalendar; also, update_on_call requires RequireManager in addition to RequireCalendar.
- **SPEC-7.406**: Kind must be one of the values accepted by validate_scheduling_template_kind ("dispatch" | "calendar").
- **SPEC-7.407**: Duration_minutes must be >= 1; travel_before_minutes / travel_after_minutes must be >= 0.
- **SPEC-7.408**: Create_template rejects a default_ticket_id that does not belong to this tenant; also, update_template rejects a default_ticket_id that does not belong to this tenant.
- **SPEC-7.409**: A field omitted from the PUT body is left unchanged (COALESCE against the stored row), never nulled.

### 7.8 Projects, phases and tasks

- **SPEC-7.410**: GET /projects runs a data query and a count query inside one tenant transaction, and both scope to
  tenant_id = $1.
- **SPEC-7.411**: GET /projects must answer 401 for a staff caller with no authenticated user. Unlike the write routes, it
  is not behind the projects module gate.
- **SPEC-7.412**: A contact caller of GET /projects must hold projects:read, else 403.
- **SPEC-7.413**: For a contact caller of GET /projects, the company_id filter is overwritten with the session's
  company_id, whatever the query string carried.
- **SPEC-7.414**: A contact caller of GET /projects and GET /projects/{id} gets ContactProjectResponse, never the staff
  ProjectResponse.
- **SPEC-7.415**: A project with a NULL company_id (a house project) never appears in a contact caller's list, because
  the stamped company_id filter cannot match NULL.
- **SPEC-7.416**: GET /projects validates the filter before querying: status longer than 100 characters or q longer than
  200 characters is a 422.
- **SPEC-7.417**: GET /projects/{id} must answer 401 for a staff caller with no authenticated user, and is not behind the
  projects module gate.
- **SPEC-7.418**: A contact caller of GET /projects/{id} must hold projects:read, else 403.
- **SPEC-7.419**: A contact caller asking for a project whose company_id is not the session's company (including a NULL
  company_id) gets 404 "Project not found", same as a missing project, so a probe cannot tell the two apart.
- **SPEC-7.420**: POST/PUT/DELETE projects and every phase, task-status, project-type, task and task-dependency route
  require RequireProjects (an authenticated staff user whose tenant has the projects module enabled), so a contact caller
  gets 401 and a tenant with the module disabled gets 404 "Projects module not found".
- **SPEC-7.421**: DELETE /projects/{id} additionally requires the admin role.
- **SPEC-7.422**: Create, update and delete of task-statuses require the admin role in addition to RequireProjects; GET
  /task-statuses needs only RequireProjects.
- **SPEC-7.423**: Create, update and delete of project-types require the admin role; GET /project-types needs only
  RequireProjects.
- **SPEC-7.424**: GET /projects/summary requires RequireProjects, so unlike GET /projects a contact caller gets 401.
- **SPEC-7.425**: The phase routes and the task-dependency routes are mounted but have no SPA caller (parity record
  2026-09-22 in the routes module header); every other projects route is consumed.
- **SPEC-7.426**: Project name must be 1 to 80 characters (create, and update when supplied), else 422.
- **SPEC-7.427**: Project_type defaults to "client" when omitted.
- **SPEC-7.428**: Status defaults to "planning" when omitted.
- **SPEC-7.429**: Billing_method defaults to "time_and_materials" when omitted.
- **SPEC-7.430**: Is_billable defaults to true when omitted.
- **SPEC-7.431**: budget_hours and budget_amount on create and update accept a JSON number (parsed from its exact text,
  not through f64), a numeric string, an empty or blank string (read as null), or null; any other JSON type or an
  unparsable string is rejected at deserialization.
- **SPEC-7.432**: budget_hours, if present, must be non-negative, at most 2 decimal places, and under the DECIMAL(10, 2)
  column magnitude, else 422 (create and update).
- **SPEC-7.433**: budget_amount, if present, must be non-negative, at most 2 decimal places, and under the DECIMAL(12, 2)
  column magnitude, else 422 (create and update).
- **SPEC-7.434**: default_due_business_days, if present, must be in 0..=365, else 422 (create and update).
- **SPEC-7.435**: On project create, project_type_id is resolved from the project_type string by an exact name match
  against the tenant's project_types rows, and is NULL if none matches. Update never changes project_type or
  project_type_id.
- **SPEC-7.436**: The projects Create audit row is written in the same transaction as the INSERT, before = NULL, after =
  the inserted row.
- **SPEC-7.437**: The create response is the freshly re-read project (GET shape), so derived fields are populated, not
  reconstructed from the request.
- **SPEC-7.438**: company_name is a tenant-scoped correlated subquery on companies; NULL if no company_id or the company
  row is gone.
- **SPEC-7.439**: project_manager_name is a tenant-scoped correlated subquery on users, NULLIF(TRIM(first || ' ' ||
  last), ''), so a blank name or a missing user is NULL.
- **SPEC-7.440**: actual_hours sums time_entries.duration_minutes / 60.0 for the project over every entry whose
  approval_status is not 'rejected', and is 0 with none.
- **SPEC-7.441**: actual_amount sums time_entries.total_amount over the same non-rejected entry set, and is 0 with none.
- **SPEC-7.442**: GET /projects/{id} for a missing or foreign-tenant id answers 404 "Project not found".
- **SPEC-7.443**: The list builds the data and count WHERE clauses with independently numbered placeholders (data query
  binds tenant, limit, offset first; count query binds tenant only), so an added filter never reuses an index between
  the two.
- **SPEC-7.444**: GET /projects sorts by created_at by default; a sort key outside name, start_date, created_at (the
  mokosh_types::sort::PROJECTS list) is a 422 naming the key.
- **SPEC-7.445**: The q filter is name ILIKE '%<q>%' with the raw value (a % or _ in q acts as a wildcard), applied as the
  last optional condition in both queries.
- **SPEC-7.446**: update_project reads the before and after row snapshots (to_jsonb) inside the same transaction as the
  UPDATE, for the audit diff.
- **SPEC-7.447**: PUT /projects/{id} applies every updatable field as COALESCE($n, column), so an omitted or null field
  leaves the stored value unchanged (a nullable column cannot be cleared through this route), and bumps updated_at.
- **SPEC-7.448**: PUT /projects/{id} with zero rows affected (missing or foreign-tenant id) answers 404 "Project not
  found" and writes no audit row.
- **SPEC-7.449**: A project update whose only audited change is a description differing solely in GFM task-list markers
  ([ ] versus [x]) writes no audit row; any other change, including adding or clearing the description, writes an Update
  audit row with before and after.
- **SPEC-7.450**: UpdateProjectRequest validates name (1 to 80 chars when supplied), default_due_business_days
  (0..=365), budget_hours, budget_amount and hourly_rate the same way create does, else 422.
- **SPEC-7.451**: DELETE /projects/{id} deletes only the row matching both tenant_id and id; zero rows affected answers
  404 "Project not found"; no audit row is written.
- **SPEC-7.452**: GET /projects/summary computes counts_by_status and total_budget in one transaction, so both describe
  the same instant.
- **SPEC-7.453**: A stored NULL billing_method reads as "time_and_materials" and a stored NULL is_billable reads as true
  (columns predating a NOT NULL default).
- **SPEC-7.454**: Creating a phase or task under a project answers 404 "Project not found" if the project does not exist
  for the tenant, and 409 "Cannot add items to a cancelled project" if its status is "cancelled" (British spelling,
  matching the migration 007 CHECK).
- **SPEC-7.455**: The cancelled-project check runs inside the caller's tenant-scoped transaction, shared with the
  subsequent phase or task INSERT.
- **SPEC-7.456**: Any project status other than "cancelled" permits attaching a phase or task; there is no other
  status-based gate.
- **SPEC-7.457**: GET /projects/{id}/phases lists only phases scoped to tenant_id and project_id, ordered by sort_order,
  paginated; an unknown project yields an empty page, not a 404.
- **SPEC-7.458**: Phase name must be 1 to 100 characters on create and update, else 422.
- **SPEC-7.459**: Phase status defaults to "not_started" when omitted, and sort_order to 0.
- **SPEC-7.460**: Phase create writes a Create audit row in the same transaction, and the returned phase is built from
  the request, not re-read.
- **SPEC-7.461**: PUT /phases/{phase_id} is a full-field UPDATE (not COALESCE'd) scoped by tenant_id and id; no matching
  row answers 404 "Project phase not found"; no audit row is written on update.
- **SPEC-7.462**: Phase update does not check the project's status, so a phase under a now-cancelled project can still
  be edited.
- **SPEC-7.463**: DELETE /phases/{phase_id} deletes by tenant_id + id; zero rows affected answers 404 "Project phase not
  found"; no audit row is written on delete.
- **SPEC-7.464**: GET /task-statuses lists the tenant's rows ordered by sort_order, name, paginated.
- **SPEC-7.465**: Task-status name must be 1 to 50 characters and color 1 to 7 characters, else 422; is_completed and
  sort_order default to false and 0 when omitted.
- **SPEC-7.466**: Task-status create writes a Create audit row in the same transaction as the INSERT; the response is
  built from the request, not re-read.
- **SPEC-7.467**: PUT /task-statuses/{id} is a full-field UPDATE scoped by tenant_id + id; zero rows affected answers 404
  "Task status not found"; no audit row is written on update.
- **SPEC-7.468**: DELETE /task-statuses/{id} deletes by tenant_id + id; zero rows affected answers 404 "Task status not
  found"; no audit row is written, and there is no FK-violation mapping (contrast with delete_project_type).
- **SPEC-7.469**: GET /project-types lists the tenant's rows ordered by sort_order, name, paginated.
- **SPEC-7.470**: Project-type name must be 1 to 50 characters, else 422; is_active defaults to true, is_default and
  sort_order default to false and 0; is_system is never settable from the wire.
- **SPEC-7.471**: Creating a project type with is_default = true first clears is_default on every other tenant row, in
  the same transaction.
- **SPEC-7.472**: Updating a project type to is_default = true clears is_default on every other tenant row except the one
  being updated, in the same transaction.
- **SPEC-7.473**: Project-type create writes a Create audit row; the new row's is_system is always false (API-created
  types are never system rows).
- **SPEC-7.474**: PUT /project-types/{id} with zero rows matched answers 404 "Project type not found"; no audit row is
  written on update; the response echoes the stored is_system flag.
- **SPEC-7.475**: DELETE /project-types/{id} answers 404 "Project type not found" for a missing row, and 409 "Cannot
  delete a system project type" for a row with is_system = true, without attempting the DELETE.
- **SPEC-7.476**: A foreign-key violation (23503, a project still references this type) on project-type delete answers
  409 "Cannot delete this project type: it is still referenced by a project" instead of a 500.
- **SPEC-7.477**: status_name and status_is_completed on a task are resolved via tenant-scoped correlated subqueries
  against task_statuses, not a join, so a missing status leaves them NULL.
- **SPEC-7.478**: Task title must be 1 to 255 characters on create and update when supplied, else 422.
- **SPEC-7.479**: Task priority defaults to "medium" when omitted on create.
- **SPEC-7.480**: estimated_hours, if present, must pass the shared hours validator (non-negative, at most 2 decimal
  places, under 100,000,000), else 422, on create and update.
- **SPEC-7.481**: Task create rejects an inverted start_date/due_date range with a 422 keyed onto due_date, message "Due
  date must be on or after the start date" (equal dates and either side None are accepted).
- **SPEC-7.482**: Task update applies the identical cross-field date check at the request layer when both dates are
  supplied in the same PUT.
- **SPEC-7.483**: On task create, an omitted due_date defaults to today + N business days, where today is the caller's
  own-timezone date and N is the project's default_due_business_days override (0 disables it) if set, else the
  tenant-wide scheduling default; N = 0 leaves due_date NULL; a supplied due_date is used as-is.
- **SPEC-7.484**: Creating a task uses the same project guard as phase creation, so a task cannot be attached to a missing
  project (404) or a cancelled one (409).
- **SPEC-7.485**: Task create writes the Create audit row in the same transaction as the INSERT, before = NULL.
- **SPEC-7.486**: The task create response is the freshly re-read task, so derived fields (status_name, assigned_to_name,
  actual_hours, logged_hours) are populated, not reconstructed.
- **SPEC-7.487**: assigned_to_name is a tenant-scoped correlated subquery against users (NULLIF(TRIM(first || ' ' ||
  last), '')), NULL when unassigned or the user is gone.
- **SPEC-7.488**: actual_hours and logged_hours are computed identically, summing duration_minutes/60.0 for every time
  entry linked to the task whose approval_status is not 'rejected' (PMS-944: approval state is not a fact about whether
  the work happened), and are 0 with none.
- **SPEC-7.489**: GET /projects/{id}/tasks lists tasks scoped to tenant_id and project_id, ordered by sort_order then
  created_at, paginated; an unknown project yields an empty page.
- **SPEC-7.490**: The task list query and its row mapping are identical to get_task's single-row query.
- **SPEC-7.491**: GET /tasks/{id} for a missing or foreign-tenant task id answers 404 "Task not found".
- **SPEC-7.492**: update_task reads the before and after row snapshots inside the same transaction as the UPDATE, for
  the audit diff.
- **SPEC-7.493**: Before the UPDATE runs, task update validates the effective start/due range, combining each supplied
  field with the stored row's value, and answers 400 "Due date must be on or after the start date" when inverted, so a
  partial PUT cannot invert the range against an unsupplied stored date.
- **SPEC-7.494**: Task update applies every field except completed_at as COALESCE($n, column), so an omitted or null
  field leaves the stored value unchanged.
- **SPEC-7.495**: completed_at is inferred from the supplied status_id's is_completed flag via a CASE, not a second
  read: moving to a completed status stamps it (if not already stamped), moving to a non-completed status clears it,
  and an omitted status_id leaves it untouched.
- **SPEC-7.496**: completed_at only stamps NOW() the first time (COALESCE keeps an existing timestamp), so re-saving an
  already-completed task does not move its completion time.
- **SPEC-7.497**: PUT /tasks/{id} with zero rows affected (missing or foreign-tenant id) answers 404 "Task not found".
- **SPEC-7.498**: Unlike update_project's task-marker-only skip, every task update writes an Update audit row, with no
  description-only exemption.
- **SPEC-7.499**: As with create, the task update response is the freshly re-read task, not reconstructed from the
  request.
- **SPEC-7.500**: DELETE /tasks/{id} deletes by tenant_id + id; zero rows affected answers 404 "Task not found"; no audit
  row is written on delete.
- **SPEC-7.501**: A stored NULL task priority reads as "medium" and a NULL sort_order reads as 0.
- **SPEC-7.502**: POST /tasks/{id}/depends-on/{other} with the same id twice answers 400 "Task cannot depend on itself"
  before any transaction opens.
- **SPEC-7.503**: A recursive CTE walks the existing depends_on chain from the candidate dependency back toward the
  task; if task_id is already reachable, adding the edge would close a cycle and is rejected with 409 "Refusing: this
  edge would create a dependency cycle".
- **SPEC-7.504**: The recursive chain and its join are scoped to tenant_id = $1 at every step, so a cross-tenant
  dependency chain can never mask or create a cycle.
- **SPEC-7.505**: The dependency INSERT uses ON CONFLICT DO NOTHING, so re-adding an existing (task_id,
  depends_on_task_id) edge is a silent no-op that still answers success, not a duplicate row or an error.
- **SPEC-7.506**: On the no-op path above, the audit re-read finds no row with the freshly generated dep_id (the
  existing row kept its own id), so `after` is None and a Create audit row is still written with before = after = None.
- **SPEC-7.507**: DELETE /tasks/{id}/depends-on/{other} deletes the edge by tenant_id, task_id and depends_on_task_id;
  this is idempotent (no error, no audit row) whether or not the edge existed.
- **SPEC-7.508**: The cycle check and the self-dependency check are the only guards; there is no existence pre-check for
  task_id or depends_on before the INSERT, so a missing task id surfaces as a database FK error (a 500), not a 404.

### 7.9 Approvals

- **SPEC-7.509**: The approvals surface supports exactly four parent entity kinds (ticket, change_request, quote,
  time_entry); ApprovalTarget::from_str rejects any other string, and the DB CHECK on the target column enforces the same
  set.
- **SPEC-7.510**: When an approval is inserted, the legacy ticket_id column is populated only for a Ticket target (set to
  the entity id); every other target inserts NULL.
- **SPEC-7.511**: entity_reference resolves to tickets.ticket_number or quotes.quote_number only, and is NULL for
  change_request and time_entry targets and for a deleted parent.
- **SPEC-7.512**: entity_label is the parent's title for ticket, change_request and quote, and for a time_entry the string
  "<duration_minutes> min on YYYY-MM-DD"; it is built with `||` so a deleted parent propagates NULL rather than a
  hollow string.
- **SPEC-7.513**: Creating an approval requires exactly one of approver_user_id, approver_role, approver_contact_id; any
  other count answers 400 before any DB write.
- **SPEC-7.514**: POST /tickets/{ticket_id}/approvals answers 404 "Ticket not found" when no tickets row matches (id,
  tenant_id), before any approver validation or insert.
- **SPEC-7.515**: The time-entry, change-request and quote create and list routes each first check the parent exists in
  the caller's tenant, answering 404 with the human noun ("Time entry", "Change request", "Quote", never the raw table
  name) when it is absent.
- **SPEC-7.516**: GET and POST /time-entries/{entity_id}/approvals are reachable only when the tenant has the timesheets
  module enabled; otherwise they answer 404 "Timesheets module not found", before the parent check.
- **SPEC-7.517**: A non-null approver_contact_id must name a contact of this tenant with is_portal_user = TRUE; it is
  checked in the service (not left to the FK) because the FK bypasses RLS.
- **SPEC-7.518**: ApprovalResponse.ticket_id is Some only when target is "ticket"; for every other target it is null and
  (target, entity_id) are the only identifiers to read.
- **SPEC-7.519**: approver_role is capped at 50 chars and notes at 4000 chars, else 422; req.validate() runs in the route
  handler before the service.
- **SPEC-7.520**: The approval INSERT omits status, decided_by_id, decided_by_contact_id and decided_at, so a new row
  always starts as the DB defaults: status 'pending' and those columns NULL.
- **SPEC-7.521**: The ticket existence check and create_for_entity's insert run as separate transactions (the first is
  dropped before the insert), so the two are not atomic with each other.
- **SPEC-7.522**: A contact-filed approval request inserts requested_by_id NULL, requested_by_contact_id = the session
  contact, approver_role fixed to 'admin' and the caller's note; a caller-specified approver is never honoured.
- **SPEC-7.523**: A staff approval request shortcut (note only) answers 404 "Ticket not found" when the ticket is absent
  from the caller's tenant, then creates the approval with approver_role fixed to 'admin'.
- **SPEC-7.524**: An approval create with zero or more than one approver kind set answers 400 "Set exactly one of
  approver_user_id, approver_role or approver_contact_id".
- **SPEC-7.525**: A create naming an approver_contact_id that is not a portal contact of this tenant answers 400
  "approver_contact_id is not a portal contact of this tenant".
- **SPEC-7.526**: POST /approvals/{id}/decision accepts only decision "approve" (status approved) or "reject" (status
  rejected); anything else is a 400 "Decision must be 'approve' or 'reject'".
- **SPEC-7.527**: A staff decision locks the approval row (FOR UPDATE) before authorization, so two concurrent decisions
  cannot both read pending and both pass.
- **SPEC-7.528**: A staff decision on an unknown (tenant, id) answers 404 "Approval not found".
- **SPEC-7.529**: A staff decision on a locked row that is not pending answers 400 "Approval is already {status}".
- **SPEC-7.530**: Staff authorization requires approver_user_id = the caller's id or approver_role = the caller's role
  string, else 403 "Only the assigned approver may decide"; approver_contact_id is never consulted, so a contact-only row
  always yields 403 on the staff route.
- **SPEC-7.531**: The staff decision UPDATE is reconditioned on status = 'pending'; zero rows affected answers 400
  "Approval is already decided".
- **SPEC-7.532**: A staff decision writes status, decision_notes, decided_by_id and decided_at, and never
  decided_by_contact_id.
- **SPEC-7.533**: A staff decision commits, then re-fetches via get() to build the response rather than constructing it
  from the UPDATE's data.
- **SPEC-7.534**: A contact caller of POST /approvals/{id}/decision must hold approvals:decide, loaded from the database
  per request, else 403, before decide_as_contact runs.
- **SPEC-7.535**: A contact decision looks the row up by (tenant_id, id, approver_contact_id = session contact); a row not
  addressed to this contact is indistinguishable from a nonexistent id, so it answers 404 "Approval not found", never
  403.
- **SPEC-7.536**: A contact decision locks the row with FOR UPDATE before checking status, for the same concurrency
  reason as the staff path.
- **SPEC-7.537**: A contact decision answers 400 "Approval is already {status}" when the row is not pending, and
  "Approval is already decided" if the UPDATE affects zero rows.
- **SPEC-7.538**: The contact decision validates the decision value exactly as the staff path: only "approve" or
  "reject", same 400 text.
- **SPEC-7.539**: A contact decision writes status, decision_notes, decided_by_contact_id and decided_at; never
  decided_by_id.
- **SPEC-7.540**: After committing, a contact decision writes a best-effort portal audit row; a failure to write it does
  not fail the decision and only logs a warn naming the tenant, contact and approval ids.
- **SPEC-7.541**: The contact id used by the contact decision and the contact pending queue comes only from the
  authenticated session, never from the request body.
- **SPEC-7.542**: DELETE /approvals/{id} on an unknown (tenant, id) answers 404 "Approval not found".
- **SPEC-7.543**: DELETE /approvals/{id} on a row that is not pending answers 400 "Approval is already {status}".
- **SPEC-7.544**: Cancel answers 403 "Only the requester may cancel" unless requested_by_id equals the caller's id, so a
  contact-filed row (requested_by_id NULL) is never cancellable by any staff caller through this route.
- **SPEC-7.545**: The cancel lookup must decode requested_by_id as Option<Uuid>, not a bare Uuid, since it is NULL on a
  contact-filed row (PMS-1236: decoding it non-optional made such a cancel 500 instead of the intended 403).
- **SPEC-7.546**: Cancel sets status = 'cancelled' and decided_at = NOW() without touching any decided_by column; the row
  is retained, not deleted, and the route answers a bare {"cancelled": true} rather than an ApprovalResponse.
- **SPEC-7.547**: Unlike the decide paths, the cancel UPDATE takes no row lock and is not reconditioned on status =
  'pending', so a concurrent decide or cancel racing between the status read and the UPDATE can overwrite an
  already-decided row's status.
- **SPEC-7.548**: Listing approvals for (target, entity_id) returns every approval in the tenant for that pair ordered by
  requested_at DESC, with no status filter and no pagination.
- **SPEC-7.549**: GET /approvals/pending for a staff caller returns approvals with status pending where approver_user_id
  = the caller or approver_role = the caller's role, ordered by requested_at ASC, across all four targets.
- **SPEC-7.550**: The staff pending queue and count pass the caller's single role as a one-element list; a future
  multi-role identity is not supported by this call site.
- **SPEC-7.551**: GET /approvals/pending/count uses an identical WHERE predicate to the staff pending list, so the count
  and the list cannot disagree for the same inputs.
- **SPEC-7.552**: The contact pending list and count filter strictly on status pending and approver_contact_id = the
  session contact, and both require approvals:decide before reading (else 403).
- **SPEC-7.553**: Every approvals query runs inside begin_with_tenant, which sets the app.current_tenant GUC
  transaction-locally so reads respect the fail-closed RLS policy.
- **SPEC-7.554**: get() answers 404 "Approval not found" when no row matches (tenant_id, id); every mutating call except
  cancel re-fetches through it to build its response.
- **SPEC-7.555**: Each *_name column (requester, approver, decider, user or contact) is NULLIF(TRIM(CONCAT(first, ' ',
  last)), '') so a blank or deleted name resolves to NULL, never an empty string.
- **SPEC-7.556**: An id set on a row whose resolved name column came back NULL is collected per logical field
  (requested_by, approver, decided_by) and logged once per call at INFO with the surface tag and up to 10 ids, never
  names; this never changes the HTTP response.
- **SPEC-7.557**: Every approvals service method takes tenant_id explicitly and filters on it in SQL, so no query here
  relies solely on RLS.
- **SPEC-7.558**: The parent-existence check opens its own tenant-scoped transaction rather than reusing a pool-level
  connection, so it stays correct now that these tables are under fail-closed RLS.

### 7.10 Notifications

- **SPEC-7.559**: Dispatch opens exactly one begin_with_tenant transaction per call, covering rule lookup, template load, preference reads and every insert, and commits it before returning.
- **SPEC-7.560**: Render_event (and enrich_with_branding it calls) never opens a second transaction; both run their reads on the connection the caller's transaction already set the tenant GUC on.
- **SPEC-7.561**: Returns the total notifications rows actually inserted and propagates any database error to the caller rather than swallowing it.
- **SPEC-7.562**: Every caller awaits dispatch inline for the row write only; the queued rows are delivered asynchronously later by DispatcherWorker.
- **SPEC-7.563**: Only active rules for this tenant and event_type are considered; inactive or other-tenant rules are never looked up.
- **SPEC-7.564**: A missing context key never matches, an array expected value matches by containment ("in"), a scalar expected value requires exact equality; absent conditions or {} match unconditionally; also, a rule whose conditions do not match the dispatch context is skipped entirely (see rule_conditions_match for the match semantics).
- **SPEC-7.565**: A rule with no template_id, a missing template, or an inactive template is skipped, logged via warn!, and contributes zero to the fanout count; dispatch never falls back to a synthetic subject/body. The warn names
  tenant, event type, rule id, rule name and template id. A template whose is_active is NULL counts as active.
- **SPEC-7.566**: Template_id is required at both the HTTP validation layer and independently here, so non-HTTP callers of create_rule/update_rule are also gated.
- **SPEC-7.567**: Recipients are the union of rule.recipients.user_ids with an optional context.recipient_user_id, of rule.recipients.emails with an optional context.recipient_email, and of rule.recipients.contacts with an optional context.recipient_contact_id, each deduplicated. A malformed UUID in a rule's user_ids or contacts list, or in a context recipient_user_id or
  recipient_contact_id, and a non-string recipient_email, is skipped without a log line.
- **SPEC-7.568**: An email address that case-insensitively matches one of this rule's user_ids' own email is dropped from the emails list before fan-out, so the same person is never queued twice.
- **SPEC-7.569**: Per (rule, channel) pair, user_ids are filtered by user preferences on every channel. On in_app the
  contact_ids are filtered by contact preferences and the standalone emails list is forced empty; on every other channel
  contact_ids is forced empty and emails passes through unfiltered (standalone addresses have no preferences).
- **SPEC-7.570**: Entity_type/entity_id are taken from context; entity_type must be non-empty and at most 50 chars, entity_id must parse as a UUID, otherwise the column stays NULL with no rejection error.
- **SPEC-7.571**: The template is rendered exactly once per rule, reused unchanged across every channel that rule fans out on.
- **SPEC-7.572**: A template with no subject leaves notifications.subject NULL rather than synthesizing one.
- **SPEC-7.573**: Body_html is rendered with Escape::Html while subject/body_text use Escape::Text; the rendered body_html is persisted on the row at dispatch time and never re-rendered by the worker.
- **SPEC-7.574**: Dispatch (unlike preview) logs one warn per message with a non-empty unresolved list; the placeholders still ship as literal {{key}} text.
- **SPEC-7.575**: One row per user_id via a single INSERT ... SELECT ... FROM UNNEST, status = 'pending', contact_id/recipient left NULL.
- **SPEC-7.576**: One row per address via a single UNNEST statement, status = 'pending', user_id/contact_id left NULL.
- **SPEC-7.577**: One row per contact_id via a single UNNEST statement, status = 'pending'; this branch only fires for in-app rows since contact_ids is empty for any other channel.
- **SPEC-7.578**: The JSON body is exactly {"fanout": <u64>} where the value is the count dispatch returned.
- **SPEC-7.579**: Preview renders through the identical render_event function dispatch uses, issues only read-only SELECTs, and commits its own begin_with_tenant transaction despite writing nothing.
- **SPEC-7.580**: One NotificationPreviewResponse per (rule, channel) pair in the same order dispatch iterates them.
- **SPEC-7.581**: User_id recipients render as their resolved email with a fallback to the bare UUID; contact_ids are left out of the response entirely.
- **SPEC-7.582**: Unresolved names the exact {{key}} placeholders that did not resolve; those keys stay literal in subject/body_text/body_html rather than being fabricated as a sample send-time value.
- **SPEC-7.583**: Preview requires only RequireAuth, not RequireAdmin, because it exposes only the caller's own tenant's templates/rule-recipients, already exposed by the list routes.
- **SPEC-7.584**: Opt-out by default: no row accepts every channel; is_enabled = false rejects every channel; is_enabled = true (or NULL) accepts only a channel in channel_types. The same function governs both user and contact (contact_notification_preferences) acceptance.
- **SPEC-7.585**: User and contact preference rows are each batch-loaded in exactly one query per dispatch call, never once per (recipient, channel) pair in a nested loop.
- **SPEC-7.586**: Upserts on the unique (user_id, event_type) constraint; the caller can only ever write their own preferences.
- **SPEC-7.587**: Is_enabled defaults to true when omitted from the request JSON.
- **SPEC-7.588**: Lists only the authenticated caller's own rows (tenant_id + user_id), ordered by event_type, paginated.
- **SPEC-7.589**: No zero-key constructor exists, so a caller cannot silently make config_encrypted a no-op.
- **SPEC-7.590**: In list_channels a decrypted config that fails to parse as JSON is returned as null without a log
  line, while a decryption failure fails the whole call; NULL is_active/is_default columns are returned as false.
- **SPEC-7.591**: Channel_type is a free-form String here; nothing in create_channel/update_channel enforces the documented set.
- **SPEC-7.592**: Channel/template/rule update and delete are tenant-scoped (WHERE tenant_id = $1 AND id = $2); a missing or other-tenant row is AppError::NotFound (404), never 403.
- **SPEC-7.593**: Create_channel/update_channel/create_template/update_template/create_rule/update_rule each write exactly one audit_write row in the mutation's transaction; the matching delete_* methods write none.
- **SPEC-7.594**: The worker recognizes only "in_app" and "email"; any other channel_type is a permanent, non-retrying failure, even though UpsertNotificationChannelRequest's doc comment lists other names as configurable.
- **SPEC-7.595**: Every dispatch and preview call enriches context with msp_name, msp_logo_url, msp_primary_color, msp_support_email, msp_footer_line, msp_footer_line_html and app_name before rendering.
- **SPEC-7.596**: A caller-supplied msp_name/msp_logo_url/msp_primary_color/msp_support_email always wins over the tenant's stored branding, since ensure_key only inserts when the key is absent.
- **SPEC-7.597**: With_app_name always overwrites any caller-supplied app_name with the deployment's configured product name, so context data can never rename the product in an outbound email.
- **SPEC-7.598**: A non-object context is replaced with {} before branding keys are attached, so those keys are never silently dropped.
- **SPEC-7.599**: Msp_name defaults to the literal "Mokosh Platform" when the tenant's name is empty or the tenant row is not found.
- **SPEC-7.600**: The tenant-derived msp_logo_url is an http(s) URL passed through unchanged, a relative stored path
  prefixed with the deployment's public API base (trailing slash trimmed), or the empty string when the logo is blank
  or no public base is configured; it is never a bare relative path.
- **SPEC-7.601**: Msp_primary_color is always a non-empty color value, defaulting to "#111827" (DEFAULT_PRIMARY_COLOR) when blank or absent.
- **SPEC-7.602**: msp_footer_line is "Sent on behalf of {name}." when the trimmed support email is empty, otherwise
  "Sent on behalf of {name}. Questions? Reply to {email}."; msp_footer_line_html is the same sentence with name and email
  HTML-escaped and the email wrapped as a mailto: link. The name is the caller-supplied msp_name when present.
- **SPEC-7.603**: Flat, non-recursive, non-conditional {{key}} substitution against the top-level fields of context only; no dotted-path or nested-object lookup.
- **SPEC-7.604**: A string value is emitted verbatim; any other JSON value type is emitted via its Display/to_string representation.
- **SPEC-7.605**: A {{key}} absent from context keeps its original internal whitespace in the output while the trimmed key is appended once (deduplicated) to the unresolved list.
- **SPEC-7.606**: An unterminated {{ with no matching }} emits the literal {{ plus the remaining input verbatim and returns immediately, adding nothing to unresolved.
- **SPEC-7.607**: Under Escape::Html every value is HTML-escaped unless its key is in MARKUP_KEYS (raw markup built in Rust); under Escape::Text nothing is ever escaped.
- **SPEC-7.608**: Exactly one tracing::trace! event at RENDER_TRACE_TARGET per render pass (subject/body_text/body_html are three separate passes, one per rule, not one per channel).
- **SPEC-7.609**: Only channel_type = 'in_app' rows, scoped to tenant_id plus either user_id or contact_id, never both in one query.
- **SPEC-7.610**: The staff arm requires CallerContext::Staff plus auth.user to be Some (staff_user), else AppError::Unauthorized.
- **SPEC-7.611**: The contact arm additionally requires a DB-loaded require_capability(caps::NOTIFICATIONS_READ) check, separate from session resolution.
- **SPEC-7.612**: Zero rows affected returns AppError::NotFound("Notification") (404); a row owned by a different user/contact/tenant is never a 403/401.
- **SPEC-7.613**: Ordered created_at DESC and paginated via the standard envelope; also, reject_unsupported_sort() runs at the route layer before the service query.
- **SPEC-7.614**: Status defaults to the literal "pending" if the DB column is unexpectedly NULL, rather than erroring.
- **SPEC-7.615**: 25 rows are drained per scheduled run() tick; the worker carries no per-tick parameter beyond this constant.
- **SPEC-7.616**: One SQL statement selects due rows (pending and ready, or sending whose 600s claim has expired), oldest first, FOR UPDATE SKIP LOCKED, and in the same statement sets status='sending', bumps attempt_count and stamps next_attempt_at = NOW() + CLAIM_TIMEOUT_SECS, recovering from a worker crash mid-tick with no extra schema.
- **SPEC-7.617**: BACKOFF_SECS = [60, 300, 1800, 7200, 21600] indexed by attempt_count - 1 (clamped to 0); once exhausted the row is marked failed with next_attempt_at = NULL.
- **SPEC-7.618**: A permanent delivery failure always sets status='failed'/next_attempt_at=NULL with no retry on first occurrence; this in_app case (no user_id and no contact_id) is one of several such cases (see also the email cases below and the unregistered-transport case); also, neither user_id nor recipient is a permanent failure; also, no resolvable address and no fallback recipient is a permanent failure; also, the worker recognizes only "in_app" and "email"; any other channel_type is a permanent, non-retrying failure, even though UpsertNotificationChannelRequest's doc comment lists other names as configurable.
- **SPEC-7.619**: A failed address lookup itself is a transient failure (the read broke, not that the notification is unsendable), so it backs off and retries rather than failing immediately.
- **SPEC-7.620**: An SMTP send failure via Mailer::send_multipart is always Transient ("smtp: {e}"), so it always gets the backoff ladder rather than an immediate permanent fail.
- **SPEC-7.621**: No database transaction is held open across any transport call; resolve_addresses resolves every address for the batch before any deliver call in the tick.
- **SPEC-7.622**: Only rows where channel == "email" and user_id is Some are looked up here; standalone-recipient rows and non-email channels are never included.
- **SPEC-7.623**: Filters to status = 'active', so an offboarded user's row is excluded and resolves to a permanent "user {uid} has no email" failure.
- **SPEC-7.624**: Committed rather than dropped, to avoid leaving the connection idle in transaction while the pool is needed for the sends this phase exists to free up.
- **SPEC-7.625**: Writes every tick's outcomes in one transaction using at most two statements regardless of batch size, each skipped entirely if its input list is empty.
- **SPEC-7.626**: Run_tick is public so the integration test suite can drive the worker deterministically; production scheduling goes through Job::run() (job name notifications_dispatcher), which calls
  run_tick(TICK_BATCH_SIZE), propagates its error, and emits a debug-level stats event only when stats.examined > 0.
- **SPEC-7.627**: On successful send, logs tracing::info! with id, channel and latency_ms (now minus created_at), making enqueue-to-sent latency observable.
- **SPEC-7.628**: Every channel/template/rule create, update and delete route and POST /notifications/dispatch require
  RequireAuth + RequireAdmin; GET /notification-channels also requires RequireAdmin; the template and rule lists, both
  /me/notification-preferences routes and POST /notifications/preview need only RequireAuth; GET /notifications and
  POST /notifications/{id}/read use RequireCallerContext (staff or contact).
- **SPEC-7.629**: DispatchNotificationRequest derives Validate but declares no field-level #[validate(...)] attributes, so req.validate()? at both the dispatch and preview routes is a structural no-op.
- **SPEC-7.630**: Documents that every route in this file is admin-surface API with no SPA caller as of the 2026-09-22 parity record, and lists the exempted paths below.

### 7.11 Additional service desk behavior

- **SPEC-7.1000**: Channel create/update validate only name (1 to 100 chars) and encrypt config with AES-256-GCM under
  the deployment key; is_active and is_default default to false when omitted. Template create/update validate name
  (1 to 100) and body_text (non-empty), and is_active defaults to true. Rule create/update validate name (1 to 100) and
  template_id; conditions defaults to null and is_active to true. event_type, channel_type, channels and recipients are
  not validated.
- **SPEC-7.1001**: Channel, template and rule lists are tenant-scoped and paginated, ordered by (channel_type, name),
  (event_type, channel_type, name) and (event_type, name) respectively, and each rejects an unsupported sort parameter.
- **SPEC-7.1002**: A rule whose conditions value is not a JSON object (null, array, string) matches every context; an
  object requires every key to match.
- **SPEC-7.1003**: Dispatch does not check that rule or context user_ids exist or are active; a row is queued for each,
  and an inactive or missing user fails permanently at send time on the email channel.
- **SPEC-7.1004**: The preview and the duplicate-email check in render_event resolve user addresses without a
  status = 'active' filter, so a deactivated user's address appears in a preview and suppresses a matching standalone
  email, although the worker would not send to it.
- **SPEC-7.1005**: msp_footer_line and msp_footer_line_html are built from the tenant's stored support email even when
  the caller supplies its own msp_support_email in the context.
- **SPEC-7.1006**: Mark-read sets read_at to NOW() on every call (a repeat call moves the timestamp), matches the row by
  tenant and owner without checking channel_type, and returns an empty 200 body; the inbox lists every status of an
  in_app row, including pending, with entity_type and entity_id for deep links.
- **SPEC-7.1007**: Preference upsert and list store event_type and channel_types as given, unvalidated; a user's
  preference list is not shared with contacts, whose preferences live in contact_notification_preferences.
- **SPEC-7.1008**: The worker claims and settles across all tenants on the migrator (BYPASSRLS) pool; only the address
  lookup runs under a tenant-scoped transaction.
- **SPEC-7.1009**: On delivery the worker sends an email row to the resolved user address when user_id is set, else to
  the row's recipient; the subject is empty when the row has none, and a non-null body_html makes the message
  multipart/alternative. An in_app row is delivered by flipping its status to sent.
- **SPEC-7.1010**: Settlement of a sent row sets status = 'sent', sent_at = NOW(), and clears next_attempt_at and
  error_message; a failed or retried row keeps the last error text in error_message.
- **SPEC-7.1011**: Worker log levels: a permanent failure and a failure after the final retry log at warn, a transient
  failure with a retry scheduled logs at info with attempt and retry_in_secs, and a failed per-tenant address lookup logs
  at error with the tenant id; each line names the notification id and channel.
- **SPEC-7.1012**: If the settle transaction fails after sends, the tick returns the error and the delivered rows stay in
  sending until their 600 s claim expires, after which they are claimed and sent again.
- **SPEC-7.1013**: Dispatch with no matching rule queues nothing and POST /notifications/dispatch answers 200 with
  {"fanout": 0}; a failure in any rule's reads or inserts rolls back the whole dispatch transaction.
- **SPEC-7.1014**: PATCH /forms/{id} for a definition that does not exist in the caller's tenant fails with 404 "Form
  definition" before any field-set or rule validation runs, because the service reads the existing definition first.
- **SPEC-7.1015**: Creating a definition checks the field set, then the rules, then slug uniqueness, and only then
  inserts the definition and its fields in one tenant transaction. Create and update both answer 200 with the
  definition re-read from the database, including the resolved kb_article_title.
- **SPEC-7.1016**: A definition's fields are inserted in request order carrying their own sort_order (default 0) and
  are always read back ordered by sort_order ASC, then name ASC.
- **SPEC-7.1017**: GET /forms/{id}/submissions does not check that the definition exists: an unknown id answers 200
  with an empty list. Each row carries id, form_definition_id, payload, submitted_by_contact_id, ticket_id and
  created_at.
- **SPEC-7.1018**: A public submission that fails validation answers 422 with every field error before anything is
  written: no submission row is stored and the link keeps all its uses.
- **SPEC-7.1019**: The stored submission payload is the normalised answer map (trimmed strings, absent answers
  omitted) with submitted_by_contact_id set to the link's contact (NULL for a link with no contact). After the ticket
  is created the submission row is stamped with ticket_id and request_token_id.
- **SPEC-7.1020**: The public form view frames its contact_info as "<organisation name> at <info>" when the definition
  sets contact_info, and falls back to the organisation's own contact phrase otherwise, so both branches name who is
  asking.
- **SPEC-7.1021**: A ticket created from a link submission has source Portal, empty custom_fields, the contact and
  company of the link, and is created under a system audit context.
- **SPEC-7.1022**: The parent container ticket of a multi-person link is titled "<form name>: <N> people", has source
  Portal and the definition's procedure article, and has its sla_id, sla_due_date, first_response_due and
  resolution_due cleared after creation. It is created in its own transaction before the token row is inserted, so a
  later failure leaves the parent behind; a forms service with no ticket service fails the issue with an internal
  error.
- **SPEC-7.1023**: Issuing a link for an unknown form_definition_id fails with 404 "Form definition". The request-link
  email uses the template key `forms.request_link`, carries the expiry as a %Y-%m-%d date, names the issuing user
  (falling back to the organisation name when the user row is missing) and the client company, and carries a
  report-abuse line only when an abuse contact address is configured.
- **SPEC-7.1024**: The public request-form surface, when over its per-IP quota, answers the shared 429 with a
  Retry-After header and retry_after_seconds of at least 1, and logs a warning. The client IP is taken through the
  trusted-proxy rules.
- **SPEC-7.1025**: Each row of GET /form-request-links carries id, form_definition_id, form_name, company_id,
  company_name, contact_id, recipient_email, expires_at, used_at, submission_id (the first submission only), people,
  submissions_remaining, parent_ticket_id and parent_ticket_number (NULL for a single-person link).
- **SPEC-7.1026**: A form draft is stored as an opaque JSON payload of any shape, and the list response lifts
  `payload.name` into a nullable `name`. The upsert answers 200 with the stored row, a user holds at most one draft
  per definition and one "new form" draft, and delete answers 204.
- **SPEC-7.1027**: FormsService::list_portal_forms and get_portal_form (SPEC-7.305 to 7.308) are not called by any
  route: no portal form endpoint is mounted, so they are not reachable over HTTP.
- **SPEC-7.1028**: The SLA routes are GET/POST /sla/policies, GET/PUT/DELETE /sla/policies/{id}, GET/POST
  /sla/policies/{id}/targets, DELETE /sla/targets/{id}, GET/POST /sla/business-hours, PUT/DELETE
  /sla/business-hours/{id}, GET/POST /sla/holiday-calendars, PUT/DELETE /sla/holiday-calendars/{id} and POST
  /sla/tickets/{id}/evaluate; every GET needs only authentication, every other route also needs an admin (RequireAdmin).
- **SPEC-7.1029**: GET /sla/policies/{id} returns 404 "SLA policy" when the id does not exist in the caller's tenant; it
  needs authentication only.
- **SPEC-7.1030**: Policy create, business-hours create and holiday-calendar create each write an audit record; policy
  update, target upsert, target delete, business-hours update and every delete write none.
- **SPEC-7.1031**: Create and update return the request values echoed back (with the new or given id), not a re-read of
  the stored row; list and get map a NULL is_default to false, and a stored NULL target operational_hours reads back as
  "business_hours".
- **SPEC-7.1032**: Upserting a target for a policy id that is not in the caller's tenant returns 404 "SLA policy";
  deleting an unknown target returns 404 "SLA target"; business-hours update and delete 404 with "Business hours" and
  holiday-calendar update and delete 404 with "Holiday calendar".
- **SPEC-7.1033**: GET /sla/policies/{id}/targets for an unknown or foreign policy id returns an empty page, not 404,
  and the page has no ORDER BY so row order is unspecified.
- **SPEC-7.1034**: Target operational_hours is not validated by the request DTO; the only enforcement is the database
  CHECK allowing "business_hours" or "24x7", so any other string is rejected by the database rather than by a 422 field
  error.
- **SPEC-7.1035**: Business-hours timezone is not validated at write time; a string that is not an IANA zone is stored
  as given and the clock later treats it as UTC without any log.
- **SPEC-7.1036**: Policy list, target list, business-hours list and holiday-calendar list all reject an unsupported
  sort parameter before querying and page with the shared limit and offset; the total counts every row in scope.
- **SPEC-7.1037**: The business_hours.holidays UUID[] column that links a schedule to holiday calendars is read by the
  evaluator but no request DTO or service method writes it, so the link can only be set outside the API.
- **SPEC-7.1038**: The evaluator treats the ticket's created_at as the start of both clocks, so re-evaluating an
  existing ticket recomputes due times from creation, not from the moment of re-evaluation.
- **SPEC-7.1039**: The evaluator writes first_response_due and resolution_due and sets sla_due_date to the same value as
  resolution_due, and bumps updated_at; when a target's hours are NULL the matching due column is overwritten with NULL.
- **SPEC-7.1040**: The evaluator's read transaction is dropped without commit before the schedule is loaded; the
  schedule and holiday reads run in their own tenant-scoped transaction, also never committed because they only read.
- **SPEC-7.1041**: After a ticket create commits and again after a ticket update commits, the ticket service calls the
  evaluator; a failure is logged at warn with the ticket id and cause and never fails the request, and with no SLA
  service wired the call does nothing.
- **SPEC-7.1042**: The sweep's cross-tenant scan inner-joins the ticket's status and treats a NULL is_closed as open; it
  reads each ticket's id, tenant, assignee, created_at, both due times and first_response_at.
- **SPEC-7.1043**: The sweep writes ledger kinds first_response_breached, first_response_at_risk, resolution_breached
  and resolution_at_risk, and dispatches the notification event sla.breached for a *_breached kind and sla.at_risk for
  an *_at_risk kind.
- **SPEC-7.1044**: A ledger claim error or a scan error is returned from the tick with `?`, ending that tick before the
  remaining tickets are processed; the scheduler job named sla_sweep reports it, and the next tick retries all tickets.
- **SPEC-7.1045**: The at-risk lead is computed by mokosh_types::tickets::sla_at_risk_lead, the same function the SLA
  status badge uses, so the badge and the alert cross the at-risk threshold at the same instant.
- **SPEC-7.1046**: The sweep is also dedupe-safe across a dispatch that fans out to zero recipients: a dispatch
  returning Ok(0) keeps the ledger row, logs the success line with fanout 0, and the milestone is never retried.
- **SPEC-7.1047**: Workflow-rule creation checks DTO validation first (field errors), then the trigger allow-list (400
  with message `Unsupported trigger_event='<value>'. Recognised: ticket.created, ticket.status_changed,
  ticket.priority_changed`), then inserts and returns the re-read rule as 200 JSON.
- **SPEC-7.1048**: The workflow-rule conditions and actions JSON are not validated on write: a non-object value, an
  unknown condition key or an unknown action key is stored as given, and at run time an unknown condition key makes the
  rule never match while an unknown action key is ignored without a trace.
- **SPEC-7.1049**: Updating a workflow rule cannot clear a field: description, conditions, actions, priority and
  is_active use COALESCE, so passing null or omitting the field keeps the stored value.
- **SPEC-7.1050**: Workflow run rows are written with entity_type 'tickets' and the ticket id as entity_id, in the
  ticket's own transaction, so they commit or roll back with the ticket change; GET /api/v1/tickets/{id}/workflow-runs
  returns them with rule_name from a LEFT JOIN (NULL when the rule is gone).
- **SPEC-7.1051**: Workflow-rule listing is unpaginated and returns a bare JSON array; created_by_name is the trimmed
  first and last name of the creator and is NULL when the user is missing or has no name.
- **SPEC-7.1052**: A cascaded status_changed or priority_changed context carries the other dimensions from the
  triggering context, not from values a rule's earlier action in the same pass just wrote, so a rule that sets both
  priority and status passes the original priority to the status cascade and the original status to the priority
  cascade.
- **SPEC-7.1053**: The workflows/rule_max_depth tenant setting is read as an unsigned integer; a stored value of any
  other JSON type is treated as absent and the default of 3 applies without a log.
- **SPEC-7.1054**: hourly_rate on project create and update, if present, must be non-negative, at most 2 decimal places,
  and under 100,000,000, else 422.
- **SPEC-7.1055**: PUT /projects/{id} cannot change company_id, contract_id, project_type, project_number or the derived
  project_type_id: UpdateProjectRequest carries none of them.
- **SPEC-7.1056**: Project status, billing_method, phase status and task priority are not validated against an allowed
  set in the application; a value outside the migration 007 CHECK sets is rejected by the database and surfaces as a
  500, not a 422.
- **SPEC-7.1057**: GET /projects/summary answers {counts_by_status, total_budget}: counts_by_status holds one entry per
  status actually present (an absent status means zero projects), and total_budget is the string sum of budget_amount
  across the tenant's projects, NULL budgets excluded, "0" when there are none.
- **SPEC-7.1058**: ContactProjectResponse carries only id, company_id, project_number, name, description, status,
  start_date, target_end_date, actual_end_date and budget_hours, each key always present (null when unset); the rate,
  budget_amount, actuals, billing fields, manager and type are never sent to a contact.
- **SPEC-7.1059**: The phase, task, task-status and project-type lists reject any sort query parameter with a 422
  ("this endpoint does not support sorting") and a per_page above the cap with a 422, before querying.
- **SPEC-7.1060**: A task update that is inverted only against a stored date answers 400, while a create or a
  both-dates update that is inverted in the request alone answers 422 keyed onto due_date.
- **SPEC-7.1061**: PUT /phases/{phase_id} builds its response from the request body plus the project_id returned by the
  UPDATE, and commits before answering 404 for an unknown phase.
- **SPEC-7.1062**: A project-type create or update that fails (including a 404 on update) rolls back its is_default
  clearing of the other rows, so the tenant never loses its default type to a failed request.
- **SPEC-7.1063**: Deleting a task status that a task still references is not mapped: the FK violation surfaces as a
  500, unlike project-type delete which answers 409.
- **SPEC-7.1064**: The default task due date uses the caller's own-timezone today (PMS-1027), not the UTC day, and is
  computed before the project guard runs, so a cancelled or missing project still answers 409 or 404.
- **SPEC-7.1065**: POST /approvals/{id}/decision validates the body before either plane runs: decision must be 4 to 16
  characters and decision_notes at most 4000 characters, else 422; a decision of other length (such as "no") is
  therefore a 422, and a 4 to 16 character value other than approve or reject is the 400 of SPEC-7.526.
- **SPEC-7.1066**: DELETE /approvals/{id} (cancel) is staff-only: it requires an authenticated user (else 401) and has no
  contact-plane arm.
- **SPEC-7.1067**: GET /approvals/pending and /approvals/pending/count answer 401 for a staff caller with no
  authenticated user, and 403 for a contact caller lacking approvals:decide.
- **SPEC-7.1068**: A staff decision on a quote approval, inside the same transaction as the approval UPDATE, lets the
  quote's own status follow its staff-addressed approvals (SPEC-13.1393, SPEC-13.1394) and writes an Update audit row
  on the quote with event "quote.approval_decided" when the status moved; contact-addressed rows and contact decisions
  never move it, and a ticket, change request or time entry target is never gated by its approvals.
- **SPEC-7.1069**: GET /approvals/pending/count answers {"count": N} with N the number of pending approvals addressed to
  the caller (by user or role for staff, by contact id for a contact).
- **SPEC-7.1070**: GET /tickets/{ticket_id}/approvals does not check that the ticket exists, so an unknown or
  foreign-tenant ticket id answers 200 with an empty array, unlike the time-entry, change-request and quote list routes.
- **SPEC-7.1071**: A contact decision's portal audit row is recorded as an Update with the event name
  portal.approval_approved or portal.approval_rejected and the session contact as actor.
- **SPEC-7.1072**: The approval parent joins (ticket, change_request, quote, time_entry) are LEFT joins, each gated on
  its own a.target value and on tenant_id = a.tenant_id, so exactly one can match and an approval whose parent was
  deleted still reads with entity_reference and entity_label NULL.
- **SPEC-7.1073**: ApprovalResponse always carries all of target, entity_id, ticket_id, entity_reference, entity_label,
  the requester, approver and decider ids and resolved names (user and contact variants), status, notes,
  decision_notes, requested_at and decided_at, with null for any unset field.
- **SPEC-7.1074**: An email-intake request that fails payload validation (400) or bearer resolution (401) writes no
  email_intake_log row; the log row is inserted only after the tenant is resolved, and a failure to insert it aborts the
  intake with the database error before any dedup, threading or ticket logic runs.
- **SPEC-7.1075**: POST /email-intake, POST /intake-tokens and GET reads answer 200 with JSON; the intake-token create
  response is the token metadata (id, kind, label, last_used_at, created_at, revoked_at) flattened together with the
  plaintext token field, DELETE /intake-tokens/{id} answers {"revoked": true}, and the token list orders unrevoked
  tokens first, then by created_at descending.
- **SPEC-7.1076**: Revoking an intake token sets revoked_at with COALESCE(revoked_at, NOW()), so revoking an
  already-revoked token succeeds without moving its timestamp.
- **SPEC-7.1077**: On a threading hit the sender contact is resolved with the same lookup-or-auto-create logic as the
  create path, so a reply from an unknown sender with a configured default company creates a contact even if the reply
  comment then fails.
- **SPEC-7.1078**: GET /email-intake-log/{id} answers 404 "Email intake log" for an id that does not exist in the
  caller's tenant, and returns raw_headers, raw_body_text, raw_body_html, received_at, ticket_id and error.
- **SPEC-7.1079**: Create_appointment defaults appointment_type to "other", timezone to "UTC" and all_day to false; a
  stored NULL status reads back as "scheduled"; title must be 1-255 chars; appointment_type, status and timezone values
  are not validated by the service.
- **SPEC-7.1080**: Update_appointment changes only title, description, appointment_type, assigned_to_id, start_time,
  end_time, all_day, timezone, status, location and team_id; every field is COALESCEd so an omitted or null field keeps
  its stored value and cannot be cleared, and the ticket, project, task, company, contact, site links, recurrence_rule
  and reminder_minutes cannot be changed.
- **SPEC-7.1081**: GET /appointments and its read-only alias GET /calendar/appointments without a full from+to pair (or
  with appointment_type) return stored rows, recurring masters unexpanded, ordered by start_time, filtered by user_id
  (assigned_to_id), appointment_type, overlap with from/to (end_time >= from, start_time <= to), team_id and my_teams
  (caller's team_members), with a total count.
- **SPEC-7.1082**: In a ranged read, one-off appointments are selected by overlap with [from, to] and recurring masters
  without any time filter, both narrowed by the same user_id, team_id and my_teams filters, then merged and sorted by
  start_time before pagination.
- **SPEC-7.1083**: No calendar API sets appointments.reminder_minutes (neither the create nor the update request carries
  it), so appointment reminders fire only for rows whose column was populated outside these routes.
- **SPEC-7.1084**: A failure of due_reminders or claim_reminder (database error) aborts the reminder tick with that
  error, while a dispatch failure only logs a warning; the dispatch context carries recipient_user_id, appointment_id,
  start (the occurrence start) and reminder_minutes.
- **SPEC-7.1085**: Only the creation of appointments, time-off requests, on-call schedules and scheduling templates and
  the update of scheduling templates write an audit entry; appointment update and delete, time-off approval and delete,
  on-call update and delete, and template delete write none.
- **SPEC-7.1086**: List time-off orders by start_date descending and filters by user_id, status, and overlap (end_date
  >= from, start_date <= to); a new request is pending, a missing id answers 404 "Time off request", and GET and DELETE
  of a time-off request apply no ownership or role check beyond the calendar module gate.
- **SPEC-7.1087**: GET /users/{user_id}/availability is readable for any user by any caller with calendar access,
  ordered by day_of_week then start_time and paginated; each window's is_available defaults to true.
- **SPEC-7.1088**: Create and update of an on-call schedule are full-body upserts (name 1-100 chars, rotation_type
  default "weekly", rotation_config default null, is_active default true), validate team_id against the tenant (400),
  answer 404 "On-call schedule" for a missing id on update or delete, and echo the request values; list orders by name.
- **SPEC-7.1089**: The dispatch board narrows appointments, availability and approved time off to assigned_to_id when
  given but never on-call coverage, compares time off against the UTC date of from and to, returns availability as
  stored week-relative windows rather than projected onto the range, and computes on-call at request time.
- **SPEC-7.1090**: Scheduling templates default appointment_type to "other" and travel minutes to 0, list ordered by
  name optionally filtered by kind (max 20 chars), answer 404 "Scheduling template" for a missing id, and rely on the
  database CHECK for appointment_type, which the service does not validate.
- **SPEC-7.1091**: The ticket number comes from ticket_sequences.last_number plus one, incremented and committed in its
  own transaction before the insert, so a create that later fails leaves a gap in the sequence.
- **SPEC-7.1092**: A create request needs company_id and a title of 1-500 characters (422 otherwise); source defaults to
  portal, is_billable to true and tags to empty; estimated_hours must lie within 0 to 99,999,999.99; email_message_id and
  email_thread_id are at most 255 characters.
- **SPEC-7.1093**: A contact-plane create needs the TICKETS_WRITE capability, forces company_id and contact_id to the
  session's own, stamps source portal and is_billable false, and takes only title, description, priority_id and type_id
  from the body. The ticket is created as the tenant's first active super_admin, admin or manager (oldest first) and
  audited as the system actor; a tenant with none answers a 500 configuration error.
- **SPEC-7.1094**: A contact PATCH on a ticket needs TICKETS_EDIT_OWN and a ticket that this contact opened in its own
  company (404 otherwise). It keeps only title and description, answers 400 "PATCH body must set at least one of title,
  description" when both are absent, and is attributed to the tenant's first active admin or manager and audited as the
  system actor.
- **SPEC-7.1095**: Listing, reading, creating, updating and assigning tickets and adding or editing notes need only an
  authenticated user of the tenant (or a contact holding the matching capability); deleting a ticket needs the manager
  role.
- **SPEC-7.1096**: add_note requires the ticket to exist in the tenant (400 "Referenced tickets not found in this
  tenant" otherwise), inserts the note (note_type defaults to internal) with its optional time_minutes, work_summary,
  parts_used and follow_up, bumps the ticket's updated_at and last_updated_by_id, and writes an audit row, all in one
  transaction.
- **SPEC-7.1097**: A note email is dispatched as the ticket.note_added template with the recipient email, ticket number,
  title, content, organisation name and contact line; without a notifications dispatcher it is sent directly with
  subject "[{ticket_number}] {title}".
- **SPEC-7.1098**: update_note rewrites only content, sets the note's updated_at, touches the ticket's updated_at and
  last_updated_by_id (never first_response_at), and writes an audit row carrying the old and new note in the same
  transaction.
- **SPEC-7.1099**: A contact's note needs TICKETS_COMMENT and a ticket in its own company; a note_type other than public
  answers 403 "Contacts may only post public notes.". The note is stored public with created_by_contact_id set, its
  created_by_id is the tenant's first active admin or manager (a 500 configuration error when none), and it stamps the
  ticket's first_response_at if unset.
- **SPEC-7.1100**: GET /tickets/{id}/notes returns every note type to staff and only public notes to a contact holding
  TICKETS_READ. Each note carries can_edit, computed from the tenant's note-editing policy and the note's state, and
  always false for a contact.
- **SPEC-7.1101**: GET /tickets/{id}/sla answers staff for any ticket of the tenant and a contact holding TICKETS_READ
  only for its own company's tickets; a ticket outside that scope is 404 "Ticket".
- **SPEC-7.1102**: POST /tickets/{id}/approvals/request takes a note of 1-2000 characters; a contact needs
  TICKETS_REQUEST_APPROVAL and a ticket in its own company (404 otherwise), a staff caller creates a staff request, and
  a deployment without an approvals service answers a 500 configuration error.
- **SPEC-7.1103**: The status, priority, queue, type and category lists need an authenticated staff user and page by
  sort_order (categories by sort_order then name); the type list returns only active types. Their create, update and
  delete need the admin role.
- **SPEC-7.1104**: Creating a status, priority, type, queue or category writes an audit row in the same transaction;
  updating or deleting one writes none.
- **SPEC-7.1105**: list_ticket_responses rejects a team_id of another tenant with 400, matches q (at most 200
  characters) case-insensitively against title, ticket number, company name and assignee full name, applies my_teams
  only for a staff caller, and scopes a contact's list to the contact's company whatever company_id was sent.
- **SPEC-7.1106**: is_overdue matches tickets whose sla_due_date is past, with no resolved_at or closed_at and a status
  that is not closed; is_open matches tickets whose status is not closed; is_unassigned matches a NULL assigned_to_id.
- **SPEC-7.1107**: A ticket response joins the names of status, priority, queue, type, category, company, contact,
  assignee, asset, procedure article and creator; a contact, assignee or creator whose name cannot be resolved is logged
  with its id.
- **SPEC-7.1108**: A saved view name is trimmed, 1-100 characters and not blank, and unique per user (409 "A saved view
  with that name already exists." on create and rename). Update changes only the supplied name, filter and sort; the
  list is ordered by name ASC; an absent or foreign view answers 404 "Saved view not found.".
- **SPEC-7.1109**: process_rules loads the tenant's active rules for the trigger ordered by priority ASC, runs every
  rule whose conditions all match, and increments run_count and sets last_run_at for each rule that ran. A database
  error aborts the run and is logged at warn by the create or update caller.
- **SPEC-7.1110**: An add_note action inserts a note of params.note_type (default internal) with params.content,
  attributed to the tenant's first active admin or manager.
- **SPEC-7.1111**: A send_notification action needs params.to, defaults the subject to the app name plus " ticket
  update" and the body to "A ticket you watch has been updated.", and dispatches the ticket.automation.notify template
  through the notifications queue or, without a dispatcher, sends through the mailer directly; a failure is logged at
  warn.
- **SPEC-7.1112**: A webhook action sends to params.url using params.method (default POST, upper-cased; GET and DELETE
  send no body and an unknown method sends POST) and params.payload (default a JSON object naming tenant, ticket, rule
  id and rule name) with a 10-second timeout; a non-2xx response is logged at warn with its status.
- **SPEC-7.1113**: The agent attachment routes list, upload (multipart part named file; 400 "Missing 'file' part in
  multipart body" when absent), download and delete the attachments of a note. Each first requires the note to belong to
  the ticket in the tenant (404); download also requires the attachment to be on that note (404), and delete answers
  204.
- **SPEC-7.1114**: POST /tickets/{id}/attachments takes JSON filename, content_type and data_base64. A contact needs
  TICKETS_ATTACH_FILE and a ticket in its company (404); invalid base64 or zero decoded bytes answer 400; the content
  type defaults to application/octet-stream; the attachment hangs off the ticket (no note) and is attributed to the
  contact or, for staff, the user.
- **SPEC-7.1115**: insert_blob writes the blob to the object store before it inserts the metadata row, and stores the
  byte length as file_size.
- **SPEC-7.1116**: Deleting an attachment removes the row first and the blob second; an absent row answers 404, a blob
  removal failure answers an error after the row is gone, and a ledger forget failure is only logged at warn.
- **SPEC-7.1117**: POST /tickets/{id}/attachments/inline (any authenticated staff user) stores an image with is_inline
  true and no note, and the response carries the public url /api/v1/public/tickets/attachments/{id}; every other
  attachment has a null url.
- **SPEC-7.1118**: Creating a template stamps created_by_id with the calling admin, a response carries created_by_name
  resolved from users (an unresolved name is logged with the id), and delete answers {"deleted": true}.
- **SPEC-7.1119**: A template is only a pre-fill: the server stores and serves it, and creating a ticket from one is a
  plain ticket create through the existing create path.

## 8. Integrations and dependencies

Each external system below is reached only through the seam named in its requirement. The requirements state what the
router wiring guarantees at the boundary; the behavior behind each seam is specified in the sections they point to.
Third-party HTTPS calls use `reqwest` with rustls; the SMTP transport uses the platform TLS library (`lettre` with
`native-tls`), per `Cargo.toml`.

### 8.1 Database and secrets

- **SPEC-8.1**: The Bunyip account-deleted webhook receiver must be handed the privileged migrator pool and not the
  request-serving pool, because it runs before any session exists and resolves its tenant from the `users` row it reads
  (tenancy rules: SPEC-9.1 through SPEC-9.11).
- **SPEC-8.2**: The tenant-secret provider (database or Infisical, section 3.2) must be chosen once at boot and passed
  into `create_api_router`; the router must hand that one provider to every billing, integration and contact-sync
  service it builds and must not select a provider itself (SPEC-3.16 through SPEC-3.25).
- **SPEC-8.3**: The login-location resolver (IP2Location) and the IP enrichment service (IP2Proxy) must each be optional
  handles: `None` disables login-location alerts or the enrichment lookup respectively, and the router must start with
  either or both absent (SPEC-4.5 through SPEC-4.7, SPEC-5.56, SPEC-5.305).

### 8.2 Identity provider

- **SPEC-8.4**: The identity-provider bearer verifier must exist only when the issuer and audience are configured; its
  absence must leave the staff and contact HS256 paths as the only credential paths, and must also omit the staff-tree
  tenant-placement and invitation hooks and the back-channel logout route (token verification: SPEC-5.113 through
  SPEC-5.129).
- **SPEC-8.5**: The identity provider must reach this server only through the `/api/v1/bunyip` tree, whose routes carry
  no session: `POST /webhooks/account-deleted` and `POST /webhooks/mokosh-grant-changed` authenticate with the
  `X-Webhook-Signature` HMAC (SPEC-5.207 through SPEC-5.216), and `POST /oauth2/backchannel-logout` authenticates by the
  logout token signature (SPEC-5.130 through SPEC-5.138).
- **SPEC-8.6**: The identity-provider user-directory client used by grant invitations must be built from configuration
  at router construction; an absent configuration must mean no directory calls, and a partial configuration must log a
  warning and be treated as absent instead of failing the boot (client behavior: SPEC-5.200 through SPEC-5.206).
- **SPEC-8.7**: The identity provider's machine credential must be accepted, as HTTP Basic, only on `GET
  /api/v1/admin/providers/status` and its `.html` form (SPEC-3.76); this server presents its own machine credential,
  also as HTTP Basic, for the host-secret read (SPEC-3.12, SPEC-3.13), the host-configuration read (section 2.7) and the
  mailer relay (the next requirement).
- **SPEC-8.8**: When `MAIL_PROVIDER=bunyip`, every outbound mail must be sent as `POST
  <BUNYIP_MAILER_URL>/v1/mailer/send` with HTTP Basic `BUNYIP_MAILER_CLIENT_ID` and `BUNYIP_MAILER_CLIENT_SECRET`, a
  JSON body of `to`, `subject`, `text` and an optional `html`, and a 10 second timeout; a transport failure must fail
  the send with an external-service error carrying the cause, a non-2xx answer with one naming the status and the
  response body, and a missing one of the three settings must fail the boot with a configuration error naming it
  (provider selection: SPEC-4.68).

### 8.3 Payments and accounting

- **SPEC-8.9**: Stripe and PayPal deliveries must be accepted only at `POST /api/v1/stripe/webhooks/{tenant_id}` and
  `POST /api/v1/paypal/webhooks/{tenant_id}`, outside the session middleware, through one shared handler that differs
  only by provider id; the tenant id in the path selects whose gateway secret verifies the delivery and is not itself a
  credential (SPEC-13.700 through SPEC-13.804).
- **SPEC-8.10**: Xero and QuickBooks deliveries must be accepted only at `POST /api/v1/webhooks/xero` and `POST
  /api/v1/webhooks/quickbooks`, one URL per provider and not per tenant, because the deployment holds one application
  per provider; the tenant is resolved from the organisation id inside the delivery (SPEC-13.1000 through SPEC-13.1092).
- **SPEC-8.11**: The Xero and QuickBooks OAuth redirect must be accepted at `GET
  /api/v1/public/invoice-issuer/{provider}/callback` without a session, identified by its single-use `state` parameter,
  and every outcome must be a redirect to the browser client (SPEC-13.1000 through SPEC-13.1092).
- **SPEC-8.12**: One invoice-issuer dispatcher, holding the Xero and QuickBooks clients (45-second request timeout) and
  the deployment's two applications, must be built per router and shared by the invoice path, the bill path and both
  webhook receivers; a deployment holding neither application must still start, and the dispatcher must refuse at the
  point a tenant tries to use one (SPEC-13.1009, SPEC-13.1010).

### 8.4 RMM, contact directories and mail

- **SPEC-8.13**: RMM agents must reach this server only through `POST /api/v1/rmm/alerts` and `POST /api/v1/rmm/status`,
  which authenticate with the `X-Signature` HMAC of the raw body instead of a session; both paths must be exempt from
  JSON body sanitising (SPEC-15.1536 through SPEC-15.1575, SPEC-15.2101 through SPEC-15.2118).
- **SPEC-8.14**: The Google and Microsoft contact-directory OAuth redirects must be accepted at `GET
  /api/v1/public/contact-sync/google/callback` and `/microsoft/callback` without a session, identified by their
  single-use `state` parameter; the Google client must be a shared handle whose value a Settings write replaces without
  a restart, and the Microsoft 365 client handle may hold none, which the Settings card reports as not available
  (SPEC-15.500 through SPEC-15.691).
- **SPEC-8.15**: The outbound mailer must be one shared swappable handle passed to every service that sends mail and to
  the settings routes, so an administrator's email-settings change takes effect without a restart (providers and failure
  behavior: SPEC-4.64 through SPEC-4.70, SPEC-15.2038 through SPEC-15.2040).

### 8.5 Object storage and attachments

- **SPEC-8.16**: Building the router must fail the boot, by panicking with `ATTACHMENT_MAX_BYTES invalid` or
  `KB_ATTACHMENT_MAX_BYTES invalid`, when the corresponding size setting is present but invalid; the router must not
  substitute the default (storage providers: SPEC-3.42 through SPEC-3.58).

## 9. Data model and migrations
