- **SPEC-10.126** When started as root: `PUID`/`PGID`, if set, must be numeric and non-zero (rejecting non-numeric or `0` with exit 1, "refusing to run the workload as root"); if unset, the resolved uid/gid must be the owner of the first `DATA_DIRS` entry when that owner is non-root, else default to `1001:1001`.
- **SPEC-10.127** The script must remap `$APP_USER` to the resolved uid/gid via `groupmod -o -g ... && usermod -o -u ... -g ...`, log the resolution source (`PUID`/`PGID`/owner-of-dir/default) to stderr, then run every file matching `/etc/entrypoint.d/*.sh` as root with `sh` (skipping if the glob matches nothing; the file need not be executable), aborting with that hook's exit code if any hook fails.
- **SPEC-10.128** For each `DATA_DIRS` entry the script must recursively `chown` (via `find`) only the files and directories under it whose uid or gid differs from the resolved pair, then must `exec gosu "$APP_USER" "$@"` (user form, not `uid:gid`, so supplementary groups resolve from `/etc/group`).

### 10.18 Image tagging (`oci-build/get-tags.nu`)

- **SPEC-10.129** `main` must accept only `release|latest|branch|dry-run` for `--mode`; any other value must error `[get-tags] Unknown mode: '<mode>'. Expected release|latest|branch|dry-run.`.
- **SPEC-10.130** Mode `release` must resolve `{train: "release", version: ref_name}` and error `[get-tags] release train requires a non-empty version...` if `ref_name` is empty. Mode `latest` must resolve `{train: "latest", version: ""}`. Mode `branch` must resolve `{train: "branch", version: ref_name}`. Mode `dry-run` must resolve to `release` when `--simulate-tag` is non-empty, to `branch` when `--ref-name` is non-empty and not `"main"`, else to `latest`.
- **SPEC-10.131** `BRANCH_ALLOW_LIST` must be the single source of truth for which branches may publish; a `branch`-train version not on the list must error `[get-tags] Branch '<name>' is not on the publish allow-list ...`. It is currently empty (no feature branch publishes); `scripts/check-oci-publish-tags.nu` keeps `build-oci-image.yml`'s own branch filter in sync with it.
- **SPEC-10.132** The final `tag` must be the version string for `release`, `branch-tag(version)` (every `/` replaced with `-`) for `branch`, and the literal `latest` for `latest`; `describe` (`git describe --tags --always`) is diagnostic only and never changes the train. With `--json`, the record `{mode, train, tag, describe}` must serialize via `to json --raw`.

### 10.19 Dev stack compose (`compose.dev.yml`)

- **SPEC-10.133** The compose project name must be `dev-mokosh-${USER}` and every `container_name`, named volume and the `private` network name must carry the `dev-mokosh-` prefix plus `-${USER}` suffix (only the shared external `network-traefik-public` is exempt), so two developers on one host never collide; `USER` has no default (`${USER:?USER missing - run via just dev}`).
- **SPEC-10.134** `infisical`, `infisical-postgres`, and `valkey` must start only under compose profile `infisical`; `minio` must start only under profile `s3`; no other service is profile-gated.
- **SPEC-10.135** Every host-published port must bind to `127.0.0.1` only: `postgres`, `mailpit` (SMTP and web UI), `infisical` and `minio` (API and console); `infisical-postgres` and `valkey` only `expose` their ports on the `private` network and publish none; the `server` service must publish no host port at all, reaching ingress solely through the external `network-traefik-public` Traefik network via its `labels`.
- **SPEC-10.136** `postgres`'s `PGDATA` must be pinned to `/var/lib/postgresql/data/pgdata`, a subdirectory of the named volume mount, to avoid both the Postgres-18 default-path change and the entrypoint's refusal to `initdb` into a non-empty directory.
- **SPEC-10.137** The `server` service must build from `Dockerfile` with `context: .`, depend on `postgres` with `condition: service_healthy` and on `mailpit` with `condition: service_started`, and must not declare a `depends_on` for `infisical`, since a hard dependency on a profiled-out service makes compose reject the whole project.
- **SPEC-10.138** `CARGO_BUILD_JOBS` must default to `1` inside the `server` container, serializing rustc to avoid earlyoom SIGTERM around roughly 1.5 GB free; an operator may override it in `.env`.
- **SPEC-10.139** The `server` service's volumes must mount `./src`, `./crates`, `./Cargo.toml`, `./Cargo.lock`, `./build.rs`, `./migrations`, `./tests`, `./e2e:ro`, and `./.config` individually, plus named volumes `server-target:/app/target` and `attachments:/data/attachments`; a new top-level directory this list omits is invisible inside the dev container.
- **SPEC-10.140** `STORAGE_ROOT` must default to `/data/attachments` in the `server` environment, matching the `attachments:/data/attachments` mount point.
- **SPEC-10.141** The `server`'s `extra_hosts` must pin `${USER}-bunyip-api.<dev-domain>` to `${BUNYIP_OP_TRAEFIK_IP:-<traefik-ip>}` so the in-container OIDC discovery fetch reaches the local Traefik with a valid certificate rather than the host's public edge.
- **SPEC-10.142** Traefik routing labels for `server` must use YAML list syntax, not map syntax, since Compose does not interpolate `${USER}` inside map keys, only inside string values.
- **SPEC-10.143** `minio`'s image must be pinned by digest `docker.io/bitnamilegacy/minio@sha256:451fe6858cb770cc9d0e77ba811ce287420f781c7c1b806a386f6896471a349c`, with its data volume mounted at `/bitnami/minio/data`, not `/data`, because the Bitnami non-root image cannot `chown` a freshly created volume mounted at `/data`.

### 10.21 Rust toolchain and workspace (`Cargo.toml`, `rust-toolchain.toml`, `.cargo/config.toml`)

- **SPEC-10.148** The workspace must resolve with `resolver = "2"` and contain exactly five members: the root `mokosh-server` package (`.`) and the four crates `crates/mokosh-types`, `crates/build-metadata`, `crates/mokosh-test-macros`, `crates/mokosh-test`; a member outside this list, or a missing one, breaks `cargo check --workspace` with an unresolved-path error.
- **SPEC-10.149** `rust-toolchain.toml` must pin `channel = "1.98.1"` with `components = ["clippy", "rustfmt"]`; every `cargo`/`rustfmt`/`clippy` invocation in this repo, dev container and CI alike, must use exactly this patch, so formatting and lint output are identical everywhere.
- **SPEC-10.150** A bump of the `rust-builder-glibc` or `rust-builder-musl` image tags (10.112, 10.114) must be accompanied, in the same change, by the matching `channel` bump in `rust-toolchain.toml`; drift between the pin and the image's actual rustc produces the same class of silent formatting/lint divergence the pin exists to prevent.
- **SPEC-10.151** `[workspace.dependencies]` must list only crate entries that at least one member inherits via `{ workspace = true }` (enforced by `check-workspace-deps.nu`, 10.179): `serde 1.0.229` (derive), `serde_json 1.0.154`, `uuid 1.11` (v4, v7, serde), `chrono 0.4.45` (serde), `async-trait 0.1.92`, `secrecy 0.10.3` (serde), `ipnetwork 0.20`, `lettre 0.11.23` (default features off; tokio1-native-tls, builder, smtp-transport, pool).
- **SPEC-10.152** `[profile.release]` must build with `lto = true`, `codegen-units = 1`, `panic = "abort"`, `strip = true`; a release binary must abort rather than unwind on panic, and ship with symbols stripped.
- **SPEC-10.153** `[profile.dev]` must build with `debug = 0` and `codegen-units = 256` (not rustc's default `debug = 2`), to keep rustc's peak RSS under the OOM threshold of memory-constrained dev containers, leaving `overflow-checks` and `debug-assertions` at their profile defaults (on); `[profile.dev.package."*"]` must set `opt-level = 3` for every dependency crate, so only the root crate itself builds unoptimized.
- **SPEC-10.154** `.cargo/config.toml` must set `[net] git-fetch-with-cli = true`, so a `git`-dependency fetch (the private git dependencies, pinned by `rev`) uses the system git CLI and its configured credential helper against the private private dependency repository, instead of libgit2, which can fail to authenticate against a private Forgejo remote.

### 10.22 Test runner configuration (`.config/nextest.toml`)

- **SPEC-10.155** `[profile.ci].default-filter` must read exactly `'not (test(/^suites::s3_storage::/) or test(/^suites::google_client_from_infisical::/))'`, character-for-character the negation of `[profile.unsupported]`'s filter `'(test(/^suites::s3_storage::/) or test(/^suites::google_client_from_infisical::/))'`.
- **SPEC-10.156** `cargo nextest run --profile ci` must still compile `tests/suites/s3_storage.rs` and `tests/suites/google_client_from_infisical.rs` into the one test binary on every pull request (a compile break in either fails the PR job) while never executing their cases; those suites run only via `[profile.unsupported]`, invoked weekly by `integration-unsupported.yml` (10.22-10.27) and locally by `just test-integration-unsupported` (10.92).
- **SPEC-10.157** `[profile.ci]` must run with `test-threads = 8` and `fail-fast = false`.
- **SPEC-10.158** `[profile.ci.slow-timeout]` must mark a case slow after `period = "60s"` and send it SIGTERM after `terminate-after = 3` consecutive periods (180s total), continuing the rest of the run rather than stalling the whole job.
- **SPEC-10.159** The override `[[profile.ci.overrides]]` for `filter = 'test(health_p99_does_not_regress_under_concurrent_argon2_burst)'` must set `threads-required = "num-test-threads"` and `retries = 2`; no other test in `[profile.ci]` is retried.
- **SPEC-10.160** `[profile.unsupported]` must `inherit = "ci"` (same slow-timeout, fail-fast, thread budget) and override only `default-filter`, plus set `failure-output = "immediate-final"` so a failing case in the weekly run prints its output without a local re-run.

### 10.23 Repo hygiene (`.gitignore`, `.gitmodules`)

- **SPEC-10.161** `.gitmodules` must declare submodule `common` at path `common`, url `https://<forge-host>/<org>/common.git`; a fresh clone must run `git submodule update --init` before any `just` recipe resolves, because the unconditional import in `justfile` (SPEC-10.52) fails first; `pre-commit`, `pre-push`, `install-hooks` and `create-release` additionally depend on the submodule's own recipe bodies.
- **SPEC-10.162** `.gitignore` must exclude every `.env*` file except `.env.example` (`.env*` then `!.env.example`), so a generated `.env` with live secrets is never committed while the template always is.
- **SPEC-10.163** `.gitignore` must exclude `/secrets/` (generated OIDC signing keys), `/gen/` (build output), `/assets/styles.css` (Tailwind-generated CSS), `data/` (the dev Postgres bind-mount directory), `.claude/` (agent scratch/config), `For AI/` (local-only AI scratch context), and `/attachments/` (the default local-storage root for a bare `cargo run` or a test).

### 10.24 Secret-scan exemptions (`.noseyparker-ignore.txt`)

- **SPEC-10.164** `.noseyparker-ignore.txt` must list only individual file/directory paths, never a widened parent glob, each with a comment stating why its matches are not real secrets, and the comments must not quote the matched fixture strings themselves, since quoting would re-trigger the scanner on the ignore file itself.
- **SPEC-10.165** A real secret committed under any exempted path must be treated as the same incident class the scanner exists to catch on a clean path; the exemption is scoped to known-safe fixtures, never a blanket allowance for the listed paths.

### 10.25 Environment variable registry file (`.env.example`)

- **SPEC-10.166** `.env.example` must hold a key (a `NAME=value` line or a commented-out `# NAME=` line) with an empty or documented-default value for every environment variable the config registry reads, except those excused in `CODE_NOT_IN_TEMPLATE`, checked by `check-env-example.nu` (10.189-10.193). Operators must not copy it to `.env` by hand; `ensure-env` (10.80) generates `.env` from it once per clone and fills every self-owned secret with a strong random value via `openssl rand`, so no placeholder password ever reaches a running `.env`.
- **SPEC-10.167** `MOKOSH_PG_HOST_PORT` (default `5433`) must be the single place the host-published Postgres port is written; `DATABASE_URL`, `MOKOSH_ADMIN_DATABASE_URL`, and `MOKOSH_APP_DATABASE_URL`'s host forms must interpolate it rather than repeat the literal, so resolving a port collision between two checkouts on one host cannot leave a host-side tool migrating a different checkout's database.
- **SPEC-10.168** `MOKOSH_APP_DATABASE_URL` must be the `mokosh_app` role's URL; if unset the server falls back to `DATABASE_URL` (`mokosh_migrator`, bypassing row-level security), which makes every `tenant_isolation` policy inert for request-serving connections. Outside `development`/`dev`/`test` `ENVIRONMENT` values, the server must refuse to boot if `MOKOSH_APP_DATABASE_URL` is unset.

### 10.26 CI gate scripts: migrations, pool safety, validate parity, mail copy

- **SPEC-10.169** `check-guarded-content-migrations.nu` must check only `migrations/*.sql` files whose numeric filename prefix is strictly greater than `209`; for such a file whose `UPDATE` matches `AND\s+<col>\s*(=|LIKE)\s*'` for any of `subject`, `body_text`, `body_html`, `name`, `description`, the file must also contain the literal `GET DIAGNOSTICS`, or the script exits 1 naming the file and the missing assertion; migrations numbered 209 or below are exempt unconditionally.
- **SPEC-10.170** `check-migration-versions-against-base.nu migrations_dir base_ref` must union migration filenames from `base_ref` (default `origin/main`, via `git ls-tree -r --name-only`) and the current `migrations_dir` on disk, group them by leading numeric prefix, and exit 1 listing every prefix shared by two or more distinct filenames as a post-merge collision.
- **SPEC-10.171** `check-pool-safety.nu` must scan every `src/**/*.rs` file except `src/db/pool.rs` for a non-comment line containing `.pool()` that is not a `migrator_pool` call; for each, it must look back up to 8 lines, and if none contain the substring `SAFETY (PMS-285`, record it as a violation and exit 1.
- **SPEC-10.172** `check-create-update-validate-parity.nu` must pair every `Create*Request`/`Upsert*Request` struct with its `Update*Request`/`Patch*Request` counterpart by stripped struct name; for each same-named field present on both sides, the normalized `#[validate(...)]` attribute text must be identical unless the pair-and-field is listed in the script's `ALLOWED` constant (currently empty); any mismatch, or a stale `ALLOWED` entry whose two sides no longer differ, exits 1.
- **SPEC-10.173** `check-no-duplicate-mail-copy.nu` must fail if any of the 8 seeded template phrases in its `PHRASES` constant (for example `"Welcome to {{app_name}}"`) appears as a substring anywhere under `src/`, and must separately fail unless the literal sentence `"has added an update to ticket"` appears verbatim in both `migrations/148_restore_ticket_note_org_identity.sql` and `src/modules/tickets/service.rs`.

### 10.27 CI gate scripts: rate limiting, route consumers, runner labels

- **SPEC-10.174** `check-rate-limit-helper.nu` must scan every `src/**/*.rs` file and fail if, outside `src/utils/error.rs`, a non-comment line contains `TOO_MANY_REQUESTS` or `AppError::RateLimited`, and must fail (even inside `src/utils/error.rs`) on any line containing the literal `let _ = retry_after`.
- **SPEC-10.175** `check-route-consumers.nu` must scan `src/modules/*/*.rs` for `.route("<path>", ...)` literals (with any `#[cfg(test)]` module stripped first); a route is exempt if its first static path segment appears as `/<segment>` and every later static segment appears delimiter-bounded (a route with no static segment is exempt) in `$MOKOSH_APPS_DIR/src/**/*.rs` (default `../mokosh-apps`), or if its own file carries a `//`-comment containing both `parity record` and a `YYYY-MM-DD` date and a separate comment naming that exact route literal; under CI (`$CI` set) a missing client checkout is a hard failure, else the check is skipped.
- **SPEC-10.176** For every job in every `.forgejo/workflows/*.yml` file, `check-runner-labels.nu` must fail a step that installs a toolchain package (`gcc`, `binutils`, `glibc-devel`, `libopenssl-devel`, `build-essential`) via a package manager at run time instead of requesting the dev image; must fail a job that runs `cargo ` natively without `RUNS_ON_OPENSUSE_BASE_HEAVY` in its `runs-on:`; and must fail any `runs-on:` line with no immediately preceding comment justifying its label.

### 10.28 CI gate scripts: OCI cache and publish-tag parity, workspace dependencies

- **SPEC-10.177** `check-oci-build-cache.nu` must select every `.forgejo/workflows/*.yml` file containing `docker buildx build`; after stripping `#`-comments, each must contain either `--driver docker-container` or a use of `<org>/common/.forgejo/actions/setup-buildx`, plus `crazy-max/ghaction-github-runtime@v3`, `cache_from = "type=gha"`, `cache_to = "type=gha,mode=max,ignore-error=true"`, `--cache-from`, `--cache-to`, and must contain none of `type=inline`, `type=registry`, `:buildcache`; any violation exits 1.
- **SPEC-10.178** `check-oci-publish-tags.nu` must verify `build-oci-image.yml`'s `on.push.branches` equals `["main"]` plus `oci-build/get-tags.nu`'s `BRANCH_ALLOW_LIST`, the `build-and-push` job's `if:` guard starts with `github.ref == 'refs/heads/main' || startsWith(github.ref, 'refs/tags/v')`, `check.yml`'s `on.pull_request.branches` includes `main` and its `on.push.branches` includes every allow-listed branch, and that `get-tags`'s own mode resolution and `branch-tag` (slash-to-hyphen) behave as specified in 10.129-10.132; a branch not on the allow-list must raise, never resolve a tag.
- **SPEC-10.179** `check-workspace-deps.nu` must fail when a `[workspace.dependencies]` entry has no workspace member that inherits it via `workspace = true`, and must fail when a member declares a dependency already in `[workspace.dependencies]` without `workspace = true` (its own pin shadowing the shared one); an unresolvable `workspace.members` manifest path exits 1 immediately.

### 10.29 CI gate scripts: documentation and configuration consistency

- **SPEC-10.180** `check-doc-links.nu` must resolve every Markdown link, image, reference-definition, and HTML `href`/`src` target in every `git ls-files "*.md"` file (skipping anchors, protocol-relative and scheme URLs, fenced code, and HTML comments), root-relative for a leading `/` and else relative to the containing file; any target that does not resolve on disk exits 1 naming `<file>:<line>`.
- **SPEC-10.181** `check-doc-recipes.nu` must check a fixed set of docs (`README.md`, `docs/README.md`, `docs/quickstart.md`, `docs/architecture.md`, `docs/binaries.md`, `docs/configuration.md`, `docs/recipes.md`, `docs/invariants/ci-release.md`, `docs/invariants/config-providers.md`) for every `just <recipe>` invocation and fail if the named recipe is absent from the union of `justfile`'s non-`[private]` recipes and `just --summary`'s resolved (imported) recipes; a missing submodule import failure must direct the operator to `git submodule update --init`.
- **SPEC-10.182** `check-config-doc-paths.nu` must scan `.env.example`, `compose.dev.yml`, and `justfile` for bare `docs/...`-shaped path references and exit 1 listing any that do not resolve on disk.
- **SPEC-10.183** `check-claude-md.nu` must exit 1 when `CLAUDE.md` exceeds `20000` UTF-8 bytes, when any non-fenced line exceeds `400` characters, or when a `](docs/...)` link's target or `#anchor` does not resolve; it must name `CLAUDE.md:<line>` for any violation.
- **SPEC-10.184** `check-build-target-storage.nu` must resolve cargo's target directory in cargo's own precedence (`CARGO_TARGET_DIR`, then `CARGO_BUILD_TARGET_DIR`, then `build.target-dir` in the repo's `.cargo/config.toml`, then in `~/.cargo/config.toml`, then `<repo>/target`), determine its filesystem type via `stat --file-system --format=%T`, and exit 1 when that type is `tmpfs` or `ramfs` unless `MOKOSH_ALLOW_TMPFS_TARGET` is `1`/`true`/`yes`.
- **SPEC-10.185** `config-docs.nu check` must fail when the registry/`variables.toml` catalog has a duplicate variable name, a malformed `since`/`required_since`/`deprecated.release`/`removed.release` value, or a `required_since` without `required: true` at a release not after `since`; when any discovered env-var read in `src/**/*.rs` or `crates/**/*.rs` is absent from the registry, `variables.toml`, and the `NOT_SERVER_CONFIG` exemption list; when `docs/configuration.md`'s `## All variables` table disagrees with the catalog on `Required`/`Added in`, is malformed, or a variable has zero or more than one row; or when the generated `Recently added` block (between its fixed marker comments) is missing, out of order, or disagrees with the computed changelog for the covered release window.
- **SPEC-10.186** `config-docs.nu generate` must rewrite only the text between the `Recently added` marker lines and the `## All variables` table rows, and running it twice in a row must be idempotent (byte-identical the second time).
- **SPEC-10.187** `config-docs.nu since <version>` must print one row per catalog change released strictly after `<version>` (labelled `WON'T START`, `FEATURE OFF: <feature>`, or blank), sorted by release, then breaking-level, then name, or print exactly `No configuration changes after <version>.` when there are none.
- **SPEC-10.188** A registry entry whose `required` flag becomes true in the same release it was added (other than the `v0.1.0` baseline) must have a matching `[[change]]` record naming an `issue` (`^[A-Z]+-\d+$`) and a non-empty `action`, or the catalog build fails; a `[[change]]` with `breaking: "feature-off"` must set a non-empty `feature`, or the catalog build fails.

### 10.30 CI gate scripts: environment-variable parity

- **SPEC-10.189** `check-env-example.nu` must union env-var names read by code (`declare_keys!` entries in `src/config/registry.rs`, plus every `env::var`/`env::var_os`/`require_env`/`required_env`/`parse_tenant_arg_env` call site and const-aliased name across `src/**/*.rs` and `crates/**/*.rs`) into one `CODE` set.
- **SPEC-10.190** Every `CODE` name must have a key in `.env.example` (including a commented-out `# NAME=` line) unless listed in `CODE_NOT_IN_TEMPLATE`, and must appear in `compose.dev.yml`'s `services.server.environment` map unless listed in `CODE_NOT_IN_COMPOSE`; a missing entry exits 1 naming it.
- **SPEC-10.191** Every `.env.example` key must be read by code or interpolated (`${NAME`) in `compose.dev.yml` unless listed in `TEMPLATE_UNREAD`; an unread key exits 1 naming it dead.
- **SPEC-10.192** A stale `CODE_NOT_IN_TEMPLATE`, `CODE_NOT_IN_COMPOSE`, or `TEMPLATE_UNREAD` entry, one whose excused asymmetry no longer holds, must itself exit 1 naming the entry to delete.

### 10.31 Operational and diagnostic scripts

- **SPEC-10.193** `audit-portal-no-credential.nu` must error `DATABASE_URL is required (point it at the target deployment).` when `DATABASE_URL` is unset, otherwise query `contacts` for rows with `is_portal_user = TRUE AND portal_password_hash IS NULL`, print a per-row and per-tenant summary, and print a `WARNING:` line when any row's age exceeds 7 days. This script is a manual survey tool with no `just` wrapper and no CI invocation.
- **SPEC-10.194** `check-ci-stalls.nu days="3"` must read each workflow job's `timeout-minutes` from `.forgejo/workflows/*.yml` (never a value hardcoded in the script), exit 1 if `FORGEJO_TOKEN` is unset, fetch Forgejo actions runs from the last `days` days and compare each run's wall-clock time against its workflow's bound (the smallest `timeout-minutes` among its jobs), and exit 1 naming every run that outlived its bound; a workflow with no `timeout-minutes` on any job is excluded from judgement, never counted as passing.
- **SPEC-10.195** `ci-job-log.nu` must resolve a target run from `--run <id>`, else the 50 most recent runs filtered by `--workflow`, then by commit-SHA prefix when `--sha` is given and by `failure` status otherwise (first match wins), then fetch and print that run's first failed job's log (or the first job overall if none failed) by calling the Forgejo actions API with a token read from `~/.local/share/forgejo-cli/keys.json`; `--list` must print the candidate run table without fetching a log.

### 10.32 E2E: environment resolution and auth state

- **SPEC-10.196** `e2e/lib/env.ts` must load `e2e/.env` via dotenv with `override: false` (a real environment variable always wins), and `required(name)` must throw `Missing required env var ${name}...` when the variable is unset or blank after trimming.
- **SPEC-10.197** `E2E_BASE_URL` must be required with no hardcoded fallback; `apiBaseURL` must resolve to `E2E_API_BASE_URL` if set, else `api.` prepended to the base URL's hostname, else the base URL itself when that hostname already starts with `api.` or fails to parse; `opBaseURL` must resolve to `E2E_OP_BASE_URL` if set, else fall back to `apiBaseURL`.
- **SPEC-10.198** `E2E_EMAIL`, `E2E_PASSWORD`, `E2E_TENANT_ID`, `E2E_OIDC_CLIENT_ID`, `E2E_OIDC_REDIRECT_URI`, `E2E_TOTP_SECRET` must each be required; `E2E_FOREIGN_COMPANY_ID` must be optional; `E2E_ENVIRONMENT` is not read by `env.ts`: `external-guard.spec.ts` reads it directly from `process.env` and treats an unset value as `unknown`; `preflightRequiredEnv()` must collect every missing required variable into one thrown error rather than failing on the first.
- **SPEC-10.199** The bearer token must be read from `e2e/.auth/token.txt`, OP session cookies from `e2e/.auth/op-state.json`, and the foreign-company canary id from `e2e/.auth/foreign-company.txt`; each reader must throw when its file is absent or its content is empty/malformed, and the last-used TOTP step must persist to `e2e/.auth/totp-last-step` so a cross-process run never resubmits a code for a step bunyip already saw.

### 10.33 E2E: Playwright configuration

- **SPEC-10.200** The suite must run with `fullyParallel: false` and `workers: 1` (serial), since tests share one tenant and bearer token; `forbidOnly` must be true, and `retries` must be 1, only when `process.env.CI` is set (else `false`/`0`).
- **SPEC-10.201** The global test timeout must be 60000ms and `expect.timeout` 15000ms; `globalTeardown` must run `./global.teardown.ts` after every run regardless of outcome; reporters must be `list` plus an `html` reporter that never auto-opens.
- **SPEC-10.202** On failure, `trace`, `screenshot`, and `video` must each be retained/captured only on failure (`retain-on-failure` / `only-on-failure`).
- **SPEC-10.203** The `preflight` project must have no dependencies and run first; `setup` must run in Firefox, depend on `preflight`, and resolve `env.baseURL`; `chromium`/`firefox`/`webkit` projects must each run `(auth|form-validation).spec.ts`, depend on `preflight`, and use `env.baseURL` (`chromium` additionally passing `--disable-dev-shm-usage`); `ui-selectors` must run only in Firefox, depending on `setup`; `api` must depend on `setup` and use `env.apiBaseURL`, never `env.baseURL`; `guard` must depend on `preflight` only.

### 10.34 E2E: login helper and request fixtures

- **SPEC-10.204** `loginViaSpa` must retry at most 4 times total, only on a rate-limit rejection (parsed backoff of the stated seconds, default 5, capped at 60 seconds, plus 1 second), a `no-form` outcome (backoff 3000ms), or an `unclear` outcome (no backoff), and must fail fast with no retry on a definite credential rejection.
- **SPEC-10.205** When post-credential navigation lands on `/login/(2fa|mfa)`, a TOTP step must be filled: the code must be generated only when at least 5 seconds remain in the current 30-second step, must wait for a step later than the last one this run used, and must make at most two attempts, each with a fresh code, before falling back to a manual submit click; on `/oauth2/consent`, the helper must click the allow/authorize/approve control to persist the grant.
- **SPEC-10.206** `expectAuthenticated`/`expectAnonymous` must assert `GET <tickets>?per_page=1` returns 200 when authenticated and 401 or 403 when not; `expectAtLoginScreen` must poll the page URL for up to 30000ms until it matches `/^\/login(\/|$)/`.
- **SPEC-10.207** The default `test` fixture must attach `Authorization: Bearer <token>` (from the token file) to every request context; the `oidcTest` fixture must replay the OP cookie storage state against `opBaseURL` and must never attach a bearer header.

### 10.35 E2E: test data tagging, factories and teardown

- **SPEC-10.208** Every created record's run suffix must have the shape `e2e-<epochMs>-<runId>-<n>`, where `runId` resolves from `GITEA_RUN_ID`, else `GITHUB_RUN_ID`, else `E2E_RUN_ID`, else the process start timestamp, sanitized and truncated to 24 characters; `isStale(name)` must consider a record stale only once its embedded epoch is more than 24 hours old.
- **SPEC-10.209** `createCompany`/`createContact` must assert a 200 response with a truthy `id`; `enableModule` must `PUT` `{is_enabled: true}` to the module's settings route and assert success, so a 403 (missing admin privilege) surfaces as a test failure rather than being swallowed.
- **SPEC-10.210** `global.teardown.ts` must throw when the bearer token file is absent (rather than silently skipping cleanup), page every list endpoint at the server's max page size (treating a 404 as an empty, disabled module), sweep a fixed, ordered list of 24 resource kinds (children before the parents that refuse deletion while referenced, companies last) deleting any record this run owns or that is more than 24 hours stale, and throw one aggregated error naming every collected failure after the full sweep completes.

### 10.36 E2E: deploy-readiness scripts, package and TypeScript configuration

- **SPEC-10.211** `check-e2e-bootstrapped.mjs` must probe the OP's `/e2e-bootstrapped` endpoint with a 15000ms timeout and set the `skip=true` output only when the JSON body's `bootstrapped` field is `false`; an unset OP URL (`E2E_OP_BASE_URL`, else `E2E_API_BASE_URL`) also runs the suite; any non-2xx, network error, or parse failure must fall through to running the suite.
- **SPEC-10.212** `health-check.mjs` must `GET <apiBaseURL>/api/v1/health` once with a 30000ms timeout, exiting 0 on an ok response and 1 otherwise.
- **SPEC-10.213** `wait-for-deploy.mjs` must resolve the expected SHA by walking `git log` back to the most recent commit touching one of the fixed build-trigger paths (`src`, `crates`, `migrations`, `.cargo`, `Cargo.toml`, `Cargo.lock`, `oci-build`, `.forgejo/workflows/build-oci-image.yml`, kept in lock-step with `build-oci-image.yml`'s own path filter, 10.39), self-healing with `git fetch --unshallow origin` (only when the clone is shallow) then `git fetch --refetch origin` if the walk finds nothing, then poll `GET <apiBaseURL>/api/v1/version` every 15000ms for up to 600000ms until `body.git_hash` prefix-matches; on total resolution failure it must warn and exit 0 rather than fail the job.
- **SPEC-10.214** The suite must run under `bun` per the committed `bun.lock`, never `npm ci`; TypeScript compilation must target `ES2022`/`ESNext` modules with `strict: true` and `noEmit: true`; `node_modules/`, `.auth/`, `playwright-report/`, `blob-report/`, `test-results/`, `playwright/.cache/`, and `.env` must never be committed under `e2e/`.
- **SPEC-10.215** `e2e/lib/api.ts`'s `MAX_PER_PAGE` constant must equal `src/utils/pagination.rs`'s `PaginationParams::MAX_PER_PAGE` (100); a Rust unit test under `pms1427_e2e_page_size` must fail the build if any `per_page` literal under `e2e/` exceeds that constant, so the two values cannot drift apart silently.
- **SPEC-10.216** The `preflight` Playwright project (`e2e/tests/preflight.setup.ts`) must call `preflightRequiredEnv()` and run before every other project, so a missing required env var is reported once, naming every gap, rather than failing the first project that happens to read it.
- **SPEC-10.217** The `setup` Playwright project (`e2e/tests/global.setup.ts`) must drive a real browser login against the SPA, capture the bearer token from the OIDC token-endpoint response as its primary signal and from the first `Authorization: Bearer`-carrying request as a backstop, and persist the token, the OP session cookie state, and the foreign-company id to the fixed `e2e/.auth/` files read by `e2e/lib/auth-state.ts` (10.199); it must prefer the response-body capture because it survives an SPA that never fires an authenticated request.

### 10.37 Deployment and operations

- Build: `oci-build/Dockerfile` builds both binaries in a musl Rust builder image with dependencies cached in a separate
  layer, then copies `mokosh-server`, `mokosh-bootstrap`, `migrations/` and the font license into an Alpine runtime
  image. Build arguments `MOKOSH_GIT_HASH`, `MOKOSH_GIT_DESCRIBE`, `MOKOSH_BUILD_DATE` and `SOURCE_DATE_EPOCH` feed the
  version banner and image labels. The release profile uses LTO, one codegen unit, `panic = "abort"` and stripping.
- Process: the image starts as root through `gosu-entrypoint.sh`, which can remap the app user's uid and gid from `PUID`
  and `PGID`, runs root hooks in `/etc/entrypoint.d/`, changes ownership of `DATA_DIRS` (`/app/attachments`), and drops
  to `appuser` (default uid 1001) with `gosu` before running `/app/mokosh-server`. Started as a non-root user it only
  checks that `DATA_DIRS` is writable.
- Port: 8080 is exposed; the listen port is `PORT`.
- Volumes: local object storage writes under `STORAGE_ROOT` (the image prepares `/app/attachments`); persist it when the
  `local` provider is used.
- Health: `GET /api/v1/health` returns `OK` without touching dependencies and is the image `HEALTHCHECK`
  (30 s interval, 3 s timeout). `GET /api/v1/ready` pings the database (3 s bound) and, when `INFISICAL_ADDRESS` is set,
  the secret manager's `/api/status` (1 s timeout); it answers `200` with `status: ready` or `503` with `not_ready`, and
  per-check results (`ok`, `skipped` or `error: ...`). It is sent with `Cache-Control: no-store`.
- Version: `GET /api/v1/version` returns the build's version information; the startup log prints the banner.
- Development: `Dockerfile` runs `cargo run` against sources mounted by `compose.dev.yml`, which also defines
  PostgreSQL, a local mail catcher, and optional profiles for a secret manager and an S3-compatible store.
- Repository checks: the `justfile` `check` recipe runs compile, clippy, rustfmt, migration immutability, route-consumer,
  configuration and documentation guards implemented as Nushell scripts under `scripts/`; integration tests live in
  `tests/` and browser tests in `e2e/`.

### 10.38 Check workflow: job layout and gating (`.forgejo/workflows/check.yml`)

- **SPEC-10.300**: `check.yml` must declare `concurrency` group `${{ github.workflow }}-${{ github.ref }}` with
  `cancel-in-progress: true`, so a new push to a pull request cancels that pull request's superseded run, while two
  different pull requests (distinct `refs/pull/<n>/merge` refs) never share a group.
- **SPEC-10.301**: `check.yml` must define four jobs: `classify`; `cargo` and `guards`, each with `needs: classify` and
  `if: needs.classify.outputs.run_gate == 'true'`; and `secrets`, which has no `needs` and no `if`, so it runs on every
  pull request, including one whose only change is comments, because its scanners read git history that such a pull
  request still extends. When `run_gate` is not `true`, `cargo` and `guards` are skipped and none of their compile,
  lint, test or guard steps run for that pull request.
- **SPEC-10.302**: The `classify` job must run on `${{ vars.RUNS_ON_OPENSUSE_BASE_MEDIUM }}`, check out with
  `fetch-depth: 0`, and expose step `classify`'s `run_gate` as a job output. For a `pull_request` event it must run `git
  fetch origin <base_ref>` and classify `FETCH_HEAD` against `HEAD`; when that fetch exits non-zero it must print the
  fetch's stderr and exit 1, failing the job instead of skipping the gate.
- **SPEC-10.303**: The `classify` step must run `nu scripts/classify-diff.nu <base> <head>`, print `content classifier
  verdict: <verdict>`, and map the verdict to `run_gate`: `code` to `true`; `comments-only` and `non-code` to `false`;
  any other output to `true`. For a `push` event whose `github.event.before` is empty or forty zeros it must not
  classify and must set `run_gate=true`; for any other non-pull-request event it must classify `github.event.before`
  against `HEAD`. It must append `run_gate=<true|false>` to `$GITHUB_OUTPUT` and print the same line.
- **SPEC-10.304**: The `cargo` job must run on `${{ vars.RUNS_ON_OPENSUSE_BASE_HEAVY }}` with `timeout-minutes: 45`, and
  must check out with the default depth and no submodules, because it runs only cargo and one Nushell script that need
  neither `origin/main` history nor `common/common.just`. A run that exceeds 45 minutes fails the job.
- **SPEC-10.305**: The `cargo` job must run these steps in order, each failing the job on a non-zero exit: set
  `CARGO_BUILD_JOBS` to `nproc/2` in `$GITHUB_ENV`; restore the Rust build cache with `shared-key: check` and
  `cache-on-failure: true`; `nu scripts/check-build-target-storage.nu`; `cargo fmt --all --check`; `cargo clippy
  --workspace --all-targets -- -D warnings`; `cargo test --workspace --lib`; `cargo test --workspace --doc`; restore the
  cargo-machete tarball cache; install and run `cargo machete`. The job does not run a separate `cargo check`: clippy
  over `--workspace --all-targets` is its compile and lint gate.
- **SPEC-10.306**: The cargo-machete install must cache `/tmp/machete.tar.gz` with `actions/cache@v4` under key
  `cargo-machete-tarball-0.9.2-linux`, download the tarball with `curl --silent --fail --location` only when that file
  is missing or empty, and verify its SHA-256 with `sha256sum --check --strict` on every run, cache hit included, so a
  wrong-version file restored from cache fails the step. The cache key's version literal must be changed together with
  `MACHETE_VERSION`.
- **SPEC-10.307**: The `guards` job must run on `${{ vars.RUNS_ON_OPENSUSE_BASE_MEDIUM }}` with `timeout-minutes: 15`,
  check out with `fetch-depth: 0` and `submodules: true`, and run no `cargo` command. A run that exceeds 15 minutes
  fails the job.
- **SPEC-10.308**: The `guards` step `routes` must set output `run=true` only when `git diff --name-only
  origin/<base_ref>...HEAD` lists a path matching
  `^(src/modules/[^/]+/.*\.rs|src/api/router\.rs|scripts/check-route-consumers\.nu)$`, else `run=false`; it runs under
  `set -euo pipefail`, so a git failure fails the job. The shallow clone of the SPA sibling repository (path
  `mokosh-apps`, `fetch-depth: 1`, token `secrets.FORGEJO_PAT`) and the `Route consumers` step must each run only when
  `steps.routes.outputs.run == 'true'`, and `Route consumers` must run with `MOKOSH_APPS_DIR=mokosh-apps`.
- **SPEC-10.309**: The `guards` job must run these steps in order, each failing the job on a non-zero exit: `just
  check-migration-versions`; `just check-migration-immutability`; `just check-migration-versions-against-base`; then the
  Nushell scripts `check-guarded-content-migrations`, `check-no-duplicate-mail-copy`, `check-pool-safety`,
  `check-create-update-validate-parity`, `check-rate-limit-helper`, `check-runner-labels`, `check-oci-build-cache`,
  `check-oci-publish-tags`, `check-workspace-deps`, `check-env-example`, `check-doc-recipes`, `check-config-doc-paths`;
  `config-docs.nu self-test` then `config-docs.nu check`; `check-doc-links`; `check-claude-md.nu --self-test` then
  `check-claude-md.nu`; and `check-route-consumers` last. The job must not run `check-build-target-storage` or `cargo
  machete`, which belong to the `cargo` job.

### 10.39 Diff classifier (`scripts/classify-diff.nu`)

- **SPEC-10.310**: `nu scripts/classify-diff.nu <base-ref> <head-ref>` must print exactly one line, `code`,
  `comments-only` or `non-code`, to stdout and exit 0. When either ref argument is missing or empty it must print
  `usage: nu classify-diff.nu <base-ref> <head-ref>  OR  --self-test` to stderr and exit 2.
- **SPEC-10.311**: When `git diff --name-only <base> <head>` exits non-zero (invalid ref, no common history), the
  classifier must print git's stderr to stderr, print `code` on stdout and exit 0, so a classifier failure can never
  skip the compile and guard gate.
- **SPEC-10.312**: A path is a code file in the C family when it ends with `.rs`, `.ts`, `.tsx`, `.js`, `.jsx`, `.mjs`,
  `.cjs`, `.css`, `.scss`, `.sql`, `.c`, `.cpp`, `.cc`, `.h`, `.hpp`, `.java`, `.go` or `.kt`, and in the hash family
  when it ends with `.nu`, `.py`, `.sh`, `.bash`, `.zsh`, `.yml`, `.yaml`, `.toml`, `.just`, `.justfile` or
  `Dockerfile`, or its basename starts with `Dockerfile.`. Every other path (for example the extensionless `justfile`,
  `Cargo.lock`, `.env.example`, `*.json`, `*.md`) is not a code file and cannot change the verdict.
- **SPEC-10.313**: A changed line is read from `git diff --unified=0 <base> <head> -- <path>`, ignoring lines that start
  with `+++`, `---` or `@@`; it counts as a comment or whitespace when its content after the `+` or `-` marker is empty
  after trimming, or in a hash-family file starts with `#`, or in a C-family file starts with `//`, `/*`, `*/`, `*` or
  `--`. Any other changed line is code.
- **SPEC-10.314**: The verdict must be `code` as soon as any code file has one changed line that is not a comment or
  whitespace; else `comments-only` when at least one code file is in the diff (a code file touched only by rename or
  mode change counts); else `non-code`. `check.yml` skips its `cargo` and `guards` jobs for both `comments-only` and
  `non-code`.
- **SPEC-10.315**: `nu scripts/classify-diff.nu --self-test` must build a throwaway git repository in a temporary
  directory and assert six cases (C-family comment-only change gives `comments-only`; code change gives `code`;
  docs-only change gives `non-code`; hash-family comment-only change gives `comments-only`; whitespace-only change gives
  `comments-only`; mixed comment and code change gives `code`), printing `ok: <case> -> <verdict>` per case and
  `classify-diff.nu self-test passed`, and must raise an error naming the failing case, exiting non-zero, on any
  mismatch.

### 10.40 End-to-end workflow: details not stated in 10.5 (`.forgejo/workflows/e2e.yml`)

- **SPEC-10.316**: The `e2e.yml` checkout must use `fetch-depth: 0` only for a `push` event or a `workflow_dispatch`
  with `inputs.environment == 'staging'` (the paths that run `wait-for-deploy.mjs`, which walks `git log`), and
  `fetch-depth: 1` for a `pull_request` or a production dispatch; the expression must stay in step with the `if:` of the
  deploy-sync step.
- **SPEC-10.317**: `e2e.yml` must map `E2E_BASE_URL`, `E2E_EMAIL`, `E2E_PASSWORD`, `E2E_TENANT_ID`, `E2E_TOTP_SECRET`
  and `E2E_FOREIGN_COMPANY_ID` to the secret of the same name with `E2E_PRODUCTION_` or `E2E_STAGING_` in place of
  `E2E_`; `E2E_OIDC_REDIRECT_URI` to `MOKOSH_APPS_REDIRECT_URIS_PRODUCTION` or `_STAGING`; `E2E_OP_BASE_URL` to
  `OIDC_ISSUER_PRODUCTION` or `_STAGING`; and `E2E_OIDC_CLIENT_ID` to `MOKOSH_OIDC_CLIENT_ID` in both environments. On
  `push` and `pull_request` the `inputs` context is empty, so every switched variable resolves to its staging secret.
- **SPEC-10.318**: The suite step must be skipped only when `steps.seeded.outputs.skip == 'true'` exactly; the `seeded`
  step does not run on a production dispatch, so there the output is empty and the suite runs. The suite step must pass
  `--grep-invert @external` when `inputs.environment == 'production'` and no extra argument otherwise.
- **SPEC-10.319**: The `Install Playwright browsers` step must run `bun x playwright install chromium firefox webkit`
  without `--with-deps`, because the runner image has no `apt-get`; the browsers and their system libraries are
  pre-baked in the image, so a matching `@playwright/test` version makes the step a no-op and a mismatched version
  downloads the missing revision.

### 10.41 Image publishing workflow: details not stated in 10.6 (`.forgejo/workflows/build-oci-image.yml`)

- **SPEC-10.320**: `build-oci-image.yml` must declare `concurrency` group `${{ github.workflow }}-${{ github.ref }}`
  with `cancel-in-progress: ${{ !startsWith(github.ref, 'refs/tags/') }}`: a newer push to `main` cancels the older
  in-flight `latest` build, but a `v*` tag build is never cancelled, because a cancelled tag run leaves the registry
  without that version.
- **SPEC-10.321**: The job must check out with `fetch-depth: 0`, so `git describe --tags` sees tags, and must run
  `docker version` and `docker buildx version` before resolving anything; a missing Docker or buildx fails the job at
  that step.
- **SPEC-10.322**: A single trigger must publish exactly one tag: a push to `main` must publish only `latest`, and a
  `v*` tag push only that version tag, and neither run may publish the other's tag, because one release commit fires
  both events and two runs writing the same tag would race.
- **SPEC-10.323**: The `Log in to container registry` step must run `docker login` for the registry host with username
  `vars.PSA_SYSTEMS_PRIVATE_PACKAGE_OWNER` and password `secrets.PSA_SYSTEMS_PRIVATE_PACKAGE_PAT`, in dry runs too, and
  the image must be named `<registry host>/<owner>/mokosh-server:<resolved tag>`; a failed login fails the job before
  the build.
- **SPEC-10.324**: The `crazy-max/ghaction-github-runtime@v3` step must run after the buildx builder step and before the
  build step, because a raw `docker buildx build` does not receive `ACTIONS_CACHE_URL` and `ACTIONS_RUNTIME_TOKEN`,
  without which the `type=gha` cache cannot be reached.
- **SPEC-10.325**: The build must run `docker buildx build -f oci-build/Dockerfile .` (the repository root is the
  context) with exactly one `-t` tag and `--cache-from type=gha`; it must add `--push --cache-to
  type=gha,mode=max,ignore-error=true` when `steps.resolve.outputs.dry_run` is not `true`, else `--load`. A failed build
  fails the job.
- **SPEC-10.326**: The resolve step must print one summary line `mode=<mode> train=<train> tag=<tag> describe=<describe>
  dry_run=<bool>`. The build step must print `Building and pushing mokosh-server with tag: <tag>` for a real run or
  `[dry-run] WOULD build and push mokosh-server with tag: <tag>` for a dry run, and the final step must print `Image
  pushed to <reference>` or `[dry-run] WOULD push image to <reference>`, so a log reader can tell a simulated run from a
  publish.

### 10.42 Test and cache workflows: details not stated in 10.3, 10.4 and 10.7

- **SPEC-10.327**: `integration.yml` must skip the pull-request run when every changed path matches `**.md`, `docs/**`,
  `LICENSE`, `.gitignore`, `.editorconfig` or `renovate.json` (`paths-ignore`); a single other changed path triggers the
  full suite.
- **SPEC-10.328**: `integration.yml` must declare `concurrency` group `${{ github.workflow }}-${{ github.ref }}` with
  `cancel-in-progress: true`, so a newer push to a pull request supersedes that pull request's obsolete run.
- **SPEC-10.329**: Every workflow step that installs cargo-nextest (`integration.yml` jobs `build` and `test`,
  `integration-unsupported.yml`, and `cache-warm.yml` job `warm-integration`) must cache `/tmp/nextest.tar.gz` with
  `actions/cache@v4` under the identical key `cargo-nextest-tarball-0.9.145-linux`, download it only when the file is
  missing or empty, verify its SHA-256 with `sha256sum --check --strict` on every run, cache hit included, and extract
  into `${CARGO_HOME:-$HOME/.cargo}/bin`. A nextest version bump must change the key, `NEXTEST_VERSION` and
  `NEXTEST_SHA256` at all four sites together.
- **SPEC-10.330**: Before building, the `integration.yml` `build` job must print the count of `tests/suites/*.rs` files
  other than `mod.rs` and the free space of the workspace filesystem (`df -P -BG .`); when under 25 GB it must exit 1
  with an `::error::` annotation that names the free space and states it is a runner-capacity problem, not a problem
  with the commit under test.
- **SPEC-10.331**: In the `integration.yml` `build` job, the archive step must print `Test binaries built in <s>s` and
  the lowest free space sampled during the build; when `cargo nextest archive` exits non-zero and that lowest sample is
  under 5000 MB it must also print an `::error::` annotation naming the disk-exhaustion signature (linker bus error)
  before exiting with the archive command's own status.
- **SPEC-10.332**: Each `integration.yml` shard must run `cargo nextest run --archive-file nextest-archive.tar.zst
  --profile ci --partition hash:<shard>/3` with `TMPDIR=$HOME/.nextest-tmp` (created first), so a given test lands in
  the same shard on every run; it must print `Shard <shard>/3 test run took <s>s` and exit with nextest's own status.
  The step must not be wrapped in a shell `timeout`: a stuck case is reported and terminated by name through the `ci`
  profile's `slow-timeout`.
- **SPEC-10.333**: Each `integration.yml` shard job must set `DATABASE_URL` to
  `postgres://postgres:postgres@postgres:5432/postgres` and `RUST_BACKTRACE` to `1` at job level, so the template-build
  step and the shard test step run in identical environments.
- **SPEC-10.334**: `cache-warm.yml` must declare `concurrency` group `${{ github.workflow }}-${{ github.ref }}` with
  `cancel-in-progress: true`, so back-to-back merges leave only the newest `main` commit warming the cache.
- **SPEC-10.335**: The `warm-check` job must run on `${{ vars.RUNS_ON_OPENSUSE_DEV_LATEST }}` with `timeout-minutes:
  20`, check out with `submodules: true`, set `CARGO_BUILD_JOBS` to `nproc/2`, and run `cargo clippy --workspace
  --all-targets -- -D warnings`, `cargo test --no-run --workspace --lib` and `cargo test --workspace --doc`. The doc
  tests execute, because cargo rejects `--no-run` for them; it runs no lib test and no `cargo check`.
- **SPEC-10.336**: The `warm-integration` job must run on `${{ vars.RUNS_ON_OPENSUSE_DEV_LATEST }}` with
  `timeout-minutes: 30` and env `SQLX_OFFLINE=true`, `RUST_BACKTRACE=1`, start no Postgres service, install the same
  pinned nextest as `integration.yml`, and run `cargo nextest archive --archive-file /tmp/nextest-archive.tar.zst
  --workspace --tests`, discarding the archive: the job exists only to fill the build cache.
- **SPEC-10.337**: `integration-unsupported.yml` must restore the Rust build cache with `shared-key: integration`, the
  same key as `integration.yml`, so the weekly run reuses the pull-request build cache.
- **SPEC-10.338**: The MinIO step of `integration-unsupported.yml` must remove the temporary container it created with
  `docker rm --volumes` when the step exits, keep MinIO data in `/tmp/minio-data` and its log in `/tmp/minio.log`, and,
  when `/minio/health/live` is still not healthy after 30 one-second attempts, print `::error::MinIO did not become
  healthy; log follows`, print the log and exit 1.
- **SPEC-10.339**: The `Unsupported integration tests` step must run `cargo nextest run --profile unsupported`, print
  `Unsupported suite took <s>s`, and exit with nextest's own status.

### 10.43 Configuration files that cannot carry comments (`renovate.json`, `e2e/package.json`, `e2e/tsconfig.json`)

- **SPEC-10.340**: `renovate.json` must carry `$schema` `https://docs.renovatebot.com/renovate-schema.json`. The
  `renovate.yml` caller passes `target_repository: ${{ github.repository }}`, so Renovate reads this file from the
  repository it runs for; its requirements are 10.50 and 10.51, cited at `renovate.yml` because JSON has no comments.
- **SPEC-10.341**: `e2e/package.json` must declare `private: true`, `type: module` and exactly the scripts `test`
  (`playwright test`), `test:headed` (`playwright test --headed`) and `report` (`playwright show-report`); it is
  installed by `e2e.yml` with `bun install --frozen-lockfile`.
- **SPEC-10.342**: `e2e/package.json` must pin `@playwright/test` to exactly `1.60.0`, `@types/node` to `22.10.2`,
  `dotenv` to `16.4.7` and `typescript` to `5.7.2`, with `otplib` (`^12.0.1`) as the only range. Because installs use
  `--frozen-lockfile`, a version edit without the matching `e2e/bun.lock` change fails `bun install`, and Renovate does
  not manage this file (10.50), so every bump is a manual change.
- **SPEC-10.343**: `e2e/tsconfig.json` must set `target` `ES2022`, `module` `ESNext`, `moduleResolution` `Bundler`,
  `esModuleInterop` `true`, `strict` `true`, `skipLibCheck` `true`, `types` `["node"]` and `noEmit` `true`, include
  `**/*.ts` and exclude `node_modules`.

### 10.44 End-to-end diagnostics helper (`e2e/lib/page-diagnostics.ts`)

- **SPEC-10.344**: `mainFrameResponseLog(page)` must return the same log object for the same page on every call and
  register its `response` listener only once, so the login helper and `attachPageDiagnostics` never double every entry;
  responses that arrived before the first call are not recorded.
- **SPEC-10.345**: The main-frame log must record a response only when its request's resource type is `document` and its
  frame is the page's main frame; a request whose `frame()` call throws (a service-worker request) must be ignored, not
  raised. Each entry holds the HTTP `status` and `url`.
- **SPEC-10.346**: For a recorded response with status below 200 or at or above 300, the log must fill the entry's
  `body` asynchronously with the response text, whitespace runs collapsed to one space and trimmed, cut to 500
  characters followed by `... (truncated)` when longer. When the body cannot be read (a redirect, a closed context)
  `body` must stay unset and the entry keeps its status and URL.
- **SPEC-10.347**: `describeLast()` must return `(none recorded)` when nothing was recorded, else `<status> <url>`
  followed by ` body="<body>"` when a body was captured; `last()` must return the newest entry or `null`, and
  `entries()` must return a copy, so callers cannot mutate the log.
- **SPEC-10.348**: `trackApiErrors(page, apiBaseURL)` must record `<status> <METHOD> <url>`, in arrival order, for every
  response whose URL starts with `apiBaseURL` and whose status is 400 or higher, and nothing for lower statuses or other
  origins; `errors()` must return a copy. Each call registers its own listener (no per-page de-duplication).
- **SPEC-10.349**: `attachPageDiagnostics(page).snapshot(label)` must return `<label>:` followed by the lines
  `currentUrl=<page url>`, `urlTrail`, `mainFrameResponses` and `requests`, each trail listing at most the last 30
  entries (main-frame navigation URLs; main-frame document responses as `<status> <url>` plus the captured body; every
  request URL) and reading `(none)` when empty. The page is bound when `attachPageDiagnostics` is called.

### 10.45 Workspace crate manifests (`crates/*/Cargo.toml`)

- **SPEC-10.350**: `crates/build-metadata/Cargo.toml` must declare package `build-metadata` version `0.1.0`, edition
  `2021`, license `Proprietary` and an empty `[dependencies]` table (the crate uses only the standard library), because
  the root package consumes it as a `[build-dependencies]` path dependency. Unlike the other member crates it sets
  `edition`, `license` and `authors` explicitly instead of inheriting `[workspace.package]`, and the values must stay
  equal to the workspace's.
- **SPEC-10.351**: `crates/mokosh-test-macros/Cargo.toml` must declare a `[lib]` with `proc-macro = true` at
  `src/lib.rs`, inherit `edition`, `license` and `authors` from the workspace, and depend only on `proc-macro2` 1,
  `quote` 1 and `syn` 2 with feature `full`; it must not depend on `sqlx`, `tokio` or `mokosh-test`, because a
  proc-macro crate exports macros only and `mokosh-test` depends on this crate.
- **SPEC-10.352**: `crates/mokosh-test/Cargo.toml` must declare a `[lib]` at `src/lib.rs`, inherit `edition`, `license`
  and `authors` from the workspace, and depend on `mokosh-test-macros` by path, `sqlx` 0.8 (features `runtime-tokio`,
  `postgres`, `migrate`), `tokio` 1 (features `rt`, `time`), `uuid` (workspace), `sha2` 0.10 and `url` 2. The root
  package must reference it only under `[dev-dependencies]`, so it never reaches a release build.
- **SPEC-10.353**: `crates/mokosh-types/Cargo.toml` must declare a `[lib]` at `src/lib.rs`, inherit `edition`, `license`
  and `authors` from the workspace, and depend only on `serde`, `serde_json`, `chrono` and `uuid` (each `{ workspace =
  true }`), `chrono-tz` 0.9, `validator` 0.19 (feature `derive`) and `rust_decimal` 1 (feature `serde`). It must not
  depend on `sqlx`, `axum`, `tokio` or another server-only crate, because it holds the data types shared between the
  server and the SPA client.

### 10.46 Gate scripts: details not stated in 10.26 to 10.31

- **SPEC-10.354**: `check-migration-versions-against-base.nu` must take `migrations_dir` (default `migrations`) and
  `base_ref` (default `origin/main`). It must print `FAIL: git ls-tree <base_ref> failed (exit <n>):` with git's stderr
  and exit 2 when `git ls-tree` fails; print `FAIL: <n> prefix collision(s) would land on main after this merge:` with
  one `prefix <p>: <file>, <file>` line per collision and exit 1; and otherwise print `migrations clean against
  <base_ref>: <n> files, no post-merge prefix collisions` and exit 0. Only `.sql` names that start with digits and an
  underscore take part, a name present on both sides counts once, and a missing `migrations_dir` on disk counts as no
  files.
- **SPEC-10.355**: `check-guarded-content-migrations.nu` must examine a migration only when its file name has a numeric
  prefix above 209 and its text contains the uppercase token `UPDATE`, and a guard matches only with an uppercase `AND`,
  so lowercase SQL is not examined. A violation must print `ERROR: guarded content UPDATE(s) with no zero-row assertion
  (PMS-1117).` and a table of file and reason to stderr and exit 1; a clean run prints `guarded-content-migration OK:
  <n> migration(s) checked above prefix 209` and exits 0.
- **SPEC-10.356**: `check-pool-safety.nu` must skip lines whose trimmed text starts with `//` and lines containing
  `migrator_pool`, and for every other line containing `.pool()` in `src/**/*.rs` except `src/db/pool.rs` it must search
  the 8 preceding lines, comment lines included, for `SAFETY (PMS-285`; without a match it must print `ERROR: bare
  .pool() serving call(s) without a // SAFETY (PMS-285 note (PMS-692).` and a table of file, line and code to stderr and
  exit 1. A clean run prints `pool-safety OK: ...` and exits 0.
- **SPEC-10.357**: `check-rate-limit-helper.nu` must scan `src/**/*.rs` and report each offending line once, with first
  match winning: `builds a 429 outside the shared helper` for a non-comment line containing `TOO_MANY_REQUESTS` outside
  `src/utils/error.rs`; `computes a retry delay and discards it` for any line containing `let _ = retry_after`,
  including inside the helper file; `constructs AppError::RateLimited directly instead of calling
  AppError::rate_limited(..)` for any line, comment lines included, containing `AppError::RateLimited` outside
  `src/utils/error.rs`. Any report prints a table of file, line, reason and code to stderr and exits 1; a clean run
  prints `rate-limit-helper OK: ...` and exits 0.
- **SPEC-10.358**: `check-no-duplicate-mail-copy.nu` must run both of its checks (the seeded phrases under
  `src/**/*.rs`, and the ticket-note sentence in both named files) before deciding the exit status, so one run reports
  every failure; it must exit 1 when either fails and 0 only when both pass. A missing named file is an uncaught file
  error that exits non-zero, not a pass.
- **SPEC-10.359**: `check-create-update-validate-parity.nu` must scan `src/**/*.rs` and `crates/*/src/**/*.rs` for
  brace-bodied `pub struct (Create|Update|Upsert|Patch)<Name>Request` declarations keyed by `<Name>`: `Create` and
  `Upsert` form the create side (a later struct with the same key replaces an earlier one), `Update` and `Patch` are
  separate update sides, and a key is a pair only when a create side and an update or patch side both exist. A struct
  with no counterpart is not checked.
- **SPEC-10.360**: For each pair `check-create-update-validate-parity.nu` must compare only fields present on both
  sides, treat a field with no `#[validate(...)]` attribute as `none`, join multi-line `#[validate(` attributes before
  comparing, ignore the order of several `#[validate]` attributes on one field, and on a mismatch print `<Name>.<field>:
  create has [<attrs>], update has [<attrs>]` to stderr and exit 1. A clean run prints `create/update validate parity
  OK: <n> pairs, ...` and exits 0.
- **SPEC-10.361**: `check-oci-build-cache.nu` must select workflows by the raw text `docker buildx build` (comments
  included), print an error and exit 1 when none contains it, and judge each selected file only on its non-comment
  lines. The docker-container driver requirement is met by either `--driver docker-container` or a reference to the
  shared `setup-buildx` composite action. Each violation is printed as `<file>: missing <what>` or `<file>:<line>:
  <what> is retired; use type=gha`, followed by exit 1.
- **SPEC-10.362**: `check-oci-publish-tags.nu` must also run `oci-build/get-tags.nu` and fail when it resolves
  differently from: mode `release` with ref `v1.2.3` gives `v1.2.3`; mode `latest` with ref `main` gives `latest`; mode
  `dry-run` with ref `main` gives `latest`; mode `dry-run` with ref `main` and simulate tag `v9.9.9` gives `v9.9.9`; for
  an allow-listed branch, mode `branch` and a `dry-run` on that branch give that branch's tag; a branch outside the
  allow-list must raise instead of resolving; and `branch-tag` of `feat/PMS-733-example` must be `feat-PMS-733-example`.
  All errors are printed to stderr before exit 1; a clean run prints `OCI publish tags OK: ...`.
- **SPEC-10.363**: `check-workspace-deps.nu` must read the `dependencies`, `dev-dependencies` and `build-dependencies`
  tables of every `workspace.members` manifest (`.` is the root `Cargo.toml`) and no target-specific table, and treat a
  dependency as inherited only when its value is a table with `workspace = true`. It must print each violation as
  `<crate>: <problem> (<manifest>)`, with problems `no member inherits it` and `own pin shadows the workspace pin`, and
  exit 1; a clean run prints `workspace-deps OK: ...`.
- **SPEC-10.364**: `check-doc-recipes.nu` must collect `just <recipe>` invocations only from inline code spans
  (odd-numbered backtick segments) of prose lines and from whole lines inside fenced blocks, count a bare `just`, or
  `just` followed by a `#` comment, as the recipe `default`, ignore an invocation whose first argument starts with `-`,
  and accept a recipe token only when it matches `^[a-z][a-z0-9-]*$`. A missing recipe is printed as `<file>:<line>:
  `just <recipe>` is not a recipe` to stderr, followed by exit 1.
- **SPEC-10.365**: `check-doc-recipes.nu` must exclude from the known recipes any justfile recipe preceded by a
  `[private]` attribute, add every name printed by `just --summary`, and, when `just --summary` fails and the justfile
  contains an `import` line, print an error that tells the operator to run `git submodule update --init` and exit 1; it
  must also exit 1 when no recipe name could be parsed.
- **SPEC-10.366**: `check-config-doc-paths.nu` must scan `.env.example`, `compose.dev.yml` and `justfile` for tokens
  shaped `docs/` followed by characters from `A-Za-z0-9._/-` (optionally preceded by `./`) that start at a line start or
  after a character outside that set, strip trailing `.`, `,`, `;`, `:`, `)`, `]`, `}`, `"` and backtick characters,
  ignore a bare `docs/`, and list every path not on disk as `<file>:<line>: <path> is not on disk` on stderr, followed
  by exit 1.
- **SPEC-10.367**: `check-claude-md.nu` must compute a heading's anchor, outside fenced blocks, as the trimmed
  lower-cased heading text with every character other than word characters, hyphens and spaces removed and spaces
  replaced by `-`, and must validate each `](docs/...)` link's `#anchor` against the target file's headings. Its
  `--self-test` must run six fixture cases (clean index; oversized file; 401-character prose line; long line inside a
  fence is exempt; missing docs file; missing anchor), print `self-test: <case>` for each pass, and exit 1 printing
  `self-test: FAIL (...)` on any mismatch.
- **SPEC-10.368**: `check-build-target-storage.nu` must ignore a blank `CARGO_TARGET_DIR` or `CARGO_BUILD_TARGET_DIR`;
  after those it must read `build.target-dir` from the repository's `.cargo/config.toml` and then from
  `~/.cargo/config.toml`, resolve a relative path against the repository root, probe the nearest existing ancestor when
  the directory does not exist yet, and print the lines `cargo target dir:`, `chosen by:` and `filesystem:`. A
  disk-backed filesystem prints `Build target storage OK: ...` and exits 0; a `tmpfs` or `ramfs` target with the allow
  variable set prints a `WARNING:` and exits 0; otherwise it prints the error to stderr and exits 1.
- **SPEC-10.369**: `check-ci-stalls.nu` must read run lists from the Forgejo actions tasks API 50 runs per page for at
  most 8 pages, stopping at the first empty or short page, authenticating with `FORGEJO_TOKEN`; an API error must print
  `ERROR: could not read the actions API: ...` and exit 1, never an empty result.
- **SPEC-10.370**: `check-ci-stalls.nu` must measure a run from `run_started_at` (else `created_at`) to `updated_at` for
  a finished status (`success`, `failure`, `cancelled`, `skipped`) and to the current time for any other status, so an
  in-flight stall is reported; ignore runs created before the look-back window; take a workflow's bound as the smallest
  `timeout-minutes` among its jobs; and judge a run over its bound when its duration exceeds it.
- **SPEC-10.371**: On a stall `check-ci-stalls.nu` must print `ERROR: <n> of <m> run(s) in the last <d> day(s) outlived
  their job's timeout-minutes (PMS-906).`, group stalled runs that finished within the same minute into one drain event
  (run count, earliest creation time, worst minutes, workflows), print per-run detail for a single-run event, and exit
  1; with no stall it prints `ci-stalls OK: ...` and exits 0. A workflow with no bound is named in a `NOTE` on stderr
  and not judged. Its `--self-test` must run on fixtures without a token and exit 1 on any failed case.
- **SPEC-10.372**: `ci-job-log.nu` must raise an error when `~/.local/share/forgejo-cli/keys.json` is missing or holds
  no key for the host, when no run matches among the 50 most recent (`no matching run in the 50 most recent; pass --run
  <id>, or --list to look`), and when the chosen run has no jobs. Without `--sha` it must select failed runs only; with
  `--sha` it must select runs whose commit starts with the given prefix; it must print `run <id>, job <id> "<name>"
  [<status>]` to stderr before the log.
- **SPEC-10.373**: `check-env-example.nu` must exit 1 with an error when `src/config/registry.rs` is missing, when no
  `declare_keys!` row can be parsed from it, or when a declared constant's identifier differs from the key name it
  declares.
- **SPEC-10.374**: `check-env-example.nu` must treat a name as present in `.env.example` when a line matches
  `^\s*#?\s*NAME=`, and as forwarded by `compose.dev.yml` only when it is a key of the `services.server.environment`
  mapping; a name that appears only as `${NAME` interpolation counts as a reader of a template key but does not satisfy
  the forwarding requirement. Each failure line names the file, the variable and the fix (add the key, forward it, or
  allowlist it with a reason); a clean run prints `env parity OK: ...` and exits 0.

### 10.47 Configuration documentation generator (`scripts/config-docs.nu`)

- **SPEC-10.375**: `nu scripts/config-docs.nu` with no subcommand must print `usage: nu scripts/config-docs.nu
  <generate|check|since <version>|release-notes <version>|self-test>` and exit 0. Each subcommand that finds a problem
  must print `ERROR: ...` and one indented line per problem to stderr and exit 1.
- **SPEC-10.376**: The registry parser must read each `Bootstrap` or `Application` declaration of the shape `IDENT =
  "NAME", since "vX.Y.Z", required|optional ["vX.Y.Z"];` in `src/config/registry.rs`; when the number of parsed
  declarations differs from the number of lines that start such a declaration, or is zero, it must raise
  `src/config/registry.rs: parsed N of M declarations; the declare_keys! shape changed`.
- **SPEC-10.377**: The catalog must be the union of the registry, the `[[variable]]` rows (`required` defaults to false)
  and the `[[removed]]` rows of `src/config/variables.toml`; every `since`, `required_since`, `deprecated.release` and
  `removed.release` must match `^vX.Y.Z$`; a name declared more than once, and a `required_since` that is not after
  `since` or lacks `required`, must be reported.
- **SPEC-10.378**: A variable added with `required` and no `required_since` in a release other than `v0.1.0` must yield
  an `Added` entry marked `Breaking: won't start`; a `required_since` must yield an extra `Changed` entry marked
  `Breaking: won't start`; a `deprecated` row must yield a `Deprecated` entry whose action names the replacement and
  says the old name makes the server refuse to boot; a `removed` row must yield a `Removed` entry carrying its record's
  issue, action and breaking level. An `Added` entry without an explicit action must read `Required: set it before the
  server starts.` when required, else `Optional. Leave it unset to keep the default.`.
- **SPEC-10.379**: A `[[change]]` record must name a group among `Added`, `Changed`, `Deprecated` and `Removed` and a
  `breaking` of empty, `wont-start` or `feature-off`, and every variable it lists must exist in the catalog; except for
  group `Changed` it must match a derived entry of the same release, group and variable, or the check reports `does not
  match the facts`; a `Changed` record with no derived match adds an explicit entry. An entry with a breaking level must
  have a non-empty action and an issue matching `^[A-Z]+-\d+$`, a `feature-off` entry must have a non-empty `feature`,
  and any issue present must match the pattern.
- **SPEC-10.380**: The `Recently added` block must list every release newer than the newest `v*` git tag, newest first,
  followed by the five newest tagged releases, each under `### <version>` (`### Unreleased (<version>)` when untagged)
  with anchor `release-vX-Y-Z`; groups appear in the order Added, Changed, Deprecated, Removed; entries are ordered
  won't-start, feature-off, unmarked, then required before optional, then by name; a release with no entries reads `No
  configuration changes.`.
- **SPEC-10.381**: `config-docs.nu generate` must print the error list and write nothing when the facts are
  inconsistent. Otherwise it must replace the text between the `BEGIN GENERATED` and `END GENERATED` marker lines,
  rewrite the `Required` and `Added in` cells and the anchor (`var-` plus the lower-cased name with `_` replaced by `-`)
  of every existing row of `## All variables` while keeping its other cells, append a row whose purpose reads `Not
  described yet: say what it does.` after the last table row for each catalog variable without a row, and print
  `docs/configuration.md is current` when nothing changed or `rewrote the generated parts of docs/configuration.md`
  after saving. Missing markers or a missing section raise an error naming the file.
- **SPEC-10.382**: `config-docs.nu check` must fail when a row of `## All variables` does not match the row shape, names
  a variable outside the catalog, has an anchor other than the expected slug, has a `Required` cell that does not begin
  with the expected `yes` or `no`, or has an `Added in` cell other than `<since>` followed by `; required since <v>`, `;
  deprecated in <v>, use <replacement>` and `; removed in <v>` as they apply; when a catalog variable has no row or more
  than one; and when a `Recently added` entry is malformed, is not a recorded change, disagrees on the Required flag,
  the breaking mark, the naming of its issue or (for feature-off) the leading `Feature: <feature>. `, links to an anchor
  that is not a row anchor, or when a covered release, group and variable is missing. A clean run prints `config docs
  OK: <n> variables, <m> changelog entries`.
- **SPEC-10.383**: The source guard of `config-docs.nu check` must recognize environment reads through `env::var`,
  `env::var_os`, `require_env`, `required_env`, `required`, `parse_tenant_arg_env` (second argument),
  `EnvFilter::from_default_env` and `try_from_default_env` (as `RUST_LOG`), the `name:` and `deprecated:` string
  literals of `src/storage/env.rs`, the `Self::X => "NAME"` arms of `src/app_secrets/mod.rs`, and const aliases of those
  calls; it must report a read that is not in the registry, `variables.toml` or `NOT_SERVER_CONFIG`, a stale
  `NOT_SERVER_CONFIG` entry, a `variables.toml` entry nothing reads, and a `variables.toml` entry that is also a
  registry key.
- **SPEC-10.384**: `config-docs.nu since <version>` must accept `--json`, printing a JSON array of records with
  `release`, `group`, `variable`, `required`, `level` (`none` when unmarked), `feature`, `issue` and `action`; without
  it, it must print the table followed by `<n> changes after <version>: <w> WON'T START (apply before restarting), <f>
  FEATURE OFF (review and acknowledge before restarting).`. Rows are sorted by release ascending, then breaking level
  (won't-start, feature-off, unmarked), then variable name.
- **SPEC-10.385**: `config-docs.nu release-notes <version> [--ref <ref>]` must print `## Configuration changes`, then a
  link to `docs/configuration.md#release-vX-Y-Z` in the repository (the tag path for the version, or the branch path
  when `--ref` differs) with the entry count and the won't-start and feature-off counts, followed by one bullet per
  breaking entry, won't-start first; for a release with no entries it must print `No configuration changes in <version>.
  Full list: `, followed by the same link in Markdown form pointing at `docs/configuration.md`.
- **SPEC-10.386**: `config-docs.nu self-test` must run its fixture cases (generated document passes; generating twice
  changes nothing; each of a missing row, a Required mismatch, an Added-in mismatch, an unknown row, a missing or
  unmarked breaking entry, a wrong mark, a missing feature, a missing anchor and an unlisted or unread variable fails)
  and print `config-docs self-test: clean`, or print `self-test: FAIL (...)` per failing case and exit 1.

### 10.48 `justfile`: recipe details not stated in 10.9 to 10.14

- **SPEC-10.387**: `fmt` must run `cargo fmt --all` and rewrite files in place, unlike `check-fmt` (10.58), which must
  not modify any file.
- **SPEC-10.388**: `dev`, `dev-infisical` and `dev-s3` must rewrite `.env` by writing the complete new text, ending with
  a newline, to `.env.new` (deleting a pre-existing `.env.new` first) and then moving it over `.env`, so an interrupted
  write never leaves a truncated `.env`.
- **SPEC-10.389**: `dev-s3` must treat a `STORAGE_S3_*` key as filled only when its `.env` value is non-empty after
  trimming; for each blank or absent key it must delete every `KEY=` and `# KEY=` line and append `KEY=<value>`, leaving
  filled keys untouched.
- **SPEC-10.390**: `ensure-env` must replace only uncommented `.env.example` lines whose text before the first `=`
  equals one of the generated keys, copy every other line (comments and other keys) unchanged, and end `.env` with a
  newline.
- **SPEC-10.391**: `check-docker` and `build-docker` must pass `MOKOSH_BUILD_DATE` formatted `%Y-%m-%dT%H:%M:%SZ` and
  expressed in UTC, because the trailing `Z` asserts UTC, matching the CI build's `date --utc` value.

## 11. Non-functional behavior

### 11.1 Logging and diagnostics

- **SPEC-11.1**: Both binaries must write `tracing` text events to standard output filtered by `RUST_LOG`, and must use
  the filter `info` when `RUST_LOG` is unset or does not parse; the long-running server therefore does not log at
  `debug` unless asked.
- **SPEC-11.2**: Every request that reaches the combined router past CORS must be recorded by the HTTP tracing layer,
  whichever of the seven route trees or the fallback handles it.
- **SPEC-11.3**: Error text produced by the readiness Infisical probe must name the configured address with its
  userinfo, query string and fragment removed, so credentials embedded in `INFISICAL_ADDRESS` never reach the response
  body or the access log.

### 11.2 Resource bounds

- **SPEC-11.4**: Every outbound HTTP client must bound a single request with a total timeout. The values in force
  include: readiness Infisical probe 1 s; identity-provider verification and directory discovery 5 s without redirects;
  identity-provider directory, host-secret, host-configuration and mailer-relay calls 10 s; SMTP 15 s; Infisical 30 s;
  RMM provider 30 s and RMM connection test 10 s, both without redirects; workflow webhook action 10 s without automatic
  redirects; update check 5 s; company website probe 5 s per scheme without redirects; Xero and QuickBooks 45 s; S3 10 s
  connect and 300 s total. The Stripe, PayPal, Google, Microsoft and iCloud clients must carry a bound as well.
- **SPEC-11.5**: The public-API rate limiter, like every other rate limiter and the revoked-session set, must be held in
  process memory: a restart must empty it and two replicas must not share it (SPEC-5.138).

### 11.3 Startup validation

- **SPEC-11.6**: When the deployment mode is `saas` and no identity-provider verifier was built, router construction
  must log at `error` the message beginning `MOKOSH_DEPLOYMENT_MODE=saas but no Bunyip RS verifier is mounted` and must
  keep local password login enabled instead of refusing to boot.
- **SPEC-11.7**: A misconfiguration the router can detect at construction must stop or announce itself before the first
  request: a malformed `CORS_ORIGIN` entry or an invalid attachment size setting panics the boot (SPEC-12.17,
  SPEC-8.16), and a partial directory configuration logs a warning naming the cause (SPEC-8.6); an invalid branding size
  cap (`branding max-bytes config invalid`) panics the boot too.

## 12. Interfaces

The interfaces are the HTTP API served by `mokosh-server` and the command line of its two binaries. Per-route behavior
is specified in the sections that own each module; this section states the mount prefix, credential plane and gate of
each route tree and the layers every request passes through.

### 12.1 Route trees and fallback

- **SPEC-12.1**: `create_api_router` must mount exactly seven route trees, each as its own nested router: `/api/v1`
  (staff API), `/api/v1/public`, `/api/v1/contact`, `/api/v1/bunyip`, `/api/v1/stripe`, `/api/v1/paypal` and
  `/api/v1/webhooks`.
- **SPEC-12.2**: A `GET` request that none of the seven trees handles, including `GET /`, must answer `404` with an HTML
  page whose title is `API endpoint`, whose heading is `This is an API endpoint.`, that carries `<meta name="robots"
  content="noindex">`, and that lists no route.
- **SPEC-12.3**: The fallback page must link to `https://` followed by the remainder of the `Host` header when the
  header begins with `api.msp.`, and otherwise (including when `Host` is absent or not visible ASCII) to the client
  origin passed to `create_api_router`; no domain may be hard-coded.
- **SPEC-12.4**: The fallback page must render with no database access, using the cached application name HTML-escaped,
  so it still renders while the database is down.

### 12.2 Global layers and body handling
