  2000 characters, a currency that is not exactly 3 characters, and any line whose description is outside 1..1000
  characters.
- **SPEC-13.1361**: POST /quotes must fail with 400 BAD_REQUEST "Unknown company <id>" when company_id is not a company
  of the caller's tenant, and must create nothing.
- **SPEC-13.1362**: POST /quotes must store as billing_contact_id the explicitly named contact only when it belongs to
  the quote's company (else the request must be refused), and otherwise the company's billing contact, or null when the
  company has none.
- **SPEC-13.1363**: A new quote must receive the next number of its tenant's gapless sequence formatted as the sequence
  prefix (default "QUO-") followed by the number zero-padded to 6 digits; the first quote of a tenant must seed the
  sequence at 1, and a rolled-back create must not consume a number.
- **SPEC-13.1364**: POST /quotes must create the quote with status draft, requested_by_id the calling user, and currency
  "USD" when none is given, and must write a Create audit row in the same transaction.
- **SPEC-13.1365**: A quote's subtotal must always equal the sum of its lines' totals (quantity multiplied by
  unit_price, negative values allowed for discounts) and total must equal subtotal plus tax_amount; no request field may
  set subtotal or total, and every line change must recompute them in the same transaction.
- **SPEC-13.1366**: On POST /quotes, a given tax_amount must be kept with no tax rate; otherwise tax_rate_id (which must
  belong to the tenant) or, when absent, the tenant's default tax rate must be frozen on the quote, and tax_amount must
  be recomputed on every line change as the sum of the totals of lines with is_taxable true multiplied by the rate
  divided by 100, rounded to 2 decimals. A line's is_taxable must default to true.
- **SPEC-13.1367**: PUT /quotes/{id} and DELETE /quotes/{id} on a quote stored as sent, accepted, declined, expired,
  converted or cancelled must fail with 409 CONFLICT "Quote in status '<status>' cannot be edited" ("cannot be
  cancelled" for DELETE) and change nothing; a missing quote must answer 404 NOT_FOUND (resource "Quote").
- **SPEC-13.1368**: A change to billing_contact_id, title, summary, description, valid_until, currency, tax_amount,
  tax_rate_id or lines through PUT /quotes/{id}, and any add, update or delete of a single line, must be refused with
  409 CONFLICT "Quote in status '<status>' cannot be edited" unless the stored status is draft or rejected; a
  status-only change must still be accepted from submitted and approved.
- **SPEC-13.1369**: PUT /quotes/{id} must accept a status change only to draft, submitted, approved, rejected or
  cancelled; sent, accepted, declined, expired and converted must be refused with 409 CONFLICT "Status '<status>' is not
  settable here; it is written by the send, portal, or convert route".
- **SPEC-13.1370**: PUT /quotes/{id} setting status approved must be refused with 409 CONFLICT "This quote is waiting on
  an approval; approve it from the approvals queue, or cancel the approval to decide it here" while any staff-addressed
  approval of the quote is pending; setting rejected must not be refused for that reason.
- **SPEC-13.1371**: PUT /quotes/{id} naming a billing_contact_id must refuse a contact that does not belong to the
  quote's company.
- **SPEC-13.1372**: PUT /quotes/{id} must keep every omitted header field, so a field cannot be reset to null; a lines
  array must replace the whole line set; a given tax_amount must clear the frozen tax rate and keep the amount, a named
  tax_rate_id must set the rate; totals must always be recomputed; an Update audit row with before and after snapshots
  must be written in the same transaction; and the full quote must be returned.
- **SPEC-13.1373**: DELETE /quotes/{id} must set the quote's status to cancelled and keep the row and its lines, write
  an audit row of action Delete with before and after snapshots in the same transaction, and return an empty success.
- **SPEC-13.1374**: POST /quotes/{id}/lines, PUT /quotes/{id}/lines/{line_id} and DELETE /quotes/{id}/lines/{line_id}
  must change the line, recompute totals and return the full quote; a line_id that is not a line of that quote must
  answer 404 NOT_FOUND (resource "Quote line") and change nothing, and the line type must be one of service, product,
  labour, expense, adjustment, discount.
- **SPEC-13.1375**: PUT /quotes/{id}/lines/{line_id} must store the request's line_type, description, quantity,
  unit_price, sort_order and is_taxable, with the line total equal to quantity multiplied by unit_price.
- **SPEC-13.1376**: POST /quotes/{id}/send must fail with 409 CONFLICT "Quote in status '<status>' cannot be sent; it
  must be internally approved first" unless the stored status is approved, and with 404 NOT_FOUND (resource "Quote") for
  a missing quote.
- **SPEC-13.1377**: POST /quotes/{id}/send must treat an absent body as delivery method email, and must fail with a
  validation error on field delivery.note when the method is other and the note is absent or blank; notes are trimmed
  before use.
- **SPEC-13.1378**: Sending by email must resolve the recipient as the quote's billing contact or, failing that, the
  company's billing contact; it must fail with 409 CONFLICT naming the company when there is none ("...has no billing
  contact..."), and with 409 CONFLICT when the contact has no non-blank email address ("...billing contact has no email
  address..."), leaving the quote approved.
- **SPEC-13.1379**: A successful send must set status sent, sent_at to now, delivery_method, and delivered_by_id to the
  calling user if not yet set; for email it must also set billing_contact_id to the recipient, clear delivery_note, and
  record emailed_to (trimmed address) and emailed_at; for postal and other it must store the trimmed note as
  delivery_note, send no mail and leave billing_contact_id and emailed_to untouched.
- **SPEC-13.1380**: An email send must dispatch the quote.sent notification event, inside the send transaction and
  before commit, with the recipient address, quote number, title, total, valid_until, a portal login link to the quote,
  and the sender organisation's name and contact line.
- **SPEC-13.1381**: If the quote email cannot be sent, because no notification service is configured, no portal origin
  is configured, the organisation identity cannot be read, or the dispatch fails, send must answer with an
  external-service error for service "mail" (the dispatch failure text must name the address and say the quote has not
  been sent), roll the transition back so the quote stays approved, log a warning with the quote id, number, address and
  error, and record a quote.send_failed audit row (quote number, method email, address, reason) in a separate
  transaction; a failure to write that audit row must be logged at error and must not replace the mail error.
- **SPEC-13.1382**: A successful send must write two audit rows in its transaction: the whole-row Update diff and a
  named quote.sent row carrying event, method, note and emailed_to.
- **SPEC-13.1383**: GET /quotes/{id}/delivery-options must return the methods email, postal and other; when the quote is
  not approved all three must be unavailable with the reason "Quote in status '<status>' cannot be sent; it must be
  internally approved first"; when approved, postal and other must be available, and email must be available with the
  trimmed recipient address only when notifications are configured and the quote's or company's billing contact exists
  with a non-blank email, else unavailable with the reason "Email is not configured on this server", "No billing contact
  is set", "Billing contact no longer exists" or "Billing contact is missing email address" as applicable.
- **SPEC-13.1384**: POST /quotes/{id}/accept and POST /quotes/{id}/decline called by a staff caller must answer 403
  FORBIDDEN "Staff use the approvals endpoint, not accept/decline."; a contact caller must hold quotes:accept, and the
  optional body notes field must be passed through.
- **SPEC-13.1385**: A client decision on a quote of another company, or on a quote not in a client-visible status, must
  answer 404 NOT_FOUND (resource "Quote") before any state check, so a 409 never reveals that quote exists.
- **SPEC-13.1386**: A client decision must be accepted only while the quote's effective status (after read-time expiry
  on the contact's today) is sent; otherwise it must fail with 409 CONFLICT "Quote in status '<status>' can no longer be
  decided" and change nothing, so a quote past valid_until, or one already decided, cannot be decided.
- **SPEC-13.1387**: An accept must set status accepted and a decline status declined, with decided_at now,
  decided_by_contact_id the deciding contact and decision_notes the given notes, and write an Update audit row with
  before and after snapshots in the same transaction.
- **SPEC-13.1388**: After the decision commits, the service must dispatch quote.accepted or quote.declined addressed to
  the quote's requested_by_id; a dispatch failure must be logged at warn with the quote id and must not undo or fail the
  decision, and no dispatch happens when no notification service is configured.
- **SPEC-13.1389**: POST /quotes/{id}/convert must fail with 409 CONFLICT "Quote in status '<status>' cannot be
  converted; the client must accept it first" unless the stored status is accepted, and with 404 NOT_FOUND (resource
  "Quote") for a missing quote.
- **SPEC-13.1390**: Converting a quote already converted with a linked project must return the quote with the same
  converted_project_id, create no second project and report success; concurrent conversions must be serialised by a row
  lock on the quote so only one project is created.
- **SPEC-13.1391**: A conversion must create in one transaction a project with the quote's title as name, its
  description, its company, project_type client, status planning, is_billable true, budget_amount equal to the quote
  total, billing_method from the request (default fixed_price), and project_manager_id, start_date, target_end_date and
  budget_hours from the request; set the quote to converted with converted_project_id; and write a Create audit row for
  the project and an Update audit row for the quote. A failure of any step must leave the quote unconverted.
- **SPEC-13.1392**: The convert body must be optional, and must be rejected with a validation error when target_end_date
  is earlier than start_date (code target_end_date_before_start_date) or billing_method is not fixed_price,
  time_and_materials or not_billable (code invalid_billing_method).
- **SPEC-13.1393**: A decision on a staff-addressed approval must move a quote only out of submitted: to rejected as
  soon as any staff-addressed approval is rejected, else to approved when none is pending, else not at all; for a quote
  in any other status the decision must be recorded and the quote left unchanged.
- **SPEC-13.1394**: apply_decision must lock the quote row, count only the quote's approvals with no approver_contact_id
  (contact-addressed approvals must not count or move the quote), run inside the approval's transaction so the count
  includes the decision being made, and return None without error when the quote no longer exists.
- **SPEC-13.1395**: has_pending_staff_approval must be true exactly when at least one approval of the quote with no
  approver_contact_id has status pending.

## 14. Time, mileage, expenses and opportunities

Normative requirements for `src/modules/time_tracking/`, `mileage_tracking/`, `expenses/` and `opportunities/`, cited as `// SPEC-14.<n>`.

### 14.1 Time tracking

- **SPEC-14.1**: Every time-tracking route (work types, time entries, timesheets, timers, rounding rules, work day,
  mileage entries) must require an authenticated caller whose tenant has the `time_tracking` module enabled; otherwise
  the request must fail with 404 so a disabled module reads as an unmounted route. Every query must be scoped to the
  caller's tenant, so an id belonging to another tenant must answer 404 exactly as an unknown id does.
- **SPEC-14.2**: Every timesheet route and every work-day route (`/timesheets*`, `/workday*`) must additionally require
  the `timesheets` module to be enabled for the tenant; otherwise the request must fail with 404.
- **SPEC-14.3**: `GET /work-types` must return the tenant's work types ordered by `sort_order` then `name`, paginated,
  with the total count; a `sort` parameter must be refused with 422 because the endpoint supports no sorting.
- **SPEC-14.4**: Creating, updating and deleting a work type must require the `super_admin` or `admin` role (403
  otherwise). A work type name must be 1 to 100 characters and `default_rate` must be a non-negative value with at most
  2 decimals below 100,000,000, or the request must fail with 422. `default_billable` and `is_active` must default to
  true and `sort_order` to 0 when omitted.
- **SPEC-14.5**: Creating a work type must write an audit row in the same transaction as the insert. Updating or
  deleting a work type that does not exist in the tenant must fail with 404 "Work type"; update must replace every field
  of the work type with the request values.
- **SPEC-14.6**: `POST /time-entries` by a caller who is not `super_admin` or `admin` must record the entry against the
  caller's own user id, replacing any other `user_id` in the body without raising an error. An admin may name any
  `user_id`.
- **SPEC-14.7**: A time entry request must be refused with 422 when `duration_minutes` or `worked_minutes` is outside
  1..=1440, when `billable_minutes` is outside 0..=1440, or when `hourly_rate` is negative, has more than 2 decimals or
  is 100,000,000 or more.
- **SPEC-14.8**: When creating an entry, the worked minutes must be taken from `worked_minutes`, else
  `duration_minutes`, else the whole minutes between `end_time` and `start_time`; the same value must be stored as both
  `worked_minutes` and `duration_minutes` and must never be rounded. An `end_time` before `start_time` must fail with
  400 "end_time must be after start_time", and an entry with none of the three sources must fail with 400 "Either
  duration_minutes or (start_time, end_time) must be supplied".
- **SPEC-14.9**: Creating an entry must verify that the work type, and the company and ticket when given, belong to the
  caller's tenant, failing with 404 "Work type", "Company" or "Ticket" otherwise; starting a timer must apply the same
  check to the ticket, company and work type it names, and updating an entry must apply it to a supplied ticket.
- **SPEC-14.10**: The entry kind of a created entry must be the requested `client` or `employee` (surrounding whitespace
  ignored, blank meaning not requested) and any other value must fail with 400 "entry_kind must be one of client,
  employee (got `<value>`)". When not requested it must be `client` if a ticket, project or task is set; otherwise
  `employee` if no company is set or the company is the tenant's own internal company; otherwise `client`.
- **SPEC-14.11**: An `employee` entry that names a ticket, project or task must fail with 400 "Employee time carries no
  ticket, project, task or contract; it is the MSP's own time, not a client's", and a `client` entry without a
  `company_id` must fail with 400 "Client work needs a company_id; log it as employee time if it belongs to no client".
- **SPEC-14.12**: An `employee` entry must always be stored as not billable with 0 billable minutes, no total amount,
  billing status `not_billed` and no contract, whatever the request says.
- **SPEC-14.13**: The work category of an entry must default to `ticketed` when a ticket is set, else `project` when a
  project is set, else `general`. A supplied category outside `ticketed`, `project`, `general` must fail with 400
  "work_category must be one of ticketed, project, general (got `<value>`)", and `ticketed` without a ticket must fail
  with 400 "work_category 'ticketed' requires a ticket_id".
- **SPEC-14.14**: The billable minutes of a billable entry must be the explicit `billable_minutes` when supplied, else
  the worked minutes passed through the tenant's default rounding rule, or the worked minutes unchanged when the tenant
  has no default rule; a non-billable entry must have 0 billable minutes.
- **SPEC-14.15**: A rounding rule must first raise the minutes to `minimum_minutes`, then round the result to a multiple
  of `increment_minutes`: `down` truncates, `up` rounds up, `nearest` rounds an exact midpoint up; an increment of 0 or
  less must leave the floored value unchanged.
- **SPEC-14.16**: Creating or updating an entry must be refused with 400 when the user's other minutes on the entry's
  date plus the entry's worked minutes exceed the tenant cap, whose message starts "Day total would exceed the <N>h/day
  cap (<M> minutes)" and states the minutes left. The cap is the `time_tracking/max_hours_per_day` setting in whole
  hours 1 to 24, defaulting to 24 hours. On update the entry itself must be excluded from the existing total and the
  check must use the target date.
- **SPEC-14.17**: The hourly rate of an entry must be the request's `hourly_rate`, else the work type's `default_rate`,
  else none; `total_amount` must be the rate times billable minutes divided by 60 for a billable entry and none
  otherwise.
- **SPEC-14.18**: A new billable entry must have billing status `ready_to_bill` as soon as it is created, a non-billable
  one `not_billed`. An update must set `ready_to_bill` or `not_billed` from the resulting billability, except that an
  entry already `billed` must stay `billed`.
- **SPEC-14.19**: A billable `client` entry with a company must be linked to that company's active contract that has a
  `block_hours` item and covers the entry date (start date on or before it, end date empty or on or after it),
  preferring the latest start date and then the lowest id; any other entry must have no contract.
- **SPEC-14.20**: After an entry linked to a contract is committed, its `duration_minutes` divided by 60 must be drawn
  from the contract's hour balance exactly once, recording the applied hours and the balance row on the entry. An entry
  fully covered by the allotment must become `prepaid`; an entry exceeding it must stay `ready_to_bill` and record the
  overage hours and the contract item's rate (none when it names none), and the server must log the overage at info. The
  draw must be skipped for an entry that is not billable, not `client`, has no contract or has no minutes.
- **SPEC-14.21**: The claim on the draw (`hours_consumed` still empty) must be taken under a row lock in the same
  transaction as the balance draw, so concurrent or repeated calls for one entry must draw at most once.
- **SPEC-14.22**: Updating or deleting a time entry must return 404 "Time entry" for an unknown id before any permission
  check, and must fail with 403 "Cannot edit another user's time entry" or "Cannot delete another user's time entry"
  when the caller is not `super_admin` or `admin` and the entry belongs to another user.
- **SPEC-14.23**: An update must keep the stored value of `date`, `notes`, `work_type_id` and `task_id` when omitted. It
  must set `ticket_id` and `project_id` to exactly the request values (an omitted one becomes null) and re-derive
  `work_category` from them. `entry_kind` and `company_id` must never change. Attaching a ticket to an `employee` entry
  must fail with 400.
- **SPEC-14.24**: On update the worked minutes must be the request's `worked_minutes`, else `duration_minutes`, else the
  minutes between the resulting start and end times, else the current worked minutes. Billable minutes must be the
  request's value, else the stored value, else derived like a new entry. The total must be recomputed from the resulting
  rate and billable minutes.
- **SPEC-14.25**: After an update the entry's earlier draw must be released back to the exact balance row that supplied
  it and the entry must be drawn again on its new figures, with the covering contract re-derived for the resulting date.
- **SPEC-14.26**: Deleting a time entry must first release any hours it drew back to the contract balance, then delete
  the row, failing with 404 "Time entry" when it does not exist.
- **SPEC-14.27**: `GET /time-entries/{id}` must return the entry with its user name, work type name, ticket number and
  title, project name and task title, failing with 404 "Time entry" when absent; a missing `worked_minutes` must be
  reported as the entry's `duration_minutes`.
- **SPEC-14.28**: `GET /time-entries` must return every entry of the tenant (not only the caller's) filtered by any of
  `user_id`, `ticket_id`, `project_id`, `date_from` and `date_to` (both dates inclusive), ordered by date descending
  unless an allowed `sort` is given, with a total that counts only the filtered set; an unknown `sort` field must be
  refused with 422.
- **SPEC-14.29**: `GET /time-entries/summary` must return `{"minutes": <n>}` as the sum of `duration_minutes` of the
  entries matching the same filters whose approval status is not `rejected`, and 0 when none match.
- **SPEC-14.30**: `GET /timesheets` must return one row per user and ISO week (Monday start) with the sum of worked
  minutes, the sum of billable minutes, the entry count and an approval status, ordered by week descending then user id,
  paginated. The status must be `rejected` if any entry of the week is rejected, else `approved` if all are approved,
  else `pending` if any is pending, else `draft`; the decider, decision time and a non-empty rejection reason of the
  week must be included when present.
- **SPEC-14.31**: The timesheet `status` filter must accept `pending`, `approved`, `rejected`, `all` or blank, and any
  other value must fail with 400 "Unknown timesheet status filter `<value>`; expected one of pending | approved |
  rejected | all". When `from` is given the span must run from the Monday of `from` to the week of `to` (default `from`)
  and `week` must be ignored; `to` before `from` must fail with 400 "`to` must be on or after `from`", and a span over
  26 weeks must fail with 400 "Timesheet range capped at 26 weeks; got <n>".
- **SPEC-14.32**: `POST /timesheets/{user_id}/{week_start}/submit` must move every entry of that user in the week of
  `week_start` that is not approved to `pending` and return the week summary, with a zero-total summary of status
  `draft` when the week has no entries; a caller who is not `super_admin` or `admin` and names another user must fail
  with 403 "Cannot submit another user's timesheet".
- **SPEC-14.33**: `POST /timesheets/{user_id}/{week_start}/withdraw` must move that week's `pending` entries back to
  `draft` and return the summary; it must fail with 409 "Cannot withdraw an approved timesheet" when any entry of the
  week is approved, and with 403 "Cannot withdraw another user's timesheet" for a non-admin naming another user.
- **SPEC-14.34**: `POST /timesheets/{user_id}/{week_start}/approve` must require the `super_admin`, `admin` or `manager`
  role (403 otherwise), set the week's `pending` entries to `approved` recording the approver and time, and return the
  summary; repeating it must change nothing. Approval must not change an entry's billing status and must not draw
  contract hours.
- **SPEC-14.35**: `POST /timesheets/{user_id}/{week_start}/reject` must require the `super_admin`, `admin` or `manager`
  role and a `reason` of 1 to 1000 characters (422 otherwise), set the week's `pending` entries to `rejected` with the
  reason, reviewer and time, leave entries in any other status untouched, and return the summary.
- **SPEC-14.36**: `GET /timers/active` must list the tenant's active timers newest first, paginated; a caller who is not
  `super_admin` or `admin` must see only their own timer, while an admin may narrow by `user_id`.
- **SPEC-14.37**: `POST /timers/start` must create a timer for the caller and fail with 409 "User already has an active
  timer; stop it first" when one exists, including when a concurrent start wins the unique constraint.
- **SPEC-14.38**: `POST /timers/{id}/stop` must act only on the caller's own timer (an unknown or foreign id fails with
  404 "Active timer"), create a time entry covering the elapsed time, and delete the timer in the same transaction. The
  duration must be the elapsed whole minutes with a minimum of 1, passed through the default rounding rule, and the
  entry must be dated with the timer owner's local day.
- **SPEC-14.39**: When stopping a timer without a work type the entry must use the tenant's first active work type by
  `sort_order`, and when none exists the stop must fail with a configuration error stating "Cannot stop timer: tenant
  has no active work_types and timer set none". The company must be the timer's, else the ticket's company, else none,
  in which case the entry is `employee` time. Billing, rate, contract and hour draw must follow the same rules as a
  manually created entry.
- **SPEC-14.40**: `GET /time-rounding-rules` must list the tenant's rules with the default rule first, then by name,
  paginated. Create, update and delete must require the `super_admin` or `admin` role; the name must be 1 to 100
  characters, `increment_minutes` 1 to 240 and `minimum_minutes` at least 0 (default 0), or the request must fail with
  422.
- **SPEC-14.41**: A rounding rule's `rounding_method` must be `up`, `down` or `nearest`, else the request must fail with
  400 "rounding_method `<value>` invalid; expected up | down | nearest". Saving a rule with `is_default` true must clear
  `is_default` on every other rule of the tenant in the same transaction, and updating or deleting an unknown rule must
  fail with 404 "Time rounding rule". Creating a rule must write an audit row.
- **SPEC-14.42**: `POST /workday/clock-in` must open a `work` segment for the caller on the body's `date` or, when
  absent, on today in the caller's own time zone; a missing body must be treated as an empty one. While the caller has
  any open segment of any date it must fail with 409 whose message names the open segment's date and elapsed time as
  "Already clocked in on <date> for <Xh Ym>..." (or "Already clocked in and on a break, on <date>..."), and a race lost
  to the one-open-segment constraint must fail with 409 "Already clocked in; clock out first".
- **SPEC-14.43**: `POST /workday/clock-out` must close the caller's open segment, work or break, at the current time and
  return it, failing with 409 "Not clocked in" when none is open.
- **SPEC-14.44**: `POST /workday/break/start` and `/workday/break/end` must fail with 404 "Break tracking" unless the
  tenant has enabled break tracking (off by default). Starting must close the open `work` segment and open a `break`
  segment on the same date at the same instant in one transaction, failing with 409 "Not clocked in; clock in first" or
  "Already on a break"; ending must close the open `break` and open a `work` segment likewise, failing with 409 "Not on
  a break" otherwise.
- **SPEC-14.45**: `GET /workday` must return the chosen day's segments in start order, whether the caller is clocked in
  or on a break, `clocked_minutes` (sum of `work` segments, an open one counting to now), `break_minutes`,
  `logged_minutes` (worked minutes of that user's entries on the date), `unlogged_minutes` as clocked minus logged, and
  a breakdown. The breakdown must group entries under a ticket line if they name a ticket, else a project line, else
  administrative if `employee`, else unattached, with tickets and projects sorted by minutes descending then id.
- **SPEC-14.46**: The day of `GET /workday` must be the requested `date`, else the date of the user's open segment, else
  today in the caller's time zone, and the response must say which of the three applied. A caller who is not
  `super_admin` or `admin` naming another `user_id` must fail with 403 "Cannot view another user's day"; an admin may
  name any user.
- **SPEC-14.47**: `PUT /workday/segments/{id}` must apply only the supplied `date`, `started_at` and `ended_at`, an
  explicit null `ended_at` reopening the segment, failing with 404 "Work day segment" for an unknown id and with 403
  "Not allowed to correct this work day segment" when the tenant's policy does not permit the caller. It must refuse
  with 400 a date more than one calendar day from the start's UTC date ("A segment's date must be the day it starts
  on"), an end before the start ("A segment cannot end before it starts") and an open segment starting in the future
  ("An open segment cannot start in the future"), and with 409 a reopen while another segment of that person is open.
  The change must be audited with before and after values in the same transaction.
- **SPEC-14.48**: `DELETE /workday/segments/{id}` must remove the segment (open or closed) under the same policy and
  errors as the correction, write an audit row with the removed values in the same transaction, and answer 204.
- **SPEC-14.49**: The segment correction policy is the tenant setting `timesheets/segment_editing` with values `off`
  (nobody may correct), `owner_or_admin` (the segment's user or a `super_admin`/`admin`) and `owner_or_manager` (the
  segment's user or a `super_admin`/`admin`/`manager`); an unset or unrecognised stored value must be treated as
  `owner_or_admin`.

### 14.2 Mileage tracking

- **SPEC-14.50**: `GET /mileage-entries` must return the tenant's mileage entries (not only the caller's) filtered by
  any of `user_id`, `ticket_id`, `project_id`, `date_from` and `date_to` (inclusive), ordered by date descending unless
  an allowed `sort` is given, with a total counting only the filtered set; an unknown `sort` field must be refused with
  422. `GET /mileage-entries/{id}` must fail with 404 "Mileage entry" when absent.
- **SPEC-14.51**: `POST /mileage-entries` by a caller who is not `super_admin` or `admin` must record the entry against
  the caller's own user id, replacing any other `user_id` without an error. `distance_miles` must be greater than 0,
  have at most 2 decimals and be below 1,000,000, and `rate_per_mile` must be non-negative with at most 4 decimals and
  below 10,000, or the request must fail with 422; a service-level distance of 0 or less must fail with 400
  "distance_miles must be greater than 0".
- **SPEC-14.52**: Creating a mileage entry must require `company_id` and verify that the company, and the ticket when
  given, belong to the caller's tenant, failing with 404 "Company" or "Ticket" otherwise.
- **SPEC-14.53**: The rate of a created mileage entry must be the request's `rate_per_mile`, else the per-mile rate of
  the tenant's default rate card, else none; `total_amount` must be rate times distance for a billable entry and none
  for a non-billable one. `is_billable` must default to true.
- **SPEC-14.54**: A created billable mileage entry must have billing status `ready_to_bill` and a non-billable one
  `not_billed`. Creating an entry must write an audit row in the same transaction as the insert.
- **SPEC-14.55**: Updating or deleting a mileage entry must return 404 "Mileage entry" for an unknown id before any
  permission check, and 403 "Cannot edit another user's mileage entry" or "Cannot delete another user's mileage entry"
  when the caller is not `super_admin` or `admin` and the entry belongs to another user.
- **SPEC-14.56**: A mileage update must keep the stored `date`, `start_address`, `end_address`, `notes` and `task_id`
  when omitted, but set `ticket_id` and `project_id` to exactly the request values (an omitted one becomes null). The
  resulting distance must be greater than 0 (400 otherwise), a supplied ticket must belong to the tenant (404 "Ticket"),
  and the total must be recomputed from the resulting rate, distance and billability. The update must not change the
  billing status.

### 14.3 Expenses

- **SPEC-14.57**: Every vendor, expense category and bill route must require the `billing` module to be enabled (404
  otherwise) and a `super_admin`, `admin` or `finance` caller (403 otherwise). Expense claim routes must require the
  `billing` module and, except where stated, any authenticated member of the tenant.
- **SPEC-14.58**: `GET /vendors` must list the tenant's vendors ordered by lower-cased name, paginated, refusing a
  `sort` parameter with 422; `GET /vendors/{id}` must fail with 404 "Vendor" when absent.
- **SPEC-14.59**: A vendor request must have a name of 1 to 200 characters, `account_number` up to 100,
  `default_currency` exactly 3 characters and `notes` up to 2000, or fail with 422. The service must store the name and
  account number trimmed and the currency trimmed and upper-cased, and update must overwrite every field, an omitted
  optional field becoming null.
- **SPEC-14.60**: Deleting a vendor referenced by a bill must fail with 409 "Cannot delete this vendor: it is still
  referenced by a bill", and an unknown vendor must fail with 404 "Vendor". Every vendor, category, bill, bill payment
  and expense create, update, delete or status change must write an audit row in the same transaction.
- **SPEC-14.61**: `GET /expense-categories` must list the tenant's categories ordered by lower-cased name, paginated (a
  `sort` parameter gives 422). Create and `PUT /expense-categories/{id}` must require a name of 1 to 100 characters,
  store it trimmed, default `is_active` to true, and fail with 409 "An expense category with that name already exists"
  on a name collision and 404 "Expense category" for an unknown id. No delete route exists.
- **SPEC-14.62**: Creating a bill must require 1 to 200 lines, a 3-character currency (stored upper-cased and trimmed),
  a `bill_number` up to 100 characters and notes up to 2000; each line needs a description of 1 to 500 characters, a
  `quantity_hundredths` of at least 1, a `unit_price_minor` and `tax_minor` of at least 0. A violation must fail with
  422, and an empty line list or non-3-letter currency reaching the service must fail with a validation error on `lines`
  or `currency`.
- **SPEC-14.63**: A created bill's line total must be `unit_price_minor * quantity_hundredths / 100` (integer division,
  truncated) plus the line's `tax_minor`, with the bill's `subtotal_minor` the sum of the untaxed line totals,
  `tax_minor` the sum of line taxes and `total_minor` their sum, all in minor units, and the bill and its lines must be
  committed in one transaction. A line `position` of 0 must be stored as its zero-based index.
- **SPEC-14.64**: Creating a bill for a vendor outside the tenant must fail with 404 "Vendor" and write nothing. A new
  bill must be stored with status `draft` and, on the local path, a null external provider and external bill id.
- **SPEC-14.65**: When the deployment has delegated bills enabled and the tenant has delegated Bills and expenses,
  creating a bill must verify the vendor (404 "Vendor"), raise the bill in the provider before the local transaction
  starts (using the issue date as due date when none is given) and store the provider name and external bill id on the
  row; a provider failure must fail the request and leave no local bill.
- **SPEC-14.66**: `POST /bills/{id}/approve` must move a `draft` bill to `approved`, and `POST /bills/{id}/void` must
  move a `draft` or `approved` bill to `void`; the row must be locked during the check, an unknown id must fail with 404
  "Bill", and any other source status must fail with 409.
- **SPEC-14.67**: A refused bill transition must answer 409 with an actionable message: for `paid` "This bill has
  already been paid, so moving it would misstate what was settled. Issue a credit or adjustment instead."; for `void`
  "This bill is void, so there is nothing left to move. Raise a new bill instead."; for the same target status "This
  bill is already '<to>'."; otherwise "This bill is '<status>', so it cannot move to '<to>'. No remedy is defined yet
  for this transition."
- **SPEC-14.68**: `GET /bills` must list the tenant's bills ordered by issue date then creation time descending,
  paginated (a `sort` parameter gives 422). The optional `status` (up to 20 characters, blank ignored) must filter by
  exact status, an unknown value returning an empty page, and `q` (up to 200 characters, blank ignored) must match the
  bill number or the vendor name case-insensitively as a substring; the total must count the filtered set.
- **SPEC-14.69**: `GET /bills/{id}` must return the bill with its lines ordered by position then creation time, failing
  with 404 "Bill" when absent.
- **SPEC-14.70**: `POST /bills/{id}/payments` must refuse with 422 an `amount_minor` of 0 or less (message naming that a
  vendor refund is a credit) and a `payment_method` (trimmed, case-insensitive) outside check, credit_card, ach, wire,
  cash, other. It must fail with 404 "Bill" for an unknown id, with 409 "A bill is paid after it is approved, and this
  one is <status>. Approve it first." for a draft bill, with 409 "This bill was voided, so there is nothing to pay." for
  a void bill, and with 409 "That is more than this bill has left to pay (<remaining> remaining of <total>)..." when the
  amount exceeds total minus paid.
- **SPEC-14.71**: Recording a payment must insert the payment row and recompute the bill's `paid_minor` as the sum of
  its payments in one transaction under a row lock; the bill's status must become `paid` once `paid_minor` reaches
  `total_minor` and otherwise stay unchanged. That recompute must be the only writer of `paid_minor` and of the move to
  `paid`.
- **SPEC-14.72**: When the deployment has delegated bills enabled and the bill carries a recognised external provider
  and id, `POST /bills/{id}/payments` must record the payment in the provider first (a provider failure failing the
  request with no local row) and append "Recorded in <provider> as payment <id>." to the payment notes.
- **SPEC-14.73**: Reconciling a provider's running paid total for a delegated bill (webhook path) must resolve the bill
  by tenant, provider and external id, record nothing when the bill is not found, is neither `approved` nor `paid`
  (logging a warning), or the provider total does not exceed `paid_minor`; otherwise it must record the difference as a
  payment of method `other`, capped at the remaining balance with a warning logging the excess, and must never push the
  payment back to the provider.
- **SPEC-14.74**: `GET /bills/{id}/payments` must return the bill's payments by payment date then creation time, newest
  first, failing with 404 "Bill" when the bill is absent.
- **SPEC-14.75**: `POST /expenses` must create an expense in status `draft` owned by the caller, require 1 to 200 lines
  (each with a description of 1 to 500 characters, `amount_minor` and `tax_minor` of at least 0), a 3-character currency
  stored upper-cased and trimmed, and notes up to 2000, or fail with 422 (or a validation error on `lines` or `currency`
  at the service). Subtotal must be the sum of line amounts, tax the sum of line taxes and total their sum, committed
  with the lines in one transaction.
- **SPEC-14.76**: `GET /expenses` must list only the caller's own claims unless the caller is `super_admin`, `admin` or
  `finance`, who see every claim; the scope must not be settable by a query parameter and the total must count the same
  scope. Results must be ordered by `incurred_on` then creation time descending, paginated (a `sort` parameter gives
  422), filtered by exact `status` (unknown value giving an empty page) and by `q` matching claim notes or line
  descriptions case-insensitively.
- **SPEC-14.77**: `GET /expenses/{id}` must return the claim with its lines ordered by position, failing with 404
  "Expense" for an unknown id before any ownership check and with 403 "That expense claim belongs to somebody else" when
  the caller is not finance-capable and not the claim's submitter.
- **SPEC-14.78**: `POST /expenses/{id}/submit` must be allowed for the claim's submitter or a finance-capable caller
  (403 "That expense claim belongs to somebody else" otherwise, 404 for an unknown id) and move a `draft` claim to
  `submitted`; approve, reject and reimburse must require the `super_admin`, `admin` or `finance` role.
- **SPEC-14.79**: Approve must move a `submitted` claim to `approved` recording the approver and approval time, reject
  must move a `submitted` claim to `rejected`, and reimburse must move an `approved` claim to `reimbursed` recording the
  reimbursement time; each must lock the row, and any other source status must fail with 409.
- **SPEC-14.80**: A refused expense transition must answer 409 with: for `rejected` "This expense was rejected, which is
  terminal. File a new expense instead."; for `reimbursed` "A reimbursed expense is immutable. File a reversing expense
  instead."; for the same target "This expense is already '<to>'."; from `draft` "This expense has not been submitted
  yet, so it cannot move to '<to>'. Submit it first."; from `submitted` to `reimbursed` "This expense has not been
  approved yet, so there is nothing to pay back. Approve it first."; from `approved` to `submitted` "This expense is
  already approved, which is past submission. There is nothing to submit."; otherwise "This expense is '<status>', so it
  cannot move to '<to>'. No remedy is defined yet for this transition."
- **SPEC-14.81**: When bills delegation is enabled for the deployment and the tenant, reimbursing a claim must confirm
  under a row lock that it is `approved` (committing before the provider call), record it in the provider as a payment
  dated today, and store the provider name and external expense id on the claim with the reimbursement; a provider
  failure must fail the request and leave the claim `approved`. Other transitions must not alter the stored provider
  pair.

### 14.4 Opportunities

- **SPEC-14.82**: All `/crm/opportunities` routes must require an authenticated caller of any role in the tenant (no
  module gate), except `DELETE /crm/opportunities/{id}`, which must require the `super_admin`, `admin` or `manager` role
  (403 otherwise). A body that fails validation must be refused with 422.
- **SPEC-14.83**: `POST /crm/opportunities` must require `company_id` and a `title` of 1 to 255 characters, return 201
  with the created opportunity, and record the caller as creator. The company must belong to the tenant and a given
  contact must belong to the tenant, otherwise the request must fail with 422 naming `company_id` ("company does not
  exist in this tenant") or `contact_id` ("contact does not exist in this tenant").
- **SPEC-14.84**: The stage of an opportunity must be one of `lead`, `qualified`, `proposal`, `negotiation`, `won`,
  `lost`, and an unknown stage must fail with 422 "unknown stage `<value>`; accepted: <list>". A new opportunity must
  default to `lead` and must be refused with 422 when created in `won` or `lost` ("an opportunity is created open; close
  it through the close endpoint").
- **SPEC-14.85**: The currency of a created or updated opportunity must default to `USD` on create, be stored
  upper-cased and be exactly 3 bytes long, otherwise the request must fail with 422 "currency must be a 3-letter ISO
  4217 code".
- **SPEC-14.86**: `GET /crm/opportunities` must return all non-deleted opportunities of the tenant, newest `updated_at`
  first, unpaginated, narrowed by `company_id`, by `stage` (unknown stage giving 422) and by `closed` (true meaning a
  close time is set, false meaning none). `GET /crm/opportunities/{id}` must fail with 404 "Opportunity" for an unknown
  or soft-deleted id.
- **SPEC-14.87**: `PUT /crm/opportunities/{id}` must apply only the supplied fields among `contact_id`, `title`,
  `value_amount`, `currency`, `stage`, `expected_close_date`, `quote_id` and `notes`, an explicit null clearing the
  nullable ones, and must refresh `updated_at`. A stage of `won` or `lost` must be refused with 422 ("close an
  opportunity through the close endpoint rather than the update path") and a `title` outside 1 to 255 characters with
  422.
- **SPEC-14.88**: Updating a closed opportunity must fail with 400 "A closed opportunity is immutable. Open a new one to
  record follow-up work.", including when a concurrent close makes the guarded write affect no row. A supplied
  `quote_id` must belong to the tenant, else 422 "quote does not exist in this tenant".
- **SPEC-14.89**: `POST /crm/opportunities/{id}/close` must require `outcome` of `won` or `lost` (else 422 "unknown
  outcome `<value>`; accepted: won, lost") and in one write set both `stage` and `outcome` to the outcome and
  `closed_at` to now, failing with 400 "This opportunity is already closed." when already closed, including a lost
  concurrent close, and 404 for an unknown id.
- **SPEC-14.90**: On a `won` close a given `quote_id` must belong to the tenant (else 422 "quote does not exist in this
  tenant") and replace the stored link; on a `lost` close, or a `won` close without `quote_id`, the existing quote link
  must be kept.
- **SPEC-14.91**: `DELETE /crm/opportunities/{id}` must soft-delete by setting `deleted_at`, answer 204, and fail with
  404 "Opportunity" when the opportunity is unknown or already deleted; a deleted opportunity must no longer be returned
  by any read.

## 15. Remaining modules

Normative requirements for `src/modules/contacts/`, `contact_sync/`, `assets/`, `asset_catalog/`, `knowledge_base/`, `documentation/`, `integrations/`, `rmm/`, `reports/`, `saved_reports/`, `dashboards/`, `settings/`, `seed/`, `branding/`, `features/`, `status/`, `data_transfer/` and `search/`, cited as `// SPEC-15.<n>`.

### 15.1 Companies and contacts

- **SPEC-15.1**: The contacts router must be mounted at `/api/v1/contacts`, serving companies (`/companies`), contacts
  (`/contacts`), sites (`/sites`), the company-industry lookup (`/company-industries`) and the portal-access lifecycle
  beneath it. Every handler must take the tenant from the authenticated staff caller and never from the request.
- **SPEC-15.2**: A request that carries a decoded contact-plane session must be answered `403` with the message "The
  Companies + Contacts CRM is staff-only." on every route of the contacts router, reads included, before any handler or
  role extractor runs. A request with no contact session must pass through to the handler's own authentication.
- **SPEC-15.3**: `GET /companies` must require an authenticated staff caller, validate the filter (a violated length cap
  is a `422`), and return a paginated envelope of company responses for the caller's tenant, each enriched with the
  rollup fields of SPEC-15.30 in one follow-up query per page.
- **SPEC-15.4**: `GET /companies/{company_id}` must return the enriched company, `404` ("Company not found") when the id
  does not exist in the caller's tenant, including when it exists in another tenant.
- **SPEC-15.5**: `POST /companies` and `PUT /companies/{company_id}` must validate the body (`422` on a violation)
  before calling the service and must return the stored company with status `200`.
- **SPEC-15.6**: `GET /companies/{company_id}/deletion-preview` must be open to any authenticated staff caller and not
  require the manager role that deletion requires.
- **SPEC-15.7**: `DELETE /companies/{company_id}`, `DELETE /contacts/{contact_id}` and `DELETE /sites/{site_id}` must
  require the `super_admin`, `admin` or `manager` role and answer `403` to any other staff role.
- **SPEC-15.8**: `GET /companies/{company_id}/contacts`, `GET /companies/{company_id}/sites` and `GET
  /company-industries` must reject any `sort` parameter with a `422` naming `sort`, and must reject `per_page` above 100
  with a `422`, rather than ignoring either.
- **SPEC-15.9**: `GET /companies/website-probe?url=<value>` must be a static route that resolves ahead of
  `/companies/{company_id}`, and `GET /contacts/field-values` and `GET /contacts/portal-roles` must likewise resolve
  ahead of `/contacts/{contact_id}`.
- **SPEC-15.10**: `GET /companies/website-probe` must be limited to 30 requests per minute per tenant. Over the limit it
  must answer `429` with a `Retry-After` header of at least 1 second, the body message "Too many website probes, please
  try again shortly" and a warn log naming the tenant and the wait.
- **SPEC-15.11**: When the website probe's HTTP client could not be built at startup, the router must log the cause at
  `error` once and `GET /companies/website-probe` must answer `500` ("The website probe is unavailable.") for every
  request that passes the rate limit; it must not report the site as unreachable.
- **SPEC-15.12**: `GET /companies/website-probe` must read and write no tenant data and must answer `200` for both a
  reachable and an unreachable site; input that cannot be a website must be a `400`, not a `200`.
- **SPEC-15.13**: `GET /company-industries` must be open to any authenticated staff caller. `POST /company-industries`,
  `PUT /company-industries/{id}` and `DELETE /company-industries/{id}` must require the `super_admin` or `admin` role
  and answer `403` otherwise.
- **SPEC-15.14**: `GET /contacts/portal-roles`, `GET` and `PUT /contacts/{contact_id}/portal-roles`, `POST
  /contacts/{contact_id}/grant-portal-access`, `POST /contacts/{contact_id}/resend-portal-invite`, `POST
  /contacts/{contact_id}/revoke-portal-access` and `POST /contacts/access-requests/{request_id}/resolve` must require
  the `super_admin`, `admin` or `manager` role and answer `403` otherwise.
- **SPEC-15.15**: `GET /contacts/{contact_id}/access-requests` must be open to any authenticated staff caller, so a
  technician can see what a customer asked for without being able to answer it.
- **SPEC-15.16**: `POST /contacts/{contact_id}/grant-portal-access` must validate the body (`422` on a violation) and
  return `200` with `portal_slug`, `portal_id` and `password_email_queued`. `POST .../resend-portal-invite`, `PUT
  .../portal-roles` and `POST .../revoke-portal-access` must return `204` with no body.
- **SPEC-15.17**: The company-scoped portal-role routes under `/companies/{company_id}/portal-roles` and
  `/companies/{company_id}/portal-roles/{role_id}` must require the `super_admin` or `admin` role. `GET` on the
  collection must return the tenant-wide roles plus that company's own roles; `POST` must create a role scoped to the
  path company.
- **SPEC-15.18**: `POST /companies/{company_id}/portal-roles` must answer `400` "company_id in body must equal the path
  company_id" when the body names a `company_id` different from the path, and must create no role.
- **SPEC-15.19**: `GET`, `PUT` and `DELETE /companies/{company_id}/portal-roles/{role_id}` must answer `404` ("Portal
  role not found") when the role is tenant-wide or belongs to a different company, before reading or changing it. A
  successful `DELETE` must answer `204`.

- **SPEC-15.20**: Creating a company must check, before any write, that `parent_company_id`, `account_manager_id` and
  `sla_id`, when present, each exist in the caller's tenant, and must answer `400` "Referenced {table} not found in this
  tenant" (`companies`, `users` or `sla_policies`) for the first missing one in that order. An absent id is not checked.
- **SPEC-15.21**: Foreign-id validation for a request must run as one query inside one tenant-scoped transaction however
  many ids are named, and must run no query when no id is named.
- **SPEC-15.22**: Creating a company must answer `409` "A company with this name already exists" when another company of
  the tenant has the same name after trimming and ignoring case, and must write no row. Companies of type `internal`
  must not count as the other company.
- **SPEC-15.23**: When a concurrent create or rename loses to the unique name index (Postgres `23505`), the service must
  answer the same `409` "A company with this name already exists", not a `500`.
- **SPEC-15.24**: Creating a company must store an absent `address` or `billing_address` as all-empty address parts,
  must write the company row and its `create` audit row in one transaction, and must return the stored company.
- **SPEC-15.25**: Updating a company must answer `404` "Company not found" when the id is not in the caller's tenant,
  and must write only the fields present in the request. A supplied `address` or `billing_address` must replace all six
  of its parts together.
- **SPEC-15.26**: Updating a company with `default_billing_contact_id` must answer `400` "Referenced contacts not found
  in this tenant" when the contact is not in the tenant, and `400` "default_billing_contact_id must reference a contact
  of this company" when the contact is neither the `company_id` of the contact row nor linked through a
  `contact_companies` row to this company.
- **SPEC-15.27**: Renaming a company must answer `409` "A company with this name already exists" when another company
  (not itself, not of type `internal`) has the same trimmed, case-insensitive name; re-saving the unchanged name must
  succeed.
- **SPEC-15.28**: A `branding` patch on a company update must be validated against the company-branding rules and
  checked to reference only the caller's own tenant and companies, with the validation error returned unchanged, and
  must be merged into the stored branding object (`||`): keys absent from the patch are kept and a key set to `null` is
  cleared.
- **SPEC-15.29**: Updating a company must write the update and an `update` audit row carrying the before and after
  snapshots in one transaction, and must name a contact as `default_billing_contact_id` only together with the invoice
  read grant of SPEC-15.112 in that same transaction, so a failed update grants nothing.
- **SPEC-15.30**: Company enrichment must set `account_manager_name` (first name, a space, last name), `contact_count`
  (distinct contacts linked through `contact_companies`), `site_count` and `open_ticket_count` (tickets with no
  `closed_at`) for each company in a page, and must do nothing for an empty page.
- **SPEC-15.31**: When a company has an `account_manager_id` but enrichment resolved no `account_manager_name`, the
  service must log the unresolved ids at `info` under the surface `contacts.companies.account_manager`, and must leave
  the name absent.
- **SPEC-15.32**: Listing companies must filter by `q` (case-insensitive substring of `name`), `company_type`, `status`
  and `account_manager_id`, combining the given filters with AND, and must return the total matching count alongside the
  page.
- **SPEC-15.33**: Listing companies without a `company_type` filter must exclude companies of type `internal`; an
  explicit `company_type` filter must return that type, and lookup by id must be unaffected.
- **SPEC-15.34**: Listing companies must order by `name` ascending by default, accept only the company sort fields
  declared in the shared sort list, and answer `422` naming `sort` for any other field.

- **SPEC-15.35**: Deleting the tenant's own company (the one named by `tenants.own_company_id`) must be refused with
  `400` "This is your organisation's own company record, which general and overhead time is logged against; it cannot be
  deleted", checked before any other refusal, and must change nothing.
- **SPEC-15.36**: Deleting a company that has any ticket, open or closed, must be refused with `400` "Cannot delete
  company: it has {n} ticket(s). Delete or reassign them first, or archive it instead by setting its status to Inactive,
  which keeps its history and takes it out of your active lists".
- **SPEC-15.37**: Deleting a company must unlink its contacts rather than delete them: remove their `contact_companies`
  rows for that company, give a contact that lost its primary link its oldest remaining link as primary (ordered by
  `created_at`, `sort_order`, `id`), and recompute each affected contact's mirror columns, all before the company row is
  deleted and in the same transaction.
- **SPEC-15.38**: When the company DELETE hits a foreign-key violation (Postgres `23503`), the service must answer `400`
  naming the blocking records by label and must not answer `500`. A retained blocker (invoices, payments, contracts,
  time entries, mileage entries) must say they are "kept as a permanent financial and billing record and must not be
  removed to allow a deletion"; a removable blocker (tickets, assets, quotes, stored credentials) must say "Remove or
  reassign them first"; both must end with the archive-instead alternative.
- **SPEC-15.39**: A foreign-key violation naming a constraint that is not in `COMPANY_BLOCKERS` must answer `400`
  "Cannot delete company: other records still reference it. Remove or reassign whatever can be moved, or archive it
  instead by setting its status to Inactive, which keeps its history and takes it out of your active lists".
- **SPEC-15.40**: `COMPANY_BLOCKERS` must list exactly these blocking record kinds, in this order: invoices, payments,
  contracts, time entries, mileage entries (all retained), then tickets, assets, quotes, stored credentials (not
  retained); `tickets` has no constraint name because the pre-flight count guards it.
- **SPEC-15.41**: A company delete must write a `delete` audit row with the before snapshot in the same transaction as
  the delete, and a refusal at any step must roll back the contact unlinking too.
- **SPEC-15.42**: Deleting a company id that does not exist in the caller's tenant must answer `404` "Company not found"
  and must write no audit row.
- **SPEC-15.43**: The deletion preview must answer `404` "Company not found" for an id not in the caller's tenant, and
  otherwise return `can_delete`, `is_own_company`, `blocking`, `unlinked` and `removed`, where `can_delete` is true only
  when `blocking` is empty and the company is not the tenant's own.
- **SPEC-15.44**: The deletion preview must list only record kinds with a count above zero. `blocking` must come from
  `COMPANY_BLOCKERS` with each entry's `retained` flag and must count tickets without a `closed_at` filter. `unlinked`
  must cover contacts, projects, appointments, running timers, RMM device mappings and sub-companies. `removed` must
  cover sites, request form links, contact company links, portal exports, portal login links and company-scoped portal
  roles.

- **SPEC-15.45**: Creating a contact must answer `422` on field `email` ("is required") when `email` is absent, empty or
  only whitespace, and must write nothing.
- **SPEC-15.46**: Creating a contact with `company_id` must answer `404` "Company not found" when the company is not in
  the caller's tenant; each company named in `companies` must exist in the tenant or the request must be refused `400`
  "Referenced companies not found in this tenant" before any row is written.
- **SPEC-15.47**: When a contact request carries an explicit `phones` list, the list must be authoritative and the
  scalar `phone`, `mobile` and `fax` in the same request must be ignored. Without a list, the scalars must become
  entries: a non-empty `phone` as a primary `work` entry, then `mobile`, then `fax`, never promoting the mobile or fax
  to primary.
- **SPEC-15.48**: Each phone entry must take its position in the list as `sort_order`; a list with no entry flagged
  primary must promote the first entry; an entry with no number must be refused `422` on field `phones[{index}].number`
  ("a phone number is required").
- **SPEC-15.49**: When a contact request carries an explicit `companies` list, the list must be authoritative; without
  one, a given `company_id` must become the contact's single primary link carrying the request's `title`.
- **SPEC-15.50**: Writing a contact's company links must upsert surviving links (keeping their `created_at`, updating
  `title`), delete links not in the new set, and make exactly one link primary: the flagged one, else the oldest link
  that already existed and survives, else the first entry of the list.
- **SPEC-15.51**: Writing a contact's company links must clear `default_billing_contact_id` on every company of the
  tenant that names the contact but is no longer in the contact's link set.
- **SPEC-15.52**: After every contact create, update, phone replace and company-delete unlink, the contact's mirror
  columns must be recomputed from the child rows: `phone` from the primary phone, `mobile` and `fax` from the first
  phone of that type by `sort_order`, `company_id` from the primary link (null when none), and the freeform
  `company_name` set to null whenever a primary link exists.
- **SPEC-15.53**: A contact must store a freeform `company_name` only when it has no company link; an empty freeform
  name must be stored as null; when a company is linked the stored freeform name must be null.
- **SPEC-15.54**: A new contact must store `timezone` "UTC" when none is given and `preferred_contact_method` "email".
- **SPEC-15.55**: Creating a contact with `create_portal_access` and both `company_id` and a non-blank email must answer
  `422` on field `email` when another portal-user contact of that company has the same email ignoring case, before the
  insert.
- **SPEC-15.56**: Creating a contact with `create_portal_access` must set `is_portal_user`, store a single-use setup
  token in the same transaction, and send the setup email only after the transaction commits; the new contact must not
  receive a password.
- **SPEC-15.57**: A portal setup token must be `{contact_id}.{secret}` with a 64-character alphanumeric random secret,
  must expire 72 hours after creation, and must be stored only as an Argon2 hash plus a SHA-256 lookup hash of the
  secret.
- **SPEC-15.58**: Sending the setup email after a create or update must skip, with a warn log naming the contact, when
  the contact has no email, has no company, or the company's Portal ID or slug cannot be ensured; a skip or a send
  failure must not undo the committed create or update.
- **SPEC-15.59**: Creating a contact must write the contact, its phones, its links, the recomputed mirrors, the optional
  portal flag and token, and a `create` audit row in one transaction, and must return the hydrated contact.
- **SPEC-15.60**: Importing a contact for contact sync must fail with an internal error ("an imported contact links no
  company and grants no portal access") when the request names `company_id`, a non-empty `companies` list or
  `create_portal_access`; otherwise it must create the contact on the caller's transaction with no company link and the
  freeform company name kept.
- **SPEC-15.61**: Replacing a contact's phones on the caller's transaction must resolve the list as SPEC-15.48 does,
  rewrite `contact_phones` wholesale, and recompute the mirrors.
- **SPEC-15.62**: Getting a contact must answer `404` "Contact not found" for an id not in the caller's tenant, and must
  return `company_name` as the linked company's current name, else the stored freeform name.
- **SPEC-15.63**: Every contact read must attach its phones (by `sort_order`), its company links (primary first, then by
  `created_at`, `sort_order`), its sync origin (the live link if any, else the most recent, with provider, source
  account email, `linked` and `deleted_in_source`) and its portal role names (alphabetical), using one query per child
  kind for the whole page.
- **SPEC-15.64**: Listing contacts must filter by `q` (case-insensitive substring of first name, last name or email),
  `company_id` (through any link, not only the primary), `contact_type`, `status` and `is_portal_user`, combining the
  given filters with AND, and must return the total matching count.
- **SPEC-15.65**: Listing contacts by `tags` must treat the value as comma-separated, trim each entry, drop blank ones,
  match a contact carrying any of them, and filter nothing when only blank entries remain.
- **SPEC-15.66**: Listing contacts by `origin` must return only contacts with no sync link for `manual`, and only
  contacts with a sync link of the matching provider for `google` and `vcard`.
- **SPEC-15.67**: Listing contacts must order by `last_name` ascending by default, accept only the contact sort fields
  declared in the shared sort list, and answer `422` naming `sort` for any other field.
- **SPEC-15.68**: `GET /contacts/field-values` must return the distinct non-empty values of `title` or `department` for
  the tenant, ordered by frequency descending then alphabetically, at most 20, filtered by the trimmed, case-insensitive
  substring `q` when it is non-blank.
- **SPEC-15.69**: Listing a company's contacts must include every contact linked to the company through any link, once
  each, ordered by `contact_type` then `last_name`, with the total count and hydrated children.
- **SPEC-15.70**: Updating a contact must answer `404` "Contact not found" for an unknown id, must refuse a `company_id`
  or `companies` entry outside the tenant with `400` "Referenced companies not found in this tenant", and must write
  only the fields present in the request.
- **SPEC-15.71**: Updating a contact with `company_id` must clear the stored freeform `company_name`; updating with an
  explicit `company_name` and no `company_id` must store it, with an empty string storing null.
- **SPEC-15.72**: Updating a contact's `phone`, `mobile` or `fax` without a `phones` list must rebuild the phone rows
  from the resulting scalars as SPEC-15.47 does; a scalar sent as an explicit `null` must clear that number, and an
  absent scalar must keep the existing value.
- **SPEC-15.73**: Updating a contact with a `companies` list must rewrite its links as SPEC-15.50 does; with only
  `company_id` the contact must end with that company as its sole primary link; with neither, links must be left as they
  are, except that a contact holding a `company_id` and no link rows must first receive the matching primary link.
- **SPEC-15.74**: Every contact update must recompute the mirror columns and must delete the contact's role assignments
  to company-scoped portal roles whose company differs from the contact's resulting `company_id`, leaving tenant-wide
  roles in place.
- **SPEC-15.75**: Updating a contact so that `is_portal_user` goes from false to true must store a single-use setup
  token in the transaction and send the setup email after commit; saving an already-portal contact with `true` again
  must not mint a token or send an email.
- **SPEC-15.76**: Updating a contact that has a contact-sync link must record the pre-edit values and lock the edited
  fields in the same transaction, so a later sync does not overwrite them.
- **SPEC-15.77**: A contact update must write the update and an `update` audit row with before and after snapshots in
  one transaction, and must return the hydrated contact.
- **SPEC-15.78**: Deleting a contact must answer `404` "Contact not found" for an unknown id, must detach every saved
  payment method on the provider side before deleting the row, and must delete the contact and write a `delete` audit
  row in one transaction.
- **SPEC-15.79**: When detaching a saved payment method fails, deleting the contact must return that error and leave the
  contact and its payment-method rows in place. When the service has no payment-method service and the contact has a
  saved payment method, it must answer `500` ("This contact has a saved payment method, but the contact service was not
  configured to detach it on delete.") and delete nothing.
- **SPEC-15.80**: `ensure_primary_company_link` must insert a primary `contact_companies` link (sort order 0, title
  copied from the contact) for a contact that has a `company_id` and no link rows at all, and must do nothing when the
  contact has any link or no `company_id`.

- **SPEC-15.81**: Creating a site must answer `404` "Company not found" when the company is not in the caller's tenant;
  must store an absent address as empty parts and an absent `timezone` as "UTC"; and must write the site and a `create`
  audit row in one transaction.
- **SPEC-15.82**: Creating a site with `is_primary` true, and updating a site to `is_primary` true, must first clear
  `is_primary` on every other site of the same company in the same transaction.
- **SPEC-15.83**: Updating a site must answer `404` "Site not found" for an unknown id, must write only the fields
  present in the request (a supplied `address` replaces all six parts), and must write an `update` audit row with before
  and after snapshots in the same transaction.
- **SPEC-15.84**: Getting a site must answer `404` "Site not found" for an id not in the caller's tenant, and a site's
  `latitude` and `longitude` must be returned as numbers.
- **SPEC-15.85**: Listing a company's sites must return them primary first then by name, with the total count.
- **SPEC-15.86**: Deleting a site must answer `404` "Site not found" for an unknown id, and otherwise delete the site
  and write a `delete` audit row with the before snapshot in one transaction.

- **SPEC-15.87**: Listing company industries must return the caller's tenant's rows (`id`, `name`, `is_active`) ordered
  by name, paginated, with the total count.
- **SPEC-15.88**: Creating a company industry must store the trimmed name, answer `409` for a name that duplicates
  another of the tenant ignoring case, and write a `create` audit row in the same transaction.
- **SPEC-15.89**: Updating a company industry must store the trimmed name and active flag, answer `404` "Company
  industry not found" for an unknown id, and answer `409` for a name that duplicates another of the tenant ignoring
  case.
- **SPEC-15.90**: Deleting a company industry must answer `404` "Company industry not found" for an unknown id and
  otherwise delete the row.

- **SPEC-15.91**: `GET /contacts/portal-roles` must list the caller's tenant-wide portal roles only, each with `id`,
  `name`, `capabilities`, `is_builtin`, `company_id` and `contacts_count` (the number of contacts holding the role),
  built-in roles first then by name.
- **SPEC-15.92**: Listing portal roles for a company must return tenant-wide roles and that company's own roles,
  built-in first, then tenant-wide before company-scoped, then by name; a tenant-wide and a company role with the same
  name must both appear.
- **SPEC-15.93**: `GET /contacts/{contact_id}/portal-roles` must answer `404` "Contact not found" for a contact not in
  the caller's tenant and otherwise return the ids of the roles assigned to it.
- **SPEC-15.94**: Granting portal access with an empty `role_ids` must answer `422` on field `role_ids` ("at least one
  portal role is required") before anything else is read.
- **SPEC-15.95**: Granting portal access must answer `404` "Contact not found" for an unknown contact, `400` "This
  contact has no company_id. Link the contact to a Company before granting portal access." when the contact has no
  company, and `400` "Portal access cannot be granted to a contact on the tenant's own_company." when its company is the
  tenant's own company.
- **SPEC-15.96**: Granting portal access, and replacing a contact's role assignments, must answer `400` "Role {id} is
  scoped to a different Company than the target contact" for any role id that is missing, belongs to another tenant, or
  is scoped to a company other than the contact's, with one message for all three cases so scope existence is not
  disclosed; a tenant-wide role must be accepted.
- **SPEC-15.97**: Granting portal access must give the contact's company a nine-digit Portal ID when it has none (random
  in 100000000 to 999999999, never overwriting a concurrent writer's value), retrying up to 5 times on collision, and
  must fail with a `500` "could not assign a unique Portal ID after 5 attempts" when none is stored.
- **SPEC-15.98**: Granting portal access, and resending an invite, must use the company's existing `portal_slug` or
  assign a random one with the same retry-and-reread behavior, failing with a `500` internal error when no unique slug
  could be stored (5 attempts when ensured outside the grant transaction, 3 inside it).
- **SPEC-15.99**: Granting portal access must, in one transaction, replace the contact's role assignments with exactly
  `role_ids` (removing others, ignoring duplicates already present) and set `is_portal_user` true.
- **SPEC-15.100**: Granting portal access to a contact that is already a portal user with a stored password must only
  rewrite the roles and write a `portal_roles_updated` audit row; it must mint no token, send no email and return
  `password_email_queued` false.
- **SPEC-15.101**: Granting portal access to any other contact must, in the same transaction, delete the contact's
  unused setup tokens, store a new one, write a `portal_access_granted` audit row, and after commit send the grant
  email, returning `password_email_queued` true; the setup link must not be serialized in the response.
- **SPEC-15.102**: The grant and resend email must be dispatched as template `auth.portal_grant` with the recipient
  email, salutation, first name, password-setup link `{app_url}/portal/{slug}/set-password?token={token}`, Portal ID,
  and, when a login intent could be stored, a magic link `{app_url}/portal/pick?token={intent_id}.{secret}` that expires
  15 minutes after creation.
- **SPEC-15.103**: When the magic-link intent cannot be stored, the grant email must still be sent without the magic
  link and the failure must be logged at warn. When the contact has no email, no notifications dispatcher is wired, or
  the dispatch fails, the failure must be logged at warn and the committed grant must stay in place.
- **SPEC-15.104**: Resending a portal invite must answer `409` "contact does not have portal access; grant it first"
  when the contact is not a portal user, `409` "contact has no email on file; add one before resending" when its email
  is blank, and `409` "contact has no company; attach one before resending the portal invite" when it has no company,
  and `404` "Contact not found" for an unknown contact.
- **SPEC-15.105**: A successful resend must ensure the company's Portal ID and slug, delete the contact's unused setup
  tokens, store a new one, write a `portal_invite_resent` audit row in one transaction, and send the grant email after
  commit.
- **SPEC-15.106**: Revoking portal access must answer `404` "Contact not found" for an unknown contact and otherwise, in
  one transaction, delete all the contact's role assignments, set `is_portal_user` false, delete its unused setup
  tokens, mark every unrevoked contact session revoked, and write a `portal_access_revoked` audit row; it must keep the
  company's slug and the contact's stored password.
- **SPEC-15.107**: Replacing a contact's role assignments must answer `404` "Contact not found" for an unknown contact,
  must accept an empty list (clearing all assignments), must ignore duplicate ids, must change neither `is_portal_user`
  nor setup tokens nor send email, and must write a `portal_roles_replaced` audit row in the same transaction.
- **SPEC-15.108**: Listing a contact's access requests must return every request for the contact in the caller's tenant,
  resolved ones included, newest `requested_at` first, each with the contact's note, `status` (`open`, `granted`,
  `declined` or `withdrawn`) and resolver and time when resolved.
- **SPEC-15.109**: Resolving an access request must lock the request row before deciding, answer `404` "access request
  not found" for an unknown id, and answer `409` "This request was already {status}." when its status is not `open`, so
  two concurrent resolutions cannot both apply.
- **SPEC-15.110**: Granting an access request must assign the tenant-wide built-in role for the request's area to the
  contact (keyed on its stable built-in key, no error if already assigned), and must answer `500` when the area is no
  longer a known area ("The portal area {area} no longer exists, so this request cannot be granted.") or the tenant has
  no such built-in role ("This tenant has no built-in {role} role to grant."), granting nothing.
- **SPEC-15.111**: Resolving an access request must set its status to `granted` (when `grant` is true) or `declined`,
  record the resolving staff user and time, write an `update` audit row on the contact with the request id, area and
  resolution, return the updated request, and do all of it in one transaction.
- **SPEC-15.112**: Setting a company's `default_billing_contact_id` must ensure the contact can read invoices: for a
  contact that is not a portal user it must do nothing; for a contact whose assigned roles already include
  `invoices:read` it must do nothing; otherwise it must assign the tenant-wide built-in Billing Contact role, write an
  `update` audit row recording the grant, and report that it changed something.
- **SPEC-15.113**: When the tenant has no built-in Billing Contact role to grant, `ensure_can_read_invoices` must log a
  warn naming the contact and must not fail the caller's company update or invoice send.
- **SPEC-15.114**: `billing_contact::assert_for_company` must answer `400` "billing_contact_id does not reference a
  contact of this company" unless the contact is in the tenant and is the company's scalar contact or linked to it
  through `contact_companies`.
- **SPEC-15.115**: `billing_contact::resolve` must, when a contact is named, validate it as SPEC-15.114 does and return
  it, and otherwise return the company's `default_billing_contact_id`, or none when the company has none or does not
  exist in the tenant.

- **SPEC-15.116**: Website-probe input must be trimmed and refused with a `400` query error on `url`: "is required" when
  empty or when the shared website normalizer returns nothing; "must not contain spaces or control characters" when it
  holds whitespace or control characters; "not a valid web address: {cause}" when it does not parse; "must use http or
  https" for another scheme; "must not contain credentials" with userinfo; "must contain a host" with no host; and "must
  use port 80 or 443" for another explicit port.
- **SPEC-15.117**: A probe must attempt `https` and `http` against the lower-cased host concurrently, each attempt
  starting at `/`, and each capped at 5 seconds end to end including redirects; an attempt over budget must be a
  `timeout` failure logged at warn with host and scheme.
- **SPEC-15.118**: Before the first request of an attempt and before following every redirect, the probe must apply the
  shared outbound-URL guard with ports 80 and 443 only; a refusal must be logged at warn with the credential-free URL
  and the cause, and must map to the failure reason `dns` when name resolution failed and `blocked_host` otherwise.
- **SPEC-15.119**: A probe attempt must follow at most 5 redirects. A chain still redirecting at the fifth hop must be
  reported as reached at the last fetched URL with `redirect_truncated` true and a warn log; a redirect whose `Location`
  cannot be joined to the current URL must fail the attempt with reason `refused` and a warn log; a 3xx response with no
  `Location` must be reported as reached with that status.
- **SPEC-15.120**: The live fetcher must send `HEAD` with the user agent `mokosh-server/website-probe`, a 5 second
  request timeout and no automatic redirects, must repeat the request as `GET` only on a `405` or `501` answer, and must
  never read a response body. A `Location` header unreadable as text must be logged at warn and treated as absent.
- **SPEC-15.121**: A transport failure must map to `timeout` for a timeout, `tls` for a connect error whose text names
  tls, certificate or handshake, and `refused` for any other connect error or other failure, and must be logged at warn
  with the underlying cause before being reduced to the reason.
- **SPEC-15.122**: The probe result must report `reachable` true when either scheme was reached, `https_ok` and
