  `http_ok` per scheme, and `canonical_url` and `final_status` from the `https` outcome when reached, else from the
  `http` outcome, else absent. A 4xx or 5xx answer must count as reached.
- **SPEC-15.123**: The probe result must set `http_redirects_to_https` true only when the `http` attempt was reached and
  its final URL uses `https`; must set `www_change` to `added` or `removed` when the canonical host gained or lost a
  leading `www.` against the requested host, else `none`; and, when neither scheme was reached, must set
  `unreachable_reason` to the `https` failure reason, else the `http` one.
- **SPEC-15.124**: The probe service must cache a result per lower-cased host for 15 minutes with at most 10,000 hosts,
  must run one probe for concurrent misses of the same host, and must return the caller's own typed `input`, not the
  cached caller's, on every response.
- **SPEC-15.125**: URLs written to probe logs must have username and password removed, because a redirect target is
  controlled by the remote origin.

- **SPEC-15.126**: The industry backfill must rewrite each company whose trimmed, lower-cased `industry` equals a known
  variant to that variant's canonical spelling, across all tenants in one statement on the privileged pool, setting
  `updated_at`; it must not touch a company already at the canonical spelling, so a second run changes nothing.
- **SPEC-15.127**: The industry backfill must leave a non-empty `industry` that matches no known variant unchanged and
  report it with its tenant and company count, ordered by tenant then count descending; a database error must be
  returned to the caller.
- **SPEC-15.128**: The industry backfill report must print "normalized {n} company industry value(s) across {t}
  tenant(s)", one "  tenant {id}: {n} updated" line per changed tenant, then either "no unmapped values remain" or the
  count of unmapped values with one "  tenant {id}: {n}x {value:?}" line each.
- **SPEC-15.129**: Every variant in the industry map must be lower-case, trimmed and unique, and every canonical name
  must also be a variant in its lower-case form, so a case-only difference is normalized.

- **SPEC-15.130**: A portal role summary read from JSON with no `company_id` must be tenant-wide and with no
  `contacts_count` must be 0; an access-request resolution body must require the boolean `grant` and accept no third
  value.

### 15.2 Contact sync

- **SPEC-15.500**: `GET /api/v1/integrations/contact-sync` must require an authenticated staff session and return the
  caller's tenant overview: `enabled`, `configured`, `connection`, `icloud_enabled`, `icloud_connection`,
  `microsoft_configured`, `microsoft_enabled`, `microsoft_connection`. Each connection field must be `null` when that
  provider has no live connection, and that case must not be an error.
- **SPEC-15.501**: `POST /api/v1/integrations/contact-sync/google/authorize` must require the admin role and return
  `{"authorize_url": ...}`; it must not redirect. It must fail with 409 when the Google switch is off, and with a
  configuration error when the host has no Google OAuth client or `PUBLIC_API_BASE_URL` is unset.
- **SPEC-15.502**: `POST /api/v1/integrations/contact-sync/microsoft/authorize` must require the admin role and return
  `{"authorize_url": ...}` for the Microsoft consent screen, under the same refusals as the Google authorize route but
  using the Microsoft switch and the host's Microsoft client.
- **SPEC-15.503**: `POST /api/v1/integrations/contact-sync/{google|icloud|microsoft}/disconnect` must require the admin
  role and answer 204 on success; it must answer 404 `<Provider> connection` when the tenant has no live connection for
  that provider.
- **SPEC-15.504**: The `provider` query parameter on the selection, schedule, preview and run-queue routes must default
  to `google` when absent or blank, and must accept only `google`, `icloud` or `microsoft` (after trimming). Any other
  value, including `vcard`, must fail with a validation error on field `provider`: "must be google, icloud, or
  microsoft".
- **SPEC-15.505**: `POST /api/v1/integrations/contact-sync/icloud/connect` must require the admin role, take `apple_id`
  and `app_password` in the JSON body, and return `{"connection_id": <uuid>, "reconnected": <bool>}`, where
  `reconnected` is true only when an existing connection to the same Apple ID was refreshed.
- **SPEC-15.506**: `POST /api/v1/integrations/contact-sync/preview` must require the admin role, accept an optional
  `group_ids` array in the body, and write nothing. A `provider` value that fails SPEC-15.504 must be refused before any
  source is contacted.
- **SPEC-15.507**: `PUT /api/v1/integrations/contact-sync/selection` must require the admin role, take `group_ids`, and
  return the updated connection status.
- **SPEC-15.508**: `PUT /api/v1/integrations/contact-sync/schedule` must require the admin role, take
  `sync_interval_minutes`, and return the updated connection status.
- **SPEC-15.509**: `GET /api/v1/integrations/contact-sync/runs` must require an authenticated staff session and take an
  optional `limit` defaulting to 20.
- **SPEC-15.510**: `POST /api/v1/integrations/contact-sync/runs` must require the admin role and answer 202 with the
  queued run row (the row to poll), never the import result.
- **SPEC-15.511**: `GET /api/v1/integrations/contact-sync/runs/{run_id}` must require an authenticated staff session.
  `POST .../runs/{run_id}/cancel` must require the admin role. Both must return the run row.
- **SPEC-15.512**: `POST /api/v1/integrations/contact-sync/vcard/uploads` must require the admin role, read the first
  multipart part named `file`, ignore other parts, and answer 201 with the stored upload. A body with no `file` part
  must fail 400 "Missing 'file' part in multipart body", and a malformed multipart body must fail 400 "Multipart parse:
  ..." or "Multipart read: ...". The route's body limit must equal the vCard reader's upload cap so an oversized file
  reaches the shared 413 rather than a framework 400.
- **SPEC-15.513**: `GET /api/v1/integrations/contact-sync/vcard/uploads` must require the admin role and return the
  recent uploads, with an optional `limit` defaulting to 20.
- **SPEC-15.514**: `POST .../vcard/uploads/{file_id}/preview` must require the admin role and write nothing. `POST
  .../vcard/uploads/{file_id}/import` must require the admin role, take `group_ids`, and answer 202 with the queued run
  row.
- **SPEC-15.515**: `GET /api/v1/integrations/contact-sync/review-queue` and `POST .../review-queue/resolve` must require
  an authenticated staff session (not admin) and act only on the caller's tenant.
- **SPEC-15.516**: `GET /api/v1/contacts/contacts/{contact_id}/sync` and `POST .../sync/unlink` must require an
  authenticated staff session; `DELETE .../sync/locks/{field}` must require the manager role and answer 204; `POST
  .../sync/remove-imported-data` must require the admin role and take a JSON body with `reason`.
- **SPEC-15.517**: The public routes `GET /api/v1/public/contact-sync/google/callback` and `.../microsoft/callback` must
  carry no session, and must always answer with a redirect to the SPA, never a JSON error. When the provider returned
  `error`, they must log it at info level and redirect to the failure URL. When `code` or `state` is missing they must
  redirect to the failure URL. When completing the connect fails, they must log a warning with the error and redirect to
  the failure URL. The redirect must carry a fixed flag and never the provider's text.
- **SPEC-15.518**: Beginning a Google connect must insert one `contact_sync_oauth_states` row (provider `google`, the
  starter's user id, a PKCE verifier, the redirect URI, expiry 10 minutes ahead) and return an authorization URL whose
  `state` is `{state_id}.{secret}`. The secret must be stored only as a password hash.
- **SPEC-15.519**: The Google redirect URI must be `PUBLIC_API_BASE_URL` (trimmed, trailing `/` removed) plus
  `/api/v1/public/contact-sync/google/callback`, and the Microsoft one the same base plus
  `/api/v1/public/contact-sync/microsoft/callback`. A missing or blank base must fail with a configuration error
  "PUBLIC_API_BASE_URL is not set, so Google has no address to return to." (Microsoft: "... so Microsoft has no address
  to return to.").
- **SPEC-15.520**: When the host holds no Google OAuth client, connecting or refreshing a token must fail with a
  configuration error "Google Contacts is not available on this deployment. Its Google sign-in client is configured by
  whoever runs it."; for Microsoft the error must read "Microsoft 365 Contacts is not available on this deployment. Its
  Entra ID sign-in client is configured by whoever runs it.".
- **SPEC-15.521**: Completing a connect (either provider) with a `state` that has no `.` or whose id part is not a UUID
  must fail 400 "That sign-in link is not valid.".
- **SPEC-15.522**: Completing a connect must fail 400 "That connection attempt is no longer valid. Start again from
  Settings." when no state row exists for that id and provider, the row is already consumed, the row is expired, or the
  secret does not verify against the stored hash. A secret-verification error (as opposed to a mismatch) must
  additionally be logged as a warning naming the state id. The tenant must come from the state row, not from any
  session.
- **SPEC-15.523**: Completing a connect must mark the state row consumed before exchanging the code, so a failed or slow
  exchange cannot be retried with the same state; a concurrent second completion that finds the row already consumed
  must fail with the same 400 as SPEC-15.522.
- **SPEC-15.524**: Completing a Google connect must fail 400 when the token response carries no refresh token ("Google
  did not return a refresh token. Remove this app from the Google account's third-party access and connect again."), and
  400 when the response carries a `scope` that lacks contacts read ("This Google account was connected without
  permission to read its contacts. Connect again and leave the contacts permission ticked."). A response with no `scope`
  field must not be refused for scope.
- **SPEC-15.525**: A successful Google connect must record the connection with the account email returned by Google and
  redirect to `{SPA base}/settings/integrations/google-contacts?contact_sync=connected`, or `contact_sync=reconnected`
  when an existing connection was refreshed.
- **SPEC-15.526**: Completing a Microsoft connect must apply the same state, consumption and scope rules as SPEC-15.521
  to SPEC-15.524 with Microsoft wording ("Microsoft did not return a refresh token. Revoke this app in the Microsoft
  account's privacy settings and connect again."; "This Microsoft account was connected without permission to read its
  contacts. Connect again and leave the Contacts permission ticked."), and on success redirect to `{SPA
  base}/settings/integrations/microsoft-contacts?contact_sync=connected` or `reconnected`.
- **SPEC-15.527**: Recording a connection for a tenant that already has a live connection to the same provider and the
  same account (email compared case-insensitively) must replace the stored credential, keep the connection id, set
  `is_active`, clear `last_error` and `failure_notified_at`, reset `consecutive_failures` to 0, set `sync_status` to
  `never` if it has never synced and `success` otherwise, write a `contact_sync.reconnected` audit row, and return
  `Reconnected`.
- **SPEC-15.528**: Recording a connection for a live connection to a different account must fail 409 "This organization
  is connected to <existing email>. Disconnect it before connecting a different <account word>." and must change
  nothing.
- **SPEC-15.529**: Recording a new connection must store the credential in the secret store before inserting the
  `contact_sync_connections` row (status `never`), write a `contact_sync.connected` audit row, and return `Connected`. A
  unique violation (a concurrent connect) must fail 409 "This tenant already has a <provider> connection. Disconnect it
  first.". The credential must never be stored in the connections table.
- **SPEC-15.530**: Connecting iCloud must require the iCloud switch to be on (409 otherwise), trim both inputs, reject
  an `apple_id` that is not an email with a validation error on `apple_id` ("must be the Apple ID's email address"),
  reject an empty `app_password` with a validation error on `app_password`, and verify the credential by one CardDAV
  address-book discovery before storing anything. Apple refusing the credential must fail 400 "Apple refused that Apple
  ID and app-specific password. ...", a throttle must fail 409 "Apple is asking us to wait before checking this account
  again. ...", and any other source failure must fail 400 with the failure message.
- **SPEC-15.531**: The failure redirect for a failed callback must be `{SPA
  base}/settings/integrations/google-contacts?contact_sync=failed`, with no provider text in it.
- **SPEC-15.532**: The overview must read each provider's enabled switch from the tenant's settings, report `configured`
  as whether the host holds a Google client and `microsoft_configured` as whether it holds a Microsoft client, and read
  each live connection scoped to the tenant.
- **SPEC-15.533**: Asserting a provider enabled must fail 409 "<Provider name> is turned off for this organization. An
  administrator can turn it back on in Settings, Integrations." when that provider's own switch is off; one provider's
  switch must never disable another.
- **SPEC-15.534**: A connection status must be read per tenant and provider, exclude disconnected connections, and
  include: the count of live links flagged deleted in source, the count of distinct external ids with an open review
  candidate, the group selection, the sync interval, the consecutive failure count, and the latest run (newest by
  creation time) or `null`.
- **SPEC-15.535**: Disconnecting must in one transaction mark the connection disconnected and inactive with its sync
  token cleared; cancel its queued runs outright and request cancellation of its running runs; close every live link
  with reason `disconnected` and the acting user; and write a `contact_sync.disconnected` audit row recording how many
  contacts were kept as local. No imported contact may be deleted.
- **SPEC-15.536**: Disconnecting must delete the stored credential only after the transaction commits. A failure to
  delete it must be logged as a warning naming the connection id and must not fail the disconnect.
- **SPEC-15.537**: Obtaining a source for preview or sync must fail 409 when the provider's switch is off, 404
  `<Provider> connection` when no live connection exists, and otherwise build the provider's client with a credential
  freshly derived for the call (Basic credentials for iCloud, a refreshed access token for Google and Microsoft).
- **SPEC-15.538**: Previewing must trim each supplied `group_id`, pass `None` through as "every labelled record", and
  call the sync engine's preview, which must write nothing.
- **SPEC-15.539**: Setting the selection must trim, sort and de-duplicate the ids; reject, with a validation error on
  `group_ids` "must be <group word> ids, at most 200", more than 200 ids or any id that is empty, longer than 255 bytes,
  or (Google) lacks the `contactGroups/` prefix, or (other providers) is neither the ungrouped sentinel nor free of
  whitespace; require a live connection (404 otherwise); and write a `contact_sync.selection_changed` audit row with the
  old and new selection. An empty list must be accepted and means nothing is imported.
- **SPEC-15.540**: Setting the schedule must reject a `sync_interval_minutes` outside 5 to 1440 inclusive with a
  validation error on `sync_interval_minutes` ("must be between 5 and 1440 minutes; turn the integration off to stop
  syncing altogether"), require a live connection, and write a `contact_sync.schedule_changed` audit row with the old
  and new value.
- **SPEC-15.541**: Queuing a run must fail 409 when the provider's switch is off, 404 when there is no live connection,
  409 "Choose at least one <group word> to import before syncing." when the selection is empty, and 409 when
  `sync_status` is `reconnect_required`. Otherwise it must insert a `queued` run whose trigger is `initial` when the
  connection has never synced and `manual` otherwise, with the requesting user, and write a `contact_sync.run_queued`
  audit row.
- **SPEC-15.542**: Queuing a run while one is already queued or running for the connection (unique violation) must fail
  409 "An import is already queued or running for this connection.". The import worker must be woken only after the
  transaction commits, and only when a wake handle is configured.
- **SPEC-15.543**: Listing runs must return the tenant's runs newest first, with `limit` clamped to 1..=100.
- **SPEC-15.544**: Reading a run that does not exist in the tenant must fail 404 "Import run".
- **SPEC-15.545**: Cancelling a run must cancel a `queued` run at once (status `cancelled`, finish time set) and, for a
  `running` run, set `cancel_requested_at` once and leave the status for the worker's next checkpoint. Cancelling a
  finished run must fail 409 "This import has already finished (<status>)."; an unknown run must fail 404. A
  `contact_sync.run_cancelled` audit row must be written.
- **SPEC-15.546**: The review queue must list, for the tenant, open candidates of every connection that is not
  disconnected (including file uploads), grouped by (connection, external id) with every candidate contact (id, match
  reason, name, email, title, company name, phone numbers in order, and whether the contact is already linked to a
  different external id of the same connection), ordered by candidate creation time, external id, then candidate contact
  id. The source label must be the snapshot's `source_label`, else the connection's account email.
- **SPEC-15.547**: Resolving a review item must close every open candidate row of that (connection, external id) in the
  same transaction: the chosen contact `linked` (for Link), all `created` (for Create), the rest `skipped`, with the
  resolving user and time, and write a `contact_sync.review_resolved` audit row. It must fail 404 "Review item" when no
  open candidate exists. Link must fail with a validation error on `contact_id` ("must be one of the contacts this
  record was matched to") when the contact was not among the candidates.
- **SPEC-15.548**: Resolving must pick the source as the one live connection holding the open record, or the one named
  by `connection_id`. When the record waits in more than one source and none is named it must fail with a validation
  error on `connection_id` ("this record is waiting in more than one source; name the one you are answering"). It must
  fail 409 when the source's switch is off (the file-upload source is exempt), and when no source is found it must first
  fail 409 if the Google switch is off, else 404 "Review item".
- **SPEC-15.549**: A resolve whose link or create hits a conflict because a sync linked the record meanwhile must fail
  409 "This record was linked by a sync while it was waiting for review. Reload the queue.".
- **SPEC-15.550**: Reading a contact's provenance must fail 404 "Contact" for a contact outside the tenant, and
  otherwise return every link (live first, then newest first) with origin, timestamps, unlink reason, suggested company,
  and for a file import the file name, uploader name and upload time, plus the contact's field locks ordered by field
  with the locking user's name. A user id that could not be resolved to a name must be logged under
  `contact_sync.provenance`.
- **SPEC-15.551**: Releasing a lock must fail with a validation error on `field` ("must be one of <fields>") for a field
  outside the sync field set, 404 "Contact" for a foreign contact, and 404 "Field lock" when the contact has no lock on
  that field. On success it must delete the lock and write a `contact_sync.lock_released` audit row.
- **SPEC-15.552**: Unlinking a contact must mark every live link for it `unlinked` with reason `unlinked` and the acting
  user, leave the contact unchanged, write one `contact_sync.unlinked` audit row per link, and fail 404 "Contact sync
  link" when the contact has no live link (404 "Contact" for a foreign contact).
- **SPEC-15.553**: Removing imported data must fail with a validation error on `reason` ("say who asked for the removal,
  or why") when the trimmed reason is empty, 404 "Contact" for a foreign contact, and 404 "Imported contact data" when
  the contact has no links. In one transaction it must write a `data_removed` suppression per link keyed on the external
  id digest (idempotent), delete the candidate rows for those external ids, the links and the field locks.
- **SPEC-15.554**: Removing imported data must delete the contact only when some link has origin `created`; a contact
  whose links are `linked` or whose origin is unknown must be kept. The response must be `{"contact_deleted",
  "links_removed"}`, and the audit row must record the reason and counts but not the removed values.
- **SPEC-15.555**: Deleting a created contact on data removal must first detach its saved payment methods at the payment
  provider. A detach failure must abort and remove nothing. When no payment-method service is configured and the contact
  has a saved payment method, it must fail with a configuration error and remove nothing.
- **SPEC-15.556**: Deleting a created contact that other records reference (foreign key violation) must fail 409 "This
  contact was imported, but tickets, invoices or other records refer to it, so it cannot be deleted. Nothing was
  removed. Reassign or remove those records first." and the whole transaction must roll back.
- **SPEC-15.557**: Obtaining an access token must send a Microsoft connection to the Microsoft token endpoint and never
  to Google's. It must fail with a configuration error "This connection's credential is missing from the secret store."
  when the stored refresh token is absent. A revoked grant must mark the connection `reconnect_required` and still
  return the revoked-grant error.
- **SPEC-15.558**: The iCloud credential must be the connection's `account_email` plus the secret-store password; it
  must fail 404 "iCloud Contacts connection" for an unknown connection and a configuration error "This connection's
  app-specific password is missing from the secret store." when the password is absent.
- **SPEC-15.559**: Marking a connection `reconnect_required` must set `last_error`, and a failure to write that state
  must be logged as a warning naming the connection id without replacing the token error being returned.
- **SPEC-15.560**: The lockable field set must be exactly `first_name`, `last_name`, `email`, `title`, `department`,
  `company_name`, `phones`, `tags`, `notes`; a sync must never write a field that has a row in `contact_field_locks` for
  the contact.
- **SPEC-15.561**: A sync must treat a record as excluded (no link, no review, no update, no deletion flag) when its
  external id belongs to a link a person unlinked from this connection, or when the SHA-256 digest of its external id is
  in `contact_sync_suppressions` for the tenant and provider. This check must come before every other decision.
- **SPEC-15.562**: A source record marked deleted must flag its live link as deleted-in-source when the link is not
  already flagged, whatever the label selection; with no link, or an already flagged link, it must count as unchanged
  and create nothing.
- **SPEC-15.563**: A non-deleted record carrying none of the selected group ids must count as not selected, except that
  on an incremental (non-full) read a record that reports no group ids at all and already has a live link must continue
  to the link rules (iCloud deltas omit membership on member cards). A record that reports group ids but none selected,
  or that has no link, must always be not selected.
- **SPEC-15.564**: A record with a live link must count as unchanged when the link's etag is non-null, equals the
  record's etag, and the link is not flagged deleted; otherwise the link must be updated, and a successful update must
  store the new etag, set `last_synced_at`, and clear `deleted_in_source_at`.
- **SPEC-15.565**: A record with no link must count as already reviewed when a reviewer skipped that external id
  earlier. Otherwise the matcher decides: one contact matched by email must be linked; several candidates must go to
  review minus the (external id, contact) pairs a human already answered, and when none remain the record must count as
  already reviewed; no match must create a new contact, with a company suggestion only when exactly one company in the
  tenant has the same normalized name as the record's organisation.
- **SPEC-15.566**: A sync run must fail without reading the source when the connection's provider differs from the
  provider handed in (internal error), when the connection is disconnected or inactive (409 "This contact sync
  connection is not active."), when the selection is empty (409 "Choose at least one <group word> to import before
  syncing." for a directory, "Choose at least one category to import before importing." for a file), or for a vCard run
  that names no uploaded file (internal error). An empty selection must never mean "everything".
- **SPEC-15.567**: A sync run must set the connection status `in_progress` before reading the source. When reading
  labels or changes fails, it must set the status to `throttled` (throttled), `reconnect_required` (unauthorized) or
  `failed` (other), store the error text in `last_error`, and return the error.
- **SPEC-15.568**: A pass must be a full read only when the source lists its whole directory and either the connection
  has no sync token or the source reported a full resync; an uploaded file must never be a full read. The report `total`
  must be the number of records the source returned.
- **SPEC-15.569**: Records must be applied in chunks of 25 per tenant transaction, each record inside a savepoint. A
  record that fails must be rolled back alone, counted in `failed`, logged as a warning with the connection id and
  external id, and recorded in `failures` (external id and a reason truncated to 300 characters) only while fewer than
  50 failures are recorded; the remaining records must still be applied.
- **SPEC-15.570**: When a run has a run id, the engine must write progress (total, full_read, processed, created,
  linked, updated, queued_for_review, skipped, deleted_in_source, failed_records, failures, heartbeat) before the first
  record, between chunks and after the last. If the run has a cancel request at a checkpoint, the engine must stop
  applying, mark the report cancelled, restore the connection's previous `sync_status`, flag no deletions, and not
  advance the sync token.
- **SPEC-15.571**: After a complete full read with zero failed records, every live link not flagged deleted whose
  external id was absent from the read must be flagged deleted-in-source (in transactions of up to 25) and counted; no
  sweep may run for a delta, a file, a cancelled run, or a pass with any failed record.
- **SPEC-15.572**: A pass with zero failed records must set the connection `success`, clear `last_error`, store the
  source's next sync token and set `last_sync_at`. A pass with failures must set the status `failed` with the message
  "<failed> of <total> contacts could not be imported. The next sync retries them." (a file: "Import the file again to
  retry them.") and must not advance the sync token.
- **SPEC-15.573**: Setting a connection status must update `last_sync_at` to now for every status except `in_progress`.
- **SPEC-15.574**: Each pass must read, scoped to the tenant, all contacts (with phones, company names, and whether
  linked to this connection), the connection's live links, answered and skipped candidates, links unlinked by a person,
  suppressions for the provider, and company names; a contact with an empty first and last name must be logged under
  `contact_sync.snapshot`.
- **SPEC-15.575**: Linking a record to an existing contact must apply the first-link field rules and insert a link with
  origin `linked`. Creating must create the contact through the contact import path with the mapped fields, the selected
  label names as tags, no portal access, and insert a link with origin `created` and the company suggestion. A contact
  created or linked in a pass must be a match target for later records of the same pass.
- **SPEC-15.576**: Putting a record to review must insert one open candidate row per (connection, external id, candidate
  contact) with the match reason and a source snapshot; when an open row already exists it must be refreshed only if its
  etag differs. The record must count as queued only when at least one row was newly inserted, otherwise as awaiting
  review.
- **SPEC-15.577**: The label names added to a contact must be only the names of selected groups the record belongs to,
  excluding the "no category" sentinel and any group whose name the source did not list.
- **SPEC-15.578**: A preview must fail 409 "This contact sync connection is not active." for a disconnected or inactive
  connection, read the source with no sync token, consider the requested selection intersected with the labels the
  source offers (all offered labels when none is requested), and write no link, candidate, run, status or token. It must
  classify each non-deleted record with the same planning rules as an import as `create`, `link`, `review`, `imported`
  (unchanged or update) or `excluded` (excluded or already reviewed), omit not-selected records, and return per-record
  group ids (offered only), the groups with member counts, the considered selection and totals counting each record
  once.
- **SPEC-15.579**: Inserting a link must store the connection's provider, the source account (the uploaded file's name
  for a file import), external id, etag, contact id, origin, suggested company id and import file id, and write a
  `contact_sync.linked` audit row.
- **SPEC-15.580**: Flagging a link deleted-in-source must set `deleted_in_source_at` only when it is unset, write a
  `contact_sync.deleted_in_source` audit row only when the flag changed, and never delete or alter the contact.
- **SPEC-15.581**: On a first link to an existing contact, a field must be written only when the contact's value is
  empty; on a later sync of an owned contact the source's value must replace names, title, department, notes and a
  freeform company name when they differ. In both passes a source value that is empty must never clear a field, `email`
  must only be filled when empty, a locked field must be skipped, the company name must not be written when the contact
  has a company link, and names must be written only when the source supplied a given, family or display name.
- **SPEC-15.582**: Tags must be extended with the selected label names the contact lacks (sorted, de-duplicated), never
  removed, and skipped when the `tags` field is locked.
- **SPEC-15.583**: Phones from the source must be added to the contact only when their normalized key is not already
  held (numbers with no key are always added); existing phones must be kept in order, the contact's existing primary
  must stay primary, a source phone may be primary only when the contact had no phones, and the `phones` lock must
  suppress any addition.
- **SPEC-15.584**: When no field changes and no phone is added, applying a record must write nothing, including no
  `updated_at` change and no audit row. Otherwise it must update the contact and write a `contacts` audit row carrying
  the before and after JSON.
- **SPEC-15.585**: A reviewer's link or create must rebuild the record from its stored snapshot without re-reading the
  source, adopt the snapshot's upload id and source label when it names a file, and apply the same rules as a sync
  (link: first-link fill-only rules; create: contact plus link with the company suggestion rule of SPEC-15.565).
- **SPEC-15.586**: The external id digest must be the lowercase hexadecimal SHA-256 of the external id bytes.
- **SPEC-15.587**: A source snapshot must hold the external id, display name, mapped first and last name, email, all
  emails, phones (number, type, primary), company, title, department, notes, label names and dropped properties, plus
  `import_file_id` and `source_label` for a file import. A snapshot with no first name must rebuild with the first name
  "(no name)".
- **SPEC-15.588**: A report's skipped count must be not-selected plus excluded plus already-reviewed records.
- **SPEC-15.589**: Each worker tick (job name `contact_sync`) must, in order: requeue stale runs, schedule due runs,
  discard expired uploads, then claim and execute up to 5 queued runs one after another. A failure of the expired-upload
  sweep must be logged as a warning and must not fail the tick; a failure of the requeue or schedule steps must fail the
  tick.
- **SPEC-15.590**: A `running` run whose latest of heartbeat, start or creation time is more than 30 minutes old must be
  set back to `queued` with its heartbeat cleared, across all tenants, and the count must be logged as a warning when
  above zero.
- **SPEC-15.591**: The scheduler must insert one `scheduled` run for a connection only when it is not disconnected, is
  active, is not a `vcard` source, has a non-empty selection, has no tenant setting `<provider>_contacts_enabled` equal
  to false, has `sync_status` other than `reconnect_required` or `in_progress`, has synced before, last synced at least
  `sync_interval_minutes` ago, and has no queued or running run; a conflict with an existing active run must insert
  nothing and not fail.
- **SPEC-15.592**: Claiming must pick the oldest queued run whose `not_before` is unset or past, lock it so two workers
  never take the same row, set it `running`, add one to `attempts`, keep the first `started_at`, and stamp the
  heartbeat.
- **SPEC-15.593**: Executing a run for a file source must load the held upload (internal error "a vCard run names no
  uploaded file" when the run names none). For any other provider it must first fail 409 "<Provider name> was turned off
  for this organization before this import ran." when that provider's own switch is off, then obtain the source from the
  factory and run the tracked sync with the run id.
- **SPEC-15.594**: The production source factory must build an iCloud provider from the stored Apple ID and app
  password, a Microsoft provider from a freshly refreshed Microsoft access token, and any other provider from a freshly
  refreshed Google access token; access tokens must not be stored.
- **SPEC-15.595**: Each executed run must log at info level one line with the run id, elapsed milliseconds and the
  report counts on success, a warning with the run id and error on failure, and an error line when recording the outcome
  fails.
- **SPEC-15.596**: A run's final status must be: `cancelled` (no error) when the report is cancelled or the connection
  was disconnected; `cancelled` with the "turned off" message when the run errored and the provider's switch is off;
  `completed` when no record failed; `failed` with "<failed> of <total> contacts could not be imported. The rest landed;
  the next sync retries these." (a file: "upload the file again to retry these.") when some records failed; `queued`
  when the run errored and the connection reads `throttled`; otherwise `failed` with the error text. Finished runs must
  get `finished_at` and a heartbeat.
- **SPEC-15.597**: A throttled run must return to `queued` with `heartbeat_at` cleared and `not_before` set to now plus
  min(5 x attempts, 60) minutes, with the error "<Vendor> is rate limiting this connection; the import resumes by
  itself.", and must not count as a failure.
- **SPEC-15.598**: When a run failed before the engine ran (an error outcome) and the connection's status is neither
  `failed` nor `reconnect_required`, the runner must set the connection `failed` with the error as `last_error`.
- **SPEC-15.599**: A `completed` non-file run must reset the connection's `consecutive_failures` to 0 and clear
  `failure_notified_at`. A `failed` non-file run must add one to `consecutive_failures`, and must dispatch one
  `contact_sync.failing` notification per streak when none was sent yet and the count has reached 3 or the status is
  `reconnect_required`, recording `failure_notified_at`. Cancelled, requeued and file runs must not change the streak.
- **SPEC-15.600**: The failing-connection notification must go to the user who connected the account when active, else
  the oldest active admin or super admin, and carry the account, failure count, last error (or "No reason was
  recorded.") and the settings URL `{SPA base}/settings/integrations/<provider>-contacts`. A failed recipient lookup or
  a dispatch failure must be logged as a warning and must neither undo the recorded outcome nor stop the notification
  when only the recipient is unknown.
- **SPEC-15.601**: After a file run ends for any status except `queued`, the held upload must be discarded; a failed
  discard must be logged as a warning naming the file id.
- **SPEC-15.602**: Executing a specific run must fail 409 "That run is not waiting to start." unless the run is in the
  tenant and `queued`, and otherwise return the run's final status.
- **SPEC-15.603**: Reading a run through the runner must fail 404 "Import run" unless the run belongs to the tenant.
- **SPEC-15.604**: The upload size cap must be the vCard reader's own maximum file size, and the same value must set the
  route's body limit (SPEC-15.511).
- **SPEC-15.605**: An uploaded file name must be reduced to its last path segment (split on `/` and `\`), with invisible
  and control characters removed, trimmed and cut to 200 characters; a name that is then empty or absent must become
  `contacts.vcf`.
- **SPEC-15.606**: Uploading a vCard must fail with a validation error on `file` "the file is empty" for zero bytes,
  with the shared oversized-upload error (413) for more bytes than the cap (before and after parsing), with a validation
  error on `file` carrying the reader's message for an unreadable file, and with a validation error on `file` "holds no
  contacts: it has no BEGIN:VCARD. Export the contacts as a vCard (.vcf) file and upload that" when the file holds zero
  cards. Parsing must run on a blocking thread.
- **SPEC-15.607**: A successful upload must store the bytes before inserting the `contact_import_files` row (file name,
  size, SHA-256, uploader, counts of cards, contacts and group cards, failures, warnings, groups, expiry 24 hours
  ahead), write a `contact_sync.file_uploaded` audit row, create no contact, and return the stored file view plus a
  preview of importing every category.
- **SPEC-15.608**: All of a tenant's uploads must import into one live `vcard` source row, created on first use with
  account `vCard files` and status `never`; concurrent first uses must resolve to the same row.
- **SPEC-15.609**: A parsed file must be served as a provider whose id is `vcard`, which lists everything is false,
  returns every card on every read regardless of any sync token, returns no next sync token and never reports a full
  resync. A card with no category must get the "No category" group, offered with its member count only when at least one
  card has none.
- **SPEC-15.610**: Loading a held upload that storage cannot return must fail 409 "The uploaded file is no longer held.
  Upload it again to import it."; a held file that is unreadable must fail as in SPEC-15.606.
- **SPEC-15.611**: Discarding an upload must delete the stored object when present and stamp `discarded_at` only if
  unset; it must be idempotent, and the `contact_sync.file_discarded` audit row must be written only when the row was
  newly stamped.
- **SPEC-15.612**: The expiry sweep must select at most 100 uploads per call, oldest expiry first, that are not
  discarded, are past `expires_at`, and have no queued or running run; a failure to discard one must be logged as a
  warning naming the file id, must not stop the others, and the call must return the number discarded.
- **SPEC-15.613**: Reading one upload must fail 404 "Uploaded file" outside the tenant, include the uploader's name and
  the newest run for the file, and log under `contact_sync.vcard_file` an uploader id whose name could not be resolved.
- **SPEC-15.614**: Listing uploads must return the tenant's uploads newest first with `limit` clamped to 1..=50, each
  with its newest run, and log under `contact_sync.vcard_files` any uploader id whose name could not be resolved.
- **SPEC-15.615**: Previewing or importing an upload that is discarded or past its expiry must fail 409 "This upload is
  no longer held. Upload the file again to import it.".
- **SPEC-15.616**: Importing an upload must fail with a validation error on `group_ids` "choose at least one of this
  file's categories" when the trimmed, de-duplicated choice is empty or names a category the file does not offer.
  Otherwise it must in one statement set the source's selection to the choice and insert a `manual` run naming the file,
  requested by the caller, and write a `contact_sync.run_queued` audit row.
- **SPEC-15.617**: Importing an upload while a run is queued or running for the vCard source, including a concurrent
  insert that hits the unique index, must fail 409 "A file import is already queued or running. Wait for it to finish,
  then import this one." and must not change the selection.
- **SPEC-15.618**: The vCard reader limits must default to a 10 MiB file, 5,000 cards per file, 256 KiB of text per card
  (photo excluded) and 1 MiB per embedded photo.
- **SPEC-15.619**: A file over the file limit must be refused whole with "This file is larger than <N> MB, the most one
  import accepts. Export the contacts in smaller groups and import each file."; a file with more cards than the card
  limit must be refused whole with "This file holds more than <limit> contacts, the most one import accepts. Export the
  contacts in smaller groups and import each file."; an I/O failure must be refused with "The file could not be read:
  <reason>.". Reading must stop one byte past the file limit rather than loading the whole input.
- **SPEC-15.620**: The reader must split the file into cards at `BEGIN:VCARD` and `END:VCARD` lines (case-insensitive,
  trailing whitespace ignored, never on a folded continuation line), strip a leading UTF-8 byte-order mark, transcode a
  whole UTF-16 file found by its byte-order mark, ignore text outside cards without error, and parse each card on its
  own.
- **SPEC-15.621**: A card with no `END:VCARD` before the next `BEGIN:VCARD` must be reported as a failure "The card has
  no END:VCARD before the next card begins, so it was skipped." and a final card cut off by the end of the file as "The
  file ends before this card's END:VCARD, so it was skipped. The export may be incomplete."; the neighbouring cards must
  still import.
- **SPEC-15.622**: A card whose text (excluding binary properties) exceeds the per-card limit must be skipped and
  reported as a failure "The card is larger than <N> KB, not counting its photo, so it was skipped."; other cards must
  still import.
- **SPEC-15.623**: `PHOTO`, `LOGO`, `SOUND` and `KEY` values must be measured and discarded as they stream past, never
  parsed as text. The first `PHOTO` must be kept as an inline photo (media type, decoded size) or, when it is a link
  (`http://`, `https://`, `VALUE=URI|URL`), as the link text only; the reader must never request that link. A card whose
  inline photo exceeds the photo limit must still import and carry the warning "The photo is larger than <N> MB and was
  ignored. Photos are not imported.". A non-empty `LOGO`, `SOUND` or `KEY` must be recorded among the card's dropped
  properties.
- **SPEC-15.624**: Each card's bytes must be decoded as UTF-8 when valid, else with the card's own first `CHARSET=`
  label, else as Windows-1252.
- **SPEC-15.625**: The content digest must be the lowercase hexadecimal SHA-256 of the card's unfolded lines with blank
  lines, `REV` and `PRODID` removed (any `group.` prefix ignored), sorted, joined by newline, so it must not change with
  property order, line folding, or a changed `REV` or `PRODID`.
- **SPEC-15.626**: A card's external id must be its `UID` when it has at most 200 characters, else `uid-sha256:` plus
  the hex SHA-256 of the `UID`, else `sha256:` plus the content digest; its etag must always be the content digest.
- **SPEC-15.627**: A card with no name (`FN`, `N`), email, phone or organisation must be reported as a failure "The card
  has no name, email address, phone number or organisation, so it was skipped.", and a card the parser cannot read as a
  vCard as "The card could not be read as a vCard, so it was skipped.". Neither may be imported.
- **SPEC-15.628**: A card whose `KIND` is `group` or whose `X-ADDRESSBOOKSERVER-KIND` is `group` must count as a group
  card, not a contact and not a failure; its `UID`, `FN` and each `X-ADDRESSBOOKSERVER-MEMBER` value (with a leading
  `urn:uuid:` removed) must be kept when it has a UID or name.
- **SPEC-15.629**: Contact fields must be read as: first non-empty `UID`, `FN`; `N` family (component 0) and given
  (component 1) names; each non-empty `EMAIL` ordered by preference rank (`PREF` number, or the `pref` type, lower
  first; unmarked last; ties in file order); each non-empty `TEL` (a leading `tel:` removed), primary when it carries
  any preference mark; `ORG` company (component 0) and department (component 1); first `TITLE`; case-insensitively
  de-duplicated `CATEGORIES`; all `NOTE` texts joined by a blank line.
- **SPEC-15.630**: An email or phone label must come from the Apple `X-ABLabel` sharing the property's group (the
  `_$!<Label>!$_` wrapper removed, lowercased), else from the card's type words (a phone: `fax` with `home` or `work`
  gives "home fax"/"work fax"/"fax", `cell` gives "mobile", else `work`, `home`, or the first type).
- **SPEC-15.631**: Properties not mapped to a contact field, other than the structural ones and vendor `X-` extensions,
  must be recorded by upper-case name in the contact's dropped properties.
- **SPEC-15.632**: Category spellings must be canonicalised across the file to the first spelling seen
  (case-insensitive), each contact must carry that spelling as its group id, and the file's groups must list each
  spelling once with the number of contacts carrying it.
- **SPEC-15.633**: A card problem must locate the card: its 1-based position, the 1-based line of its `BEGIN:VCARD`, and
  a hint of its first non-`VERSION` property (up to 80 characters, invisible characters removed) or "(empty card)".
- **SPEC-15.634**: The Google provider must be read-only: it must issue only `GET /v1/people/me/connections` and `GET
  /v1/contactGroups` against `https://people.googleapis.com`, each with the connection's access token as a Bearer
  credential, and must request only the person fields
  `names,emailAddresses,phoneNumbers,organizations,memberships,metadata`.
- **SPEC-15.635**: Reading the address book must page with a page size of 1000, send `requestSyncToken=true` and the
  same parameters on every page (plus `syncToken` when one is held and `pageToken` after the first page), return the
  last page's next sync token, and fail with "Google Contacts kept returning pages past any plausible address book."
  after 1000 pages.
- **SPEC-15.636**: A sync token Google refuses as expired (status 410, or status 400 whose body names
  `EXPIRED_SYNC_TOKEN`) must trigger one full re-read with no token and the result must report `was_full_resync`; if no
  token was sent, or the full re-read is also refused as expired, the read must fail with "Google Contacts refused a
  full read as an expired sync token.".
- **SPEC-15.637**: A request must be retried, up to 5 attempts in total, after a network error, 429, 503 or other 5xx,
  or a 403 whose body names a rate limit (`RATE_LIMIT_EXCEEDED`, `rateLimitExceeded` or `RESOURCE_EXHAUSTED`). The wait
  must be full jitter over an exponential ceiling (1 s doubling, capped at 32 s), with `Retry-After` seconds as a floor
  never exceeding the cap.
- **SPEC-15.638**: After the last attempt, a 403, 429 or 503 must yield the throttled error (never a failure); other 5xx
  must fail "Google Contacts answered <status> after <n> attempts."; a network error must be logged as a warning and
  fail "Google Contacts could not be reached.".
- **SPEC-15.639**: A 401, or a 403 that is not a rate limit, must yield the unauthorized error without retry. Any other
  non-success status must fail "Google Contacts refused the request (<status>)." and an unreadable success body must
  fail "Google Contacts answered with a response this version cannot read." (logged as a warning). A response body must
  never be copied into an error message.
- **SPEC-15.640**: Listing groups must page the contact groups and offer only the user's own labels (type
  `USER_CONTACT_GROUP`) and the system groups `contactGroups/myContacts` and `contactGroups/starred`, with the id as the
  resource name, the name as the formatted name, else the name, else the resource name, and the member count when
  present; it must fail "Google Contacts kept returning label pages." after 1000 pages and "Google Contacts refused the
  label list." when the list is refused as expired.
- **SPEC-15.641**: A Google person must map to a source record with the resource name as external id and Google's etag;
  the display, given and family names from the person's primary name (else the first); the company, title and department
  from the primary organization (else the first); emails with the primary first and lowercase type labels; phones in
  source order with canonical form, lowercase label and primary flag; the resource names of its contact-group
  memberships as group ids; blank values treated as absent; and `deleted` from the person's metadata. Photos, notes and
  addresses must not be read.
- **SPEC-15.642**: The Microsoft provider must be read-only: it must issue only `GET /v1.0/me/contacts/delta` and `GET
  /v1.0/me/contactFolders` against `https://graph.microsoft.com`, each with the access token as a Bearer credential,
  selecting only
  `id,givenName,surname,displayName,emailAddresses,homePhones,businessPhones,mobilePhone,companyName,jobTitle,department,categories`
  for contacts and a page size of 100; the consent scope must be exactly `Contacts.Read offline_access`.
- **SPEC-15.643**: A delta read must follow `@odata.nextLink` until a page carries `@odata.deltaLink`, store that link
  verbatim as the next sync token, and send a stored token back as the start URL of the next read. A last page with
  neither link must return the contacts with no next sync token. A read must fail "Microsoft Graph kept returning pages
  past any plausible address book." after 1000 pages.
- **SPEC-15.644**: A delta token Graph refuses as stale (410, or 400 whose body names `syncStateNotFound`,
  `syncStateInvalid` or `resyncRequired`) must trigger one full re-read from the start path and the result must report
  `was_full_resync`; if no token was sent, or the full re-read is also refused as stale, the read must fail "Microsoft
  Graph refused a full read as a stale delta token.".
- **SPEC-15.645**: A request must be retried, up to 5 attempts in total, after a network error, 429 or 5xx. The wait
  must be the `Retry-After` seconds capped at 30 s when sent, else full jitter over an exponential ceiling (500 ms
  doubling, capped at 30 s). After the last attempt a 429 or 503 must yield the throttled error, another 5xx must fail
  "Microsoft Graph answered <status> after <n> attempts.", and a network error must be logged as a warning and fail
  "Microsoft Graph could not be reached.".
- **SPEC-15.646**: A 401, or a 403 whose body does not name `TooManyRequests` or `ApplicationThrottled`, must yield the
  unauthorized error without retry. Any other non-success status (including a throttle-named 403) must fail "Microsoft
  Graph refused the request (<status>).", and an unreadable success body must fail "Microsoft Graph answered with a
  response this version cannot read." (logged as a warning). A response body must never be copied into an error message.
- **SPEC-15.647**: Listing groups must read the contact folders (following `@odata.nextLink`), returning each folder's
  id as the group id and its display name (else its id) as the name with no member count; it must fail "Microsoft Graph
  refused the folder list." when refused as stale and "Microsoft Graph kept returning folder pages." after 1000 pages.
- **SPEC-15.648**: A Graph contact must map to a source record with its `id` as external id and its `@odata.etag`; blank
  names, company, title and department treated as absent; emails in Graph's order without labels; phones in the order
  mobile (primary, label `mobile`), business (`work`), home (`home`) with blanks skipped; its `categories` as group ids;
  and `deleted` true exactly when the record carries an `@removed` object.
- **SPEC-15.649**: The Google consent URL must be built on `https://accounts.google.com/o/oauth2/v2/auth` with,
  URL-encoded: the host's client id, the redirect URI, `response_type=code`, scope `contacts.readonly openid email` (no
  write scope), `access_type=offline`, `prompt=consent`, `include_granted_scopes=false`, the state, and a PKCE S256 code
  challenge. The client secret and the verifier must never appear in it.
- **SPEC-15.650**: The Microsoft consent URL must be built on the `/common/` Entra authorize endpoint with, URL-encoded:
  the client id, the redirect URI, `response_type=code`, `response_mode=query`, scope `Contacts.Read offline_access
  openid email`, `prompt=consent`, the state, and a PKCE S256 challenge; the client secret and the verifier must never
  appear in it.
- **SPEC-15.651**: A PKCE pair must be a 64-character random verifier and a challenge equal to the unpadded URL-safe
  base64 of the SHA-256 of the verifier.
- **SPEC-15.652**: A granted scope string (space-delimited, any order) must count as covering contact reads only when it
  contains, as a whole word, the read scope (Google: `https://www.googleapis.com/auth/contacts.readonly` or
  `https://www.googleapis.com/auth/contacts`; Microsoft: `Contacts.Read` or `Contacts.ReadWrite`); a scope that merely
  starts the same way must not count.
- **SPEC-15.653**: Token exchange and refresh must POST a form to the provider's token endpoint (Google:
  `https://oauth2.googleapis.com/token`; Microsoft: the `/common/` v2.0 token endpoint) carrying the client id and
  secret, the code and PKCE verifier (exchange) or the refresh token (refresh), and for Microsoft the full scope set on
  both calls.
- **SPEC-15.654**: A token endpoint error body whose `error` is `invalid_grant` (Microsoft also `interaction_required`)
  must classify as a revoked grant; any other failure must classify as refused with only `<error code> (HTTP <status>)`
  or `HTTP <status>`; a success body that cannot be parsed must be refused with "token response was not understood:
  <parse error>"; a transport failure must classify as a transport error. No request value (secret, code, verifier,
  refresh token) may appear in any of these messages.
- **SPEC-15.655**: A revoked grant must surface to the caller as 400 "Google has revoked this connection. Connect the
  account again."; a refused token request must surface as an external-service error naming `google` with "token request
  refused: <detail>", and a transport failure as "token request failed: <detail>".
- **SPEC-15.656**: The connected account's email must be read once at connect time from the provider's userinfo endpoint
  with the access token; a transport failure, a non-success status, an unparseable body, or an absent or blank `email`
  must fail as an external-service error ("userinfo failed: ...", "userinfo refused (<status>)", "userinfo not JSON:
  ...", "userinfo carried no email address") for the provider, and no connection may be recorded.
- **SPEC-15.657**: The host's OAuth client must be resolved from the application-tier secret store as a trimmed,
  non-blank id and secret pair: both present is a configured client, both absent is no client (connecting is
  unavailable), and exactly one present must fail with a configuration error naming the key that is missing ("<Provider>
  is half configured: <present key> is set and <missing key> is not. ... add <missing key> beside it or remove both.").
- **SPEC-15.658**: The shared client handle must let the running process replace the OAuth client without a restart (the
  next connect or refresh must use the new value), must serialize writes of the id and secret pair, and its `Debug`
  output must report only whether a client is held, never the id or secret.
- **SPEC-15.659**: The CardDAV client must authenticate every request with HTTP Basic using the Apple ID and
  app-specific password, send an XML body with `Depth` set per request, and default to the base
  `https://contacts.icloud.com`; a DAV href must be joined to the base unless it is already an absolute http(s) URL.
- **SPEC-15.660**: Address-book discovery must issue three PROPFINDs in order (current-user-principal at `/` depth 0;
  addressbook-home-set at the principal depth 0; the home set depth 1) and return the href of the first collection whose
  resource type includes `addressbook`. It must fail with "The contact server did not say which account this credential
  belongs to.", "The contact server did not say where this account's contacts live." or "This account has no contacts
  address book to read." when the respective answer is missing.
- **SPEC-15.661**: A CardDAV response must classify as: 401, or a 403 whose `DAV` header does not mention `addressbook`,
  unauthorized (no retry); 429 or any 5xx throttled; 507, or a 403 with an addressbook `DAV` header, a failure whose
  message contains "sync token is no longer valid"; any other status outside success and 207 a failure "The contact
  server refused the request with status <n>."; a network error a failure "The contact server could not be reached: it
  timed out|the connection failed"; an unreadable body "The contact server's response could not be read.".
- **SPEC-15.662**: A multistatus body must be parsed into responses, each with its href, etag (quotes stripped), address
  data, resource types (lowercase, namespace-free), first status, and named properties (a nested href stored under its
  parent property name), plus the document-level and per-collection sync token; entity references and CDATA must be
  preserved in text.
- **SPEC-15.663**: A multistatus parse must fail rather than return an empty result when the body has no `multistatus`
  element ("The contact server's response was not a CardDAV multistatus document."), when it ends with unclosed elements
  ("The contact server's CardDAV response ended mid-document, so it cannot be read as the whole address book."), or when
  the XML is malformed ("The contact server's response could not be read as CardDAV XML: <error>").
- **SPEC-15.664**: A delta read must send a `sync-collection` REPORT (depth 1, sync level 1) with the token XML-escaped
  in the body and return the changed cards, the hrefs reported gone (responses with a 404 status) separately, and the
  next sync token; its status classification must follow SPEC-15.661 except that a 403 must always read as the
  stale-token failure.
- **SPEC-15.665**: Parsing an iCloud response's cards must pass each card through the vCard reader with default limits,
  keeping contacts and group cards separately, and must skip a card the reader refuses as a whole without failing the
  read.
- **SPEC-15.666**: The iCloud groups offered must be each group card that has a UID (named by its FN, else "Untitled
  group", with a member count of only the members present as cards in the book), sorted case-insensitively by name,
  followed by the group "Ungrouped" (id `mokosh:ungrouped`) counting contacts named by no group card.
- **SPEC-15.667**: Membership must be stamped onto contacts from group cards by matching each member id to a contact's
  external id, adding the group id to the contact's group ids once.
- **SPEC-15.668**: An iCloud read with a sync token must use the delta when it reports no removals. When the delta
  reports any removed href, or the server refuses the token as no longer valid, it must read the whole address book (one
  `addressbook-query` REPORT), fetch a fresh sync token, and report a full resync; any other failure of the delta must
  fail the read and must not fall back to a full read.
- **SPEC-15.669**: An iCloud read with no sync token must read the whole address book, apply group membership, and
  return the book's current sync token when available (a failure to fetch the token must leave it absent).
- **SPEC-15.670**: The supported contact-source providers must be exactly `google`, `vcard`, `icloud` and `microsoft`;
  any other string, including a different case, must not be supported.
- **SPEC-15.671**: User-facing words per provider must be: Google "Google Contacts", group "Google label", account
  "Google account", vendor "Google"; iCloud "iCloud Contacts", group "iCloud group", account "Apple ID", vendor "Apple";
  Microsoft "Microsoft 365 Contacts", group "Microsoft 365 folder", account "Microsoft account", vendor "Microsoft"; any
  other provider (including `vcard`) "Contact import", group "category", account "source". The credential-gone sentence
  must be "Google has revoked this connection. Connect the account again", "Apple no longer accepts this app-specific
  password. Enter a new one in Settings, Integrations", or "Microsoft has revoked this connection. Connect the account
  again" for the first three.
- **SPEC-15.672**: A source error must read "The contact provider is rate limiting this connection." (throttled), "The
  contact provider refused this connection's credential." (unauthorized), or its own reason (failed), and must convert
  to an integration error carrying that text.
- **SPEC-15.673**: A provider's `changes_since` must return the whole source or an error, never a partial list; an
  expired cursor must yield a full read flagged `was_full_resync`; `lists_everything` must default to true, and a
  provider that returns false must never cause an absent record to be flagged deleted.
- **SPEC-15.674**: Reading a provider's tenant switch must return that provider's own setting for `google`, `icloud` and
  `microsoft` (unset means enabled) and must fail with an internal error "<provider> has no contact-sync switch, so
  nothing can be read for it" for any other provider, including `vcard`; it must never answer another provider's
  setting.
- **SPEC-15.675**: The one-shot client-secret cleanup must list every tenant, delete each tenant's stored Google OAuth
  client secret, count successes in `cleared` and failures in `failed`, log each failure as a warning naming the tenant
  id and continue with the remaining tenants, log an info summary when anything was addressed, and never delete a
  tenant's contact-sync refresh token.
- **SPEC-15.676**: A contact edit must capture the lockable fields only when the contact has a live (not unlinked) sync
  link; the captured values must treat NULL and empty text as equal, tags as a sorted list, and phones as an ordered
  list of type, number and extension.
- **SPEC-15.677**: After an edit, every lockable field whose captured value changed must get a `contact_field_locks` row
  with the editing user; a field already locked must keep its original locker and time, only newly locked fields must be
  returned, and a `contact_sync.fields_locked` audit row listing them must be written only when at least one was newly
  locked.
- **SPEC-15.678**: The email match key must be the trimmed, Unicode-lowercased address with any `+tag` removed from the
  local part and dots kept; an address without exactly one `@`, with an empty local part or domain, or whose local part
  is empty after removing the tag must have no key.
- **SPEC-15.679**: The phone match key must be the digits of the trimmed number, prefixed with `+` when the number
  starts with `+` or `00` (a leading `00` removed); a national number must stay digits-only with no country guessed; a
  number with fewer than 7 digits must have no key.
- **SPEC-15.680**: The name match key must be the Unicode-lowercased text with internal whitespace collapsed to single
  spaces and trimmed, keeping its script; an empty result must have no key.
- **SPEC-15.681**: A source contact's names must map as: given name to first name and family name to last name; with
  only a family name, the family name becomes the first name and the last name is empty; with neither, the first name is
  the display name, else the organisation, else the first email address, else the literal `(no name)`, and the last name
  is empty.
- **SPEC-15.682**: Every mapped text value must have invisible characters removed, be trimmed, be dropped when empty,
  and be cut on a character boundary to its column width: names 100, email 255, company 255, title 100, department 100,
  notes 10,000.
- **SPEC-15.683**: Only the first email address (the source orders primary first) must be kept as the contact's email;
  each additional address must be counted in the record's dropped list as "<n> additional email address(es)".
- **SPEC-15.684**: A phone must be stored as the source's canonical number when that is storable, else the
  formatting-stripped number (spaces, tabs, non-breaking spaces, hyphens, parentheses and dots removed). A number is
  storable only when it is an optional `+` followed by 2 to 15 digits whose first digit is 1 to 9, and at most 50
  characters. An unstorable number must be dropped from the contact and listed as "unstorable phone number <number>",
  without failing the contact; a repeated stored number must be kept once.
- **SPEC-15.685**: Phone labels must map `mobile`, `work` and `home` (case-insensitive) to those types, any label ending
  in `fax` to fax, and every other or missing label to `other`.
- **SPEC-15.686**: A mapped contact with phones must have exactly one primary phone: the first one the source marked
  primary, else the first phone.
- **SPEC-15.687**: A source photo must never be fetched or stored; it must be listed as "photo" (embedded) or "photo (a
  link, not fetched)", and the source's dropped properties must be appended to the dropped list. An organisation must
  map to a free-text company name only and never create or link a company.
- **SPEC-15.688**: A source record must link automatically to a Mokosh contact only when exactly one contact shares a
  normalized email with any of the record's addresses (not only the primary) and that contact is not already linked to
  another record of the same connection.
- **SPEC-15.689**: When several contacts share an email with the record, or the single email match is already linked,
  every email-matched contact must be put to review with reason `email_ambiguous`.
- **SPEC-15.690**: A contact sharing a phone key with the record must be put to review with reason `phone`; a contact
  with the same name key and sharing a company key (a linked company's name or the freeform company name) must be put to
  review with reason `name_company`; a name alone must never produce a match.
- **SPEC-15.691**: A contact that qualifies under more than one rule must appear once, with the strongest reason
  (`email_ambiguous`, then `phone`, then `name_company`); review pairs must be ordered by contact id; no match must
  yield a new contact.

### 15.3 Assets and asset catalog

- **SPEC-15.1000**: Every asset-catalog route (`/asset-models`, `/asset-models/signature-detector`,
  `/asset-models/{id}`, `/asset-templates`, `/asset-templates/{id}`) must authenticate the caller with the assets-module
  extractor before any handler logic, so an unauthenticated or unauthorized caller receives the auth error, not the
  feature-off 404.
- **SPEC-15.1001**: When the `AssetsCatalog` feature toggle is off, or no feature snapshot is present, every
  asset-catalog route must answer 404 with the message "This endpoint is not enabled on this deployment" before any
  database access.
- **SPEC-15.1002**: `POST`, `PUT` and `DELETE` on `/asset-models` and `/asset-templates` must additionally require an
  admin caller; a non-admin must be rejected. `GET` routes require only the assets-module permission.
- **SPEC-15.1003**: `GET /asset-models/signature-detector` must be served by the signature handler and never parsed as
  an `{id}` of `/asset-models/{id}`.
- **SPEC-15.1004**: `GET /asset-models` must reject a `q` longer than 200 characters with a validation error. A
  non-empty `q`, trimmed and lowercased, must match case-insensitively as a substring of `manufacturer + " " + model`.
- **SPEC-15.1005**: `GET /asset-models` must apply `limit` default 10 when omitted and clamp any supplied value to the
  range 1..=50.
- **SPEC-15.1006**: `GET /asset-models` with a missing, empty or whitespace-only `q` must return the caller tenant's
  models without filtering. Results must be ordered by `uses_count` descending, then lowercased manufacturer, then
  lowercased model.
- **SPEC-15.1007**: `POST /asset-models` must validate `manufacturer` and `model` as 1..=100 characters,
  `warranty_months` and `end_of_life_months` as 0..=600, `default_department` at most 100 and `default_license_vendor`
  at most 150 characters. It must reject an `asset_type_id` that is not a type of the caller's tenant with a field
  validation error on `asset_type_id` ("asset type does not exist in this tenant"). It must store `source` as
  `tenant_authored` whatever the body says and answer 201 with the stored row.
- **SPEC-15.1008**: `POST /asset-models` for a manufacturer, model and asset type that already exists in the tenant
  (compared case-insensitively) must answer 409 "A catalog row for this manufacturer / model / type already exists."
- **SPEC-15.1009**: `POST /asset-models` must store `specs` as the empty JSON object `{}` when the field is omitted.
- **SPEC-15.1010**: `GET /asset-models/{id}` must answer 404 "Asset model" when the id does not exist in the caller's
  tenant, including when it exists in another tenant.
- **SPEC-15.1011**: `PUT /asset-models/{id}` must update only the fields present in the body (an absent or null field
  keeps its stored value), apply the same bounds as create, reject a foreign `asset_type_id` as in SPEC-15.1007, answer
  409 "Another catalog row already has this manufacturer / model / type." when the change collides with another row,
  answer 404 "Asset model" when no row matches, and otherwise return the refreshed row.
- **SPEC-15.1012**: `DELETE /asset-models/{id}` must answer 204 and remove the row, must keep assets that referenced it
  (their model link becomes null), must remove templates that reference it, and must answer 404 "Asset model" when no
  row matches in the caller's tenant.
- **SPEC-15.1013**: `GET /asset-templates` must return every template of the caller's tenant joined to its model
  (manufacturer, model, asset type), ordered by `updated_at` descending.
- **SPEC-15.1014**: `GET /asset-templates/{id}` must answer 404 "Asset template" when the id does not exist in the
  caller's tenant.
- **SPEC-15.1015**: `POST /asset-templates` must validate `name` as 1..=150 characters, `department` at most 100 and
  `license_seat_count` as 0..=100000. It must answer 404 "Asset model" when `asset_model_id` is not a model of the
  caller's tenant, record the calling user as `created_by`, answer 409 "A template with this name already exists." on a
  duplicate name, and answer 201 with the joined template row.
- **SPEC-15.1016**: `PUT /asset-templates/{id}` must update only the fields present in the body, answer 404 "Asset
  model" for a foreign `asset_model_id`, answer 409 "Another template already uses this name." on a name collision,
  answer 404 "Asset template" when no row matches, and otherwise return the refreshed joined row.
- **SPEC-15.1017**: `DELETE /asset-templates/{id}` must answer 204 and remove the template, or 404 "Asset template" when
  no row matches in the caller's tenant.
- **SPEC-15.1018**: `GET /asset-models/signature-detector` must return `signature: null` when the tenant has no
  candidate, otherwise the candidate with the highest recent group count (7-day window, `window_days` 7). A candidate
  whose manufacturer, model and type (case-insensitive) match a `tenant_authored` model must be suppressed; one matching
  only an `auto_derived` model must be returned with that model's id as `existing_model_id`. The
  `template_suggestion.name_hint` must be "<manufacturer> <model>".
- **SPEC-15.1019**: The signature-candidate view must be refreshed concurrently every 60 seconds by the
  `asset_signature_detector_refresh` job. A failed refresh must return the database error to the scheduler instead of
  reporting success.
- **SPEC-15.1020**: Resolving a template for bulk creation must answer 404 "Asset template" when the template does not
  exist in the caller's tenant.
- **SPEC-15.1021**: Every catalog query must filter by the caller's tenant and run in a tenant-scoped transaction.
- **SPEC-15.1022**: `GET /asset-types` must return the caller tenant's asset types as a paginated list ordered by name,
  and must answer 422 on a `sort` parameter because the endpoint is unsorted.
- **SPEC-15.1023**: `POST /asset-types` must require an admin, validate `name` as 1..=100 characters and `itil_category`
  as at most 50, default `is_active` to true, store the type in the caller's tenant with an audit entry in the same
  transaction, and return the stored type.
- **SPEC-15.1024**: `PUT /asset-types/{id}` must require an admin and replace `name`, `icon`, `parent_type_id`,
  `is_active` and `itil_category` with the body values (an omitted `icon`, `parent_type_id` or `itil_category` becomes
  null, an omitted `is_active` becomes true), and must answer 404 "Asset type" when no row of the caller's tenant
  matches.
- **SPEC-15.1025**: `DELETE /asset-types/{id}` must require an admin and answer 404 "Asset type" when no row of the
  caller's tenant matches.
- **SPEC-15.1026**: `GET /assets` must accept a staff caller with an authenticated user, or a contact caller holding the
  `assets:read` capability (loaded from the database per request). For a contact caller it must force the `company_id`
  filter to the contact's own company whatever the query says, and must answer with the contact projection (id,
  company_id, asset_tag, name, asset_type_id, status, manufacturer, model, serial_number, warranty_expiry, end_of_life)
  and no other asset field. A staff caller without an authenticated user must receive 401.
- **SPEC-15.1027**: `GET /assets` must AND-combine the supplied filters: equality on `company_id`, `asset_type_id`,
  `site_id`, `assigned_user_id`, `status`, `department`, `manufacturer` and `model`; `tag` as membership in the asset's
  tags; `warranty_within_days` as warranty expiry between today and today plus N days; `end_of_life_before` as end of
  life strictly earlier than the date; `q` as a case-insensitive substring match on name or serial number. It must
  reject `warranty_within_days` outside 0..=36500, `q` over 200 characters and any text filter over 100 characters with
  a validation error, and must order results by name.
- **SPEC-15.1028**: When a listed, searched, fetched or bulk-created asset has an `assigned_user_id` that resolves to no
  user name, the response must carry a null `assigned_user_name` and the server must log the unresolved user id.
- **SPEC-15.1029**: `GET /assets/{id}` must answer 404 "Asset" when the id is not in the caller's tenant. For a contact
  caller it must require the `assets:read` capability, answer 404 "Asset" (not 403) for an asset of another company, and
  return the contact projection.
- **SPEC-15.1030**: An asset response must report `status` "active" when the stored status is null and `tags` as an
  empty list when the stored tags are null.
- **SPEC-15.1031**: `POST /assets` must require the assets module, validate `name` as 1..=255 characters, `hostname` at
  most 255, `ip_address` as a valid IP of at most 45 characters, `mac_address` as a valid MAC of at most 50,
  `department` at most 100, `itil_lifecycle_stage` at most 50, `license_vendor` at most 150 and `license_seat_count` at
  least 0, default `status` to "active", and answer 422 on field `asset_tag` ("asset_tag is auto-generated and cannot be
  supplied on create") when the body contains an `asset_tag`.
- **SPEC-15.1032**: The server must issue every asset tag as "AST-" plus the number zero-padded to at least 3 digits,
  from a per-tenant counter advanced atomically. The first reservation for a tenant must start above the highest
  `AST-<n>` already present in the tenant. A reservation of N tags must return N consecutive numbers.
- **SPEC-15.1033**: Creating an asset must write the asset, a `created` row in the asset audit log performed by the
  caller, and a generic audit entry in one transaction, so a failure of any of them leaves no asset.
- **SPEC-15.1034**: `POST /assets` must return the full asset response including the resolved asset type name, company
  name, contact name and assigned user name.
- **SPEC-15.1035**: `PUT /assets/{id}` must update only the fields present in the body (an absent field keeps its
  value), answer 422 on field `asset_tag` ("asset_tag is read-only; delete and recreate the asset to issue a new one")
  when the body contains an `asset_tag`, answer 404 "Asset" when the asset is not in the caller's tenant, and return the
  refreshed asset.
- **SPEC-15.1036**: `PUT /assets/{id}` that sets `itil_lifecycle_stage` to exactly "retired" without a `status` must set
  the status to "retired". An explicit `status` must win.
- **SPEC-15.1037**: A successful `PUT` or `PATCH` of an asset must write one asset audit-log row performed by the
  caller, with action `status_changed` when the body supplies a status that differs from the stored one and `updated`
  otherwise, and with the field-level before and after differences as `changes`.
- **SPEC-15.1038**: `PATCH /assets/{id}` must treat an absent key as "leave unchanged", a present key with null as
  "write NULL" and a present key with a value as "write the value" for each nullable field. It must answer 422 on field
  `asset_tag` ("asset_tag is read-only; delete and recreate the asset to issue a new one") when the key `asset_tag` is
  present, even with null, and must apply the create-time validation bounds to the fields it carries.
- **SPEC-15.1039**: `PATCH /assets/{id}` must write only the supplied columns. `tags` must replace the whole list (an
  empty list clears it) and `notes` null must clear the note. A body with no supplied column must return the current
  asset and write no row and no audit entry.
- **SPEC-15.1040**: `PATCH /assets/{id}` must answer 404 "Asset" when the asset is not in the caller's tenant.
- **SPEC-15.1041**: `PATCH /assets/{id}` that sets `itil_lifecycle_stage` to "retired" (case-insensitive) without a
  `status` must set the status to "retired"; an explicit `status` must win.
- **SPEC-15.1042**: `DELETE /assets/{id}` must require an admin, write a `deleted` asset audit-log row before removing
  the asset in the same transaction, and answer 404 "Asset" (leaving no audit row) when the asset is not in the caller's
  tenant.
