- **SPEC-15.1043**: `GET /assets/{id}/relationships` must return the relationships of the caller's tenant in which the
  asset is the parent or the child, paginated, and must answer 422 on a `sort` parameter.
- **SPEC-15.1044**: `POST /assets/{id}/relationships` must store a relationship with the path asset as parent, the body
  `child_asset_id` as child and the body `relationship_type` as given, write an audit entry in the same transaction and
  return the stored relationship.
- **SPEC-15.1045**: `DELETE /asset-relationships/{id}` must answer 404 "Asset relationship" when the id is not in the
  caller's tenant.
- **SPEC-15.1046**: `GET /assets/{id}/impact` must answer 400 "Unknown direction='<value>'; expected upstream |
  downstream | both" for any other `direction` (default "both"), answer 404 "Asset" when the root asset is not in the
  caller's tenant, and return `root_asset_id`, the effective `depth`, the `direction` and the walked `nodes`. Each node
  must carry the neighbouring asset id and name, the edge's parent and child ids and type, a `direction` of "upstream"
  or "downstream", and a `depth` starting at 1. Downstream nodes must precede upstream nodes, each half ordered by depth
  then asset name.
- **SPEC-15.1047**: The impact walk depth must be the requested `depth` (default 10) clamped to 1..=10 and then limited
  to the tenant's `ci/impact_max_depth` setting, and the response must report that effective depth. A cycle in the
  relationships must not make the walk unbounded.
- **SPEC-15.1048**: `GET /assets/{id}/configuration-items` must list the asset's items ordered by name, paginated,
  without the secret value, and must answer 422 on a `sort` parameter.
- **SPEC-15.1049**: `GET /configuration-items/{id}` must return the decrypted value, write an asset audit-log row
  (action `synced`, changes `{"event":"config_item_revealed"}`) performed by the caller in the same transaction, answer
  404 "Configuration item" when the id is not in the caller's tenant, and return an error without writing the audit row
  when decryption fails.
- **SPEC-15.1050**: `POST /assets/{id}/configuration-items` must validate `name` as 1..=100 characters, store the value
  encrypted under the server key (never in plaintext), write an audit snapshot that excludes the encrypted value, and
  return the item including the plaintext value.
- **SPEC-15.1051**: `DELETE /configuration-items/{id}` must answer 404 "Configuration item" when the id is not in the
  caller's tenant.
- **SPEC-15.1052**: `GET /assets/{id}/credentials` must list the asset's credentials ordered by name, paginated, and
  must never include username, password or notes.
- **SPEC-15.1053**: Listing credentials for a company must return every credential of the tenant whose `company_id` is
  the company, both asset-linked and company-scoped, ordered by name, without any secret field.
- **SPEC-15.1054**: `GET /credentials/{id}` must return the decrypted username, password and notes, write an asset
  audit-log row (action `synced`, changes `{"event":"credential_read"}`) performed by the caller in the same
  transaction, answer 404 "Credential" when the id is not in the caller's tenant, and return an error without writing
  the audit row when decryption fails.
- **SPEC-15.1055**: `POST /assets/{id}/credentials` must validate `name` as 1..=100 characters and `url`, when present,
  as a syntactically valid URL of any scheme. It must store username, password and notes encrypted, copy the asset's
  `company_id` onto the credential, write an asset audit-log row (action `updated`, changes
  `{"event":"credential_created"}`), write a generic audit entry whose snapshot excludes the encrypted columns, and
  return the credential.
- **SPEC-15.1056**: `DELETE /credentials/{id}` must write a generic audit entry whose snapshot excludes the encrypted
  columns in the same transaction as the delete, and answer 404 "Credential" when the id is not in the caller's tenant.
- **SPEC-15.1057**: `GET /assets/{id}/audit-log` must require an admin, return the asset's audit-log rows newest first,
  paginated, with `performed_by_name` as "<first> <last>" falling back to the user's email when the name is blank, and
  must log the ids of performers that resolve to no user. It must answer 422 on a `sort` parameter.
- **SPEC-15.1058**: `POST /assets/search` and `POST /assets/search/facets` must answer 404 "This endpoint is not enabled
  on this deployment" before any database access when the `assets_search_v2` feature is off or no feature snapshot is
  present.
- **SPEC-15.1059**: The search body must be rejected with 422 on field `filters[<i>]` ("field + op combination is not
  supported for this facet") when a filter pairs `contains_tag` with any field but `tags`, uses any operator on `tags`
  other than `contains_tag`, gives `is_null` or `is_not_null` any value, uses `within` on a non-date field or without an
  integer `days`, uses `before` or `after` on a non-date field or without exactly one value, gives `eq` other than
  exactly one value, or gives `in` or `not_in` no value. The date fields are `warranty_expiry`, `end_of_life`,
  `purchase_date` and `installed_date`. A `q` over 200 characters must be rejected with a validation error.
- **SPEC-15.1060**: `POST /assets/search` must AND-combine the filters, match a non-blank `q` (trimmed, lowercased) as a
  substring of the search haystack, clamp a `within` window to 0..=3650 days, order by the requested sort clauses
  (default name ascending) using only the known field names, return the paginated asset list, and answer 422 on a `sort`
  query parameter.
- **SPEC-15.1061**: `POST /assets/search/facets` must return, under the same filters, for each of `status`, `company`,
  `asset_type`, `assigned_user`, `department`, `manufacturer` and `itil_lifecycle_stage` the top 10 non-null values by
  descending count, with a label (the company, type or user name for id facets), plus `warranty_expiring_in_30_days`
  (warranty expiry between today and today plus 30 days) and `end_of_life_passed` (end of life before today).
- **SPEC-15.1062**: Search and facet queries must always include the caller's tenant as the first condition.
- **SPEC-15.1063**: `POST /assets/exists` must validate `serials` as 1..=500 entries, ignore blank entries after
  trimming, match case-insensitively against assets of the given company in the caller's tenant, and return only the
  matching serials, trimmed, in first-occurrence order with duplicates collapsed. It must not depend on a feature
  toggle.
- **SPEC-15.1064**: `POST /assets/bulk-create` must answer 404 "This endpoint is not enabled on this deployment" before
  any database access when the `AssetsCatalog` feature is off, and otherwise answer 201 with `created` (the full asset
  responses) and `count`.
- **SPEC-15.1065**: The bulk-create body must be rejected with a validation error unless `serials` has 1..=500 entries
  and each has `serial_number` of 1..=100 characters, `name` of 1..=255, `asset_tag` of at most 100, `hostname` of at
  most 255 and a valid `ip_address` and `mac_address`. Any serial entry carrying an `asset_tag` must be rejected with
  422 on field `serials[<i>].asset_tag` ("asset_tag is auto-generated and cannot be supplied on create").
- **SPEC-15.1066**: Bulk create must use `template_id` when present (its model), else `asset_model_id`. With neither it
  must answer 422 on `asset_model_id` ("either template_id or asset_model_id must be set"). An unknown template must
  answer 422 on `template_id` ("template does not exist in this tenant") and an unknown model 422 on `asset_model_id`
  ("asset model does not exist in this tenant").
- **SPEC-15.1067**: When a template is used, its company, site, default assignee and department must override the
  request's values where the template sets them. The department must otherwise fall back to the model's default
  department.
- **SPEC-15.1068**: Before inserting any row, bulk create must verify that the effective company, site and assignee
  exist in the caller's tenant and otherwise answer 422 on `company_id` ("company does not exist in this tenant"),
  `site_id` ("site does not exist in this tenant") or `assigned_user_id` ("user does not exist in this tenant").
- **SPEC-15.1069**: Bulk create must set each asset's warranty expiry and end of life to the purchase date plus the
  model's warranty or end-of-life months, and leave them null when the purchase date or the months are absent.
- **SPEC-15.1070**: Each bulk-created asset must have status "active", the model's manufacturer, model and asset type,
  the model link, a server-issued asset tag (consecutive in request order), and the name given or "<manufacturer>
  <model> #<serial>".
- **SPEC-15.1071**: A bulk create where any serial collides with an existing asset must answer 422 on field
  `serials[<i>].serial_number` ("serial `<serial>` is already assigned to an asset in this tenant") and must persist no
  asset of the batch. Any other insert error must be returned and must persist no asset of the batch.
- **SPEC-15.1072**: Bulk create must write one `created` asset audit-log row per asset, add the batch size to the
  model's `uses_count` and, when a template was used, to the template's `uses_count`, all in the transaction that
  inserts the assets.
- **SPEC-15.1073**: Bulk create must return the created assets in request order and must answer 404 "Asset" if a created
  asset cannot be read back.
- **SPEC-15.1074**: `POST /assets/{id}/report-issue` must answer 404 "Asset" when the asset is not in the caller's
  tenant, must answer a configuration error "Ticket service not configured" when no ticket service is wired, and for a
  contact caller must require the `assets:report_issue` capability and answer 404 "Asset" for an asset of another
  company. A staff caller must be authenticated.
- **SPEC-15.1075**: The reported ticket's title must be the trimmed `summary`, or "Reported issue: <asset name>" when
  the summary is missing or blank, and its description the trimmed `description`, or none when blank.
- **SPEC-15.1076**: A contact's report must create a ticket with source `portal`, the contact as requester and the
  asset's company, link it to the asset, and return the refreshed ticket; a failure to link must answer an internal
  server error whose message begins "stamp asset_id on report-issue ticket" or "commit asset_id stamp".
- **SPEC-15.1077**: A staff report must create an `internal` ticket for the asset's company with `asset_id` set, created
  by the calling user, and return the refreshed ticket.
- **SPEC-15.1078**: Asset secrets (configuration item values and credential username, password and notes) must be
  encrypted under the configured 32-byte key before storage; the service must have no constructor without a key.
- **SPEC-15.1079**: Every asset, asset type, relationship, configuration item, credential and audit-log query must
  filter by the caller's tenant and run in a tenant-scoped transaction.
- **SPEC-15.1080**: The contact asset projection must always contain every one of its keys, using null for an unset
  value, so its shape is stable.
- **SPEC-15.1081**: An asset type with a null stored `is_active` must be reported as active.

### 15.4 Knowledge base

- **SPEC-15.1082**: A comment anchor must be a JSON object with exactly the keys `type`, `exact`, and optionally
  `prefix`, `suffix` and `refinedBy`; any other shape or unknown key must be rejected with 422 on field `anchor` ("not a
  TextQuoteSelector: <cause>"), and a `type` other than "TextQuoteSelector" with 422 on `anchor.type`.
- **SPEC-15.1083**: An anchor's `exact` must be 1..=2000 characters (counted as characters, not bytes); an empty value
  must be rejected with 422 on `anchor.exact` ("the quoted text is required") and a longer one with 422 on
  `anchor.exact` ("the quoted text is longer than 2000 characters").
- **SPEC-15.1084**: An anchor's `prefix` and `suffix` must each be at most 64 characters; a longer one must be rejected
  with 422 on `anchor.prefix` or `anchor.suffix` ("context is longer than 64 characters").
- **SPEC-15.1085**: An anchor's `refinedBy`, when present, must have `type` "TextPositionSelector" (else 422 on
  `anchor.refinedBy.type`), `start` of at least 0 (else 422 on `anchor.refinedBy.start`, "must not be negative") and
  `end` not before `start` (else 422 on `anchor.refinedBy.end`, "must not be before start"). The server must store the
  anchor as given and must not check whether it resolves against the article text.
- **SPEC-15.1086**: A mention token must be an `@` not preceded by a letter, digit, `.`, `_` or `-`, followed by a run
  of letters, digits, `.`, `_` and `-`, with trailing `.`, `-` and `_` removed. An `@` with an empty run must yield no
  token. Tokens must be lowercased, unique and in order of first appearance.
- **SPEC-15.1087**: A person must answer to these handles, compared case-insensitively: the local part of their email,
  their first name, their first and last name joined by "." and their first and last name joined with nothing. The last
  name alone must not be a handle.
- **SPEC-15.1088**: A mention token must resolve to a person only when exactly one person answers to it; a token that
  names nobody, two or more people, or is empty must resolve to nobody.
- **SPEC-15.1089**: The people mentioned by a comment body must be unique, in order of first mention, and any person
  with a blank first and last name must have their id logged as an unresolved person name.
- **SPEC-15.1090**: Rendering an article that declares no template variables must return the stored content unchanged
  byte for byte, without running the template engine, even if it contains `{{` or `{%`.
- **SPEC-15.1091**: Rendering must use each declared variable's `default` unless the caller's value for that name is
  supplied, and a supplied value must win over the default.
- **SPEC-15.1092**: Rendering must replace a bare `{{ name }}` block whose name is declared but has neither a value nor
  a default with the text "[missing: name]". An undefined name in a `{% if %}` condition must take the else branch, and
  an expression other than a bare identifier on an undefined name must render empty.
- **SPEC-15.1093**: A template that fails to parse or render must answer 400 "Template render failed: <engine message>."
  and never 500.
- **SPEC-15.1094**: The attachment move must select, across all tenants in `created_at` order, every KB attachment that
  has no file-ledger row or whose ledger path starts with "kb-articles/".
- **SPEC-15.1095**: For each selected attachment the move must count it as already moved when its object exists at the
  tenant-scoped location, rename it from the legacy location when only that exists, and otherwise count it missing and
  leave both the object and the ledger untouched.
- **SPEC-15.1096**: After a file is at the tenant-scoped location the move must update the attachment's ledger
  `storage_path` to that location, scoped to the attachment's tenant; an attachment with no ledger row must update
  nothing.
- **SPEC-15.1097**: A storage or database error during the move must abort the pass and be returned to the caller. A
  pass that considered at least one attachment must log "kb_attachment_move: pass complete" with the moved,
  already-moved and missing counts. The pass runs once per process start under the name `kb_attachment_move`.
- **SPEC-15.1098**: The KB attachment size limit must be `KB_ATTACHMENT_MAX_BYTES` when set, else 5 MiB (5242880 bytes);
  an invalid value must fail configuration loading with a configuration error.
- **SPEC-15.1099**: `POST /kb/articles/{id}/attachments` must require a manager, take the first multipart part named
  `file` (file name defaulting to "image", content type to "application/octet-stream"), answer 400 "Missing 'file' part
  in multipart body" when there is none, answer 400 "Multipart parse: <cause>" or "Multipart read: <cause>" on a
  malformed body, and apply a request-body limit derived from the attachment size limit.
- **SPEC-15.1100**: Uploading a KB attachment must refuse a content type outside the shared inline-image allowlist (SVG
  included), answer 400 "The uploaded file is empty" for zero bytes, and refuse more bytes than the size limit with the
  shared oversized-upload error naming "KB image" and the limit.
- **SPEC-15.1101**: Uploading a KB attachment must answer 404 "Article" when the article is not in the caller's tenant,
  insert the attachment row, store the bytes at the tenant-scoped object key derived from the attachment id (never from
  the file name), record the file in the ledger with entity type `kb_attachment`, and only then commit, so a failure at
  any step leaves no attachment row. The response must carry `id`, `article_id`, `file_name`, `mime_type`, `file_size`,
  `created_at` and `url` ("/api/v1/public/kb/attachments/<id>").
- **SPEC-15.1102**: `GET /kb/articles/{id}/attachments` must require a manager and list the article's attachments newest
  first (then by id).
- **SPEC-15.1103**: `DELETE /kb/articles/{id}/attachments/{attachment_id}` must require a manager, answer 404
  "Attachment" when no row matches in the tenant and article, otherwise delete the row and commit, then delete the
  object. A failure deleting the tenant-scoped object must be returned to the caller after the legacy-object and ledger
  cleanup were attempted; failures deleting the legacy object or the ledger row must be logged as warnings only.
- **SPEC-15.1104**: `GET /api/v1/public/kb/attachments/{attachment_id}` must need no authentication, answer 404
  "Attachment" identically for an unknown and a deleted id, and otherwise stream the object with the stored
  `Content-Type`, `Content-Length` equal to the stored size, `Cache-Control: public, max-age=31536000, immutable`,
  `ETag` of the form "<id>-<size>" in double quotes and `X-Content-Type-Options: nosniff`.
- **SPEC-15.1105**: A public attachment request whose `If-None-Match` lists the current ETag (weak comparison, a
  comma-separated list, or `*`) must answer 304 with `Cache-Control` and `ETag` and must not open the object.
- **SPEC-15.1106**: When the object is missing at the tenant-scoped key the public read must try the legacy flat key of
  the same tenant (taken from the attachment row, never the request), and answer 404 "Attachment" when neither can be
  opened.
- **SPEC-15.1107**: A read error while streaming a public attachment must be logged at error level with the attachment
  id.
- **SPEC-15.1108**: Every KB execution route (`GET` and `POST /tickets/{ticket_id}/kb-executions`, `GET
  /kb-executions/{id}`, `PATCH /kb-executions/{id}/steps/{index}`) must require an authenticated staff user and scope
  every query to that user's tenant.
- **SPEC-15.1109**: `GET /tickets/{ticket_id}/kb-executions` must answer 404 "Ticket" when the ticket is not in the
  caller's tenant, otherwise list the ticket's executions newest first, each with the article title, starter name,
  `total_steps` and `checked_steps`.
- **SPEC-15.1110**: `POST /tickets/{ticket_id}/kb-executions` must render the article with the supplied values (its 404,
  422 and 400 errors propagating), answer 404 "Ticket" when the ticket is not in the tenant, and in one transaction
  store the execution (with the values given, the caller as starter and the id of the article's highest version, or null
  when it has none) and one step per parsed task item, then return the full execution. A step written as already checked
  must be stored checked at creation time by the creating user.
- **SPEC-15.1111**: Step parsing of the rendered Markdown must treat a line as a step only when, after leading
  whitespace, it starts with `- `, `* `, `+ `, or digits followed by `. ` or `) `, then `[ ]`, `[x]` or `[X]`. The step
  text must be the trimmed remainder, indexes must be 0-based in document order including nested items, and lines inside
  a fenced block (backtick or tilde, three or more) must not be steps; an unclosed fence must hide the rest of the
  document.
- **SPEC-15.1112**: `GET /kb-executions/{id}` must answer 404 "KB article execution" when the id is not in the caller's
  tenant, and otherwise return the execution with its steps ordered by index and the starter and checker names, or
  "Unknown" for the starter when the user cannot be resolved.
- **SPEC-15.1113**: `PATCH /kb-executions/{id}/steps/{index}` must answer 404 "KB execution step" when the step does not
  exist in the caller's tenant. `checked: true` must set the check time and checker only when the step is unchecked
  (keeping the first checker otherwise), `checked: false` must clear both, both must be idempotent, and the updated step
  must be returned.
- **SPEC-15.1114**: `GET /kb/categories`, `GET /kb/articles`, `GET /kb/articles/{id}` and `POST
  /kb/articles/{id}/render` must accept a staff caller who is authenticated and whose tenant has the `knowledge_base`
  module on (else 404 "Knowledge base module"), or a contact caller holding the `kb:read` capability; the contact arm
  must not consult the module flag.
- **SPEC-15.1115**: `GET /kb/categories` must return categories ordered by `sort_order` then name, paginated, and must
  answer 422 on a `sort` parameter. A contact must receive only categories whose visibility is not `internal`.
- **SPEC-15.1116**: `POST /kb/categories` must require a manager, validate `name` and `slug` as 1..=100 characters,
  default `visibility` to "internal" and `sort_order` to 0, answer 409 "KbCategory slug '<slug>' already exists" for a
  slug already used in the tenant, write an audit entry in the same transaction and return the category.
- **SPEC-15.1117**: `PUT /kb/categories/{id}` must require a manager, replace all category fields with the body values
  and answer 404 "KB category" when no row matches in the tenant. `DELETE /kb/categories/{id}` must require a manager
  and answer 404 "KB category" when no row matches.
- **SPEC-15.1118**: `GET /kb/articles` for staff must AND-combine `category_id`, `status`, `visibility`,
  `parent_article_id`, `company_id` (article scoped to that company) and `q`. It must reject `q` over 200 characters and
  `status` or `visibility` over 100 characters with a validation error, order by word similarity descending then
  `updated_at` descending when `q` is given and by `updated_at` descending otherwise, and be paginated.
- **SPEC-15.1119**: `GET /kb/articles` for a contact must return only published articles that are `public` or
  `client_specific` naming the contact's own company, ignore any `status`, `visibility` and `company_id` parameter,
  still apply `category_id`, `parent_article_id` and `q`, and answer with the contact projection (id, title, slug,
  content, summary, category_id, published_at, tags, template_variables, updated_at).
- **SPEC-15.1120**: `POST /kb/articles` must require a manager, validate `title` and `slug` as 1..=255 characters and
  `content` as non-empty, default `visibility` to "internal" and `status` to "draft", and answer 409 "KbArticle slug
  '<slug>' already exists" for a slug already used in the tenant.
- **SPEC-15.1121**: An article whose effective visibility is `client_specific` must have at least one company or be
  rejected with 422 on `company_ids` ("client_specific articles require at least one company"), and every supplied
  company id must belong to the tenant or the request must be rejected with 400 "One or more company_ids do not belong
  to this tenant". For any other visibility the stored company list must be empty.
- **SPEC-15.1122**: A parent article link must be rejected with 422 on `parent_article_id` when the article would be its
  own parent ("an article cannot be its own parent"), the parent is not in the tenant ("parent article does not exist in
  this tenant"), the parent has a parent itself ("parent article is itself a variant; one-level hierarchy only"), or the
  article being given a parent already has children ("this article already has children; it cannot itself be given a
  parent").
- **SPEC-15.1123**: Declared template variables must be rejected with 422 when a name is empty
  (`template_variables.name`, "name must not be empty"), a name is duplicated (`template_variables.name`, "duplicate
  variable name '<name>'"), or a default is not one of a non-empty `allowed_values` (`template_variables.default`,
  "default '<default>' for '<name>' is not one of allowed_values").
- **SPEC-15.1124**: Creating an article must seed version 1 with change kind `create` by the author, set `published_at`
  to now only when the status is "published", write an audit entry, commit them together and return the article without
  counting a view.
- **SPEC-15.1125**: `GET /kb/articles/{id}` for staff must answer 404 "KB article" when absent in the tenant and
  increment `view_count` by one after the read commits; a failed increment must be logged as a warning and must not
  change the response. For a contact it must answer 404 "KB article" for an article that is unpublished, internal or
  scoped to another company, must not increment `view_count`, and must return the contact projection.
- **SPEC-15.1126**: An article response must give `author_name` and `updated_by_name` as the user's name or "Unknown"
  with the unresolved user id logged, `current_version` as the highest version number (0 when none), `updated_by` as the
  row's last editor else the latest version's editor, `company_names` sorted alphabetically with unresolvable companies
  omitted, and `status` "draft" and `visibility` "internal" when stored null.
- **SPEC-15.1127**: `PUT /kb/articles/{id}` must require a manager, answer 404 "KB article" when absent, and update only
  the supplied fields. `parent_article_id` absent must keep the parent, null must clear it and a value must set it under
  SPEC-15.1122. `template_variables` supplied must replace the whole set under SPEC-15.1123. When the resulting
  visibility is `client_specific` the company list must be the supplied one (validated) or else the existing one and
  must be non-empty; otherwise it must be cleared.
- **SPEC-15.1128**: Setting an article to "published" must set `published_at` to now only if it is null, and
  `published_at` must never be reset by later edits or status changes.
- **SPEC-15.1129**: An article update must append a version (next number, change kind `edit`, the trimmed `change_note`,
  null when blank) only when the supplied title or content differs from the stored value, record the editor as last
  editor, delete that editor's own draft of the article, and write an audit entry, all in one transaction. A
  `change_note` over 500 characters must be rejected with a validation error.
- **SPEC-15.1130**: `PUT /kb/articles/{id}/draft` must require a manager, validate `title` as 1..=255 characters, answer
  404 "KB article" when the article is absent, upsert one draft per article and user without creating a version and
  return it. `GET` must return the caller's own draft or 404 "Draft", and `DELETE` must answer 204 whether or not a
  draft existed.
- **SPEC-15.1131**: `GET /kb/articles/{id}/versions` must answer 404 "KB article" when absent in the tenant and
  otherwise list versions newest first, paginated, with `edited_by_name` ("Unknown" when unresolved), `change_note`,
  `change_kind` and `restored_from_version`; it must answer 422 on a `sort` parameter.
- **SPEC-15.1132**: `POST /kb/articles/{id}/versions/{version_number}/restore` must require a manager, answer 404 "KB
  article" or 404 "KB article version", copy only that version's title and content onto the article, append a new
  version with change kind `restore`, `restored_from_version` set to the restored number and the trimmed `change_note`
  (at most 500 characters), write an audit entry in the same transaction and return the new version row.
- **SPEC-15.1133**: `POST /kb/articles/{id}/helpful` and `POST /kb/articles/{id}/not_helpful` must keep at most one vote
  per user and article: repeating the same vote must remove it, the opposite vote must replace it. They must recompute
  both tallies from the stored votes, store them on the article, answer 404 "KB article" when absent in the tenant, and
  return `id`, both counts and `my_vote` (null after a removal).
- **SPEC-15.1134**: `GET /kb/articles/{id}/vote` must return the article's stored counts and the caller's current vote
  without changing anything, and answer 404 "KB article" when absent in the tenant.
- **SPEC-15.1135**: `DELETE /kb/articles/{id}` must require a manager, answer 404 "KB article" when absent in the
  tenant, write an audit entry holding the prior row in the same transaction, and after commit delete the stored blobs
  of the article's attachments.
- **SPEC-15.1136**: `GET /kb/articles/{id}/tickets` must answer 404 "KB article" when absent in the tenant and list
  tickets whose source or procedure article is it, with `relation` "procedure" when the procedure link matches and
  "source" otherwise, open tickets first then by `updated_at` descending, paginated, and answer 422 on a `sort`
  parameter.
- **SPEC-15.1137**: `GET /kb/top-ticket-driving-articles` must default `days` to 90 and clamp it to 1..=365, default
  `limit` to 20 and clamp it to 1..=100, count tickets created within the window by their source article, and order by
  count descending then title ascending.
- **SPEC-15.1138**: `GET /kb/articles/{id}/measured-duration` must default `from` to 90 days before today and `to` to
  today, answer 404 "Article" when absent in the tenant, and measure only tickets created from a request-form submission
  whose form points at the article, using time entries dated within `from` and `to`. With no such time it must return
  `ticket_count`, `total_minutes` and `average_minutes` all null, never zero.
- **SPEC-15.1139**: `POST /kb/articles/{id}/render` must treat an absent body as no values, answer 422 on `values`
  ("unknown template variable '<name>'") for an undeclared name and 422 on `values` ("value '<value>' for '<name>' is
  not one of allowed_values") for a value outside a non-empty `allowed_values`, strip invisible characters from the
  output, and return `id` and `content`. A contact must get the same 404 as the article read for an article it may not
  see. A staff render must not count a view.
- **SPEC-15.1140**: `GET /kb/articles/{id}/comments` must require the knowledge base module, answer 404 "KB article"
  when absent in the tenant, and return root comments oldest first, each with its replies oldest first; a deleted
  comment must keep its place with `deleted` true and an empty body.
- **SPEC-15.1141**: `POST /kb/articles/{id}/comments` must validate `body` as 1..=20000 characters, store it trimmed,
  answer 404 "KB article" when absent, and answer 201 with the comment. A reply must answer a live top-level comment of
  the same article or be rejected with 422 on `parent_id` ("a reply answers a top-level comment on this article"), and
  must carry no anchor or be rejected with 422 on `anchor` ("a reply carries no anchor; anchor the root it answers"). A
  root's anchor must pass the anchor rules and record the article's highest version as `anchor_version`.
- **SPEC-15.1142**: `PUT /kb/comments/{id}` must allow only the comment's author or an admin (else 403 "You can only
  edit comments you wrote."), answer 409 "This comment was deleted." for a deleted comment, answer 404 "Comment" when
  absent in the tenant, store the trimmed body and `edited_at`, and write an audit entry.
- **SPEC-15.1143**: `DELETE /kb/comments/{id}` must allow only the author or an admin (else 403 "You can only delete
  comments you wrote."), answer 409 "This comment was deleted." for a deleted comment and 404 "Comment" when absent,
  mark the comment deleted without removing the row, write an audit entry and answer 204.
- **SPEC-15.1144**: `POST /kb/comments/{id}/resolve` and `/unresolve` must be open to any staff role, answer 422 on `id`
  ("resolve the thread, not a reply in it") for a reply, answer 409 "This comment was deleted." for a deleted root, set
  or clear the resolution time and resolver, write an audit entry and return the comment.
- **SPEC-15.1145**: Creating or editing a comment must record one mention row per person named by an `@handle` in the
  body among the tenant's active users, once per comment and person, and must treat as newly mentioned only people whose
  row that write inserted, excluding the author.
- **SPEC-15.1146**: After the comment commits, each newly mentioned person must receive one `kb.comment.mention`
  notification (article title, author name, first 200 characters of the body), and a delivered one must stamp the
  mention's `notified_at`. A dispatch failure, a title lookup failure or a stamp failure must be logged at error level
  and must not fail the request. When no dispatcher is configured a warning must be logged and nobody notified.
- **SPEC-15.1147**: Every KB route other than the four dual-plane reads must require the `knowledge_base` module and a
  staff user, so a contact bearer is refused, and article create, update and delete, category create, update and delete,
  draft routes, version restore and attachment routes must additionally require a manager.
- **SPEC-15.1148**: Every KB query and write must filter by the caller's tenant and run in a tenant-scoped transaction,
  except the public attachment read, which resolves the tenant from the attachment row.

### 15.5 Documentation

- **SPEC-15.1149**: `GET /companies/{company_id}/documentation` must require the assets module and an authenticated
  user, and must return an object with exactly the lists `assets`, `credentials` and `articles`.
- **SPEC-15.1150**: The `assets` list must hold the first page of at most 100 assets of the caller's tenant for the
  company, ordered by name, and the response must carry no total for it.
- **SPEC-15.1151**: The `credentials` list must hold every credential reference of the tenant for the company, both
  asset-linked and company-scoped, ordered by name, with no username, password or notes and no 100-item limit.
- **SPEC-15.1152**: The `articles` list must hold at most 100 articles of the tenant whose company list contains the
  company, newest update first, in every status, and must not depend on the `knowledge_base` module flag.
- **SPEC-15.1153**: A company id that does not exist in the caller's tenant, including one belonging to another tenant,
  must produce a 200 response with three empty lists, because no company existence check is made.
- **SPEC-15.1154**: The three lists must be read concurrently; if any read fails the request must fail with that error
  and return no partial body.

### 15.6 Integrations

- **SPEC-15.1500**: `GET /api/v1/integrations` must require an authenticated caller whose role is `super_admin` or
  `admin`; any other authenticated role must receive 403 "You do not have permission to do that". No module gate
  applies.
- **SPEC-15.1501**: `GET /api/v1/integrations` must be the only route the integrations module mounts; per-provider
  `GET`/`PUT /integrations/{provider}` and `POST /integrations/{provider}/connect` and `/disconnect` must not be routed.
- **SPEC-15.1502**: The list must contain exactly one entry per registry provider, in the order stripe, paypal,
  quickbooks, xero, google, microsoft, icloud, including providers for which the tenant has no row.
- **SPEC-15.1503**: An entry for a provider with no tenant row must report status `not_connected`, an empty
  `enabled_capabilities`, an empty `config` object, and no `connected_at`, `disconnected_at`, `last_error` or
  `poll_interval_minutes`.
- **SPEC-15.1504**: Each entry must carry `display_name`, `description` and `supported_capabilities` (each with `key`,
  `label` and `description`) from the registry. The supported keys must be `payments` for stripe and paypal, `invoicing`
  and `bills_and_expenses` for quickbooks and xero, and `contacts` for google, microsoft and icloud.
- **SPEC-15.1505**: Each entry must report `available` as true for a provider whose registry build state is built, and
  `configurable_here` as true only for a provider whose credential home is the integrations surface itself; both stripe
  and paypal (payment gateway home), the two invoice issuers and the three contact sources must report it false.
- **SPEC-15.1506**: Each entry must carry a `setup` object (`kind`, `label`) naming the settings surface that owns the
  provider: `payment_gateway` / "Settings > Payment Gateways" for stripe and paypal, `invoice_issuer_xero` / "Settings >
  Xero", `invoice_issuer_quickbooks` / "Settings > QuickBooks", `contact_sync_google` / "Settings > Google Contacts",
  `contact_sync_icloud` / "Settings > iCloud Contacts" and `contact_sync_microsoft` / "Settings > Microsoft 365
  Contacts"; the field must be omitted for a provider with no surface.
- **SPEC-15.1507**: An entry must carry `managed_elsewhere` (`table`, `configured_at`) only for a provider whose
  connection lives in another subsystem (google, microsoft, icloud, table `contact_sync_connections`), and must omit it
  otherwise.
- **SPEC-15.1508**: An entry must carry `credential_elsewhere` (`kind`, `entered_at`) whenever the provider's credential
  home is not the integrations surface. `kind` must be the snake_case home (`payment_gateway`, `contact_sync`,
  `invoice_issuer`), and `entered_at` must be the setup surface label, else the home's own label, else the text "its own
  settings page".
- **SPEC-15.1509**: An entry must carry `polling` (`default_minutes`, `min_minutes`) only for a provider that polls, and
  must omit it otherwise. The registry polling defaults must be 15 minutes default and 5 minutes minimum, and no current
  provider polls.
- **SPEC-15.1510**: For a provider with a row in `integrations`, the entry must report the row's status, enabled
  capabilities, config, poll interval, `connected_at`, `disconnected_at` and `last_error`.
- **SPEC-15.1511**: If an `integrations` row holds a status string that is not one of `not_connected`, `connected`,
  `error` or `disconnected`, the entry must report status `error` and the server must log a warning naming the provider
  and the unrecognised value.
- **SPEC-15.1512**: For google, microsoft and icloud the entry must take its status from the tenant's
  `contact_sync_connections` row, not from `integrations`: `disconnected` when `disconnected_at` is set or the
  connection is inactive, `error` when the sync status is `failed` or `reconnect_required`, otherwise `connected`; with
  no connection row the entry must read as a provider with no row.
- **SPEC-15.1513**: For a contact-sync entry, `last_error` must be reported only while the derived status is `error`,
  `connected_at` must be the connection's creation time, and `disconnected_at` must be the connection's
  `disconnected_at`.
- **SPEC-15.1514**: For a contact-sync entry, `enabled_capabilities` must list the provider's full supported set only
  when the tenant-wide contacts switch for that provider is on and the derived status is `connected` or `error`;
  otherwise it must be empty.
- **SPEC-15.1515**: A `contact_sync_connections` row whose provider is not an integrations provider (for example the
  `vcard` upload row) must be ignored by the list.
- **SPEC-15.1516**: Every integrations read and write must run in a tenant-scoped transaction and must also filter on
  the caller's `tenant_id`, so one tenant's list never contains another tenant's rows. A database failure must fail the
  whole request with an error rather than return a partial list.
- **SPEC-15.1517**: When a capability list is validated for a provider, an unknown key must be refused with 400 "`<key>`
  is not a capability. The capabilities are: <all keys>", a key the provider does not support with 400 "<provider name>
  does not provide <key>. It provides: <supported keys>", and a repeated key with 400 "<key> is named more than once".
  An accepted list must be stored in the registry's order of that provider's capabilities.
- **SPEC-15.1518**: A provider `config` supplied on connect or update must be a JSON object; any other JSON type must be
  refused with 400 "integrations.config must be a JSON object of settings".
- **SPEC-15.1519**: A poll interval supplied for a provider that does not poll must be refused with 400 "<provider name>
  is not polled, so it has no poll interval", and one below the provider's minimum must be refused with 400 naming the
  interval, the minimum and the provider.
- **SPEC-15.1520**: Connect and update must refuse a provider whose connection home is another subsystem with 409,
  naming the configured-at page and the owning table, and must write no `integrations` row for it.
- **SPEC-15.1521**: Connect and update must refuse a provider whose registry build state is planned with 409 stating
  that this build has nothing behind it; disconnect must not be refused for that reason.
- **SPEC-15.1522**: Connect for a provider whose credential home is the integrations surface must refuse with 400 when
  no credential is supplied. With one, it must write the credential to the secret provider under the tenant and provider
  before the row, then upsert the `integrations` row as `connected` (resetting `disconnected_at` and `last_error`,
  stamping `connected_at` and the connecting user), and must never store, log or return the credential.
- **SPEC-15.1523**: Connect must treat an omitted capability list as every capability the provider supports, and an
  explicitly empty list as connected with nothing delegated.
- **SPEC-15.1524**: Connect for a payment-gateway provider must refuse with 400 when a credential is supplied (stating
  credentials are entered under Settings > Payment gateways), when the tenant has no `payment_gateway_configs` row, and
  when that row holds no ciphertext and the secret provider holds no gateway credential.
- **SPEC-15.1525**: A successful payment-gateway connect must record the provider as connected through the shared
  payment-connection writer, and must change `enabled_capabilities`, `config` or the poll interval only for the fields
  the request supplied, so connecting never widens an existing delegation.
- **SPEC-15.1526**: Connect for a provider whose credential home is neither the integrations surface nor the payment
  gateway must refuse with 400 stating it cannot be connected here yet.
- **SPEC-15.1527**: Update must refuse with 404 "<provider name> is not connected, so there is nothing to configure"
  when the tenant has no row. Fields the request omits must keep their stored values, and a poll interval sent as null
  must clear the override.
- **SPEC-15.1528**: Disconnect must refuse with 404 "<provider name> is not connected" when the tenant has no row;
  otherwise it must keep the row, set status `disconnected`, stamp `disconnected_at` and clear `last_error`.
- **SPEC-15.1529**: Disconnect must commit the row change before deleting the credential, and must delete the stored
  credential only for a provider whose credential home is the integrations surface; a payment-gateway credential must be
  left in place.
- **SPEC-15.1530**: Connect, update and disconnect must each write an audit record in the same transaction (create or
  update for connect depending on whether a row existed, update, and delete respectively) whose before and after
  snapshots hold only provider, status, enabled capabilities, config and poll interval.
- **SPEC-15.1531**: The payment-connection writer must upsert the tenant's `integrations` row for the provider: on
  connect it must set `connected` and stamp `connected_at`; on disconnect of an existing row it must set `disconnected`
  and stamp `disconnected_at`; a row created while disconnecting must be `not_connected`. It must clear `last_error`,
  keep the earlier connecting user when none is given, and keep both timestamps once set.
- **SPEC-15.1532**: A row created by the payment-connection writer must start with enabled capabilities `{payments}`,
  and an existing row's enabled capabilities must not be changed by it.
- **SPEC-15.1533**: The payment-connection writer must set `payment_gateway_configs.is_active` to the same connected
  value in the same transaction; no serving read may use that column.
- **SPEC-15.1534**: The payment-connection writer must write nothing and return success, after a debug log naming the
  provider, for a provider that has no integrations entry (such as `authorize_net`); a database failure must be returned
  as a database error.
- **SPEC-15.1535**: A payment gateway must count as connected for serving reads only through a join to an `integrations`
  row of the same tenant and provider with status `connected`; a gateway with no such row must be reported as not
  connected by the list read.

### 15.7 RMM

- **SPEC-15.1536**: Every `/api/v1/rmm/*` route except `POST /api/v1/rmm/alerts` must require an authenticated caller
  and the `rmm_integration` module to be enabled for the caller's tenant; with the module disabled the route must answer
  404 as if it were not mounted.
- **SPEC-15.1537**: All connection routes (list, create, get, update, delete, test) and the create, update and delete
  routes for device mappings and alert rules must additionally require the `super_admin` or `admin` role and otherwise
  answer 403; `GET /rmm/device-mappings` and `GET /rmm/alert-rules` must be open to any authenticated user of a tenant
  with the module enabled.
- **SPEC-15.1538**: The list routes (connections, device mappings, alert rules) must return a paginated envelope with
  the total row count of the same filter, must answer 422 for a `sort` parameter or a `per_page` above 100, and must
  order by name (device mappings by device name) ascending.
- **SPEC-15.1539**: `GET /rmm/device-mappings` and `GET /rmm/alert-rules` must accept an optional `rmm_connection_id`
  query filter that restricts both the page and the total to that connection; without it they must list the whole
  tenant.
- **SPEC-15.1540**: `POST /rmm/connections` must reject a `provider` other than `tactical_rmm`, `mesh_central`, `datto`,
  `connectwise` or `ninja_rmm` with 400 "Provider <value> not supported; pick tactical_rmm | mesh_central | datto |
  connectwise | ninja_rmm", and must reject a `name` outside 1-100 characters or an `api_url` that is not a URL with a
  validation error.
- **SPEC-15.1541**: `POST /rmm/connections` must store `api_key` and any `api_secret` as AES-256-GCM ciphertext under
  the deployment key, must default `is_active` to false and `sync_interval_minutes` to 60, must answer with sync status
  `never` and no last sync time, and must write a `create` audit record in the same transaction.
- **SPEC-15.1542**: No RMM response may contain `api_key` or `api_secret`; a connection response must carry only id,
  name, provider, api_url, is_active, sync_interval_minutes, last_sync_at, sync_status, last_error and created_at.
- **SPEC-15.1543**: `GET`, `PUT` and `DELETE /rmm/connections/{id}` must be scoped to the caller's tenant and must
  answer 404 naming "RMM connection" when no such connection exists in that tenant.
- **SPEC-15.1544**: `PUT /rmm/connections/{id}` must update only the supplied fields among name, api_url, api_key,
  api_secret, is_active and sync_interval_minutes, must re-encrypt a credential only when it is supplied, must not allow
  the provider to change, and must answer with the post-update row.
- **SPEC-15.1545**: `POST /rmm/connections/{id}/test` must answer 404 when the connection is missing, must fail with an
  error when the stored api key cannot be decrypted, and otherwise must send one HEAD request to the stored `api_url`
  with a 10 second timeout and without following redirects.
- **SPEC-15.1546**: The connection test must screen `api_url` with the outbound URL guard before connecting. An
  unparsable URL must yield `{"reachable": false, "error": "api_url is not a valid URL: ..."}` and a refused target must
  yield `{"reachable": false, "error": "api_url refused: ..."}` with a hint naming `OUTBOUND_PRIVATE_ALLOWLIST` when the
  target is blocked as private; each case must log a warning naming the connection id.
- **SPEC-15.1547**: The connection test must answer 200 with `{"reachable": true, "status": <http status>}` for any HTTP
  response received, and `{"reachable": false, "error": <text>}` when no response was received, and must record
  `sync_status` `success` or `failed` and `last_sync_at` now on the connection.
- **SPEC-15.1548**: `POST /rmm/device-mappings` must require `rmm_device_id` of 1-255 characters, must write a `create`
  audit record in the same transaction, and must answer with the mapping including the owning connection's name and a
  sync status of `pending` unless one is stored.
- **SPEC-15.1549**: `PUT /rmm/device-mappings/{id}` must update only the supplied fields among `rmm_device_id`,
  `asset_id`, `company_id` and `device_name`, must not allow the connection to change, and must answer 404 naming "RMM
  device mapping" when the mapping does not exist in the tenant; `DELETE` must answer 404 likewise.
- **SPEC-15.1550**: `POST /rmm/alert-rules` must require `name` of 1-100 characters, must default `auto_create_ticket`
  and `is_active` to true and `ticket_template` to an empty object, must write a `create` audit record in the same
  transaction, and must answer with the rule including the owning connection's name.
- **SPEC-15.1551**: `PUT /rmm/alert-rules/{id}` must update only the supplied fields among name, alert_type,
  auto_create_ticket, assign_to_id, queue_id, ticket_template and is_active, must not allow the connection to change,
  and must answer 404 naming "RMM alert rule" when the rule does not exist in the tenant; `DELETE` must answer 404
  likewise.
- **SPEC-15.1552**: `POST /rmm/alerts` must not require a session; it must take the tenant from the `X-Tenant-Id` header
  and authenticate the body with an `X-Signature` header holding the standard-alphabet base64 of the HMAC-SHA256 of the
  exact received body bytes keyed by the connection's decrypted `api_secret`, compared in constant time.
- **SPEC-15.1553**: `POST /rmm/alerts` must answer 401 without detail when the body is not a valid alert JSON document,
  the `X-Signature` header is missing, the `X-Tenant-Id` header is missing or not a UUID, the connection does not exist
  in that tenant, the connection has no `api_secret`, or the signature does not match.
- **SPEC-15.1554**: `POST /rmm/alerts` must require `title` of 1-255 characters and answer a validation error otherwise;
  on success it must answer 200 with `{"tickets_created": <count>}`, where the count is 0 when no rule produced a
  ticket.
- **SPEC-15.1555**: Alert ingest must consider only active rules of the signed connection whose `alert_type` equals the
  alert's `alert_type` or is null, and must skip a rule whose `auto_create_ticket` is not true.
- **SPEC-15.1556**: For each considered rule, alert ingest must skip the rule and log a warning naming the rule and
  connection when no device mapping with a company exists for the alert's `rmm_device_id` on that connection; the
  ticket's company must be that mapping's company.
- **SPEC-15.1557**: A rule whose `suppression_rules.min_severity` is set must suppress an alert whose severity ranks
  below it (ranks: `low`/`info` 1, `medium`/`warning` 2, `high` 3, `critical` 4, absent or any other value highest),
  logging at debug level; a rule with no `min_severity` must never suppress by severity.
- **SPEC-15.1558**: A rule whose `suppression_rules.dedupe_window_minutes` is a positive integer must skip an alert when
  an open (status not closed) ticket of source `rmm` for the same company and the same rendered title was created within
  that many minutes, logging at debug level; a closed ticket must not block a new one.
- **SPEC-15.1559**: Alert ingest must render the ticket title and description from the rule's `ticket_template` `title`
  and `description` using `{{key}}` substitution over the alert's title, message, alert_type, severity, rmm_device_id
  and rmm_connection_id, falling back to the alert's own title and message (empty when absent) for any template key not
  present.
- **SPEC-15.1560**: Alert ingest must create each ticket through the ticket service with source `rmm`, the rule's
  `queue_id` and `assign_to_id`, `is_billable` false, an audit actor of the tenant's system, and the oldest active user
  of role `super_admin`, `admin` or `manager` as creator; with no such user the rule must be skipped with a warning
  naming the rule and connection.
- **SPEC-15.1561**: If a ticket creation fails during alert ingest, the request must fail with that error and the
  remaining rules must not be processed; tickets already created for earlier rules in the same request must remain.
- **SPEC-15.1562**: The provider factory must return the Tactical RMM provider for `tactical_rmm` and, for every other
  provider value, a provider whose every operation fails with an internal error "RMM provider '<name>' is not
  implemented yet".
- **SPEC-15.1563**: The Tactical RMM provider must call `GET agents/`, `GET alerts/` and `HEAD core/version/` under the
  connection's `api_url` (trailing slash trimmed), sending `Authorization: Token <api_key>` and user agent
  `mokosh-server/rmm`, with a 30 second timeout and without following redirects.
- **SPEC-15.1564**: The Tactical RMM provider must screen every request URL with the outbound URL guard (honouring
  `OUTBOUND_PRIVATE_ALLOWLIST`), failing with a configuration error "RMM api_url is not a valid URL: ..." for an
  unparsable URL and "RMM api_url refused: ..." for a refused target (with the allow-list hint when blocked), and must
  log a warning with the connection id and host but never the credential.
- **SPEC-15.1565**: The Tactical RMM provider must fail with a configuration error "tactical_rmm <operation> redirected
  (<status>); point api_url at the final URL, redirects are not followed" on a 3xx response, and with an internal error
  naming the operation for any other non-2xx status, a transport failure or a body that is not the expected JSON array.
- **SPEC-15.1566**: The Tactical RMM provider must map each agent to a device with id from `agent_id`, hostname from
  `hostname`, serial number from `serial_number` else `wmi_detail.bios.SerialNumber`, last-seen from `last_seen` parsed
  as RFC 3339 (absent when unparsable), and the full agent JSON as the raw payload.
- **SPEC-15.1567**: The sync worker must run as the job `rmm_sync` and on each tick must select, across all tenants, the
  connections that are active, not `in_progress`, and either never synced or last synced at least
  `sync_interval_minutes` ago.
- **SPEC-15.1568**: The sync worker must isolate failures per connection: a credential decryption failure must log an
  error and mark the connection `failed` with last_error "decrypt: <cause>", a sync failure must log a warning and mark
  it `failed` with the error text and `last_sync_at` now, a failure to record the failure must be logged at error level,
  and the tick must continue with the next connection.
- **SPEC-15.1569**: A sync must first claim the connection with an atomic update that succeeds only when its status is
  not `in_progress`; a sync that loses the claim must return empty statistics and must not call the provider.
- **SPEC-15.1570**: A sync must fetch the provider's device list and upsert one `rmm_device_mappings` row per device,
  keyed by connection and device id, setting device name to the hostname, device info to the raw payload, last seen, and
  sync status `synced`; an error at any step must abort the sync, keeping mappings already written.
- **SPEC-15.1571**: A successful sync must set the connection's `sync_status` to `success`, stamp `last_sync_at` now and
  clear `last_error`, and must report devices seen, mappings upserted, assets created and assets updated.
- **SPEC-15.1572**: During a sync, a mapping with no `company_id` must not create or link any asset. A mapping with an
  `asset_id` must update that asset's `last_sync_at` and `rmm_device_id` and write an `asset_audit_log` entry `synced`.
- **SPEC-15.1573**: During a sync, a mapping with a company and no asset must be matched first to a tenant asset with
  the same non-empty serial number, then to one whose name equals the non-empty hostname; a match must be linked to the
  mapping, updated as above and audited `synced`.
- **SPEC-15.1574**: During a sync, a company mapping with no matching asset must create an active asset in that company
  named after the hostname (else `rmm:<device id>`), with the device's serial number and device id, using the tenant's
  oldest asset type, link it to the mapping and audit it `created`; when the tenant has no asset type, the mapping must
  stay unlinked and a warning naming the tenant and device must be logged.
- **SPEC-15.1575**: Every sync read and write of tenant data must run under the connection's tenant scope, and only the
  cross-tenant connection pick and the connection status updates may use the unscoped pool.

### 15.8 Reports, saved reports and dashboards

- **SPEC-15.1576**: Every `/api/v1/reports/*` route must require an authenticated caller and the `reports` module to be
  enabled for the caller's tenant; with the module disabled the route must answer 404 as if it were not mounted.
- **SPEC-15.1577**: `GET /reports` must return the report registry as a JSON array, in the order `dashboard`, `tickets`,
  `time`, `billing`, `request-types`, `custom`, `projects`, `clients`, each with exactly `key`, `name`, `description`
  and `parameters` (`name`, `kind` of `date` or `uuid`, `required`); `tickets`, `time` and `request-types` must declare
  the optional date parameters `from` and `to`, `billing` the optional uuid `company_id`, and the others none.
- **SPEC-15.1578**: `GET /reports/billing`, `GET /reports/clients` and the exports of the `billing` and `clients` keys
  must require a role that may manage billing (`super_admin`, `admin` or `finance`) and otherwise answer 403 "You do not
  have permission to do that"; the export gate must apply before the format is used, so the PDF format cannot bypass it.
- **SPEC-15.1579**: `GET /reports/dashboard` must return the open tickets (status not closed) grouped by priority name
  in name order, the SLA warning and breach counts, and the 30-day ticket trend, all restricted to the caller's tenant.
  With a `team_id` query parameter every aggregate must additionally be restricted to that team, and a team id that
  matches no ticket of the tenant must produce zero counts and empty lists rather than an error.
- **SPEC-15.1580**: Dashboard `sla_warnings` must count tickets whose SLA clock is running and whose `sla_due_date` lies
  within the next 2 hours, and `sla_breached` must count tickets whose SLA clock is running and whose `sla_due_date` is
  in the past. The SLA clock must count as running only while the ticket has no `resolved_at`, no `closed_at` and a
  status that is not closed.
- **SPEC-15.1581**: Dashboard `ticket_trend_30d` must count tickets by creation date in the caller's time zone, for each
  date from 30 days before the caller's today onward, in ascending date order, omitting dates with no tickets.
- **SPEC-15.1582**: `GET /reports/tickets` must default `from` to 30 days before the caller's today and `to` to the
  caller's today, include both bounds, and return `opened_by_status` (tickets created in range, by status name in name
  order), `closed_total` (tickets whose `closed_at` falls in range) and `opened_by_assignee` (id, name and count).
- **SPEC-15.1583**: In `opened_by_assignee` the name must be the assignee's full name, else the email, and must be
  absent for an unassigned ticket; an assignee id whose name did not resolve must be logged by id and must not be logged
  for an unassigned ticket.
- **SPEC-15.1584**: `GET /reports/time` must use the same default date range as the tickets report and return the sum of
  `duration_minutes` of the tenant's time entries dated within the range, grouped by user (id, name, minutes) and by
  work type (id, name, minutes). A user name must be the full name, else the email; an unresolved user must be named
  "Unknown user" and logged by id, and an unresolved work type must be named "Unknown work type" and logged by id.
- **SPEC-15.1585**: `GET /reports/billing` must return `invoiced`, `paid` and `outstanding` as the sums of the tenant's
  invoice `total`, `amount_paid` and `balance_due` (zero when there are no invoices), restricted to `company_id` when
  given, and `aging` as the sum of `balance_due` of invoices with a positive balance in the buckets `current` (due today
  or later), `1-30`, `31-60`, `61-90` and `90+` days overdue, listing only non-empty buckets.
- **SPEC-15.1586**: The billing report must include `company_name` when `company_id` names a company of the caller's
  tenant and `null` otherwise.
- **SPEC-15.1587**: `GET /reports/projects` must return `by_status` with the buckets `planning`, `active`, `on_hold`,
  `completed` and `cancelled` always present in that order (zero when empty) followed by any other status sorted by
  name, the summed `budget_hours` and `budget_amount` of all the tenant's projects, `actual_amount` and `actual_hours`
  (minutes divided by 60) from the tenant's time entries that have a project, `tasks_total`, `tasks_completed` (tasks
  whose status is completed), and `overdue` (projects whose `target_end_date` is before today and whose status is not
  `completed` or `cancelled`).
- **SPEC-15.1588**: `GET /reports/clients` must return `companies_total` and `companies_active` (status `active`)
  excluding companies of type `internal`; `assets_total`; `assets_by_type` by type name in name order;
  `assets_by_status` with `active`, `inactive`, `retired`, `in_repair` and `in_stock` always present in that order
  followed by any other status sorted by name; `warranty_expiring_90d` (warranty expiry from today through 90 days
  ahead); `contracts_active`; and `contracts_renewing_90d` (active contracts with an end date from today through 90 days
  ahead).
- **SPEC-15.1589**: `GET /reports/request-types` must default `from` to the first day of the caller's current month and
  `to` to the caller's today, and return every request type (form definition) of the tenant in name order with its slug
  and linked knowledge-base article title, counting only time entries dated in range on tickets created from a
  submission of that request type.
- **SPEC-15.1590**: A request type with no time entry in range must report `ticket_count`, `total_minutes` and
  `average_minutes` as null, not zero; otherwise `ticket_count` must be the number of distinct tickets with time and
  `average_minutes` must be the total minutes divided by that count.
- **SPEC-15.1591**: `GET /reports/{report}/export` must read `format` (default `csv`, case-insensitive `csv` or `pdf`)
  before resolving the report key, answering 400 with the parameter name `format` and the message "must be 'csv' or
  'pdf', not <value>" for any other value, and 404 "Report <key>" when the key is not in the registry.
- **SPEC-15.1592**: `GET /reports/custom/export` must answer 400 stating that the custom report cannot be exported
  through GET because its spec travels in a request body, and that `POST /reports/custom` with `"format": "csv"` must be
  used instead.
- **SPEC-15.1593**: An export must serve the report with the same data and query parameters as its JSON route (`from`
  and `to` for tickets, time and request-types, `company_id` for billing, `team_id` for dashboard) with Content-Type
  `text/csv; charset=utf-8` and a Content-Disposition filename `<key>.csv` for CSV, or Content-Type `application/pdf`
  and filename `<key>.pdf` for PDF.
- **SPEC-15.1594**: A PDF export must be titled with the report's registry name, dated with the date of the request in
  UTC, and must fail the request with the rendering error if the PDF cannot be produced.
- **SPEC-15.1595**: Every CSV writer must quote a free-text cell that contains a comma, a double quote or a newline,
  doubling embedded quotes; an assignee in the tickets CSV must be written as its id, or `unassigned`.
- **SPEC-15.1596**: The request-types CSV and PDF must leave the count, total and average cells empty when the values
  are null, and must write the average with one decimal place.
- **SPEC-15.1597**: The tickets PDF must name an assignee with no resolved name "Unassigned", must log an assignee id
  whose name did not resolve, and the billing PDF must be subtitled with the company name or "All clients".
- **SPEC-15.1598**: `GET /reports/custom/schema` must return exactly three sources: `tickets` (dimensions status,
  priority, assignee, created_date, created_month; measure count; filters status, priority; date range), `time_entries`
  (dimensions user, work_type, date, month, billable, project, contract; measures count, minutes, hours, worked_minutes,
  billable_minutes, realization, amount; filter work_type; date range) and `assets` (dimensions type, status, company,
  manufacturer; measure count; filters status, type; no date range), each key with its label.
- **SPEC-15.1599**: `POST /reports/custom` must answer 400 "Unknown report source <key>" for an unknown source, 400 "At
  least one measure is required" when no measure is given, 400 "Unknown dimension <key> for source <source>" or "Unknown
  measure <key> for source <source>" for a key outside the catalog, 400 "Unsupported filter op <op>; only 'eq' is
  supported" for an operator other than empty or `eq`, and 400 "Unknown filter field <field> for source <source>"; all
  checks must run before any SQL is built.
- **SPEC-15.1600**: A custom report must be generated only from catalog expressions with every filter value and date
  bound as a parameter, must always filter on the caller's tenant, must apply `eq` filters as equality on the filter's
  column, and for a source with a date column must apply `from` and `to` as inclusive date bounds (a source without one
  must ignore them).
- **SPEC-15.1601**: A custom report with dimensions must group and order by all of them in the given order, and its row
  limit must default to 100 and be clamped into 1 to 1000.
- **SPEC-15.1602**: A custom report response must carry `columns` (dimension labels then measure labels), `rows` of
  nullable strings, and `totals` mapping each measure label to the sum of that column over the returned rows
  (non-numeric cells ignored), written without a fractional part when whole and with two decimals otherwise.
- **SPEC-15.1603**: `POST /reports/custom` with `"format": "csv"` must answer `text/csv; charset=utf-8` containing the
  column labels as a header line then one line per row with null cells empty and cells quoted per the CSV rule; any
  other `format` value must answer the JSON envelope.
- **SPEC-15.1604**: In a custom tickets report, a ticket with no assignee or an unnamed assignee must show the
  `assignee` dimension as "Unassigned", and an assignee id that is set but whose name did not resolve must be logged by
  id.
- **SPEC-15.1605**: A custom report must run read-only in a tenant-scoped transaction that is never committed.
- **SPEC-15.1606**: The saved-report routes (`/reports/saved`, `/reports/saved/{id}`, `/reports/saved/{id}/execute`,
  `/reports/saved/{id}/schedules`, `/reports/schedules/{schedule_id}`) must require an authenticated caller only; they
  must not require the `reports` module or any role.
- **SPEC-15.1607**: `GET /reports/saved` must list the saved reports of the caller's tenant newest-updated first,
  restricted by `scope`: `mine` (created by the caller), `shared` (`is_shared`, any author) or `any` (the default; the
  union of both); any other `scope` value must be refused with 400 "Unknown scope='<value>'; expected mine | shared |
  any". An `entity_type` parameter must additionally restrict the list to reports of exactly that entity type.
- **SPEC-15.1608**: A saved-report response must carry `created_by_name` as the author's trimmed first and last name,
  and `null` when it is empty or the author no longer exists; a list or get that returns reports whose author name is
  `null` must log the unresolved author ids.
- **SPEC-15.1609**: `GET /reports/saved/{id}`, execute and schedule creation must treat a saved report as visible only
  to its author or, when `is_shared` is true, to any user of the tenant; for anyone else, and for an unknown id, they
  must answer 404 "Saved report".
- **SPEC-15.1610**: `POST /reports/saved` must require `name` of 1-200 characters and `entity_type` of 1-50 characters,
  must default `filters` to `{}`, `columns`, `group_by` and `sort` to `[]` and `is_shared` to false, must record the
  caller as author, and must not check `entity_type` against the supported entities until the report is executed.
- **SPEC-15.1611**: `PATCH /reports/saved/{id}` must be allowed only for the author; any other user, including one who
  can see the report because it is shared, must receive 404 "Saved report". It must change only the supplied fields
  among name (1-200 characters), description, filters, columns, group_by, sort and is_shared, must not change
  `entity_type`, and must answer with the updated report.
- **SPEC-15.1612**: `DELETE /reports/saved/{id}` must be allowed only for the author, answering `{"deleted": true}`, and
  must answer 404 "Saved report" for anyone else or an unknown id.
- **SPEC-15.1613**: `POST /reports/saved/{id}/execute` must read `page` (default 1) and `per_page` (default 100) from
  the query string, clamp the effective page size into 1 to 10000, skip `(page - 1) * page size` rows (page 0 behaves as
  page 1), and answer `rows`, `total` (all matching rows ignoring paging), `page` (as requested), `per_page` (effective)
  and `aliases` (the ordered display headers).
- **SPEC-15.1614**: Execution must run the count and row queries inside the caller's tenant-scoped transaction, with the
  tenant condition always the first condition of the generated query and every other value bound as a parameter.
- **SPEC-15.1615**: Execution must refuse a report whose `entity_type` is not `tickets` with 400 "Unsupported
  entity_type='<value>'. Phase 2 only supports 'tickets'."
- **SPEC-15.1616**: The report `columns` must be a JSON array of strings or of objects with a `field` and an optional
  `header`, with the header defaulting to the field. Execution must answer 400 for a non-array ("saved_reports.columns
  must be a JSON array"), for an entry that is neither string nor object, for an object without a string `field`, for a
  field outside the ticket whitelist ("Unsupported column '<field>' for entity 'tickets'..."), for a header containing a
  double quote, and for a header longer than 100 characters.
- **SPEC-15.1617**: An empty `columns` array must execute with the default columns `ticket_number`, `title`,
  `status_name`, `priority_name`, `company_name`, `assigned_to_name`, `created_at` and `updated_at`.
- **SPEC-15.1618**: The ticket column whitelist must be exactly `ticket_number`, `title`, `description`, `source`,
  `is_billable`, `billing_status`, `created_at`, `updated_at`, `closed_at`, `status_id`, `priority_id`, `queue_id`,
  `type_id`, `company_id`, `contact_id`, `assigned_to_id`, `status_name`, `priority_name`, `queue_name`, `type_name`,
  `category_name`, `company_name`, `contact_name`, `assigned_to_name`, `asset_name` and `created_by_name`, used alike
  for columns, filters and sort.
- **SPEC-15.1619**: No caller-supplied text may reach the generated SQL: output names must derive from whitelist keys,
  with a repeated field given a `_2`, `_3`, ... suffix, and the caller's headers must be applied only to the response,
  where a repeated header becomes `<header> (2)`, `<header> (3)`, ... and each row must be keyed by its header in the
  declared column order with a missing value as `null`.
- **SPEC-15.1620**: Report `filters` must be a JSON object of whitelisted field to value, applied together with AND,
  where a scalar means equality and an array means membership. Execution must answer 400 for an unsupported field
  ("Unsupported filter field '<field>' for entity 'tickets'."), an empty array, a uuid column whose value is not a valid
  UUID string, a value of a type the column does not accept ("Filter '<field>' has an unexpected value type for its
  column"), and an array filter on a boolean column.
- **SPEC-15.1621**: Report `sort` must be an array of `{field, dir}` with a whitelisted field and `dir` of `asc` (the
  default) or `desc` in any letter case; execution must answer 400 for an entry that is not an object, lacks `field`,
  names an unsupported field ("sort[<i>] unsupported field '<field>'") or has another `dir`. An absent, empty or
  non-array `sort` must order by ticket `updated_at` descending.
- **SPEC-15.1622**: Execution must include only tickets that have a status, priority, queue and company, and must use
  the same joins for the total as for the rows.
- **SPEC-15.1623**: When a report selects both a person id column and its name column (`contact_id` and `contact_name`,
  `assigned_to_id` and `assigned_to_name`, `created_by_id` and `created_by_name`), execution must log once per
  execution, at info level, the ids of rows whose name came back not a string; it must log ids only.
- **SPEC-15.1624**: `POST /reports/saved/{id}/schedules` must require the parent report to be visible to the caller (404
  "Saved report" otherwise), a `cron_expr` of 1-100 characters accepted by the cron parser (second-resolution form), an
  optional `recipient_email` that is a valid address of at most 255 characters, and default `is_active` to true; it must
  record the caller as the schedule owner and set `next_run_at` to the first firing strictly after the current time.
- **SPEC-15.1625**: When a cron expression cannot be parsed while computing a firing, the request must answer 400
  "Invalid cron expression: <cause>", and an expression with no future firing must fail with an internal error "Cron
  '<expr>' has no future firings".
- **SPEC-15.1626**: `GET /reports/saved/{id}/schedules` must require the parent report to be visible to the caller and
  then list all schedules of that report, newest first, whoever owns them.
- **SPEC-15.1627**: `GET /reports/schedules/{schedule_id}` must return the schedule of the caller's tenant with that id
  (cron_expr, channel, format, recipient_email, is_active, last_run_at, next_run_at, last_error, timestamps), and 404
  "Scheduled report" when there is none.
- **SPEC-15.1628**: `PATCH /reports/schedules/{schedule_id}` and `DELETE` must be allowed only for the schedule owner,
  and otherwise answer 404 "Scheduled report"; a patch must change only the supplied fields among `cron_expr`,
  `recipient_email` and `is_active`, must recompute `next_run_at` from the current time only when `cron_expr` is
  supplied, and a delete must answer `{"deleted": true}`.
- **SPEC-15.1629**: The scheduled-report worker must run as the job `scheduled_reports` and on each tick must select,
  across all tenants, up to 10 active schedules whose `next_run_at` is not in the future, oldest first, locking them so
  that concurrent workers skip rows already locked.
- **SPEC-15.1630**: For each due schedule the worker must execute the saved report as the schedule owner (first page, up
  to 10000 rows), so a report the owner can no longer see or that fails to compile counts as a failed delivery, and must
  render the rows as CSV with the display headers as the first line, empty cells for null or missing values, and a cell
  quoted when it contains a comma, double quote, CR or LF.
- **SPEC-15.1631**: The worker must address the delivery to the schedule's non-blank `recipient_email`, else to the
  owner's email, failing the delivery with "schedule owner <id> has no email and no recipient override" when neither
  exists, and must insert a `notifications` row of channel `email`, status `pending`, subject "<report name> - <UTC date
  as YYYY-MM-DD>" and a body that starts with "Your scheduled report is attached inline below (<n> rows, <total>
  matched)." followed by a blank line and the CSV.
- **SPEC-15.1632**: After each due schedule the worker must set `last_run_at` to now, `next_run_at` to the first firing
  after now, and `last_error` to the failure text or null, whether or not delivery succeeded; a failed delivery must be
  logged as a warning naming the schedule and tenant, and must not stop the next schedule.
- **SPEC-15.1633**: If the next firing of a due schedule cannot be computed, the worker must log an error naming the
  schedule, set `is_active` to false with `last_error` "Disabled: <cause>", count it as skipped and not record a
  delivery.
- **SPEC-15.1634**: The dashboard routes (`/dashboards`, `/dashboards/default`, `/dashboards/{id}`,
  `/dashboards/{id}/schedules`, `/dashboards/schedules/{schedule_id}`) must require an authenticated caller only; they
  must not require a module or role, and `/dashboards/default` must be matched before `/dashboards/{id}`.
- **SPEC-15.1635**: Saved dashboards must be private to the user who created them within their tenant: `GET /dashboards`
  must list only the caller's own dashboards, default first and then by name ascending.
- **SPEC-15.1636**: `GET /dashboards/default` must answer 200 with the caller's default dashboard, or 200 with `null`
  when the caller has none, never 404.
- **SPEC-15.1637**: `GET /dashboards/{id}` must answer the caller's own dashboard, and 404 "Dashboard" for an unknown id
  or a dashboard owned by another user, including one in the same tenant.
- **SPEC-15.1638**: `POST /dashboards` must require `name` of 1-200 characters, must store an omitted `layout` as an
  empty JSON object and an omitted `is_default` as false, and must store and return `layout` verbatim without validating
  its shape.
- **SPEC-15.1639**: Creating a dashboard with `is_default` true, or updating one to `is_default` true, must clear the
  caller's previous default in the same transaction so at most one default exists per user; updating to false must only
  clear the flag.
- **SPEC-15.1640**: `PATCH /dashboards/{id}` must change only the supplied fields among name (1-200 characters), layout
  and is_default, and must answer 404 "Dashboard" for a dashboard the caller does not own before changing anything.
- **SPEC-15.1641**: `DELETE /dashboards/{id}` must answer `{"deleted": true}` for the caller's own dashboard and 404
  "Dashboard" otherwise.
- **SPEC-15.1642**: `POST /dashboards/{id}/schedules` must require the parent dashboard to belong to the caller (404
  "Dashboard" otherwise), a `cron_expr` of 1-100 characters accepted by the cron parser (second-resolution form), an
  optional valid `recipient_email` of at most 255 characters, and default `is_active` to true; it must record the caller
  as the schedule owner and set `next_run_at` to the first firing strictly after the current time.
- **SPEC-15.1643**: When a cron expression cannot be parsed while computing a firing, the request must answer 400
  "Invalid cron expression: <cause>", and an expression with no future firing must fail with an internal error "Cron
  '<expr>' has no future firings".
- **SPEC-15.1644**: `GET /dashboards/{id}/schedules` must require the parent dashboard to belong to the caller (404
  "Dashboard" otherwise) and list its schedules newest first.
- **SPEC-15.1645**: `GET /dashboards/schedules/{schedule_id}` must return the tenant's schedule with that id (including
  channel, recipient_email, is_active, last_run_at, next_run_at, last_error) and 404 "Scheduled dashboard" when there is
  none.
