- **SPEC-15.1646**: `PATCH /dashboards/schedules/{schedule_id}` and `DELETE` must be allowed only for the schedule owner
  and otherwise answer 404 "Scheduled dashboard"; a patch must change only the supplied fields among `cron_expr`,
  `recipient_email` and `is_active`, must recompute `next_run_at` from the current time only when `cron_expr` is
  supplied, and a delete must answer `{"deleted": true}`.
- **SPEC-15.1647**: The scheduled-dashboard worker must run as the job `scheduled_dashboards` and on each tick must
  select, across all tenants, up to 10 active schedules whose `next_run_at` is not in the future, oldest first, locking
  them so that concurrent workers skip rows already locked.
- **SPEC-15.1648**: For each due schedule the worker must load the dashboard as the schedule owner, so a dashboard that
  was deleted or is not the owner's fails the delivery, and must build a text snapshot "Snapshot of dashboard: <name>"
  followed by a blank line, then either "(no widgets configured)" or "Widgets:" with one line "  - <key>" per widget
  key, then a blank line and "This is an automated scheduled delivery."
- **SPEC-15.1649**: Widget keys must be collected by walking the whole layout document in order: for every JSON object,
  its string `widget_key`, else `key`, else `label`; and every string element of every array; a layout of any other
  shape must yield no keys.
- **SPEC-15.1650**: The worker must address the delivery to the schedule's non-blank `recipient_email`, else to the
  owner's email, failing the delivery with "schedule owner <id> has no email and no recipient override" when neither
  exists, and must insert a `notifications` row of channel `email`, status `pending`, subject "Dashboard: <name> - <UTC
  date as YYYY-MM-DD>" and the snapshot as body.
- **SPEC-15.1651**: After each due schedule the worker must set `last_run_at` to now, `next_run_at` to the first firing
  after now, and `last_error` to the failure text or null, whether or not delivery succeeded; a failed delivery must be
  logged as a warning naming the schedule and tenant, and must not stop the next schedule.
- **SPEC-15.1652**: If the next firing of a due schedule cannot be computed, the worker must log an error naming the
  schedule, set `is_active` to false with `last_error` "Disabled: <cause>", count it as skipped and not record a
  delivery.

### 15.9 Settings

- **SPEC-15.2000**: GET /settings/app-name must be callable only by the deployment operator and must return JSON
  {app_name, effective, default}, where app_name is null when no override is stored, effective is the stored name or the
  default product name, and default is the built-in default product name.
- **SPEC-15.2001**: PUT /settings/app-name must treat an empty or whitespace-only app_name as "clear the override": it
  must delete the stored row and return app_name null with effective equal to the default name.
- **SPEC-15.2002**: PUT /settings/app-name must run a non-empty app_name through the shared name sanitizer and must
  answer 422 with a field error on app_name, naming the reason, when the sanitizer refuses it; nothing is stored in that
  case.
- **SPEC-15.2003**: PUT /settings/app-name must store the sanitized name as one system value on the default tenant (id
  1, category "system", key "app_name") with upsert semantics, and must refresh the in-process name cache in the same
  request so the next email and the next 404 page carry the new name without a restart.
- **SPEC-15.2004**: At boot, resolving the stored app name must drop a stored value that fails the sanitizer, log a
  warning naming the stored value and the reason, and fall back to the default name; a database read failure must be
  returned as an error.
- **SPEC-15.2005**: GET and PUT /settings/email, POST /settings/email/test-send, POST /settings/email/verify, GET and
  PUT /settings/google-contacts-client and GET and PUT /settings/app-name must be callable only by the deployment
  operator; any other authenticated caller, including another organisation's admin, must be refused.
- **SPEC-15.2006**: GET /settings must require authentication, must list only the caller's tenant settings ordered by
  category then key with limit/offset pagination and a total count, and must reject an unsupported sort parameter.
- **SPEC-15.2007**: PUT /settings (body category, key, value) must require an admin, must reject a category outside 1-50
  characters or a key outside 1-100 characters, must run the same value validation as the per-key route, and must upsert
  the (tenant, category, key) row and return its id, category, key and value.
- **SPEC-15.2008**: When the category is "branding", PUT /settings and PUT /settings/{category}/{key} must additionally
  verify that any tenant or company id embedded in the value belongs to the caller's tenant, and must answer 422 with a
  field error on "value" carrying the refusal message when it does not; nothing is stored in that case.
- **SPEC-15.2009**: GET /settings/{category} must require authentication and must return the caller's settings in that
  category ordered by key, as an unpaginated array that is empty when the category has no rows.
- **SPEC-15.2010**: GET /settings/{category}/{key} must require authentication and must answer 404 "Tenant setting" when
  the caller's tenant has no such row.
- **SPEC-15.2011**: PUT /settings/{category}/{key} (body {value}) must require an admin, must validate the value against
  the (category, key) shape table before writing, and must upsert the row, updating its updated_at on conflict.
- **SPEC-15.2012**: DELETE /settings/{category}/{key} must require an admin, must delete the caller's tenant row, and
  must answer 404 "Tenant setting" when no row was deleted.
- **SPEC-15.2013**: The literal routes under /settings (modules, email, google-contacts-client, app-name) must be
  matched before the generic /settings/{category} routes, and /settings/{category} must never write a system value.
- **SPEC-15.2014**: GET /settings/modules must require authentication and must list the caller's module configs ordered
  by module name with limit/offset pagination, a total count and unsupported-sort rejection.
- **SPEC-15.2015**: GET /settings/modules/{module} must require authentication and, when the tenant has no row for the
  module, must return a soft default with id null, is_enabled false and config {} instead of 404.
- **SPEC-15.2016**: PUT /settings/modules/{module} must require an admin and must upsert the tenant's row, replacing
  is_enabled and config and returning the stored row's id.
- **SPEC-15.2017**: Module-enabled checks must read a missing module_config row, or a null is_enabled, as disabled.
- **SPEC-15.2018**: Setting values for timesheets/track_breaks, integrations/google_contacts_enabled,
  integrations/icloud_contacts_enabled, integrations/microsoft_contacts_enabled, notifications/channel_email_enabled and
  notifications/channel_in_app_enabled must be booleans; any other JSON type must be refused with 422 "expected a
  boolean" on field "value".
- **SPEC-15.2019**: tickets/note_editing must be one of "off", "author_or_admin", "author_or_manager" and
  timesheets/segment_editing must be one of "off", "owner_or_admin", "owner_or_manager"; any other value, including a
  non-string, must be refused with 422 on field "value" naming the allowed set.
- **SPEC-15.2020**: notifications/default_locale must be a non-empty string of at most 10 bytes, else 422 "expected a
  non-empty locale string (max 10)".
- **SPEC-15.2021**: Branding values must be validated by the shared tenant-branding validator, so the settings endpoints
  and the tenant update endpoint agree on every key; an unknown branding key must be refused with 422 on field "value".
- **SPEC-15.2022**: billing_prefs/currency must be a 3-letter uppercase ASCII string, and
  billing_prefs/invoice_numbering must be exactly "tenant_sequence" or "company_prefix"; anything else must be refused
  with 422 on field "value".
- **SPEC-15.2023**: billing_reminders/enabled must be a boolean; billing_reminders/schedule must be a strictly ascending
  array of 1 to 10 integers each in 1..=365; billing_reminders/send_hour must be an integer in 0..=23; violations must
  be refused with 422 on field "value".
- **SPEC-15.2024**: ticketing/auto_close_resolved_after_days must be an integer in 1..=90,
  time_tracking/max_hours_per_day an integer in 1..=24, ci/impact_max_depth and workflows/rule_max_depth an integer in
  1..=10, and scheduling/default_due_business_days an integer in 0..=365; violations must be refused with 422 on field
  "value".
- **SPEC-15.2025**: email_intake/default_company_id must be a string that parses as a UUID, else 422 on field "value".
- **SPEC-15.2026**: A value for an unknown (category, key) outside branding must be accepted verbatim and a warning must
  be logged with the category, key, value type and value length; the logged value must be "<redacted>" when the category
  or key (case-insensitive) contains secret, password, passwd, token, credential, private, apikey, api_key or auth, and
  must otherwise be cut at 1024 bytes (on a character boundary) with a trailing "...".
- **SPEC-15.2027**: read_default_due_business_days must return the stored scheduling/default_due_business_days capped at
  365, and 0 (no default due date) when the row is missing or not an unsigned integer.
- **SPEC-15.2028**: read_max_minutes_per_day must return the stored time_tracking/max_hours_per_day clamped to 1..=24
  and multiplied by 60, and 1440 when the row is missing or not an unsigned integer.
- **SPEC-15.2029**: read_tenant_zone must return the timezone of the tenant's earliest-created default business_hours
  row, and "UTC" when the tenant has none.
- **SPEC-15.2030**: read_invoice_reminder_settings must default to enabled false, an empty schedule and send_hour 8 when
  rows are absent, must ignore a send_hour above 23, and must treat a non-boolean enabled as false.
- **SPEC-15.2031**: read_track_breaks must return false when the row is missing or not a boolean.
- **SPEC-15.2032**: read_note_editing and read_segment_editing must return the stored string, or None when the row is
  missing or not a string, leaving the default to the caller.
- **SPEC-15.2033**: read_google_contacts_enabled, read_icloud_contacts_enabled and read_microsoft_contacts_enabled must
  each read their own integrations key and must return true when the row is missing or not a boolean.
- **SPEC-15.2034**: read_default_currency must return the stored billing_prefs/currency string, and "USD" when the row
  is missing or not a string.
- **SPEC-15.2035**: read_email_intake_default_company must return None when the row is missing, not a string, or not a
  UUID.
- **SPEC-15.2036**: read_ci_impact_max_depth must return the stored value clamped to 1..=10 and 5 when unset;
  read_workflow_rule_max_depth must return the stored value clamped to 1..=10 and 3 when unset.
- **SPEC-15.2037**: GET /settings/email must return host, port, username, from, tls and password_set for the
  system-tenant email row, must never return the SMTP password, and with no stored row must return all fields null and
  password_set false.
- **SPEC-15.2038**: PUT /settings/email must keep a stored field when the input field is omitted, must clear a text
  field (falling back to the environment value) when it is an empty string, must clear the stored password when password
  is an empty string, and must store a non-empty password AES-256-GCM encrypted under the deployment encryption key,
  never in plaintext.
- **SPEC-15.2039**: PUT /settings/email must refuse an unparsable tls value and a from value that is not a valid
  mailbox, the latter with 400 "From <value> is not a valid address: <cause>", before storing anything.
- **SPEC-15.2040**: PUT /settings/email must build a mailer from the full effective configuration (environment baseline
  overridden by non-empty stored fields) before persisting, and must refuse the write without storing it when that
  fails, including with a Configuration error when a username is set without a password.
- **SPEC-15.2041**: After PUT /settings/email stores the row, the request must rebuild the mailer of the process's
  selected provider kind and swap it into the live handle so the change applies without a restart; the settings must
  shape the SMTP transport only and must not switch a deployment between the log and smtp providers.
- **SPEC-15.2042**: A stored email row that is not valid JSON for the email shape must fail the read with a 500 Internal
  error naming the cause.
- **SPEC-15.2043**: POST /settings/email/test-send (body {to}) must send a text email with subject "<app name> test
  email" to the address through the live mailer, must answer 204 on success, and must return the mailer's error
  unchanged when the address is malformed or delivery fails.
- **SPEC-15.2044**: POST /settings/email/verify must exercise the live mailer's transport without sending a message,
  must answer 204 when it succeeds, and must return the transport failure when it does not.
- **SPEC-15.2045**: GET /settings/google-contacts-client must return only client_id_set, client_secret_set, configured
  (both set), provider (the declared app-secret provider name), writable and restart_required (always false), and must
  never return the id or the secret.
- **SPEC-15.2046**: A Google client half must count as set only when the declared app-secret provider holds a non-blank
  value for it; a value in another provider must not count.
- **SPEC-15.2047**: PUT /settings/google-contacts-client must trim both client_id and client_secret, and must answer 422
  with a field error on the empty one (client_id first) when either is empty after trimming.
- **SPEC-15.2048**: PUT /settings/google-contacts-client must refuse a client_id that starts with "GOCSPX-" and a
  client_secret that ends with ".apps.googleusercontent.com" with a 422 field error saying the fields look swapped,
  without echoing the submitted value.
- **SPEC-15.2049**: PUT /settings/google-contacts-client must fail with a Configuration error when the declared
  app-secret provider cannot be built, and with 422 on client_id when the provider is not writable, in both cases
  storing nothing.
- **SPEC-15.2050**: PUT /settings/google-contacts-client must write the id then the secret to the declared provider
  while holding the live client's write lock across both writes, reading each value back after writing, and must fail
  with a Configuration error "Storing <secret> in the <provider> provider failed" if a write or read-back fails.
- **SPEC-15.2051**: After a successful Google client write the request must rebuild the live client from the stored
  values and swap it into the running process before writing the audit row, and must return the new view.
- **SPEC-15.2052**: PUT /settings/google-contacts-client must write one audit row on the system tenant (action update,
  entity "app_secrets") with event "google_contacts.client_set", the two secret names, the provider, configured, and
  replaced_a_configured_client; the row must never contain either value.

### 15.10 Seed data

- **SPEC-15.2053**: First-visit demo seeding must be enabled only when ENVIRONMENT (trimmed, case-insensitive, default
  "development") equals "production", or when MOKOSH_DEMO_SEED (trimmed, case-insensitive) is one of 1, true, yes, on;
  the decision must be made once per process and any other value must leave seeding off.
- **SPEC-15.2054**: The tenant named by OIDC_DEFAULT_TENANT_ID must never receive demo data: seeding it must be skipped,
  the tenant marked seen, and a debug line logged; when that variable does not parse as a UUID a warning naming the
  parse error must be logged and no tenant is excluded.
- **SPEC-15.2055**: The seed middleware must run after authentication; for a request carrying both a tenant and a user
  whose tenant the process has not yet settled, it must spawn the seed detached and call the next handler without
  waiting, and for a settled tenant it must spawn nothing and do no database work.
- **SPEC-15.2056**: ensure_demo_seeded must do nothing when seeding is disabled or the tenant is already seen; on
  success (seeded or not) it must mark the tenant seen, and on failure it must log a warning with the error and tenant
  id and leave the tenant unseen so the next authenticated request retries.
- **SPEC-15.2057**: The first-visit run must claim the tenant by atomically setting tenants.settings.demo_seeded to true
  only where it is not already true, and must insert nothing when the claim finds it already set.
- **SPEC-15.2058**: When a claimed tenant already has a company whose type is not "internal", the first-visit run must
  insert nothing, must leave demo_seeded set, and must log a debug line.
- **SPEC-15.2059**: load_demo_data (explicit load) must return AlreadyHasData without writing for the shared landing
  tenant or for a tenant that has a non-internal company; otherwise it must seed, set demo_seeded (logging a warning
  with the tenant id and error if that claim fails), mark the tenant seen, and return Seeded; a seeding failure must be
  returned as an error.
- **SPEC-15.2060**: The demo dataset must come from the embedded bundle: two companies and four contacts tagged "demo"
  (companies with portal access enabled), five tickets tagged "demo", two projects, and one non-default SLA policy
  attached only to the bundle's designated company; the first contact must be linked to both companies when at least two
  exist, with two phone numbers and the second link non-primary.
- **SPEC-15.2061**: Each demo project must be numbered DEMO-PRJ-001, DEMO-PRJ-002 and so on, be a billable client
  time-and-materials project at 150.00 per hour with a 40.00-hour and 10000.00 budget, start today and end in 30 days,
  be managed by the triggering user, and, when the bundle names one, get an in_progress phase running today to today
  plus 14 days and an example task in the tenant's first task status by sort order.
- **SPEC-15.2062**: Demo tickets must leave priority, status and queue unset so the tenant defaults apply, must link the
  bundle's company and contact, and must be billable; a ticket whose company index does not resolve must be skipped.
- **SPEC-15.2063**: During demo seeding a failure creating the SLA policy, a company, a contact or a project must abort
  the run with that error, while a failure creating a phase, a task or a ticket must log a warning with the error and
  tenant id and continue.
- **SPEC-15.2064**: portal_dev_seed must refuse to run unless ENVIRONMENT (case-insensitive, default "development") is
  development, dev or test, returning an error "portal-dev-seed refuses to run outside dev/test (ENVIRONMENT=<value>)"
  with no override and no writes.
- **SPEC-15.2065**: portal_dev_seed must be idempotent by slug and create three tenants: "acme" (active, with branding
  values), "beta" (active, empty branding) and "inact" (suspended, empty branding), each with one company and one portal
  contact, and an admin agent user for acme and beta only; it must return a report listing each row and whether anything
  was newly written, and an error naming the tenant slug and step for any failure.
- **SPEC-15.2066**: The portal contact seeded by portal_dev_seed must be created with is_portal_user true, a password
  hashed from the fixed development portal password, and its primary company link ensured in the same transaction; an
  existing contact with the same email in the tenant must be left untouched.
- **SPEC-15.2067**: The agent user seeded by portal_dev_seed must be an active, email-verified admin with a password
  hashed from the fixed development agent password, first name the capitalised slug and last name "Agent"; an existing
  user with the same email in the tenant must be left untouched.
- **SPEC-15.2068**: portal_dev_seed must copy the default tenant's notification templates and their rules for the event
  types appointment.reminder, sla.at_risk, sla.breached, auth.password_reset, auth.welcome, auth.portal_password_reset,
  auth.portal_welcome and forms.request_link into each seeded tenant that has no templates yet, relinking each rule to
  the copied template, and must skip the default tenant itself.
- **SPEC-15.2069**: confirm_qa_tenant must return BadRequest naming the tenant when it does not exist, Forbidden when
  settings.environment is "production" or "prod" (case-insensitive), and Forbidden unless settings.is_qa is the boolean
  true; every refusal must happen before any write.
- **SPEC-15.2070**: qa_seed and qa_teardown must call confirm_qa_tenant first and must not write to a tenant it refuses.
- **SPEC-15.2071**: qa_seed must be idempotent: when any company named with the "QA-" prefix exists in the tenant it
  must return a report with skipped true and write nothing.
- **SPEC-15.2072**: qa_seed must attribute its records to the tenant's oldest user and must fail with BadRequest "QA
  seed refused: tenant <id> has no users to attribute records to" when the tenant has none.
- **SPEC-15.2073**: The QA dataset must name every named record with the "QA-" prefix and tag every taggable record
  "qa-seed", and must include 35 tickets, projects with phases and tasks, time entries, contracts, products, invoices
  with payments, a credited invoice with a credit note, assets, knowledge-base articles, an SLA policy with a target,
  and appointments; any creation failure must be returned as an error.
- **SPEC-15.2074**: Seeded QA invoices that are paid or credited must first be moved to status sent with delivery method
  other and a note that delivery happened outside Mokosh, so that no email is sent and no payment is recorded against a
  draft.
- **SPEC-15.2075**: qa_teardown must delete the QA-prefixed dataset and the QA lookup rows it created (work types, task
  statuses, asset types, knowledge-base categories) in foreign-key order inside one transaction, must return the
  per-entity deleted counts, and must roll everything back and return the error if any statement fails.
- **SPEC-15.2076**: confirm_showcase_tenant must apply the QA guardrail to settings.is_showcase: BadRequest when the
  tenant does not exist, Forbidden when settings.environment is "production" or "prod", and Forbidden unless is_showcase
  is the boolean true, all before any write; showcase_seed, showcase_refresh and showcase_teardown must call it first.
- **SPEC-15.2077**: showcase_seed must be idempotent: when any company named with the "SHOWCASE-" prefix exists it must
  return skipped true and write nothing, and when the tenant has no users it must fail with BadRequest "Showcase seed
  refused: tenant <id> has no users to attribute records to".
- **SPEC-15.2078**: The showcase dataset must contain 20 "SHOWCASE-" companies with one contact each, 5 projects with
  two phases and tasks each, and time entries for the operator user for last week and this week; it must then submit and
  approve both weeks' timesheets as the operator, reporting approved_weeks 2.
- **SPEC-15.2079**: Showcase ticket creation (24 tickets) must be best-effort: a ticket that cannot be created must log
  a warning with the error and tenant id, be skipped, and not be counted; every other creation failure must abort the
  seed with the error.
- **SPEC-15.2080**: showcase_refresh must tear the showcase dataset down and then seed it again in one call, and
  showcase_teardown must delete the "SHOWCASE-" dataset and its lookup rows (work types, task statuses) in foreign-key
  order inside one transaction, returning the deleted counts and rolling back on any failure.

### 15.11 Branding

- **SPEC-15.2081**: effective_branding must merge tenant and company branding field by field over logo_url, logo_mime,
  favicon_url, favicon_mime, primary_color, secondary_color, background_color, background_url, background_mime,
  display_name, company_name, support_email, support_phone, support_contact_name and portal_domain, taking the company
  value when present and the tenant value otherwise, and leaving a field absent when neither has it; secondary_color
  must fall back from the company value to the tenant secondary_color and then to the tenant accent_color.
- **SPEC-15.2082**: customer_branding must start from the effective branding and, only when neither display_name nor
  company_name is non-blank after trimming, must set company_name to the trimmed organization name when that is
  non-empty; it must never invent display_name and must never override a configured name.
- **SPEC-15.2083**: Branding image uploads must accept only image/png, image/jpeg, image/webp and image/gif, comparing
  the content type case-insensitively after dropping any ";" parameters, and must refuse anything else, SVG included,
  with 400 "Unsupported image type `<type>`. Use PNG, JPEG, WebP or GIF.".
- **SPEC-15.2084**: Storing a branding image must refuse an empty body with 400 "The uploaded file is empty." and a body
  larger than the configured cap for its scope and kind with the shared oversized-upload error.
- **SPEC-15.2085**: The upload cap must come from the configuration key for the scope and kind (tenant logo
  TENANT_LOGO_MAX_BYTES, the other tenant and company kinds their BRANDING_TENANT_* and BRANDING_COMPANY_* keys) and
  must default to 1 MiB for logos, 512 KiB for favicons and 2 MiB for backgrounds; an invalid configured value must fail
  with a Configuration error.
- **SPEC-15.2086**: A tenant logo must be stored through the shared object store under the tenant-logo key for its
  extension, and, when a file ledger is attached, recorded there with entity type "tenant_logo", the logo size and no
  uploader; every other tenant kind and every company kind must be written to the storage root under
  <tenant>/branding/<kind>.<ext> for tenants and <tenant>/branding/company-<logos|favicons|backgrounds>/<company>.<ext>
  for companies, creating directories as needed and failing with a 500 Internal error naming the cause on a write
  failure.
- **SPEC-15.2087**: After a branding image is stored, copies of the same asset under the other allowed extensions and
  the legacy locations must be deleted, and a failed deletion must be logged as a warning naming the key or path and
  error without failing the upload; removing an asset must delete every allowed extension the same way.
- **SPEC-15.2088**: Reading, statting or opening a branding asset must look in the current location first and then the
  legacy location, must refuse an unsupported stored type with 400, and must answer 404 "Asset" when neither exists.
- **SPEC-15.2089**: The ETag of a filesystem asset must be the quoted string "<scope id>-<kind directory>-<size>", and
  that of a tenant logo "<tenant id>-logo-<size>" with the size taken from the file ledger; a tenant logo with no ledger
  attached or no ledger record must be 404 "Asset".
- **SPEC-15.2090**: Public branding URLs must be /api/v1/public/tenants/{id}/{logo|favicon|background} for tenant assets
  and /api/v1/public/companies/{id}/{logo|favicon|background} for company assets.
- **SPEC-15.2091**: PUT /companies/{company_id}/{asset} must require an admin (else 403 "You do not have permission to
  perform this action."), must answer 404 "asset kind" for an asset segment other than logo, favicon or background, must
  answer 404 "Company" when the company is not in the caller's tenant, and must limit the request body to the largest
  configured company cap.
- **SPEC-15.2092**: PUT /tenants/current/branding/{asset} must require an admin with the same 403 and 404 "asset kind"
  behaviour, must write the caller's own tenant, and must limit the request body to the largest configured tenant cap.
- **SPEC-15.2093**: DELETE /companies/{company_id}/{asset} and DELETE /tenants/current/branding/{asset} must require an
  admin, must apply the same asset-segment and company-in-tenant checks, and must answer {"ok": true}.
- **SPEC-15.2094**: PUT and DELETE /companies/self/{asset} on the contact plane must require a contact session holding
  the settings:manage_company_branding capability and must act only on the session's own company and tenant, answering
  404 "asset kind" for an unknown asset segment.
- **SPEC-15.2095**: An upload must read the multipart part named "file", use that part's content type
  (application/octet-stream when absent, which is refused), ignore other parts, and answer 400 "Missing 'file' part in
  the multipart body." when it is absent and 400 "Could not parse the multipart body: <cause>." or "Could not read the
  multipart body: <cause>." when the body is malformed.
- **SPEC-15.2096**: A successful upload must store the file and then merge <kind>_url (the public asset path) and
  <kind>_mime into the branding JSON of the company or tenant row, and must answer 200 {ok: true, asset, url, mime};
  when no company or tenant row is updated it must answer 404 "Company" or "Tenant".
- **SPEC-15.2097**: A delete must first set <kind>_url and <kind>_mime to null in the branding JSON (404 "Company" or
  "Tenant" when no row is updated) and only then remove the stored files, logging a warning for any file that cannot be
  removed.
- **SPEC-15.2098**: GET /api/v1/public/companies/{company_id}/{asset} and GET /api/v1/public/tenants/{tenant_id}/{asset}
  must require no authentication, must answer 404 "Asset" when the entity has no stored <kind>_mime or the file is
  missing, and 404 "asset kind" for an unknown segment.
- **SPEC-15.2099**: A served branding asset must answer 200 with Content-Type the stored mime, Content-Length the file
  size, Cache-Control "public, max-age=3600" and the ETag, streaming the body and logging an error when a stream read
  fails; when If-None-Match lists the ETag (comma-separated, optional W/ prefix) or "*" it must answer 304 with the same
  Cache-Control and ETag and no body.
- **SPEC-15.2100**: At boot the branding mover must run once as the one-shot "branding_mover_pms_1397" and move files
  from the legacy tenant-favicons, tenant-backgrounds, company-logos, company-favicons and company-backgrounds
  directories to the current layout, resolving a company file's tenant from the companies table; it must skip with a
  warning a file whose name is not a UUID or whose company does not exist, must delete the legacy file when the
  destination already exists, must copy then delete otherwise (logging a warning if the delete fails), must abort with a
  500 Internal error naming the path on a directory read or copy failure, and must log the moved and skipped counts at
  info.

### 15.12 Features and status

- **SPEC-15.2101**: The feature registry must define exactly the switches integrations_overview, assets_search_v2,
  assets_catalog, delegated_invoice_issuer and delegated_bills, each with a unique lowercase key made of a-z, 0-9 and
  underscore starting with a letter, and a label, help text and tracker reference.
- **SPEC-15.2102**: A feature must read as on only when a feature_toggles row for its key has enabled true; a missing
  row, an enabled false row, and a row whose key names no registered feature must all read as off, and the last must log
  one warning per key per process naming the key.
- **SPEC-15.2103**: GET /settings/feature-toggles must be callable only by the deployment operator and must return every
  registered feature in registry order with key, label, help, issue and enabled (false without a row), plus updated_at
  and updated_by only when a row exists; a database failure must answer with a Database error "could not read
  feature_toggles: <cause>".
- **SPEC-15.2104**: PUT /settings/feature-toggles/{key} (body {enabled}) must be callable only by the deployment
  operator and must answer 404 "no feature named <key>; this build registers <comma-separated keys>" for an unregistered
  key, writing nothing.
- **SPEC-15.2105**: Setting a feature must upsert its row with enabled, updated_at now and updated_by the caller, and
  must write an audit row on the system tenant in the same transaction (action update, entity feature_toggles, old value
  {key, enabled before, false when there was no row}, new value {event "feature_toggle.set", key, enabled, issue}); on
  any failure nothing may be committed and the error must be a Database error "could not write the feature toggle:
  <cause>", and success must log an info line with key, enabled and previous state.
- **SPEC-15.2106**: After a successful PUT the handler must reload every row and swap the process's snapshot before
  answering, so the caller's next request sees the new state, and must answer with the feature view including updated_at
  and updated_by.
- **SPEC-15.2107**: The job "feature_toggle_refresh" must reload all feature_toggles rows every 60 seconds and once at
  startup, replacing the snapshot and logging an info line with the new state when it differs; when a load fails it must
  return the error and leave the previous snapshot in place.
- **SPEC-15.2108**: GET /config must require no authentication and must return {"features": {<key>: <bool>}} listing
  every registered feature from the current snapshot, with false for features that are off or unset.
- **SPEC-15.2109**: POST /rmm/status must authenticate by an HMAC-SHA256 of the raw request body keyed with the
  connection's stored api_secret, sent base64-encoded in X-Signature, with the tenant named by a UUID in X-Tenant-Id and
  compared in constant time; an unparsable body, a missing or malformed header, a connection without a secret for that
  tenant, or a signature mismatch must answer 401 Unauthorized and record nothing.
- **SPEC-15.2110**: An ingested status must be refused with 422 on field check_kind when it is not one of backup, disk,
  patch, antivirus and on field outcome when it is not one of success, warning, failure, unknown, each message naming
  the rejected value and the accepted set.
- **SPEC-15.2111**: Ingest must resolve the company from the rmm_device_mappings row for the tenant, connection and
  device id and, when none exists, must answer 422 on field rmm_device_id with a message naming the device id and
  telling the operator to map it, writing nothing.
- **SPEC-15.2112**: Ingest must upsert the monitored system keyed on tenant, source "tactical_rmm" and device id,
  setting last_seen_at to now, updating company_id from the mapping, clearing any soft deletion, keeping the stored name
  unless the system had been soft-deleted (then using system_name), and setting first_seen_at only on creation.
- **SPEC-15.2113**: Ingest must insert the observation (check_kind, outcome, observed_at, payload) once per (system,
  check_kind, observed_at) and must answer 204 No Content both when it was recorded and when it was a duplicate, which
  must change nothing.
- **SPEC-15.2114**: GET /status/systems/{id}/current must require authentication and return the system's id, tenant,
  company, source, external id, name, first and last seen times and the latest observation per check kind, answering 404
  "Monitored system" when the system is not in the caller's tenant or is soft-deleted.
- **SPEC-15.2115**: GET /status/companies/{company_id}/backup must require authentication and return every non-deleted
  monitored system of the company in the caller's tenant ordered by name, each with its latest backup observation or
  null when it has none.
- **SPEC-15.2116**: GET /reports/status/backup-success-rate must require authentication and company_id, from and to,
  must answer 422 on field from "from must be earlier than to" unless from is before to, and must count backup
  observations in the half-open window [from, to) for the caller's tenant, returning success, total and rate = success /
  total, or 1.0 when total is 0.
- **SPEC-15.2117**: GET /reports/status/uptime must apply the same authentication and window rules and count
  observations of every check kind in [from, to), treating success and warning as up and failure and unknown as not up,
  returning up_observations, total_observations and rate = up / total, or 1.0 when total is 0.
- **SPEC-15.2118**: The job "status_retention" must delete every status_observations row, across all tenants, whose
  observed_at is older than the retention window (default 395 days) every 6 hours, logging an info line with the cutoff
  and count when it removed rows and a debug line otherwise, and must return the database error when the delete fails.

### 15.13 Data transfer and search

- **SPEC-15.2119**: GET /search must be open to any authenticated tenant member, must use at most the first 200
  characters of the q parameter (default empty), and must return an empty envelope (empty lists and zero counts) without
  touching the database when q is empty or whitespace-only after trimming.
- **SPEC-15.2120**: Search must match the trimmed query case-insensitively as a substring, treating backslash, percent
  and underscore in the query literally, and must run all five entity searches in one transaction scoped to the caller's
  tenant, so another tenant's rows are never returned.
- **SPEC-15.2121**: Search must return at most 5 hits per section while counts carries the total number of matches per
  section: tickets (title, ticket number or description; newest update first; label "<number> <title>", secondary the
  company name), contacts (first name, last name or email; ordered by last then first name; label "<first> <last>",
  secondary the company name), companies (name; ordered by name; secondary the industry), assets (name, serial number or
  asset tag; ordered by name; secondary the company name, else the serial number) and projects (name; newest update
  first; secondary the company name).
- **SPEC-15.2122**: Search must answer with the JSON object {tickets, contacts, companies, assets, projects, counts:
  {tickets, contacts, companies, assets, projects}} with each hit {id, label, secondary}, and must fail the whole
  request with the database error rather than return a partial result when any section query fails.
- **SPEC-15.2123**: GET /data/export must require an admin and must export every public-schema table that has a
  tenant_id column, except payment_gateway_configs, credential_vault, api_keys, rmm_connections, users, user_sessions,
  password_reset_tokens, portal_setup_tokens, tenant_intake_tokens, tenant_invitations, audit_log, asset_audit_log and
  email_intake_log, limited to the caller's tenant rows, and must drop from every row each column whose name contains
  "encrypted", "password_hash", "_secret", "mfa_secret", "api_key", "api_secret" or "private_key".
- **SPEC-15.2124**: The export must respond 200 as an attachment named mokosh-export-<tenant id>.json with content type
  application/json; charset=utf-8 and a pretty-printed envelope holding schema_version 1, tenant_id, tenant_name,
  included_tables, excluded_tables, redacted_column_patterns, a notes string stating attachments are metadata-only, and
  entities keyed by table; it must record an export audit row (entity tenant_data) in the same transaction and must
  return the error and no file when any query, the audit write or the serialisation fails.
- **SPEC-15.2125**: POST /data/import must require an admin, must accept a JSON body of at most 25 MiB shaped {confirm,
  export: {schema_version, entities}}, and must refuse an export whose schema_version is not 1 with 400 "Unsupported
  schema_version <n> (expected 1)".
- **SPEC-15.2126**: Import must refuse with 400 "Envelope contains an unexpected table: <name>" any entity name that is
  not a lowercase identifier or is on the export exclusion list, and with 400 "Envelope table <name> is not a current
  tenant table (schema drift)" any entity that is not a current table with a tenant_id column, in both cases before
  writing anything.
- **SPEC-15.2127**: Import must refuse with 400 "Confirmation does not match the tenant name" unless the trimmed confirm
  string equals the trimmed name of the caller's tenant, and must write nothing in that case.
- **SPEC-15.2128**: Import must run in one transaction with constraints deferred: it must delete the caller's tenant
  rows from every tenant table except users and user_sessions, then insert every envelope row after setting tenant_id to
  the caller's tenant and replacing each string value equal to an exported row id with one new UUID chosen consistently
  across all tables, then rewrite each tenants column that referenced an imported table to the remapped id of its
  previous value.
- **SPEC-15.2129**: After a successful import the request must record an import audit row (entity tenant_data) in the
  same transaction, commit, clear the in-process seeded-tenant record for the tenant, and answer 200 {status:
  "imported", tenant_id, imported: {<table>: <row count>}}; any failing statement must roll the whole import back and
  return the error.
- **SPEC-15.2130**: POST /data/seed-demo must require an admin and load the demo dataset into the caller's tenant
  through the seed service, answering 200 {seeded: true, message} when loaded and {seeded: false, message} when the
  tenant already has data, and returning the error when seeding fails.
